PythonQt.Qt.QAbstractAnimation.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

The class defines the functions for the functionality shared by all animations. By
inheriting this class, you can create custom animations that plug into the rest of the
animation framework.

The progress of an animation is given by its current time
([currentLoopTime](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractanimation.html#currentLoopTime)()),
which is measured in milliseconds from the start of the animation (0) to its end
([duration](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractanimation.html#duration)()). The
value is updated automatically while the animation is running. It can also be set
directly with
[setCurrentTime](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractanimation.html#currentTime-prop)().

At any point an animation is in one of three states:
[Running](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractanimation.html#State-enum),
[Stopped](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractanimation.html#State-enum), or
[Paused](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractanimation.html#State-enum)--as
defined by the
[State](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractanimation.html#State-enum) enum. The
current state can be changed by calling
[start](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractanimation.html#start)(),
[stop](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractanimation.html#stop)(),
[pause](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractanimation.html#pause)(), or
[resume](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractanimation.html#resume)(). An
animation will always reset its [current
time](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractanimation.html#currentTime-prop) when
it is started. If paused, it will continue with the same current time when resumed. When
an animation is stopped, it cannot be resumed, but will keep its current time (until
started again). QAbstractAnimation will emit
[stateChanged](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractanimation.html#stateChanged)()
whenever its state changes.

An animation can loop any number of times by setting the
[loopCount](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractanimation.html#loopCount-prop)
property. When an animation's current time reaches its
[duration](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractanimation.html#duration)(), it
will reset the current time and keep running. A loop count of 1 (the default value)
means that the animation will run one time. Note that a duration of -1 means that the
animation will run until stopped; the current time will increase indefinitely. When the
current time equals
[duration](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractanimation.html#duration)() and
the animation is in its final loop, the
[Stopped](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractanimation.html#State-enum) state
is entered, and the
[finished](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractanimation.html#finished)() signal
is emitted.

QAbstractAnimation provides pure virtual functions used by subclasses to track the
progress of the animation:
[duration](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractanimation.html#duration)() and
[updateCurrentTime](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractanimation.html#updateCurrentTime)().
The [duration](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractanimation.html#duration)()
function lets you report a duration for the animation (as discussed above). The
animation framework calls
[updateCurrentTime](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractanimation.html#updateCurrentTime)()
when current time has changed. By reimplementing this function, you can track the
animation progress. Note that neither the interval between calls nor the number of calls
to this function are defined; though, it will normally be 60 updates per second.

By reimplementing
[updateState](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractanimation.html#updateState)(),
you can track the animation's state changes, which is particularly useful for animations
that are not driven by time.

### currentLoop : const int

This property holds the current loop of the animation

This property describes the current loop of the animation. By default, the animation's
loop count is 1, and so the current loop will always be 0\. If the loop count is 2 and
the animation runs past its duration, it will automatically rewind and restart at
current time 0, and current loop 1, and so on.

When the current loop changes,
[QAbstractAnimation](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractanimation.html) emits
the
[currentLoopChanged](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractanimation.html#currentLoopChanged)()
signal.

### currentTime : int

This property holds the current time and progress of the animation

This property describes the animation's current time. You can change the current time by
calling setCurrentTime, or you can call
[start](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractanimation.html#start)() and let the
animation run, setting the current time automatically as the animation progresses.

The animation's current time starts at 0, and ends at
[totalDuration](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractanimation.html#totalDuration)().

Qt 5 reference:

### duration : const int

This property holds the duration of the animation.

If the duration is -1, it means that the duration is undefined. In this case,
[loopCount](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractanimation.html#loopCount-prop)
is ignored.

**Access functions:**

| virtual int | **[duration](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractanimation.html#duration)**() const \= 0 |
| --- | --- |

### `[pure virtual]` int QAbstractAnimation::duration() const

This pure virtual function returns the duration of the animation, and defines for how
long [QAbstractAnimation](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractanimation.html)
should update the current time. This duration is local, and does not include the loop
count.

A return value of -1 indicates that the animation has no defined duration; the animation
should run forever until stopped. This is useful for animations that are not time
driven, or where you cannot easily predict its duration (e.g., event driven audio
playback in a game).

If the animation is a parallel
[QAnimationGroup](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qanimationgroup.html), the duration
will be the longest duration of all its animations. If the animation is a sequential
[QAnimationGroup](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qanimationgroup.html), the duration
will be the sum of the duration of all its animations.

**Note:** Getter function for property duration.

**See also**
[loopCount](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractanimation.html#loopCount-prop).

### loopCount : int

This property holds the loop count of the animation

This property describes the loop count of the animation as an integer. By default this
value is 1, indicating that the animation should run once only, and then stop. By
changing it you can let the animation loop several times. With a value of 0, the
animation will not run at all, and with a value of -1, the animation will loop forever
until stopped. It is not supported to have loop on an animation that has an undefined
duration. It will only run once.

**Access functions:**

| int | **loopCount**() const |
| --- | --- |
| void | **setLoopCount**(int *loopCount*) |

### `[slot]` void QAbstractAnimation::pause()

Pauses the animation. When the animation is paused,
[state](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractanimation.html#state-prop)() returns
Paused. The value of
[currentTime](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractanimation.html#currentTime-prop)
will remain unchanged until
[resume](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractanimation.html#resume)() or
[start](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractanimation.html#start)() is called.
If you want to continue from the current time, call
[resume](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractanimation.html#resume)().

**See also**
[start](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractanimation.html#start)(),
[state](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractanimation.html#state-prop)(), and
[resume](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractanimation.html#resume)().

### `[slot]` void QAbstractAnimation::resume()

resumed() and

**See also**
[start](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractanimation.html#start)(),
[pause](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractanimation.html#pause)(), and

PythonQt.Qt.QAbstractAnimation.start.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

### `[slot]` void QAbstractAnimation::start([QAbstractAnimation::DeletionPolicy](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractanimation.html#DeletionPolicy-enum) *policy* \= KeepWhenStopped)

Starts the animation. The *policy* argument says whether or not the animation should be
deleted when it's done. When the animation starts, the
[stateChanged](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractanimation.html#stateChanged)()
signal is emitted, and
[state](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractanimation.html#state-prop)() returns
Running. When control reaches the event loop, the animation will run by itself,
periodically calling
[updateCurrentTime](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractanimation.html#updateCurrentTime)()
as the animation progresses.

If the animation is currently stopped or has already reached the end, calling start()
will rewind the animation and start again from the beginning. When the animation reaches
the end, the animation will either stop, or if the loop level is more than 1, it will
rewind and continue from the beginning.

If the animation is already running, this function does nothing.

**See also** [stop](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractanimation.html#stop)()
and [state](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractanimation.html#state-prop)().

### `[slot]` void QAbstractAnimation::stop()

Stops the animation. When the animation is stopped, it emits the
[stateChanged](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractanimation.html#stateChanged)()
signal, and
[state](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractanimation.html#state-prop)() returns
Stopped. The current time is not changed.

If the animation stops by itself after reaching the end (i.e.,
[currentLoopTime](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractanimation.html#currentLoopTime)()
\=\= [duration](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractanimation.html#duration)()
and
[currentLoop](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractanimation.html#currentLoop-prop)()
\>
[loopCount](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractanimation.html#loopCount-prop)()
\- 1), the
[finished](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractanimation.html#finished)() signal
is emitted.

**See also** [start](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractanimation.html#start)()
and [state](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractanimation.html#state-prop)().

PythonQt.Qt.QAbstractButton.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

This class implements an *abstract* button. Subclasses of this class handle user
actions, and specify how the button is drawn.

QAbstractButton provides support for both push buttons and checkable (toggle) buttons.
Checkable buttons are implemented in the
[QRadioButton](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qradiobutton.html) and
[QCheckBox](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcheckbox.html) classes. Push buttons are
implemented in the [QPushButton](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpushbutton.html)
and [QToolButton](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtoolbutton.html) classes; these
also provide toggle behavior if required.

Any button can display a label containing text and an icon.
[setText](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractbutton.html#text-prop)() sets the
text; [setIcon](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractbutton.html#icon-prop)()
sets the icon. If a button is disabled, its label is changed to give the button a
"disabled" appearance.

If the button is a text button with a string containing an ampersand ('\&'),
QAbstractButton automatically creates a shortcut key. For example:

```
QPushButton *button = new QPushButton(tr("Ro&ck && Roll"), this);
```

The **Alt\+C** shortcut is assigned to the button, i.e., when the user presses
**Alt\+C** the button will call
[animateClick](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractbutton.html#animateClick)().
See the [QShortcut](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qshortcut.html#mnemonic)
documentation for details. To display an actual ampersand, use '\&\&'.

You can also set a custom shortcut key using the
[setShortcut](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractbutton.html#shortcut-prop)()
function. This is useful mostly for buttons that do not have any text, and therefore
can't have any automatic shortcut.

```
button->setIcon(QIcon(":/images/print.png"));
button->setShortcut(tr("Alt+F7"));
```

All the buttons provided by Qt
([QPushButton](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpushbutton.html),
[QToolButton](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtoolbutton.html),
[QCheckBox](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcheckbox.html), and
[QRadioButton](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qradiobutton.html)) can display both
[text](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractbutton.html#text-prop) and
[icons](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/stylesheet-reference.html#icon).

A button can be made the default button in a dialog by means of
[QPushButton::setDefault](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpushbutton.html#default-prop)()
and
[QPushButton::setAutoDefault](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpushbutton.html#autoDefault-prop)().

QAbstractButton provides most of the states used for buttons:

- [isDown](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractbutton.html#down-prop)() indicates whether the button is *pressed* down.
- [isChecked](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractbutton.html#checked-prop)() indicates whether the button is *checked*. Only checkable buttons can be checked and unchecked (see below).
- [isEnabled](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#enabled-prop)() indicates whether the button can be pressed by the user.

  **Note:** As opposed to other widgets, buttons derived from QAbstractButton accept mouse
  and context menu events when disabled.
- [setAutoRepeat](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractbutton.html#autoRepeat-prop)() sets whether the button will auto-repeat if the user holds it down. [autoRepeatDelay](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractbutton.html#autoRepeatDelay-prop) and [autoRepeatInterval](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractbutton.html#autoRepeatInterval-prop) define how auto-repetition is done.
- [setCheckable](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractbutton.html#checkable-prop)() sets whether the button is a toggle button or not.

The difference between
[isDown](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractbutton.html#down-prop)() and
[isChecked](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractbutton.html#checked-prop)() is
as follows. When the user clicks a toggle button to check it, the button is first
*pressed* then released into the *checked* state. When the user clicks it again (to
uncheck it), the button moves first to the *pressed* state, then to the *unchecked*
state
([isChecked](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractbutton.html#checked-prop)() and
[isDown](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractbutton.html#down-prop)() are both
false).

QAbstractButton provides four signals:

1. [pressed](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractbutton.html#pressed)() is emitted when the left mouse button is pressed while the mouse cursor is inside the button.
2. [released](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractbutton.html#released)() is emitted when the left mouse button is released.
3. [clicked](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractbutton.html#clicked)() is emitted when the button is first pressed and then released, when the shortcut key is typed, or when [click](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractbutton.html#click)() or [animateClick](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractbutton.html#animateClick)() is called.
4. [toggled](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractbutton.html#toggled)() is emitted when the state of a toggle button changes.

To subclass QAbstractButton, you must reimplement at least
[paintEvent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractbutton.html#paintEvent)() to
draw the button's outline and its text or pixmap. It is generally advisable to
reimplement [sizeHint](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#sizeHint-prop)()
as well, and sometimes
[hitButton](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractbutton.html#hitButton)() (to
determine whether a button press is within the button). For buttons with more than two
states (like tri-state buttons), you will also have to reimplement
[checkStateSet](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractbutton.html#checkStateSet)()
and
[nextCheckState](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractbutton.html#nextCheckState)().

behave as if they were part of the same exclusive button group. In an exclusive button

PythonQt.Qt.QAbstractButton.toggled.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

### `[signal]` void QAbstractButton::toggled(bool *checked*)

This signal is emitted whenever a checkable button changes its state. *checked* is true
if the button is checked, or false if the button is unchecked.

This may be the result of a user action,
[click](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractbutton.html#click)() slot
activation, or because
[setChecked](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractbutton.html#checked-prop)() is
called.

The states of buttons in exclusive button groups are updated before this signal is
emitted. This means that slots can act on either the "off" signal or the "on" signal
emitted by the buttons in the group whose states have changed.

For example, a slot that reacts to signals emitted by newly checked buttons but which
ignores signals from buttons that have been unchecked can be implemented using the
following pattern:

```
void MyWidget::reactToToggle(bool checked)
{
   if (checked) {
      // Examine the new button states.
      ...
   }
}
```

Button groups can be created using the
[QButtonGroup](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qbuttongroup.html) class, and updates
to the button states monitored with the
[QButtonGroup::buttonClicked](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qbuttongroup.html#buttonClicked)()
signal.

**Note:** Notifier signal for property
[checked](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractbutton.html#checked-prop).

**See also**
[checked](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractbutton.html#checked-prop) and
[clicked](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractbutton.html#clicked)().

PythonQt.Qt.QAbstractItemDelegate.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

A QAbstractItemDelegate provides the interface and common functionality for delegates in
the model/view architecture. Delegates display individual items in views, and handle the
editing of model data.

The QAbstractItemDelegate class is one of the [Model/View
Classes](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/model-view-programming.html#model-view-classes)
and is part of Qt's [model/view
framework](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/model-view-programming.html).

To render an item in a custom way, you must implement
[paint](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemdelegate.html#paint)() and
[sizeHint](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemdelegate.html#sizeHint)().
The [QStyledItemDelegate](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstyleditemdelegate.html)
class provides default implementations for these functions; if you do not need custom
rendering, subclass that class instead.

We give an example of drawing a progress bar in items; in our case for a package
management program.

![](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/images/widgetdelegate.png)

We create the `WidgetDelegate` class, which inherits from
[QStyledItemDelegate](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstyleditemdelegate.html). We
do the drawing in the
[paint](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemdelegate.html#paint)() function:

```
void WidgetDelegate::paint(QPainter *painter, const QStyleOptionViewItem &option,
                           const QModelIndex &index) const
{
    if (index.column() == 1) {
        int progress = index.data().toInt();

        QStyleOptionProgressBar progressBarOption;
        progressBarOption.rect = option.rect;
        progressBarOption.minimum = 0;
        progressBarOption.maximum = 100;
        progressBarOption.progress = progress;
        progressBarOption.text = QString::number(progress) + "%";
        progressBarOption.textVisible = true;

        QApplication::style()->drawControl(QStyle::CE_ProgressBar,
                                           &progressBarOption, painter);
    } else
        QStyledItemDelegate::paint(painter, option, index);
```

Notice that we use a
[QStyleOptionProgressBar](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstyleoptionprogressbar.html)
and initialize its members. We can then use the current
[QStyle](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstyle.html) to draw it.

To provide custom editing, there are two approaches that can be used. The first approach
is to create an editor widget and display it directly on top of the item. To do this you
must reimplement
[createEditor](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemdelegate.html#createEditor)()
to provide an editor widget,
[setEditorData](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemdelegate.html#setEditorData)()
to populate the editor with the data from the model, and
[setModelData](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemdelegate.html#setModelData)()
so that the delegate can update the model with data from the editor.

The second approach is to handle user events directly by reimplementing
[editorEvent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemdelegate.html#editorEvent)().

PythonQt.Qt.QAbstractItemModel.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

The QAbstractItemModel class defines the standard interface that item models must use to
be able to interoperate with other components in the model/view architecture. It is not
supposed to be instantiated directly. Instead, you should subclass it to create new
models.

The QAbstractItemModel class is one of the [Model/View
Classes](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/model-view-programming.html#model-view-classes)
and is part of Qt's [model/view
framework](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/model-view-programming.html). It can be
used as the underlying data model for the item view elements in QML or the item view
classes in the Qt Widgets module.

If you need a model to use with an item view such as QML's List View element or the
C\+\+ widgets [QListView](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qlistview.html) or
[QTableView](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtableview.html), you should consider
subclassing
[QAbstractListModel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractlistmodel.html) or
[QAbstractTableModel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstracttablemodel.html)
instead of this class.

The underlying data model is exposed to views and delegates as a hierarchy of tables. If
you do not make use of the hierarchy, then the model is a simple table of rows and
columns. Each item has a unique index specified by a
[QModelIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmodelindex.html).

![](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/images/modelindex-no-parent.png)

Every item of data that can be accessed via a model has an associated model index. You
can obtain this model index using the
[index](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#index)() function.
Each index may have a
[sibling](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#sibling)() index;
child items have a
[parent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#parent)() index.

Each item has a number of data elements associated with it and they can be retrieved by
specifying a role (see
[Qt::ItemDataRole](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#ItemDataRole-enum)) to the
model's [data](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#data)()
function. Data for all available roles can be obtained at the same time using the
[itemData](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#itemData)()
function.

Data for each role is set using a particular
[Qt::ItemDataRole](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#ItemDataRole-enum). Data
for individual roles are set individually with
[setData](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#setData)(), or they
can be set for all roles with
[setItemData](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#setItemData)().

Items can be queried with
[flags](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#flags)() (see
[Qt::ItemFlag](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#ItemFlag-enum)) to see if they
can be selected, dragged, or manipulated in other ways.

If an item has child objects,
[hasChildren](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#hasChildren)()
returns `true` for the corresponding index.

The model has a
[rowCount](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#rowCount)() and a
[columnCount](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#columnCount)()
for each level of the hierarchy. Rows and columns can be inserted and removed with
[insertRows](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#insertRows)(),
[insertColumns](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#insertColumns)(),
[removeRows](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#removeRows)(),
and
[removeColumns](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#removeColumns)().

The model emits signals to indicate changes. For example,
[dataChanged](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#dataChanged)()
is emitted whenever items of data made available by the model are changed. Changes to
the headers supplied by the model cause
[headerDataChanged](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#headerDataChanged)()
to be emitted. If the structure of the underlying data changes, the model can emit
[layoutChanged](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#layoutChanged)()
to indicate to any attached views that they should redisplay any items shown, taking the
new structure into account.

The items available through the model can be searched for particular data using the
[match](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#match)() function.

To sort the model, you can use
[sort](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#sort)().

### Subclassing

**Note:** Some general guidelines for subclassing models are available in the [Model
Subclassing
Reference](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/model-view-programming.html#model-subclassing-reference).

When subclassing QAbstractItemModel, at the very least you must implement
[index](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#index)(),
[parent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#parent)(),
[rowCount](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#rowCount)(),
[columnCount](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#columnCount)(),
and [data](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#data)(). These
functions are used in all read-only models, and form the basis of editable models.

You can also reimplement
[hasChildren](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#hasChildren)()
to provide special behavior for models where the implementation of
[rowCount](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#rowCount)() is
expensive. This makes it possible for models to restrict the amount of data requested by
views, and can be used as a way to implement lazy population of model data.

To enable editing in your model, you must also implement
[setData](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#setData)(), and
reimplement [flags](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#flags)()
to ensure that `ItemIsEditable` is returned. You can also reimplement
[headerData](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#headerData)()
and
[setHeaderData](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#setHeaderData)()
to control the way the headers for your model are presented.

The
[dataChanged](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#dataChanged)()
and
[headerDataChanged](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#headerDataChanged)()
signals must be emitted explicitly when reimplementing the
[setData](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#setData)() and
[setHeaderData](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#setHeaderData)()
functions, respectively.

Custom models need to create model indexes for other components to use. To do this, call
[createIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#createIndex)()
with suitable row and column numbers for the item, and an identifier for it, either as a
pointer or as an integer value. The combination of these values must be unique for each
item. Custom models typically use these unique identifiers in other reimplemented
functions to retrieve item data and access information about the item's parents and
children. See the [Simple Tree Model
Example](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtwidgets-itemviews-simpletreemodel-example.html)
for more information about unique identifiers.

It is not necessary to support every role defined in
[Qt::ItemDataRole](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#ItemDataRole-enum).
Depending on the type of data contained within a model, it may only be useful to
implement the [data](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#data)()
function to return valid information for some of the more common roles. Most models
provide at least a textual representation of item data for the
[Qt::DisplayRole](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#ItemDataRole-enum), and
well-behaved models should also provide valid information for the
[Qt::ToolTipRole](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#ItemDataRole-enum) and
[Qt::WhatsThisRole](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#ItemDataRole-enum).
Supporting these roles enables models to be used with standard Qt views. However, for
some models that handle highly-specialized data, it may be appropriate to provide data
only for user-defined roles.

Models that provide interfaces to resizable data structures can provide implementations
of
[insertRows](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#insertRows)(),
[removeRows](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#removeRows)(),
[insertColumns](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#insertColumns)(),and
[removeColumns](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#removeColumns)().
When implementing these functions, it is important to notify any connected views about
changes to the model's dimensions both *before* and *after* they occur:

- An [insertRows](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#insertRows)() implementation must call [beginInsertRows](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#beginInsertRows)() *before* inserting new rows into the data structure, and [endInsertRows](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#endInsertRows)() *immediately afterwards*.
- An [insertColumns](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#insertColumns)() implementation must call [beginInsertColumns](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#beginInsertColumns)() *before* inserting new columns into the data structure, and [endInsertColumns](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#endInsertColumns)() *immediately afterwards*.
- A [removeRows](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#removeRows)() implementation must call [beginRemoveRows](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#beginRemoveRows)() *before* the rows are removed from the data structure, and [endRemoveRows](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#endRemoveRows)() *immediately afterwards*.
- A [removeColumns](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#removeColumns)() implementation must call [beginRemoveColumns](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#beginRemoveColumns)() *before* the columns are removed from the data structure, and [endRemoveColumns](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#endRemoveColumns)() *immediately afterwards*.

The *private* signals that these functions emit give attached components the chance to
take action before any data becomes unavailable. The encapsulation of the insert and
remove operations with these begin and end functions also enables the model to manage
[persistent model
indexes](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpersistentmodelindex.html) correctly. **If
you want selections to be handled properly, you must ensure that you call these
functions.** If you insert or remove an item with children, you do not need to call
these functions for the child items. In other words, the parent item will take care of
its child items.

To create models that populate incrementally, you can reimplement
[fetchMore](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#fetchMore)() and
[canFetchMore](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#canFetchMore)().
If the reimplementation of
[fetchMore](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#fetchMore)() adds
rows to the model,
[beginInsertRows()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#beginInsertRows)
and
[endInsertRows()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#endInsertRows)
must be called.

PythonQt.Qt.QAbstractItemModel.beginInse.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

### `[protected]` void QAbstractItemModel::beginInsertColumns(const [QModelIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmodelindex.html) \&*parent*, int *first*, int *last*)

Begins a column insertion operation.

When reimplementing
[insertColumns](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#insertColumns)()
in a subclass, you must call this function *before* inserting data into the model's
underlying data store.

The *parent* index corresponds to the parent into which the new columns are inserted;
*first* and *last* are the column numbers of the new columns will have after they have
been inserted.

| Inserting columns | Specify the first and last column numbers for the span of columns you want to insert into an item in a model. For example, as shown in the diagram, we insert three columns before column 4, so *first* is 4 and *last* is 6:  ``` beginInsertColumns(parent, 4, 6); ```  This inserts the three new columns as columns 4, 5, and 6\. |

### `[protected]` bool QAbstractItemModel::beginMoveColumns(const [QModelIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmodelindex.html) \&*sourceParent*, int *sourceFirst*, int *sourceLast*, const [QModelIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmodelindex.html) \&*destinationParent*, int *destinationChild*)

Begins a column move operation.

When reimplementing a subclass, this method simplifies moving entities in your model.
This method is responsible for moving persistent indexes in the model, which you would
otherwise be required to do yourself. Using beginMoveColumns and
[endMoveColumns](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#endMoveColumns)
is an alternative to emitting
[layoutAboutToBeChanged](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#layoutAboutToBeChanged)
and
[layoutChanged](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#layoutChanged)
directly along with
[changePersistentIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#changePersistentIndex).

The *sourceParent* index corresponds to the parent from which the columns are moved;
*sourceFirst* and *sourceLast* are the first and last column numbers of the columns to
be moved. The *destinationParent* index corresponds to the parent into which those
columns are moved. The *destinationChild* is the column to which the columns will be
moved. That is, the index at column *sourceFirst* in *sourceParent* will become column
*destinationChild* in *destinationParent*, followed by all other columns up to
*sourceLast*.

However, when moving columns down in the same parent (*sourceParent* and
*destinationParent* are equal), the columns will be placed before the *destinationChild*
index. That is, if you wish to move columns 0 and 1 so they will become columns 1 and 2,
*destinationChild* should be 3\. In this case, the new index for the source column `i`
(which is between *sourceFirst* and *sourceLast*) is equal to
`(destinationChild-sourceLast-1+i)`.

Note that if *sourceParent* and *destinationParent* are the same, you must ensure that
the *destinationChild* is not within the range of *sourceFirst* and *sourceLast* \+ 1\.
You must also ensure that you do not attempt to move a column to one of its own children
or ancestors. This method returns `false` if either condition is true, in which case you
should abort your move operation.

This function was introduced in Qt 4.6.

**See also**
[endMoveColumns](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#endMoveColumns)().

ancestors. This method returns `false` if either condition is true, in which case you
should abort your move operation.

Also specify the row in the destination parent to move the span to. For example, as shown in the diagram, we move three rows from row 2 to 4 in the source, so *sourceFirst* is 2 and *sourceLast* is 4\. ### `[protected]` void QAbstractItemModel::beginResetModel()

Begins a model reset operation.

A reset operation resets the model to its current state in any attached views.

**Note:** Any views attached to this model will be reset as well.

When a model is reset it means that any previous data reported from the model is now
invalid and has to be queried for again. This also means that the current item and any
selected items will become invalid.

When a model radically changes its data it can sometimes be easier to just call this
function rather than emit
[dataChanged](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#dataChanged)()
to inform other components when the underlying data source, or its structure, has
changed.

You must call this function before resetting any internal data structures in your model
or proxy model.

This function emits the signal
[modelAboutToBeReset](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#modelAboutToBeReset)().

This function was introduced in Qt 4.6.

**See also**
[modelAboutToBeReset](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#modelAboutToBeReset)(),
[modelReset](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#modelReset)(),
and
[endResetModel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#endResetModel)().

### `[protected]` [QModelIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmodelindex.html) QAbstractItemModel::createIndex(int *row*, int *column*, void \**ptr* \= nullptr) const

Creates a model index for the given *row* and *column* with the internal pointer *ptr*.

When using a
[QSortFilterProxyModel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsortfilterproxymodel.html),
its indexes have their own internal pointer. It is not advisable to access this internal
pointer outside of the model. Use the
[data](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#data)() function
instead.

This function provides a consistent interface that model subclasses must use to create
model indexes.

*id*.

This function provides a consistent interface that model subclasses must use to create

### `[signal]` void QAbstractItemModel::dataChanged(const [QModelIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmodelindex.html) \&*topLeft*, const [QModelIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmodelindex.html) \&*bottomRight*, const [QVector](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qvector.html)\<int\> \&*roles* \= QVector\<int\>())

This signal is emitted whenever the data in an existing item changes.

If the items are of the same parent, the affected ones are those between *topLeft* and
*bottomRight* inclusive. If the items do not have the same parent, the behavior is
undefined.

When reimplementing the
[setData](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#setData)()
function, this signal must be emitted explicitly.

The optional *roles* argument can be used to specify which data roles have actually been
modified. An empty vector in the roles argument means that all roles should be
considered modified. The order of elements in the roles argument does not have any
relevance.

**See also**
[headerDataChanged](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#headerDataChanged)(),
[setData](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#setData)(), and
[layoutChanged](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#layoutChanged)().

PythonQt.Qt.QAbstractItemModel.dropMimeD.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

### `[virtual]` bool QAbstractItemModel::dropMimeData(const [QMimeData](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmimedata.html) \**data*, [Qt::DropAction](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#DropAction-enum) *action*, int *row*, int *column*, const [QModelIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmodelindex.html) \&*parent*)

Handles the *data* supplied by a drag and drop operation that ended with the given
*action*.

Returns `true` if the data and action were handled by the model; otherwise returns
`false`.

The specified *row*, *column* and *parent* indicate the location of an item in the model
where the operation ended. It is the responsibility of the model to complete the action
at the correct location.

For instance, a drop action on an item in a
[QTreeView](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtreeview.html) can result in new items
either being inserted as children of the item specified by *row*, *column*, and
*parent*, or as siblings of the item.

When *row* and *column* are -1 it means that the dropped data should be considered as
dropped directly on *parent*. Usually this will mean appending the data as child items
of *parent*. If *row* and *column* are greater than or equal zero, it means that the
drop occurred just before the specified *row* and *column* in the specified *parent*.

The [mimeTypes](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#mimeTypes)()
member is called to get the list of acceptable MIME types. This default implementation
assumes the default implementation of
[mimeTypes](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#mimeTypes)(),
which returns a single default MIME type. If you reimplement
[mimeTypes](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#mimeTypes)() in
your custom model to return multiple MIME types, you must reimplement this function to
make use of them.

**See also**
[supportedDropActions](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#supportedDropActions)(),
[canDropMimeData](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#canDropMimeData)(),
and [Using drag and drop with item
views](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/model-view-programming.html#using-drag-and-drop-with-item-views).
signatures: dropMimeData(self, data: PySide2.QtCore.QMimeData, action: PySide2.QtCore.Qt.DropAction, row: int, column: int, parent: PySide2.QtCore.QModelIndex) -> bool

### `[signal]` void QAbstractItemModel::headerDataChanged([Qt::Orientation](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#Orientation-enum) *orientation*, int *first*, int *last*)

This signal is emitted whenever a header is changed. The *orientation* indicates whether
the horizontal or vertical header has changed. The sections in the header from the

### `[virtual]` bool QAbstractItemModel::insertColumns(int *column*, int *count*, const [QModelIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmodelindex.html) \&*parent* \= QModelIndex())

On models that support this, inserts *count* new columns into the model before the given
*column*. The items in each new column will be children of the item represented by the
*parent* model index.

If *column* is 0, the columns are prepended to any existing columns.

If *column* is
[columnCount](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#columnCount)(),
the columns are appended to any existing columns.

If *parent* has no children, a single row with *count* columns is inserted.

Returns `true` if the columns were successfully inserted; otherwise returns `false`.

The base class implementation does nothing and returns `false`.

If you implement your own model, you can reimplement this function if you want to
support insertions. Alternatively, you can provide your own API for altering the data.

**See also**
[insertRows](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#insertRows)(),
[removeColumns](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#removeColumns)(),
[beginInsertColumns](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#beginInsertColumns)(),
and
[endInsertColumns](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#endInsertColumns)().
signatures: insertColumns(self, column: int, count: int, parent: PySide2.QtCore.QModelIndex=...) -> bool

### `[virtual]` bool QAbstractItemModel::insertRows(int *row*, int *count*, const [QModelIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmodelindex.html) \&*parent* \= QModelIndex())

**Note:** The base class implementation of this function does nothing and returns
`false`.

On models that support this, inserts *count* rows into the model before the given *row*.
Items in the new row will be children of the item represented by the *parent* model
index.

If *row* is 0, the rows are prepended to any existing rows in the parent.

If *row* is
[rowCount](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#rowCount)(), the
rows are appended to any existing rows in the parent.

If *parent* has no children, a single column with *count* rows is inserted.

Returns `true` if the rows were successfully inserted; otherwise returns `false`.

If you implement your own model, you can reimplement this function if you want to
support insertions. Alternatively, you can provide your own API for altering the data.
In either case, you will need to call
[beginInsertRows](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#beginInsertRows)()
and
[endInsertRows](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#endInsertRows)()
to notify other components that the model has changed.

**See also**
[insertColumns](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#insertColumns)(),
[removeRows](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#removeRows)(),
[beginInsertRows](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#beginInsertRows)(),
and
[endInsertRows](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#endInsertRows)().
signatures: insertRows(self, row: int, count: int, parent: PySide2.QtCore.QModelIndex=...) -> bool

### `[signal]` void QAbstractItemModel::layoutAboutToBeChanged(const [QList](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qlist.html)\<[QPersistentModelIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpersistentmodelindex.html)\> \&*parents* \= QList\<QPersistentModelIndex\>(), [QAbstractItemModel::LayoutChangeHint](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#LayoutChangeHint-enum) *hint* \= QAbstractItemModel::NoLayoutChangeHint)

This signal is emitted just before the layout of a model is changed. Components
connected to this signal use it to adapt to changes in the model's layout.

Subclasses should update any persistent model indexes after emitting
layoutAboutToBeChanged().

The optional *parents* parameter is used to give a more specific notification about what
parts of the layout of the model are changing. An empty list indicates a change to the
layout of the entire model. The order of elements in the *parents* list is not
significant. The optional *hint* parameter is used to give a hint about what is
happening while the model is relayouting.

This function was introduced in Qt 5.0.

**See also**
[layoutChanged](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#layoutChanged)()
and
[changePersistentIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#changePersistentIndex)().

### `[signal]` void QAbstractItemModel::layoutChanged(const [QList](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qlist.html)\<[QPersistentModelIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpersistentmodelindex.html)\> \&*parents* \= QList\<QPersistentModelIndex\>(), [QAbstractItemModel::LayoutChangeHint](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#LayoutChangeHint-enum) *hint* \= QAbstractItemModel::NoLayoutChangeHint)

This signal is emitted whenever the layout of items exposed by the model has changed;
for example, when the model has been sorted. When this signal is received by a view, it
should update the layout of items to reflect this change.

When subclassing
[QAbstractItemModel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html) or
[QAbstractProxyModel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractproxymodel.html),
ensure that you emit
[layoutAboutToBeChanged](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#layoutAboutToBeChanged)()
before changing the order of items or altering the structure of the data you expose to
views, and emit layoutChanged() after changing the layout.

The optional *parents* parameter is used to give a more specific notification about what
parts of the layout of the model are changing. An empty list indicates a change to the
layout of the entire model. The order of elements in the *parents* list is not
significant. The optional *hint* parameter is used to give a hint about what is
happening while the model is relayouting.

Subclasses should update any persistent model indexes before emitting layoutChanged().
In other words, when the structure changes:

- emit [layoutAboutToBeChanged](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#layoutAboutToBeChanged)
- Remember the [QModelIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmodelindex.html) that will change
- Update your internal data
- Call [changePersistentIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#changePersistentIndex)()
- emit layoutChanged

This function was introduced in Qt 5.0.

**See also**
[layoutAboutToBeChanged](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#layoutAboutToBeChanged)(),
[dataChanged](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#dataChanged)(),
[headerDataChanged](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#headerDataChanged)(),
[modelReset](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#modelReset)(),
and

### `[virtual]` [QModelIndexList](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmodelindex.html#QModelIndexList-typedef) QAbstractItemModel::match(const [QModelIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmodelindex.html) \&*start*, int *role*, const [QVariant](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qvariant.html) \&*value*, int *hits* \= 1, [Qt::MatchFlags](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#MatchFlag-enum) *flags* \= Qt::MatchFlags(Qt::MatchStartsWith\|Qt::MatchWrap)) const

Returns a list of indexes for the items in the column of the *start* index where data
stored under the given *role* matches the specified *value*. The way the search is
performed is defined by the *flags* given. The list that is returned may be empty. Note
also that the order of results in the list may not correspond to the order in the model,
if for example a proxy model is used. The order of the results cannot be relied upon.

The search begins from the *start* index, and continues until the number of matching
data items equals *hits*, the search reaches the last row, or the search reaches *start*
again \- depending on whether `MatchWrap` is specified in *flags*. If you want to search
for all matching items, use *hits* \= -1.

By default, this function will perform a wrapping, string-based comparison on all items,
searching for items that begin with the search term specified by *value*.

**Note:** The default implementation of this function only searches columns. Reimplement
this function to include a different search behavior.

**Note:** This function can be invoked via the meta-object system and from QML. See
[Q\_INVOKABLE](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qobject.html#Q_INVOKABLE).

### `[pure virtual]` [QModelIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmodelindex.html) QAbstractItemModel::parent(const [QModelIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmodelindex.html) \&*index*) const

Returns the parent of the model item with the given *index*. If the item has no parent,
an invalid [QModelIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmodelindex.html) is
returned.

A common convention used in models that expose tree data structures is that only items
in the first column have children. For that case, when reimplementing this function in a
subclass the column of the returned
[QModelIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmodelindex.html) would be 0\.

When reimplementing this function in a subclass, be careful to avoid calling
[QModelIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmodelindex.html) member functions,
such as
[QModelIndex::parent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmodelindex.html#parent)(),
since indexes belonging to your model will simply call your implementation, leading to
infinite recursion.

**Note:** This function can be invoked via the meta-object system and from QML. See
[Q\_INVOKABLE](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qobject.html#Q_INVOKABLE).

**See also**
[createIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#createIndex)().

### `[signal]` void QAbstractItemModel::rowsRemoved(const [QModelIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmodelindex.html) \&*parent*, int *first*, int *last*)

This signal is emitted after rows have been removed from the model. The removed items
are those between *first* and *last* inclusive, under the given *parent* item.

**Note:** Components connected to this signal use it to adapt to changes in the model's
dimensions. It can only be emitted by the
[QAbstractItemModel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html)
implementation, and cannot be explicitly emitted in subclass code.

**Note:** This is a private signal. It can be used in signal connections but cannot be
emitted by the user.

**See also**
[removeRows](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#removeRows)()
and
[beginRemoveRows](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#beginRemoveRows)().

PythonQt.Qt.QAbstractItemView.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

QAbstractItemView class is the base class for every standard view that uses a
[QAbstractItemModel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html).
QAbstractItemView is an abstract class and cannot itself be instantiated. It provides a
standard interface for interoperating with models through the signals and slots
mechanism, enabling subclasses to be kept up-to-date with changes to their models. This
class provides standard support for keyboard and mouse navigation, viewport scrolling,
item editing, and selections. The keyboard navigation implements this functionality:

| Keys | Functionality |
| --- | --- |
| Arrow keys | Changes the current item and selects it. |
| Ctrl\+Arrow keys | Changes the current item but does not select it. |
| Shift\+Arrow keys | Changes the current item and selects it. The previously selected item(s) is not deselected. |
| Ctr\+Space | Toggles selection of the current item. |
| Tab/Backtab | Changes the current item to the next/previous item. |
| Home/End | Selects the first/last item in the model. |
| Page up/Page down | Scrolls the rows shown up/down by the number of visible rows in the view. |
| Ctrl\+A | Selects all items in the model. |

Note that the above table assumes that the [selection
mode](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemview.html#selectionMode-prop)
allows the operations. For instance, you cannot select items if the selection mode is
[QAbstractItemView::NoSelection](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemview.html#SelectionMode-enum).

The QAbstractItemView class is one of the [Model/View
Classes](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/model-view-programming.html#model-view-classes)
and is part of Qt's [model/view
framework](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/model-view-programming.html).

The view classes that inherit QAbstractItemView only need to implement their own
view-specific functionality, such as drawing items, returning the geometry of items,
finding items, etc.

QAbstractItemView provides common slots such as
[edit](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemview.html#edit)() and
[setCurrentIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemview.html#setCurrentIndex)().
Many protected slots are also provided, including
[dataChanged](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemview.html#dataChanged)(),
[rowsInserted](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemview.html#rowsInserted)(),
[rowsAboutToBeRemoved](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemview.html#rowsAboutToBeRemoved)(),
[selectionChanged](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemview.html#selectionChanged)(),
and
[currentChanged](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemview.html#currentChanged)().

The root item is returned by
[rootIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemview.html#rootIndex)(), and
the current item by
[currentIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemview.html#currentIndex)().
To make sure that an item is visible use
[scrollTo](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemview.html#scrollTo)().

Some of QAbstractItemView's functions are concerned with scrolling, for example
[setHorizontalScrollMode](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemview.html#horizontalScrollMode-prop)()
and
[setVerticalScrollMode](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemview.html#verticalScrollMode-prop)().
To set the range of the scroll bars, you can, for example, reimplement the view's
[resizeEvent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemview.html#resizeEvent)()
function:

```
void MyView::resizeEvent(QResizeEvent *event) {
    horizontalScrollBar()->setRange(0, realWidth - width());
    ...
}
```

Note that the range is not updated until the widget is shown.

Several other functions are concerned with selection control; for example
[setSelectionMode](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemview.html#selectionMode-prop)(),
and
[setSelectionBehavior](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemview.html#selectionBehavior-prop)().
This class provides a default selection model to work with
([selectionModel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemview.html#selectionModel)()),
but this can be replaced by using
[setSelectionModel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemview.html#setSelectionModel)()
with an instance of
[QItemSelectionModel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qitemselectionmodel.html).

For complete control over the display and editing of items you can specify a delegate
with
[setItemDelegate](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemview.html#setItemDelegate)().

QAbstractItemView provides a lot of protected functions. Some are concerned with
editing, for example,
[edit](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemview.html#edit)(), and
[commitData](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemview.html#commitData)(),
whilst others are keyboard and mouse event handlers.

**Note:** If you inherit QAbstractItemView and intend to update the contents of the
viewport, you should use
viewport-\>[update](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemview.html#update)()
instead of [update()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#update) as all
painting operations take place on the viewport.

### `[signal]` void QAbstractItemView::activated(const [QModelIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmodelindex.html) \&*index*)

This signal is emitted when the item specified by *index* is activated by the user. How
to activate items depends on the platform; e.g., by single- or double-clicking the item,
or by pressing the Return or Enter key when the item is current.

**See also**
[clicked](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemview.html#clicked)(),
[doubleClicked](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemview.html#doubleClicked)(),
[entered](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemview.html#entered)(), and
[pressed](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemview.html#pressed)().

### autoScroll : bool

This property holds whether autoscrolling in drag move events is enabled

If this property is set to true (the default), the
[QAbstractItemView](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemview.html)
automatically scrolls the contents of the view if the user drags within 16 pixels of the
viewport edge. If the current item changes, then the view will scroll automatically to
ensure that the current item is fully visible.

This property only works if the viewport accepts drops. Autoscroll is switched off by
setting this property to false.

**Access functions:**

| bool | **hasAutoScroll**() const |
| --- | --- |
| void | **setAutoScroll**(bool *enable*) |

This property holds the size of the area when auto scrolling is triggered

This property controls the size of the area at the edge of the viewport that triggers
autoscrolling. The default value is 16 pixels.

This property was introduced in Qt 4.4.

**Access functions:**

### dragDropOverwriteMode : bool

This property holds the view's drag and drop behavior

If its value is `true`, the selected data will overwrite the existing item data when
dropped, while moving the data will clear the item. If its value is `false`, the
selected data will be inserted as a new item when the data is dropped. When the data is
moved, the item is removed as well.

The default value is `false`, as in the
[QListView](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qlistview.html) and
[QTreeView](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtreeview.html) subclasses. In the
[QTableView](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtableview.html) subclass, on the other
hand, the property has been set to `true`.

Note: This is not intended to prevent overwriting of items. The model's implementation
of flags() should do that by not returning
[Qt::ItemIsDropEnabled](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#ItemFlag-enum).

This property was introduced in Qt 4.2.

**Access functions:**

| bool | **dragDropOverwriteMode**() const |
| --- | --- |
| void | **setDragDropOverwriteMode**(bool *overwrite*) |

**See also**
[dragDropMode](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemview.html#dragDropMode-prop).

PythonQt.Qt.QAbstractItemView.edit.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

### `[slot]` void QAbstractItemView::edit(const [QModelIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmodelindex.html) \&*index*)

Starts editing the item corresponding to the given *index* if it is editable.

Note that this function does not change the current index. Since the current index
defines the next and previous items to edit, users may find that keyboard navigation
does not work as expected. To provide consistent navigation behavior, call
[setCurrentIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemview.html#setCurrentIndex)()
before this function with the same model index.

**See also**
[QModelIndex::flags](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmodelindex.html#flags)().

### `[virtual protected]` bool QAbstractItemView::edit(const [QModelIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmodelindex.html) \&*index*, [QAbstractItemView::EditTrigger](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemview.html#EditTrigger-enum) *trigger*, [QEvent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qevent.html) \**event*)

Starts editing the item at *index*, creating an editor if necessary, and returns `true`
if the view's
[State](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemview.html#State-enum) is now
[EditingState](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemview.html#State-enum);
otherwise returns `false`.

The action that caused the editing process is described by *trigger*, and the associated
event is specified by *event*.

Editing can be forced by specifying the *trigger* to be
[QAbstractItemView::AllEditTriggers](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemview.html#EditTrigger-enum).

**See also**
[closeEditor](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemview.html#closeEditor)().
signatures: edit(self, index: PySide2.QtCore.QModelIndex, trigger: PySide2.QtWidgets.QAbstractItemView.EditTrigger, event: PySide2.QtCore.QEvent) -> bool

### `[protected]` void QAbstractItemView::scrollDirtyRegion(int *dx*, int *dy*)

Prepares the view for scrolling by (*dx*,*dy*) pixels by moving the dirty regions in the
opposite direction. You only need to call this function if you are implementing a
scrolling viewport in your view subclass.

If you implement
[scrollContentsBy](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractscrollarea.html#scrollContentsBy)()
in a subclass of
[QAbstractItemView](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemview.html), call
this function before you call
[QWidget::scroll](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#scroll)() on the
viewport. Alternatively, just call
[update](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemview.html#update)().

example, in the code snippet below, the

```

...
setIndexWidget(index, new QTextEdit);
```

This function should only be used to display static content within the visible area
corresponding to an item of data. If you want to display custom dynamic content or
implement a custom editor widget, subclass
[QStyledItemDelegate](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstyleditemdelegate.html)

### void QAbstractItemView::setItemDelegate([QAbstractItemDelegate](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemdelegate.html) \**delegate*)

Sets the item delegate for this view and its model to *delegate*. This is useful if you
want complete control over the editing and display of items.

Any existing delegate will be removed, but not deleted.
[QAbstractItemView](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemview.html) does not
take ownership of *delegate*.

**Warning:** You should not share the same instance of a delegate between views. Doing
so can cause incorrect or unintuitive editing behavior since each view connected to a
given delegate may receive the
[closeEditor()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemdelegate.html#closeEditor)
signal, and attempt to access, modify or close an editor that has already been closed.

**See also**
[itemDelegate](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemview.html#itemDelegate)().

Qt 5 reference:

### void QAbstractItemView::setItemDelegateForColumn(int *column*, [QAbstractItemDelegate](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemdelegate.html) \**delegate*)

Sets the given item *delegate* used by this view and model for the given *column*. All
items on *column* will be drawn and managed by *delegate* instead of using the default
delegate (i.e.,
[itemDelegate](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemview.html#itemDelegate)()).

Any existing column delegate for *column* will be removed, but not deleted.
[QAbstractItemView](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemview.html) does not
take ownership of *delegate*.

**Note:** If a delegate has been assigned to both a row and a column, the row delegate
will take precedence and manage the intersecting cell index.

**Warning:** You should not share the same instance of a delegate between views. Doing
so can cause incorrect or unintuitive editing behavior since each view connected to a
given delegate may receive the
[closeEditor()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemdelegate.html#closeEditor)
signal, and attempt to access, modify or close an editor that has already been closed.

This function was introduced in Qt 4.2.

**See also**
[itemDelegateForColumn](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemview.html#itemDelegateForColumn)(),
[setItemDelegateForRow](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemview.html#setItemDelegateForRow)(),

Qt 5 reference:

### `[virtual]` void QAbstractItemView::setModel([QAbstractItemModel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html) \**model*)

Sets the *model* for the view to present.

This function will create and set a new selection model, replacing any model that was
previously set with
[setSelectionModel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemview.html#setSelectionModel)().
However, the old selection model will not be deleted as it may be shared between several
views. We recommend that you delete the old selection model if it is no longer required.
This is done with the following code:

```
QItemSelectionModel *m = view->selectionModel();
view->setModel(new model);
delete m;
```

If both the old model and the old selection model do not have parents, or if their
parents are long-lived objects, it may be preferable to call their
[deleteLater](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qobject.html#deleteLater)() functions
to explicitly delete them.

The view *does not* take ownership of the model unless it is the model's parent object
because the model may be shared between many different views.

**See also** [model](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemview.html#model)(),
[selectionModel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemview.html#selectionModel)(),
and
[setSelectionModel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemview.html#setSelectionModel)().

PythonQt.Qt.QAbstractListModel.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

QAbstractListModel provides a standard interface for models that represent their data as
a simple non-hierarchical sequence of items. It is not used directly, but must be
subclassed.

Since the model provides a more specialized interface than
[QAbstractItemModel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html), it is
not suitable for use with tree views; you will need to subclass
[QAbstractItemModel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html) if you
want to provide a model for that purpose. If you need to use a number of list models to
manage data, it may be more appropriate to subclass
[QAbstractTableModel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstracttablemodel.html)
instead.

Simple models can be created by subclassing this class and implementing the minimum
number of required functions. For example, we could implement a simple read-only
[QStringList](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstringlist.html)-based model that
provides a list of strings to a
[QListView](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qlistview.html) widget. In such a case,
we only need to implement the
[rowCount](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#rowCount)()
function to return the number of items in the list, and the
[data](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#data)() function to
retrieve items from the list.

Since the model represents a one-dimensional structure, the
[rowCount](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#rowCount)()
function returns the total number of items in the model. The
[columnCount](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#columnCount)()
function is implemented for interoperability with all kinds of views, but by default
informs views that the model contains only one column.

### Subclassing

When subclassing QAbstractListModel, you must provide implementations of the
[rowCount](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#rowCount)() and
[data](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#data)() functions.
Well behaved models also provide a
[headerData](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#headerData)()
implementation.

If your model is used within QML and requires roles other than the default ones provided
by the
[roleNames](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#roleNames)()
function, you must override it.

For editable list models, you must also provide an implementation of
[setData](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#setData)(), and
implement the
[flags](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractlistmodel.html#flags)() function so
that it returns a value containing
[Qt::ItemIsEditable](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#ItemFlag-enum).

Note that QAbstractListModel provides a default implementation of
[columnCount](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#columnCount)()
that informs views that there is only a single column of items in this model.

Models that provide interfaces to resizable list-like data structures can provide
implementations of
[insertRows](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#insertRows)()
and
[removeRows](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#removeRows)().
When implementing these functions, it is important to call the appropriate functions so
that all connected views are aware of any changes:

- An [insertRows](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#insertRows)() implementation must call [beginInsertRows](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#beginInsertRows)() *before* inserting new rows into the data structure, and it must call [endInsertRows](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#endInsertRows)() *immediately afterwards*.
- A [removeRows](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#removeRows)() implementation must call [beginRemoveRows](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#beginRemoveRows)() *before* the rows are removed from the data structure, and it must call [endRemoveRows](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#endRemoveRows)() *immediately afterwards*.

**Note:** Some general guidelines for subclassing models are available in the [Model
Subclassing
Reference](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/model-view-programming.html#model-subclassing-reference).

PythonQt.Qt.QAbstractMessageHandler.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

QAbstractMessageHandler is an abstract base class that provides a callback interface for
handling messages. For example, class
[QXmlQuery](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qxmlquery.html) parses and runs an
[XQuery](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/xmlprocessing.html). When it detects a
compile or runtime error, it generates an appropriate error message, but rather than
output the message itself, it passes the message to the
[message](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractmessagehandler.html#message)()
function of its QAbstractMessageHandler. See
[QXmlQuery::setMessageHandler](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qxmlquery.html#setMessageHandler)().

You create a message handler by subclassing QAbstractMessageHandler and implementing
[handleMessage](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractmessagehandler.html#handleMessage)().
You then pass a pointer to an instance of your subclass to any classes that must
generate messages. The messages are sent to the message handler via the
[message](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractmessagehandler.html#message)()
function, which forwards them to your handleMessge().

A single instance of QAbstractMessageHandler can be called on to handle messages from
multiple sources. Hence, the content of a message, which is the *description* parameter
passed to
[message](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractmessagehandler.html#message)() and
[handleMessage](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractmessagehandler.html#handleMessage)(),
must be interpreted in light of the context that required the message to be sent. That
context is specified by the *identifier* and *sourceLocation* parameters to
[message](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractmessagehandler.html#message)()
[handleMessage](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractmessagehandler.html#handleMessage)().

Qt 5 reference:

### `[pure virtual protected]` void QAbstractMessageHandler::handleMessage([QtMsgType](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtglobal.html#QtMsgType-enum) *type*, const [QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html) \&*description*, const [QUrl](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qurl.html) \&*identifier* \= QUrl(), const [QSourceLocation](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsourcelocation.html) \&*sourceLocation* \= QSourceLocation())

This function must be implemented by the sub-class.
[message](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractmessagehandler.html#message)()
will call this function, passing in its parameters, *type*, *description*, *identifier*
and *sourceLocation* unmodified.

This function can potentially be called from multiple threads. It's the
reimplementation's responsibility to ensure thread safety.
signatures: handleMessage(self, type: PySide2.QtCore.QtMsgType, description: str, identifier: PySide2.QtCore.QUrl, sourceLocation: PySide2.QtXmlPatterns.QSourceLocation) -> None

PythonQt.Qt.QAbstractMessageHandler.mess.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

### void QAbstractMessageHandler::message([QtMsgType](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtglobal.html#QtMsgType-enum) *type*, const [QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html) \&*description*, const [QUrl](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qurl.html) \&*identifier* \= QUrl(), const [QSourceLocation](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsourcelocation.html) \&*sourceLocation* \= QSourceLocation())

Sends a message to this message handler. *type* is the kind of message being sent.
*description* is the message content. The *identifier* is a URI that identifies the
message and is the key to interpreting the other arguments.

Typically, this class is used for reporting errors, as is the case for
[QXmlQuery](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qxmlquery.html), which uses a
[QAbstractMessageHandler](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractmessagehandler.html)
to report compile and runtime
[XQuery](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/xmlprocessing.html) errors. Hence, using a
[QUrl](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qurl.html) as the message *identifier* is was
inspired by the explanation of [error handling in the XQuery
language](http://www.w3.org/TR/xquery/#errors). Because the *identifier* is composed of
a namespace URI and a local part, identifiers with the same local part are unique. The
caller is responsible for ensuring that *identifier* is either a valid
[QUrl](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qurl.html) or a default constructed
[QUrl](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qurl.html).

*sourceLocation* identifies a location in a resource (i.e., file or document) where the
need for reporting a message was detected.

This function unconditionally calls
[handleMessage](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractmessagehandler.html#handleMessage)(),
passing all its parameters unmodified.

**See also** <http://www.w3.org/TR/xquery/#errors>.
signatures: message(self, type: PySide2.QtCore.QtMsgType, description: str, identifier: PySide2.QtCore.QUrl=..., sourceLocation: PySide2.QtXmlPatterns.QSourceLocation=...) -> None
