## Detailed Description

This class defines the standard interface that proxy models must use to be able to
interoperate correctly with other model/view components. It is not supposed to be
instantiated directly.

All standard proxy models are derived from the QAbstractProxyModel class. If you need to
create a new proxy model class, it is usually better to subclass an existing class that
provides the closest behavior to the one you want to provide.

Proxy models that filter or sort items of data from a source model should be created by
using or subclassing
[QSortFilterProxyModel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsortfilterproxymodel.html).

To subclass QAbstractProxyModel, you need to implement
[mapFromSource](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractproxymodel.html#mapFromSource)()
and
[mapToSource](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractproxymodel.html#mapToSource)().
The
[mapSelectionFromSource](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractproxymodel.html#mapSelectionFromSource)()
and
[mapSelectionToSource](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractproxymodel.html#mapSelectionToSource)()
functions only need to be reimplemented if you need a behavior different from the
default behavior.

**Note:** If the source model is deleted or no source model is specified, the proxy
model operates on a empty placeholder model.

PythonQt.Qt.QAbstractScrollArea.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

QAbstractScrollArea is a low-level abstraction of a scrolling area. The area provides a
central widget called the viewport, in which the contents of the area is to be scrolled
(i.e, the visible parts of the contents are rendered in the viewport).

Next to the viewport is a vertical scroll bar, and below is a horizontal scroll bar.
When all of the area contents fits in the viewport, each scroll bar can be either
visible or hidden depending on the scroll bar's
[Qt::ScrollBarPolicy](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#ScrollBarPolicy-enum).
When a scroll bar is hidden, the viewport expands in order to cover all available space.
When a scroll bar becomes visible again, the viewport shrinks in order to make room for
the scroll bar.

It is possible to reserve a margin area around the viewport, see
[setViewportMargins](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractscrollarea.html#setViewportMargins)().
The feature is mostly used to place a
[QHeaderView](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qheaderview.html) widget above or
beside the scrolling area. Subclasses of QAbstractScrollArea should implement margins.

When inheriting QAbstractScrollArea, you need to do the following:

- Control the scroll bars by setting their range, value, page step, and tracking their movements.
- Draw the contents of the area in the viewport according to the values of the scroll bars.
- Handle events received by the viewport in [viewportEvent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractscrollarea.html#viewportEvent)() \- notably resize events.
- Use `viewport->update()` to update the contents of the viewport instead of [update()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#update) as all painting operations take place on the viewport.

With a scroll bar policy of
[Qt::ScrollBarAsNeeded](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#ScrollBarPolicy-enum)
(the default), QAbstractScrollArea shows scroll bars when they provide a non-zero
scrolling range, and hides them otherwise.

The scroll bars and viewport should be updated whenever the viewport receives a resize
event or the size of the contents changes. The viewport also needs to be updated when
the scroll bars values change. The initial values of the scroll bars are often set when
the area receives new contents.

We give a simple example, in which we have implemented a scroll area that can scroll any
[QWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html). We make the widget a child
of the viewport; this way, we do not have to calculate which part of the widget to draw
but can simply move the widget with
[QWidget::move](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#pos-prop)(). When the
area contents or the viewport size changes, we do the following:

```
    QSize areaSize = viewport()->size();
    QSize  widgetSize = widget->size();

    verticalScrollBar()->setPageStep(areaSize.height());
    horizontalScrollBar()->setPageStep(areaSize.width());
    verticalScrollBar()->setRange(0, widgetSize.height() - areaSize.height());
    horizontalScrollBar()->setRange(0, widgetSize.width() - areaSize.width());
    updateWidgetPosition();
```

When the scroll bars change value, we need to update the widget position, i.e., find the
part of the widget that is to be drawn in the viewport:

```
    int hvalue = horizontalScrollBar()->value();
    int vvalue = verticalScrollBar()->value();
    QPoint topLeft = viewport()->rect().topLeft();

    widget->move(topLeft.x() - hvalue, topLeft.y() - vvalue);
```

In order to track scroll bar movements, reimplement the virtual function
[scrollContentsBy](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractscrollarea.html#scrollContentsBy)().
In order to fine-tune scrolling behavior, connect to a scroll bar's
[QAbstractSlider::actionTriggered](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html#actionTriggered)()
signal and adjust the
[QAbstractSlider::sliderPosition](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html#sliderPosition-prop)
as you wish.

For convenience, QAbstractScrollArea makes all viewport events available in the virtual
[viewportEvent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractscrollarea.html#viewportEvent)()
handler. [QWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html)'s specialized
handlers are remapped to viewport events in the cases where this makes sense. The
remapped specialized handlers are:
[paintEvent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractscrollarea.html#paintEvent)(),
[mousePressEvent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractscrollarea.html#mousePressEvent)(),
[mouseReleaseEvent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractscrollarea.html#mouseReleaseEvent)(),
[mouseDoubleClickEvent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractscrollarea.html#mouseDoubleClickEvent)(),
[mouseMoveEvent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractscrollarea.html#mouseMoveEvent)(),
[wheelEvent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractscrollarea.html#wheelEvent)(),
[dragEnterEvent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractscrollarea.html#dragEnterEvent)(),
[dragMoveEvent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractscrollarea.html#dragMoveEvent)(),
[dragLeaveEvent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractscrollarea.html#dragLeaveEvent)(),
[dropEvent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractscrollarea.html#dropEvent)(),
[contextMenuEvent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractscrollarea.html#contextMenuEvent)(),
and
[resizeEvent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractscrollarea.html#resizeEvent)().

[QScrollArea](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qscrollarea.html), which inherits
QAbstractScrollArea, provides smooth scrolling for any
[QWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html) (i.e., the widget is scrolled
pixel by pixel). You only need to subclass QAbstractScrollArea if you need more
specialized behavior. This is, for instance, true if the entire contents of the area is
not suitable for being drawn on a
[QWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html) or if you do not want smooth
scrolling.

### void QAbstractScrollArea::addScrollBarWidget([QWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#QWidget) \**widget*, [Qt::Alignment](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#AlignmentFlag-enum) *alignment*)

Adds *widget* as a scroll bar widget in the location specified by *alignment*.

Scroll bar widgets are shown next to the horizontal or vertical scroll bar, and can be
placed on either side of it. If you want the scroll bar widgets to be always visible,
set the scrollBarPolicy for the corresponding scroll bar to `AlwaysOn`.

*alignment* must be one of Qt::Alignleft and
[Qt::AlignRight](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#AlignmentFlag-enum), which
maps to the horizontal scroll bar, or
[Qt::AlignTop](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#AlignmentFlag-enum) and
[Qt::AlignBottom](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#AlignmentFlag-enum), which
maps to the vertical scroll bar.

A scroll bar widget can be removed by either re-parenting the widget or deleting it.
It's also possible to hide a widget with
[QWidget::hide](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#hide)()

The scroll bar widget will be resized to fit the scroll bar geometry for the current
style. The following describes the case for scroll bar widgets on the horizontal scroll
bar:

The height of the widget will be set to match the height of the scroll bar. To control
the width of the widget, use
[QWidget::setMinimumWidth](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#minimumWidth-prop)
and
[QWidget::setMaximumWidth](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#maximumWidth-prop),
or implement
[QWidget::sizeHint](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#sizeHint-prop)() and
set a horizontal size policy. If you want a square widget, call
[QStyle::pixelMetric](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstyle.html#pixelMetric)([QStyle::PM\_ScrollBarExtent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstyle.html#PixelMetric-enum))
and set the width to this value.

This function was introduced in Qt 4.2.

### `[virtual protected]` void QAbstractScrollArea::scrollContentsBy(int *dx*, int *dy*)

This virtual handler is called when the scroll bars are moved by *dx*, *dy*, and
consequently the viewport's contents should be scrolled accordingly.

The default implementation simply calls
[update](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#update)() on the entire
[viewport](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractscrollarea.html#viewport)(),
subclasses can reimplement this handler for optimization purposes, or \- like
[QScrollArea](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qscrollarea.html) \- to move a contents
widget. The parameters *dx* and *dy* are there for convenience, so that the class knows
how much should be scrolled (useful e.g. when doing pixel-shifts). You may just as well
ignore these values and scroll directly to the position the scroll bars indicate.

Calling this function in order to scroll programmatically is an error, use the scroll
bars instead (e.g. by calling
[QScrollBar::setValue](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html#value-prop)()
directly).
signatures: scrollContentsBy(self, dx: int, dy: int) -> None

### void QAbstractScrollArea::setCornerWidget([QWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#QWidget) \**widget*)

Sets the widget in the corner between the two scroll bars to be *widget*.

You will probably also want to set at least one of the scroll bar modes to `AlwaysOn`.

Passing `nullptr` shows no widget in the corner.

Any previous corner widget is hidden.

You may call setCornerWidget() with the same widget at different times.

All widgets set here will be deleted by the scroll area when it is destroyed unless you
separately reparent the widget after setting some other corner widget (or `nullptr`).

Any *newly* set widget should have no current parent.

By default, no corner widget is present.

This function was introduced in Qt 4.2.

**See also**
[cornerWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractscrollarea.html#cornerWidget)(),
[horizontalScrollBarPolicy](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractscrollarea.html#horizontalScrollBarPolicy-prop),

### `[protected]` void QAbstractScrollArea::setViewportMargins(int *left*, int *top*, int *right*, int *bottom*)

is useful for applications such as spreadsheets with "locked" rows and columns. The

[viewport](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractscrollarea.html#viewport)()

reasonable default behavior.

needs no further processing; otherwise returns `false` to indicate that the event should
be propagated further.

specialized event handlers instead.

[paintEvent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractscrollarea.html#paintEvent)(),

PythonQt.Qt.QAbstractSlider.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

The class is designed as a common super class for widgets like
[QScrollBar](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qscrollbar.html),
[QSlider](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qslider.html) and
[QDial](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdial.html).

Here are the main properties of the class:

1. [value](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html#value-prop): The bounded integer that QAbstractSlider maintains.
2. [minimum](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html#minimum-prop): The lowest possible value.
3. [maximum](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html#maximum-prop): The highest possible value.
4. [singleStep](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html#singleStep-prop): The smaller of two natural steps that an abstract sliders provides and typically corresponds to the user pressing an arrow key.
5. [pageStep](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html#pageStep-prop): The larger of two natural steps that an abstract slider provides and typically corresponds to the user pressing PageUp or PageDown.
6. [tracking](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html#tracking-prop): Whether slider tracking is enabled.
7. [sliderPosition](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html#sliderPosition-prop): The current position of the slider. If [tracking](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html#tracking-prop) is enabled (the default), this is identical to [value](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html#value-prop).

Unity (1) may be viewed as a third step size.
[setValue](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html#value-prop)() lets
you set the current value to any integer in the allowed range, not just
[minimum](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html#minimum-prop)() \+ *n*
\*
[singleStep](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html#singleStep-prop)()
for integer values of *n*. Some widgets may allow the user to set any value at all;
others may just provide multiples of
[singleStep](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html#singleStep-prop)()
or [pageStep](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html#pageStep-prop)().

QAbstractSlider emits a comprehensive set of signals:

| Signal | Emitted when |
| --- | --- |
| [valueChanged](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html#valueChanged)() | the value has changed. The [tracking](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html#tracking-prop) determines whether this signal is emitted during user interaction. |
| [sliderPressed](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html#sliderPressed)() | the user starts to drag the slider. |
| [sliderMoved](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html#sliderMoved)() | the user drags the slider. |
| [sliderReleased](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html#sliderReleased)() | the user releases the slider. |
| [actionTriggered](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html#actionTriggered)() | a slider action was triggered. |
| [rangeChanged](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html#rangeChanged)() | a the range has changed. |

QAbstractSlider provides a virtual
[sliderChange](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html#sliderChange)()
function that is well suited for updating the on-screen representation of sliders. By
calling
[triggerAction](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html#triggerAction)(),
subclasses trigger slider actions. Two helper functions
[QStyle::sliderPositionFromValue](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstyle.html#sliderPositionFromValue)()
and
[QStyle::sliderValueFromPosition](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstyle.html#sliderValueFromPosition)()
help subclasses and styles to map screen coordinates to logical range values.

PythonQt.Qt.QAbstractSlider.actionTrigge.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

### `[signal]` void QAbstractSlider::actionTriggered(int *action*)

This signal is emitted when the slider action *action* is triggered. Actions are
[SliderSingleStepAdd](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html#SliderAction-enum),
[SliderSingleStepSub](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html#SliderAction-enum),
[SliderPageStepAdd](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html#SliderAction-enum),
[SliderPageStepSub](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html#SliderAction-enum),
[SliderToMinimum](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html#SliderAction-enum),
[SliderToMaximum](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html#SliderAction-enum),
and
[SliderMove](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html#SliderAction-enum).

When the signal is emitted, the
[sliderPosition](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html#sliderPosition-prop)
has been adjusted according to the action, but the
[value](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html#value-prop) has not yet
been propagated (meaning the
[valueChanged](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html#valueChanged)()
signal was not yet emitted), and the visual display has not been updated. In slots
connected to this signal you can thus safely adjust any action by calling
[setSliderPosition](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html#sliderPosition-prop)()
yourself, based on both the action and the slider's value.

**See also**
[triggerAction](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html#triggerAction)().

### invertedAppearance : bool

This property holds whether or not a slider shows its values inverted.

If this property is `false` (the default), the minimum and maximum will be shown in its
classic position for the inherited widget. If the value is true, the minimum and maximum
appear at their opposite location.

Note: This property makes most sense for sliders and dials. For scroll bars, the visual
effect of the scroll bar subcontrols depends on whether or not the styles understand
inverted appearance; most styles ignore this property for scroll bars.

PythonQt.Qt.QAbstractSocket.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

QAbstractSocket is the base class for
[QTcpSocket](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtcpsocket.html) and
[QUdpSocket](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qudpsocket.html) and contains all common
functionality of these two classes. If you need a socket, you have two options:

- Instantiate [QTcpSocket](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtcpsocket.html) or [QUdpSocket](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qudpsocket.html).
- Create a native socket descriptor, instantiate QAbstractSocket, and call [setSocketDescriptor](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#setSocketDescriptor)() to wrap the native socket.

TCP (Transmission Control Protocol) is a reliable, stream-oriented, connection-oriented
transport protocol. UDP (User Datagram Protocol) is an unreliable, datagram-oriented,
connectionless protocol. In practice, this means that TCP is better suited for
continuous transmission of data, whereas the more lightweight UDP can be used when
reliability isn't important.

QAbstractSocket's API unifies most of the differences between the two protocols. For
example, although UDP is connectionless,
[connectToHost](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#connectToHost)()
establishes a virtual connection for UDP sockets, enabling you to use QAbstractSocket in
more or less the same way regardless of the underlying protocol. Internally,
QAbstractSocket remembers the address and port passed to
[connectToHost](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#connectToHost)(),
and functions like [read](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qiodevice.html#read)() and
[write](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qiodevice.html#write)() use these values.

At any time, QAbstractSocket has a state (returned by
[state](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#state)()). The initial
state is
[UnconnectedState](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#SocketState-enum).
After calling
[connectToHost](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#connectToHost)(),
the socket first enters
[HostLookupState](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#SocketState-enum).
If the host is found, QAbstractSocket enters
[ConnectingState](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#SocketState-enum)
and emits the
[hostFound](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#hostFound)() signal.
When the connection has been established, it enters
[ConnectedState](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#SocketState-enum)
and emits
[connected](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#connected)(). If an
error occurs at any stage,
[errorOccurred](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#errorOccurred)()
is emitted. Whenever the state changes,
[stateChanged](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#stateChanged)()
is emitted. For convenience,
[isValid](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#isValid)() returns
`true` if the socket is ready for reading and writing, but note that the socket's state
must be
[ConnectedState](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#SocketState-enum)
before reading and writing can occur.

Read or write data by calling
[read](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qiodevice.html#read)() or
[write](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qiodevice.html#write)(), or use the
convenience functions
[readLine](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qiodevice.html#readLine)() and
[readAll](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qiodevice.html#readAll)(). QAbstractSocket
also inherits [getChar](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qiodevice.html#getChar)(),
[putChar](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qiodevice.html#putChar)(), and
[ungetChar](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qiodevice.html#ungetChar)() from
[QIODevice](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qiodevice.html), which work on single
bytes. The
[bytesWritten](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qiodevice.html#bytesWritten)() signal
is emitted when data has been written to the socket. Note that Qt does not limit the
write buffer size. You can monitor its size by listening to this signal.

The [readyRead](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qiodevice.html#readyRead)() signal is
emitted every time a new chunk of data has arrived.
[bytesAvailable](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#bytesAvailable)()
then returns the number of bytes that are available for reading. Typically, you would
connect the [readyRead](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qiodevice.html#readyRead)()
signal to a slot and read all available data there. If you don't read all the data at
once, the remaining data will still be available later, and any new incoming data will
be appended to QAbstractSocket's internal read buffer. To limit the size of the read
buffer, call
[setReadBufferSize](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#setReadBufferSize)().

To close the socket, call
[disconnectFromHost](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#disconnectFromHost)().
QAbstractSocket enters
[QAbstractSocket::ClosingState](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#SocketState-enum).
After all pending data has been written to the socket, QAbstractSocket actually closes
the socket, enters
[QAbstractSocket::UnconnectedState](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#SocketState-enum),
and emits
[disconnected](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#disconnected)().
If you want to abort a connection immediately, discarding all pending data, call
[abort](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#abort)() instead. If the
remote host closes the connection, QAbstractSocket will emit
[errorOccurred](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#errorOccurred)([QAbstractSocket::RemoteHostClosedError](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#SocketError-enum)),
during which the socket state will still be
[ConnectedState](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#SocketState-enum),
and then the
[disconnected](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#disconnected)()
signal will be emitted.

The port and address of the connected peer is fetched by calling
[peerPort](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#peerPort)() and
[peerAddress](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#peerAddress)().
[peerName](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#peerName)() returns
the host name of the peer, as passed to
[connectToHost](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#connectToHost)().
[localPort](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#localPort)() and
[localAddress](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#localAddress)()
return the port and address of the local socket.

QAbstractSocket provides a set of functions that suspend the calling thread until
certain signals are emitted. These functions can be used to implement blocking sockets:

- [waitForConnected](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#waitForConnected)() blocks until a connection has been established.
- [waitForReadyRead](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#waitForReadyRead)() blocks until new data is available for reading.
- [waitForBytesWritten](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#waitForBytesWritten)() blocks until one payload of data has been written to the socket.
- [waitForDisconnected](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#waitForDisconnected)() blocks until the connection has closed.

We show an example:

```
    int numRead = 0, numReadTotal = 0;
    char buffer[50];

    forever {
        numRead  = socket.read(buffer, 50);

        // do whatever with array

        numReadTotal += numRead;
        if (numRead == 0 && !socket.waitForReadyRead())
            break;
    }
```

If
[waitForReadyRead()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qiodevice.html#waitForReadyRead)
returns `false`, the connection has been closed or an error has occurred.

Programming with a blocking socket is radically different from programming with a
non-blocking socket. A blocking socket doesn't require an event loop and typically leads
to simpler code. However, in a GUI application, blocking sockets should only be used in
non-GUI threads, to avoid freezing the user interface. See the
[fortuneclient](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtnetwork-fortuneclient-example.html)
and
[blockingfortuneclient](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtnetwork-blockingfortuneclient-example.html)
examples for an overview of both approaches.

**Note:** We discourage the use of the blocking functions together with signals. One of
the two possibilities should be used.

QAbstractSocket can be used with
[QTextStream](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextstream.html) and
[QDataStream](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdatastream.html)'s stream operators
(operator\<\<() and operator\>\>()). There is one issue to be aware of, though: You must
make sure that enough data is available before attempting to read it using
operator\>\>().

Aborts the current connection and resets the socket. Unlike
[disconnectFromHost](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#disconnectFromHost)(),

buffer.

### bool QAbstractSocket::bind(const [QHostAddress](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qhostaddress.html) \&*address*, [quint16](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtglobal.html#quint16-typedef) *port* \= 0, [QAbstractSocket::BindMode](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#BindFlag-enum) *mode* \= ...)

Binds to *address* on port *port*, using the
[BindMode](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#BindFlag-enum)
*mode*.

For UDP sockets, after binding, the signal
[QUdpSocket::readyRead](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qiodevice.html#readyRead)()
is emitted whenever a UDP datagram arrives on the specified address and port. Thus, this
function is useful to write UDP servers.

For TCP sockets, this function may be used to specify which interface to use for an
outgoing connection, which is useful in case of multiple network interfaces.

By default, the socket is bound using the
[DefaultForPlatform](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#BindFlag-enum)
[BindMode](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#BindFlag-enum). If a
port is not specified, a random port is chosen.

On success, the function returns `true` and the socket enters
[BoundState](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#SocketState-enum);
otherwise it returns `false`.

This function was introduced in Qt 5.0.

Qt 5 reference:

### `[virtual]` void QAbstractSocket::connectToHost(const [QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html) \&*hostName*, [quint16](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtglobal.html#quint16-typedef) *port*, [QIODevice::OpenMode](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qiodevice.html#OpenModeFlag-enum) *openMode* \= ReadWrite, [QAbstractSocket::NetworkLayerProtocol](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#NetworkLayerProtocol-enum) *protocol* \= AnyIPProtocol)

Attempts to make a connection to *hostName* on the given *port*. The *protocol*
parameter can be used to specify which network protocol to use (eg. IPv4 or IPv6).

The socket is opened in the given *openMode* and first enters
[HostLookupState](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#SocketState-enum),
then performs a host name lookup of *hostName*. If the lookup succeeds,
[hostFound](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#hostFound)() is
emitted and [QAbstractSocket](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html)
enters
[ConnectingState](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#SocketState-enum).
It then attempts to connect to the address or addresses returned by the lookup. Finally,
if a connection is established,
[QAbstractSocket](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html) enters
[ConnectedState](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#SocketState-enum)
and emits
[connected](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#connected)().

At any point, the socket can emit
[errorOccurred](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#errorOccurred)()
to signal that an error occurred.

*hostName* may be an IP address in string form (e.g., "43.195.83.32"), or it may be a
host name (e.g., "example.com").
[QAbstractSocket](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html) will do a
lookup only if required. *port* is in native byte order.

**See also** [state](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#state)(),
[peerName](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#peerName)(),
[peerAddress](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#peerAddress)(),
[peerPort](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#peerPort)(), and
[waitForConnected](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#waitForConnected)().

### `[virtual]` void QAbstractSocket::connectToHost(const [QHostAddress](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qhostaddress.html) \&*address*, [quint16](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtglobal.html#quint16-typedef) *port*, [QIODevice::OpenMode](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qiodevice.html#OpenModeFlag-enum) *openMode* \= ReadWrite)

### `[virtual]` void QAbstractSocket::disconnectFromHost()

Attempts to close the socket. If there is pending data waiting to be written,
[QAbstractSocket](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html) will enter
[ClosingState](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#SocketState-enum)
and wait until all data has been written. Eventually, it will enter
[UnconnectedState](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#SocketState-enum)
and emit the
[disconnected](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#disconnected)()
signal.

[connectToHost](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#connectToHost)().

Qt 5 reference:

### `[signal]` void QAbstractSocket::errorOccurred([QAbstractSocket::SocketError](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#SocketError-enum) *socketError*)

This signal is emitted after an error occurred. The *socketError* parameter describes
the type of error that occurred.

When this signal is emitted, the socket may not be ready for a reconnect attempt. In
that case, attempts to reconnect should be done from the event loop. For example, use a
[QTimer::singleShot](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtimer.html#singleShot)() with 0
as the timeout.

[QAbstractSocket::SocketError](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#SocketError-enum)
is not a registered metatype, so for queued connections, you will have to register it
with
[Q\_DECLARE\_METATYPE](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmetatype.html#Q_DECLARE_METATYPE)()
and
[qRegisterMetaType](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmetatype.html#qRegisterMetaType-1)().

This function was introduced in Qt 5.15.

**See also** [error](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#error)(),
[errorString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qiodevice.html#errorString)(), and
[Creating Custom Qt Types](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/custom-types.html).

### bool QAbstractSocket::flush()

This function writes as much as possible from the internal write buffer to the
underlying network socket, without blocking. If any data was written, this function
returns `true`; otherwise false is returned.

Call this function if you need
[QAbstractSocket](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html) to start
sending buffered data immediately. The number of bytes successfully written depends on
the operating system. In most cases, you do not need to call this function, because
[QAbstractSocket](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html) will start
sending data automatically once control goes back to the event loop. In the absence of
an event loop, call
[waitForBytesWritten](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#waitForBytesWritten)()
instead.

**See also** [write](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qiodevice.html#write)() and
[waitForBytesWritten](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#waitForBytesWritten)().

PythonQt.Qt.QAbstractSocket.setReadBuffe.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

### `[virtual]` void QAbstractSocket::setReadBufferSize([qint64](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtglobal.html#qint64-typedef) *size*)

Sets the size of
[QAbstractSocket](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html)'s internal
read buffer to be *size* bytes.

If the buffer size is limited to a certain size,
[QAbstractSocket](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html) won't buffer
more than this size of data. Exceptionally, a buffer size of 0 means that the read
buffer is unlimited and all incoming data is buffered. This is the default.

This option is useful if you only read the data at certain points in time (e.g., in a
real-time streaming application) or if you want to protect your socket against receiving
too much data, which may eventually cause your application to run out of memory.

Only [QTcpSocket](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtcpsocket.html) uses
[QAbstractSocket](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html)'s internal
buffer; [QUdpSocket](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qudpsocket.html) does not use
any buffering at all, but rather relies on the implicit buffering provided by the
operating system. Because of this, calling this function on
[QUdpSocket](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qudpsocket.html) has no effect.

**See also**
[readBufferSize](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#readBufferSize)()
and [read](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qiodevice.html#read)().

### `[override virtual]` bool QAbstractSocket::waitForBytesWritten(int *msecs* \= 30000\)

Reimplements:
[QIODevice::waitForBytesWritten](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qiodevice.html#waitForBytesWritten)(int

This function blocks until at least one byte has been written on the socket and the
[bytesWritten()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qiodevice.html#bytesWritten) signal
has been emitted. The function will timeout after *msecs* milliseconds; the default

The function returns `true` if the

is emitted; otherwise it returns `false` (if an error occurred or the operation timed
out).

**Note:** This function may fail randomly on Windows. Consider using the event loop and
the [bytesWritten](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qiodevice.html#bytesWritten)()
signal if your software will run on Windows.

[waitForReadyRead](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#waitForReadyRead)().

PythonQt.Qt.QAbstractSocket.waitForConne.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

### `[virtual]` bool QAbstractSocket::waitForConnected(int *msecs* \= 30000\)

Waits until the socket is connected, up to *msecs* milliseconds. If the connection has
been established, this function returns `true`; otherwise it returns `false`. In the
case where it returns `false`, you can call
[error](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#error)() to determine
the cause of the error.

The following example waits up to one second for a connection to be established:

```
socket->connectToHost("imap", 143);
if (socket->waitForConnected(1000))
    qDebug("Connected!");
```

If msecs is -1, this function will not time out.

**Note:** This function may wait slightly longer than *msecs*, depending on the time it
takes to complete the host lookup.

**Note:** Multiple calls to this functions do not accumulate the time. If the function
times out, the connecting process will be aborted.

the [connected](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#connected)()

PythonQt.Qt.QAbstractSocket.waitForDisco.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

### `[virtual]` bool QAbstractSocket::waitForDisconnected(int *msecs* \= 30000\)

Waits until the socket has disconnected, up to *msecs* milliseconds. If the connection
was successfully disconnected, this function returns `true`; otherwise it returns
`false` (if the operation timed out, if an error occurred, or if this
[QAbstractSocket](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html) is already
disconnected). In the case where it returns `false`, you can call
[error](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#error)() to determine
the cause of the error.

The following example waits up to one second for a connection to be closed:

```
socket->disconnectFromHost();
if (socket->state() == QAbstractSocket::UnconnectedState
    || socket->waitForDisconnected(1000)) {
        qDebug("Disconnected!");
}
```

If msecs is -1, this function will not time out.

**Note:** This function may fail randomly on Windows. Consider using the event loop and
the
[disconnected](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#disconnected)()
signal if your software will run on Windows.

**See also**
[disconnectFromHost](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#disconnectFromHost)()
and [close](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#close)().

PythonQt.Qt.QAbstractSpinBox.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

The class is designed as a common super class for widgets like
[QSpinBox](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qspinbox.html),
[QDoubleSpinBox](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdoublespinbox.html) and
[QDateTimeEdit](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdatetimeedit.html)

Here are the main properties of the class:

1. [text](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractspinbox.html#text-prop): The text that is displayed in the QAbstractSpinBox.
2. [alignment](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/stylesheet-reference.html#alignment): The alignment of the text in the QAbstractSpinBox.
3. [wrapping](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractspinbox.html#wrapping-prop): Whether the QAbstractSpinBox wraps from the minimum value to the maximum value and vice versa.

QAbstractSpinBox provides a virtual
[stepBy](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractspinbox.html#stepBy)() function
that is called whenever the user triggers a step. This function takes an integer value
to signify how many steps were taken. E.g. Pressing
[Qt::Key\_Down](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#Key-enum) will trigger a call
to [stepBy](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractspinbox.html#stepBy)(-1).

When the user triggers a step whilst holding the
[Qt::ControlModifier](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#KeyboardModifier-enum),
QAbstractSpinBox steps by 10 instead of making a single step. This step modifier affects
wheel events, key events and interaction with the spinbox buttons. Note that on macOS,
Control corresponds to the Command key.

Since Qt 5.12,
[QStyle::SH\_SpinBox\_StepModifier](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstyle.html#StyleHint-enum)
can be used to select which
[Qt::KeyboardModifier](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#KeyboardModifier-enum)
increases the step rate.
[Qt::NoModifier](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#KeyboardModifier-enum)
disables this feature.

QAbstractSpinBox also provide a virtual function
[stepEnabled](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractspinbox.html#stepEnabled)() to
determine whether stepping up/down is allowed at any point. This function returns a
bitset of
[StepEnabled](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractspinbox.html#StepEnabledFlag-enum).

### keyboardTracking : bool

This property holds whether keyboard tracking is enabled for the spinbox.

If keyboard tracking is enabled (the default), the spinbox emits the valueChanged() and
textChanged() signals while the new value is being entered from the keyboard.

signals with the values 6, 60, and 600 respectively.

textChanged() signals while typing. It emits the signals later, when the return key is
pressed, when keyboard focus is lost, or when other spinbox functionality is used, e.g.

### specialValueText : [QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html)

This property holds the special-value text

If set, the spin box will display this text instead of a numeric value whenever the
current value is equal to minimum(). Typical use is to indicate that this choice has a
special (default) meaning.

For example, if your spin box allows the user to choose a scale factor (or zoom level)
for displaying an image, and your application is able to automatically choose one that
will enable the image to fit completely within the display window, you can set up the
spin box like this:

```
    QSpinBox *zoomSpinBox = new QSpinBox;
    zoomSpinBox->setRange(0, 1000);
    zoomSpinBox->setSingleStep(10);
    zoomSpinBox->setSuffix("%");
    zoomSpinBox->setSpecialValueText(tr("Automatic"));
    zoomSpinBox->setValue(100);
```

The user will then be able to choose a scale from 1% to 1000% or select "Auto" to leave
it up to the application to choose. Your code must then interpret the spin box value of
0 as a request from the user to scale the image to fit inside the window.

All values are displayed with the prefix and suffix (if set), *except* for the special
value, which only shows the special value text. This special text is passed in the
[QSpinBox::textChanged](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qspinbox.html#textChanged)()
signal that passes a [QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html).

To turn off the special-value text display, call this function with an empty string. The
default is no special-value text, i.e. the numeric value is shown as usual.

If no special-value text is set, specialValueText() returns an empty string.

**Access functions:**

| QString | **specialValueText**() const |
| --- | --- |
| void | **setSpecialValueText**(const QString \&*txt*) |

PythonQt.Qt.QAbstractSpinBox.stepBy.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

### `[virtual]` void QAbstractSpinBox::stepBy(int *steps*)

Virtual function that is called whenever the user triggers a step. The *steps* parameter
indicates how many steps were taken. For example, pressing `Qt::Key_Down` will trigger a
call to `stepBy(-1)`, whereas pressing `Qt::Key_PageUp` will trigger a call to
`stepBy(10)`.

If you subclass `QAbstractSpinBox` you must reimplement this function. Note that this
function is called even if the resulting value will be outside the bounds of minimum and

### wrapping : bool

This property holds whether the spin box is circular.

If wrapping is true stepping up from maximum() value will take you to the minimum()
value and vice versa. Wrapping only make sense if you have minimum() and maximum()
values set.

```
QSpinBox *spinBox = new QSpinBox(this);
spinBox->setRange(0, 100);
spinBox->setWrapping(true);
spinBox->setValue(100);
spinBox->stepBy(1);

## Detailed Description

The QAbstractState class is the abstract base class of states that are part of a
[QStateMachine](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstatemachine.html). It defines the
interface that all state objects have in common. QAbstractState is part of [The State
Machine Framework](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/statemachine-api.html).

The [entered](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractstate.html#entered)() signal
is emitted when the state has been entered. The
[exited](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractstate.html#exited)() signal is
emitted when the state has been exited.

The [parentState](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractstate.html#parentState)()
function returns the state's parent state. The
[machine](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractstate.html#machine)() function
returns the state machine that the state is part of.

### Subclassing

The [onEntry](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractstate.html#onEntry)() function
is called when the state is entered; reimplement this function to perform custom
processing when the state is entered.

The [onExit](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractstate.html#onExit)() function
is called when the state is exited; reimplement this function to perform custom
processing when the state is exited.

Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

QAbstractTableModel provides a standard interface for models that represent their data
as a two-dimensional array of items. It is not used directly, but must be subclassed.

Since the model provides a more specialized interface than
[QAbstractItemModel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html), it is
not suitable for use with tree views, although it can be used to provide data to a
[QListView](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qlistview.html). If you need to represent
a simple list of items, and only need a model to contain a single column of data,
subclassing the
[QAbstractListModel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractlistmodel.html) may be
more appropriate.

The [rowCount](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#rowCount)()
and
[columnCount](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#columnCount)()
functions return the dimensions of the table. To retrieve a model index corresponding to
an item in the model, use
[index](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstracttablemodel.html#index)() and provide
only the row and column numbers.

### Subclassing

When subclassing QAbstractTableModel, you must implement
[rowCount](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#rowCount)(),
[columnCount](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#columnCount)(),
and [data](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#data)(). Default
implementations of the
[index](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstracttablemodel.html#index)() and
[parent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#parent)() functions
are provided by QAbstractTableModel. Well behaved models will also implement
[headerData](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#headerData)().

Editable models need to implement
[setData](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#setData)(), and
implement [flags](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstracttablemodel.html#flags)()
to return a value containing
[Qt::ItemIsEditable](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#ItemFlag-enum).

Models that provide interfaces to resizable data structures can provide implementations
of
[insertRows](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#insertRows)(),
[removeRows](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#removeRows)(),
[insertColumns](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#insertColumns)(),
and
[removeColumns](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#removeColumns)().
When implementing these functions, it is important to call the appropriate functions so
that all connected views are aware of any changes:

- An [insertRows](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#insertRows)() implementation must call [beginInsertRows](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#beginInsertRows)() *before* inserting new rows into the data structure, and it must call [endInsertRows](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#endInsertRows)() *immediately afterwards*.
- An [insertColumns](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#insertColumns)() implementation must call [beginInsertColumns](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#beginInsertColumns)() *before* inserting new columns into the data structure, and it must call [endInsertColumns](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#endInsertColumns)() *immediately afterwards*.
- A [removeRows](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#removeRows)() implementation must call [beginRemoveRows](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#beginRemoveRows)() *before* the rows are removed from the data structure, and it must call [endRemoveRows](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#endRemoveRows)() *immediately afterwards*.
- A [removeColumns](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#removeColumns)() implementation must call [beginRemoveColumns](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#beginRemoveColumns)() *before* the columns are removed from the data structure, and it must call [endRemoveColumns](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#endRemoveColumns)() *immediately afterwards*.

**Note:** Some general guidelines for subclassing models are available in the [Model
Subclassing
Reference](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/model-view-programming.html#model-subclassing-reference).

Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

The standard layout provided by Qt can handle simple word processing including inline
images, lists and tables.

Some applications, e.g., a word processor or a DTP application might need more features
than the ones provided by Qt's layout engine, in which case you can subclass
QAbstractTextDocumentLayout to provide custom layout behavior for your text documents.

An instance of the QAbstractTextDocumentLayout subclass can be installed on a
[QTextDocument](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html) object with the
[setDocumentLayout()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html#setDocumentLayout)
function.

You can insert custom objects into a
[QTextDocument](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html); see the
[QTextObjectInterface](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextobjectinterface.html)
class description for details.

Qt 5 reference:

### `[pure virtual protected]` void QAbstractTextDocumentLayout::documentChanged(int *position*, int *charsRemoved*, int *charsAdded*)

This function is called whenever the contents of the document change. A change occurs
when text is inserted, removed, or a combination of these two. The change is specified
by *position*, *charsRemoved*, and *charsAdded* corresponding to the starting character
position of the change, the number of characters removed from the document, and the
number of characters added.

For example, when inserting the text "Hello" into an empty document, *charsRemoved*
would be 0 and *charsAdded* would be 5 (the length of the string).

Replacing text is a combination of removing and inserting. For example, if the text
"Hello" gets replaced by "Hi", *charsRemoved* would be 5 and *charsAdded* would be 2\.

For subclasses of
[QAbstractTextDocumentLayout](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstracttextdocumentlayout.html),
this is the central function where a large portion of the work to lay out and position
document contents is done.

For example, in a subclass that only arranges blocks of text, an implementation of this
function would have to do the following:

- Determine the list of changed [QTextBlock](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextblock.html)(s) using the parameters provided.
- Each [QTextBlock](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextblock.html) object's corresponding [QTextLayout](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextlayout.html) object needs to be processed. You can access the [QTextBlock](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextblock.html)'s layout using the [QTextBlock::layout](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextblock.html#layout)() function. This processing should take the document's page size into consideration.
- If the total number of pages changed, the [pageCountChanged](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstracttextdocumentlayout.html#pageCountChanged)() signal should be emitted.
- If the total size changed, the [documentSizeChanged](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstracttextdocumentlayout.html#documentSizeChanged)() signal should be emitted.
- The [update](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstracttextdocumentlayout.html#update)() signal should be emitted to schedule a repaint of areas in the layout that require repainting.

**See also** [QTextLayout](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextlayout.html).
signatures: documentChanged(self, from_: int, charsRemoved: int, charsAdded: int) -> None

Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

The QAbstractTransition class is the abstract base class of transitions between states
([QAbstractState](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractstate.html) objects) of a
[QStateMachine](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstatemachine.html).
QAbstractTransition is part of [The State Machine
Framework](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/statemachine-api.html).

The
[sourceState](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstracttransition.html#sourceState)()
function returns the source of the transition. The
[targetStates](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstracttransition.html#targetStates)()
function returns the targets of the transition. The
[machine](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstracttransition.html#machine)()
function returns the state machine that the transition is part of.

The [triggered](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstracttransition.html#triggered)()
signal is emitted when the transition has been triggered.

Transitions can cause animations to be played. Use the
[addAnimation](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstracttransition.html#addAnimation)()
function to add an animation to the transition.

### Subclassing

The [eventTest](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstracttransition.html#eventTest)()
function is called by the state machine to determine whether an event should trigger the
transition. In your reimplementation you typically check the event type and cast the
event object to the proper type, and check that one or more properties of the event meet
your criteria.

The
[onTransition](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstracttransition.html#onTransition)()
function is called when the transition is triggered; reimplement this function to
perform custom processing for the transition.

## Detailed Description

For example, one could write a QAbstractUriResolver subclass that rewrites library ISBN
number URIs as book title URLs, e.g., *urn:isbn:0-345-33973-8* would be rewritten as

### `[pure virtual]` [QUrl](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qurl.html) QAbstractUriResolver::resolve(const [QUrl](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qurl.html) \&*relative*, const [QUrl](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qurl.html) \&*baseURI*) const

Returns the *relative* URI resolved using the *baseURI*.

The caller guarantees that both *relative* and *baseURI* are valid, and that *baseURI*
is absolute. *relative* can be relative, absolute, or empty.

The returned [QUrl](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qurl.html) can be a default
constructed [QUrl](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qurl.html). If it is not a default
constructed [QUrl](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qurl.html), it will be absolute
and valid. If a default constructed [QUrl](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qurl.html)
is returned, it means the *relative* URI was not accepted to be resolved.

If the reimplemented resolve() function decides it has nothing to do about resolving the
*relative* URI, it should simply return the *relative* URI resolved against the
*baseURI*, i.e.:

```
return baseURI.resolved(relative);
```

Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

The QAbstractXmlNodeModel specifies the interface that a node model must implement for
that node model be accessible to the query engine for processing
[XQuery](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/xmlprocessing.html) queries. A node model
represents data as a structure that can be queried as if the data were XML.

The node model represented by a subclass of QAbstractXmlNodeModel is meant to be
accessed by the Qt XML Patterns query engine. If the API seems a little strange in a few
places, it is because the member functions are called by the query engine as it
evaluates an [XQuery](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/xmlprocessing.html). They
aren't meant to be used programatically.

### Usage

QAbstractXmlNodeModel bridges the gap between the arbitrary structure of the non-XML
data to be queried and the well-defined structure of XML data understood by
[QXmlQuery](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qxmlquery.html).

Consider a chemistry application that reads the file `chemistryData`, which contains
non-XML data that represents a chemical structure composed of molecules and atoms. The
application will query this chemistry data with an
[XQuery](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/xmlprocessing.html) it reads from file
`queryFile`. We write a custom subclass of QAbstractXmlNodeModel (`ChemistryNodeModel`)
that reads `chemistryData` and builds a data structure, perhaps composed of objects of
our own classes `molecule` and `atom`. Clearly, this data structure is not XML. Our
custom subclass will know how to traverse this non-XML structure and present it through
the [XPath Data Model interface](http://www.w3.org/TR/xpath-datamodel/).

```
QFile queryFile(argv[1]);
QFile chemistryData(argv[2]);
QString moleculeName = argv[3];

QXmlQuery query;
query.setQuery(&queryFile, QUrl::fromLocalFile(queryFile.fileName()));

ChemistryNodeModel myNodeModel(query.namePool(), chemistryData);
QXmlNodeModelIndex startNode = myNodeModel.nodeFor(moleculeName);
query.bindVariable("queryRoot", startNode);

QFile out;
out.open(stdout, QIODevice::WriteOnly);

QXmlSerializer serializer(query, &out);
query.evaluateTo(&serializer);
```

The application first creates an instance of
[QXmlQuery](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qxmlquery.html) and calls
[setQuery()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qxmlquery.html#setQuery) to read
`queryFile` containing the
[XQuery](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/xmlprocessing.html) we want to run. Then it
creates an instance of our custom node model class, `ChemistryNodeModel`, which is a
subclass of QAbstractXmlNodeModel. Its constructor is called with the [name
pool](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qxmlnamepool.html) obtained from our
[QXmlQuery](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qxmlquery.html), and with the
`chemistryFile` containing the structure of molecules and atoms to be queried. The [name
pool](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qxmlnamepool.html) is required because our
custom node model has the member function
[name()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractxmlnodemodel.html#name), which
returns the [name](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qxmlname.html) of any node in the
model. The [query](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qxmlquery.html) and the custom
node model must use the same name pool for constructing these
[names](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qxmlname.html). The constructor would then
read `chemistryFile` and build the custom node model structure.

To connect the `query` to the custom node model, we must bind a variable name used in
the query to a node in the model. The variable can then be used in the query as a
starting node. First, an
[index](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qxmlnodemodelindex.html) for the desired
starting node is retrieved by calling
[QAbstractXmlNodeModel::createIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractxmlnodemodel.html#createIndex)().
Then the index is bound to a variable name, in this case `queryRoot`, by passing the
name and the index to
[QXmlQuery::bindVariable](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qxmlquery.html#bindVariable)().
The query can then use a variable reference `$queryRoot` to refer to the starting node.
Note that if the [query](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qxmlquery.html) uses
multiple variable references, a call to
[QXmlQuery::bindVariable](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qxmlquery.html#bindVariable)()
is required to bind each different variable name to a node in the model.

The query is executed when the application calls one of the
[QXmlQuery](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qxmlquery.html) evaluation functions. The
application uses
[QXmlQuery::evaluateTo](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qxmlquery.html#evaluateTo)([QAbstractXmlReceiver](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractxmlreceiver.html)
\*), because it then uses a
[serializer](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qxmlserializer.html) to out the query
result as XML to `stdout`. We could have used
[QXmlQuery::evaluateTo](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qxmlquery.html#evaluateTo)([QXmlResultItems](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qxmlresultitems.html)
\*) to get a list of result items, or
[QXmlQuery::evaluateTo](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qxmlquery.html#evaluateTo)([QStringList](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstringlist.html)
\*) if the query evaluated to a sequence of `xs:string` values.

During query execution, the engine iterates over the node model using
[nextFromSimpleAxis](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractxmlnodemodel.html#nextFromSimpleAxis)()
to get the [index](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qxmlnodemodelindex.html) of the
next node to be visited. The engine can get the name of a node by calling
[name](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractxmlnodemodel.html#name)() with the
node's [index](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qxmlnodemodelindex.html).
[stringValue](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractxmlnodemodel.html#stringValue)(),
[baseUri](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractxmlnodemodel.html#baseUri)(),
[documentUri](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractxmlnodemodel.html#documentUri)()
and [kind](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractxmlnodemodel.html#kind)() are
also called as needed with a node
[index](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qxmlnodemodelindex.html).

The example demonstrates the standard pattern for using a subclass of
QAbstractXmlNodeModel in combination with
[QXmlQuery](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qxmlquery.html) to perform an
[XQuery](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/xmlprocessing.html).

1. Instantiate [QXmlQuery](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qxmlquery.html) and give it the [XQuery](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/xmlprocessing.html) to be run;
2. Instantiate a subclass of QAbstractXmlNodeModel or [QSimpleXmlNodeModel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsimplexmlnodemodel.html);
3. Retrieve a [QXmlNodeModelIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qxmlnodemodelindex.html) for the node in the model where the [QXmlQuery](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qxmlquery.html) should start the query;
4. Use [QXmlQuery::bindVariable](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qxmlquery.html#bindVariable)() to bind the [QXmlNodeModelIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qxmlnodemodelindex.html) to `$variable name`;
5. Call one of the [QXmlQuery](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qxmlquery.html) evaluation functions to run the query.

### Subclassing

Because the [XPath Data Model interface](http://www.w3.org/TR/xpath-datamodel/)
presented by QAbstractXmlNodeModel allows
[QXmlQuery](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qxmlquery.html) to operate on non-XML
data as if it were XML, implementing subclasses of QAbstractXmlNodeModel can involve a
significant amount of work. The
[QSimpleXmlNodeModel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsimplexmlnodemodel.html) class
is provided to simplify the implementation for many common use cases.

### Thread Safety

Because the node model can be accessed concurrently by threads in the Qt XML Patterns
module, subclasses of QAbstractXmlNodeModel must be written to be
[thread-safe](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qxmlquery.html#reentrancy-and-thread-safety).
Classes that simplify implementing thread-safety include
[QReadLocker](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qreadlocker.html) and
[QWriteLocker](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwritelocker.html).

See the example [File System
Example](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtxmlpatterns-filetree-example.html) for a
demonstration.

### `[pure virtual]` [QUrl](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qurl.html) QAbstractXmlNodeModel::baseUri(const [QXmlNodeModelIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qxmlnodemodelindex.html) \&*n*) const

Returns the base URI for the node whose index is *n*. The caller guarantees that *n* is
not `null` and that it belongs to a node in this node model.

The base URI of a node can be extracted using the `fn:base-uri()` function. The base URI
is typically used for resolving relative URIs that appear in the node or its children.
It is conformant to just return the document URI, although that might not properly
reflect the underlying data.

This function maps to the `dm:base-uri` accessor, which returns a base URI according to
the following:

- For document nodes, the base URI and the document URI are the same.
- For elements, the base URI is the URI appearing in the element's `xml:base` attribute, if present, or it is resolved to the parent element's base URI.
- Namespace nodes have no base URI.
- The base URI for a processing instruction, comment, attribute, or text node is the base URI of the node's parent element.

The implementation guarantees to return a valid
[QUrl](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qurl.html), or a default constructed
[QUrl](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qurl.html). If a node has no base URI, as in
the case where a comment has no parent, a default constructed
[QUrl](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qurl.html) is returned.

**See also** [XQuery 1.0 and XPath 2.0 Data Model (XDM), 5.2 base-uri
Accessor](http://www.w3.org/TR/xpath-datamodel/#dm-base-uri).

*ni2*. It is used for the `Is` operator and for sorting nodes in document order.

The caller guarantees that *ni1* and *ni2* are not `null` and that both identify nodes
in this node model.

If *ni1* is identical to *ni2*,
[QXmlNodeModelIndex::Is](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qxmlnodemodelindex.html#DocumentOrder-enum)

[QXmlNodeModelIndex::Follows](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qxmlnodemodelindex.html#DocumentOrder-enum)
is returned.

### `[pure virtual]` [QUrl](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qurl.html) QAbstractXmlNodeModel::documentUri(const [QXmlNodeModelIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qxmlnodemodelindex.html) \&*n*) const

Returns the document URI of *n*. The document URI identifies the resource which is the
document. For example, the document could be a regular file, e.g., `file:/`, or it could
be the `http://` URL of the location of a file. The document URI is used for resolving
URIs and to simply know where the document is.

If the node model maps to a URI in a natural way, return that URI. Otherwise, return the
company or product URI. The document URI can be any URI as long as its valid and
absolute.

The caller guarantees that *n* is not `null` and that it belongs to this
[QAbstractXmlNodeModel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractxmlnodemodel.html).

This function maps to the `dm:document-uri` accessor, which returns a document URI
according to the following:

- If *n* is a document node, return an absolute [QUrl](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qurl.html) containing the document URI, or a default constructed [QUrl](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qurl.html). The latter signals that no document URI is available for the document node.
- For all other nodes, return a default constructed [QUrl](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qurl.html).

**See also** [XQuery 1.0 and XPath 2.0 Data Model (XDM), 5.4 document-uri
Accessor](http://www.w3.org/TR/xpath-datamodel/#dm-document-uri),
[QUrl::isValid](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qurl.html#isValid)(), and
[QUrl::isRelative](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qurl.html#isRelative)().

### `[pure virtual]` [QXmlNodeModelIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qxmlnodemodelindex.html) QAbstractXmlNodeModel::elementById(const [QXmlName](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qxmlname.html) \&*id*) const

Returns the index of the element identified as *id*.
[XQuery](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/xmlprocessing.html)'s `id()` function calls
this function.

The node index returned will be the element node whose value is of type `ID` and equals
*id*, or it will be the element node that has an attribute whose typed value is of type
`ID` and equals *id*. If there is no such element, a default constructed
[QXmlNodeModelIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qxmlnodemodelindex.html)
instance is returned. The implementor guarantees that if the returned node index is not
null, it identifies an element.

It is not sufficient for an attribute or element to merely be called `id`. Its value
type must also be `ID`. However, the reserved name `xml:id` is sufficient.

In *id*, the `namespace URI` and the `prefix` are undefined, and the `local name` is the
ID that should be looked up.

**See also** [XQuery 1.0 and XPath 2.0 Functions and Operators, 15.5.2
fn:id](http://www.w3.org/TR/xpath-functions/#func-id).

### `[pure virtual protected]` [QXmlNodeModelIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qxmlnodemodelindex.html) QAbstractXmlNodeModel::nextFromSimpleAxis([QAbstractXmlNodeModel::SimpleAxis](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractxmlnodemodel.html#SimpleAxis-enum) *axis*, const [QXmlNodeModelIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qxmlnodemodelindex.html) \&*origin*) const

When Qt XML Patterns evaluate path expressions, it emulate them through a combination of
calls with
[QSimpleXmlNodeModel::SimpleAxis](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractxmlnodemodel.html#SimpleAxis-enum)
values. Therefore, the implementation of this function must return the node, if any,
that appears on the *axis* emanating from the *origin*.

If no such node is available, a default constructed
[QXmlNodeModelIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qxmlnodemodelindex.html) is
returned.

[QSimpleXmlNodeModel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsimplexmlnodemodel.html)
eliminates the need to handle redundant corner cases by guaranteeing that it will never
ask for:

- Children or siblings for attributes.
- Children for comments, processing instructions, and text nodes.
- Siblings or parents for document nodes.

A typical implementation performs a `switch` on the value of *axis*:

```
QXmlNodeModelIndex MyTreeModel::nextFromSimpleAxis(SimpleAxis axis, const QXmlNodeModelIndex &origin) const
{
  // Convert the QXmlNodeModelIndex to a value that is specific to what we represent.
  const MyValue value = toMyValue(ni);

  switch(axis)
  {
      case Parent:
          return toNodeIndex(value.parent());
      case FirstChild:
      case PreviousSibling:
      case NextSibling:
          // and so on
  }
}
```

### `[pure virtual]` [QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html) QAbstractXmlNodeModel::stringValue(const [QXmlNodeModelIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qxmlnodemodelindex.html) \&*n*) const

Returns the string value for node *n*.

The caller guarantees that *n* is not `null` and that it belong to this
[QAbstractXmlNodeModel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractxmlnodemodel.html)
instance.

This function maps to the `dm:string-value()` accessor, which the specification
completely specifies. Here's a summary:

- For processing instructions, the string value is the data section(excluding any whitespace appearing between the name and the data).
- For text nodes, the string value equals the text node.
- For comments, the content of the comment
- For elements, the concatenation of all text nodes that are descendants. Note, this is not only the children, but the childrens' childrens' text nodes, and so forth.
- For document nodes, the concatenation of all text nodes in the document.
