PythonQt.Qt.QSharedMemory.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

QSharedMemory provides access to a shared memory segment by multiple threads and
processes. It also provides a way for a single thread or process to lock the memory for
exclusive access.

When using this class, be aware of the following platform differences:

- Windows: QSharedMemory does not "own" the shared memory segment. When all threads or processes that have an instance of QSharedMemory attached to a particular shared memory segment have either destroyed their instance of QSharedMemory or exited, the Windows kernel releases the shared memory segment automatically.
- Unix: QSharedMemory "owns" the shared memory segment. When the last thread or process that has an instance of QSharedMemory attached to a particular shared memory segment detaches from the segment by destroying its instance of QSharedMemory, the Unix kernel release the shared memory segment. But if that last thread or process crashes without running the QSharedMemory destructor, the shared memory segment survives the crash.
- HP-UX: Only one attach to a shared memory segment is allowed per process. This means that QSharedMemory should not be used across multiple threads in the same process in HP-UX.

Remember to lock the shared memory with
[lock](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsharedmemory.html#lock)() before reading from
or writing to the shared memory, and remember to release the lock with
[unlock](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsharedmemory.html#unlock)() after you are
done.

QSharedMemory automatically destroys the shared memory segment when the last instance of
QSharedMemory is detached from the segment, and no references to the segment remain.

**Warning:** QSharedMemory changes the key in a Qt-specific way, unless otherwise
specified. Interoperation with non-Qt applications is achieved by first creating a
default shared memory with QSharedMemory() and then setting a native key with
[setNativeKey](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsharedmemory.html#setNativeKey)().
When using native keys, shared memory is not protected against multiple accesses on it
(for example, unable to
[lock](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsharedmemory.html#lock)()) and a user-defined
mechanism should be used to achieve such protection.

### bool QSharedMemory::attach([QSharedMemory::AccessMode](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsharedmemory.html#AccessMode-enum) *mode* \= ReadWrite)

Attempts to attach the process to the shared memory segment identified by the key that
was passed to the constructor or to a call to
[setKey](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsharedmemory.html#setKey)() or
[setNativeKey](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsharedmemory.html#setNativeKey)().
The access *mode* is
[ReadWrite](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsharedmemory.html#AccessMode-enum) by
default. It can also be
[ReadOnly](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsharedmemory.html#AccessMode-enum).
Returns `true` if the attach operation is successful. If false is returned, call
[error](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsharedmemory.html#error)() to determine
which error occurred. After attaching the shared memory segment, a pointer to the shared
memory can be obtained by calling
[data](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsharedmemory.html#data)().

**See also**
[isAttached](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsharedmemory.html#isAttached)(),
[detach](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsharedmemory.html#detach)(), and
[create](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsharedmemory.html#create)().

or writing to the shared memory, and remember to release the lock with

### bool QSharedMemory::create(int *size*, [QSharedMemory::AccessMode](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsharedmemory.html#AccessMode-enum) *mode* \= ReadWrite)

Creates a shared memory segment of *size* bytes with the key passed to the constructor,
set with [setKey](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsharedmemory.html#setKey)() or set
with
[setNativeKey](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsharedmemory.html#setNativeKey)(),
then attaches to the new shared memory segment with the given access *mode* and returns
`true`. If a shared memory segment identified by the key already exists, the attach
operation is not performed and `false` is returned. When the return value is `false`,
call [error](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsharedmemory.html#error)() to determine
which error occurred.

**See also** [error](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsharedmemory.html#error)().

### bool QSharedMemory::lock()

This is a semaphore that locks the shared memory segment for access by this process and
returns `true`. If another process has locked the segment, this function blocks until
the lock is released. Then it acquires the lock and returns `true`. If this function
returns `false`, it means that you have ignored a false return from
[create](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsharedmemory.html#create)() or
[attach](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsharedmemory.html#attach)(), that you have
set the key with
[setNativeKey](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsharedmemory.html#setNativeKey)() or
that
[QSystemSemaphore::acquire](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsystemsemaphore.html#acquire)()
failed due to an unknown system error.

**See also** [unlock](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsharedmemory.html#unlock)(),
[data](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsharedmemory.html#data)(), and
[QSystemSemaphore::acquire](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsystemsemaphore.html#acquire)().

### [QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html) QSharedMemory::nativeKey() const

Returns the native, platform specific, key for this shared memory object. The native key
is the identifier used by the operating system to identify the shared memory segment.

You can use the native key to access shared memory segments that have not been created
by Qt, or to grant shared memory access to non-Qt applications.

This function was introduced in Qt 4.8.

**See also** [setKey](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsharedmemory.html#setKey)()
and
[setNativeKey](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsharedmemory.html#setNativeKey)().

PythonQt.Qt.QSharedMemory.setKey.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

### void QSharedMemory::setKey(const [QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html) \&*key*)

Sets the platform independent *key* for this shared memory object. If *key* is the same
as the current key, the function returns without doing anything.

You can call [key](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsharedmemory.html#key)() to
retrieve the platform independent key. Internally,
[QSharedMemory](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsharedmemory.html) converts this key
into a platform specific key. If you instead call
[nativeKey](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsharedmemory.html#nativeKey)(), you will
get the platform specific, converted key.

If the shared memory object is attached to an underlying shared memory segment, it will
[detach](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsharedmemory.html#detach) from it before
setting the new key. This function does not do an
[attach](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsharedmemory.html#attach)().

**See also** [key](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsharedmemory.html#key)(),
[nativeKey](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsharedmemory.html#nativeKey)(), and
[isAttached](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsharedmemory.html#isAttached)().

PythonQt.Qt.QSharedMemory.setNativeKey.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

### void QSharedMemory::setNativeKey(const [QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html) \&*key*)

Sets the native, platform specific, *key* for this shared memory object. If *key* is the
same as the current native key, the function returns without doing anything. If all you
want is to assign a key to a segment, you should call
[setKey](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsharedmemory.html#setKey)() instead.

You can call
[nativeKey](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsharedmemory.html#nativeKey)() to
retrieve the native key. If a native key has been assigned, calling
[key](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsharedmemory.html#key)() will return a null
string.

If the shared memory object is attached to an underlying shared memory segment, it will
[detach](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsharedmemory.html#detach) from it before
setting the new key. This function does not do an
[attach](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsharedmemory.html#attach)().

The application will not be portable if you set a native key.

This function was introduced in Qt 4.8.

**See also**
[nativeKey](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsharedmemory.html#nativeKey)(),
[key](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsharedmemory.html#key)(), and
[isAttached](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsharedmemory.html#isAttached)().

### bool QSharedMemory::unlock()

Releases the lock on the shared memory segment and returns `true`, if the lock is
currently held by this process. If the segment is not locked, or if the lock is held by
another process, nothing happens and false is returned.

**See also** [lock](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsharedmemory.html#lock)().

PythonQt.Qt.QShortcut.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

The QShortcut class provides a way of connecting keyboard shortcuts to Qt's [signals and
slots](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/signalsandslots.html) mechanism, so that
objects can be informed when a shortcut is executed. The shortcut can be set up to
contain all the key presses necessary to describe a keyboard shortcut, including the
states of modifier keys such as **Shift**, **Ctrl**, and **Alt**.

On certain widgets, using '\&' in front of a character will automatically create a
mnemonic (a shortcut) for that character, e.g. "E\&xit" will create the shortcut
**Alt\+X** (use '\&\&' to display an actual ampersand). The widget might consume and
perform an action on a given shortcut. On X11 the ampersand will not be shown and the
character will be underlined. On Windows, shortcuts are normally not displayed until the
user presses the **Alt** key, but this is a setting the user can change. On Mac,
shortcuts are disabled by default. Call
[qt\_set\_sequence\_auto\_mnemonic](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qkeysequence.html#qt_set_sequence_auto_mnemonic)()
to enable them. However, because mnemonic shortcuts do not fit in with Aqua's
guidelines, Qt will not show the shortcut character underlined.

For applications that use menus, it may be more convenient to use the convenience
functions provided in the [QMenu](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmenu.html) class
to assign keyboard shortcuts to menu items as they are created. Alternatively, shortcuts
may be associated with other types of actions in the
[QAction](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qaction.html) class.

The simplest way to create a shortcut for a particular widget is to construct the
shortcut with a key sequence. For example:

```
shortcut = new QShortcut(QKeySequence(tr("Ctrl+O", "File|Open")),
                         parent);
```

When the user types the [key
sequence](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qkeysequence.html) for a given shortcut,
the shortcut's
[activated](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qshortcut.html#activated)() signal is
emitted. (In the case of ambiguity, the
[activatedAmbiguously](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qshortcut.html#activatedAmbiguously)()
signal is emitted.) A shortcut is "listened for" by Qt's event loop when the shortcut's
parent widget is receiving events.

A shortcut's key sequence can be set with
[setKey](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qshortcut.html#key-prop)() and retrieved
with [key](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qshortcut.html#key-prop)(). A shortcut can
be enabled or disabled with
[setEnabled](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qshortcut.html#enabled-prop)(), and can
have "What's This?" help text set with
[setWhatsThis](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qshortcut.html#whatsThis-prop)().

PythonQt.Qt.QShortcut.activatedAmbiguous.doc:

### `[signal]` void QShortcut::activatedAmbiguously()

When a key sequence is being typed at the keyboard, it is said to be ambiguous as long
as it matches the start of more than one shortcut.

When a shortcut's key sequence is completed, activatedAmbiguously() is emitted if the
key sequence is still ambiguous (i.e., it is the start of one or more other shortcuts).
The [activated](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qshortcut.html#activated)() signal is
not emitted in this case.

**See also** [activated](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qshortcut.html#activated)().

### key : [QKeySequence](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qkeysequence.html)

This property holds the shortcut's key sequence

This is a key sequence with an optional combination of Shift, Ctrl, and Alt. The key
sequence may be supplied in a number of ways:

```
setKey(0);                  // no signal emitted
setKey(QKeySequence());     // no signal emitted
setKey(0x3b1);              // Greek letter alpha
setKey(Qt::Key_D);              // 'd', e.g. to delete
setKey('q');                // 'q', e.g. to quit
setKey(Qt::CTRL + Qt::Key_P);       // Ctrl+P, e.g. to print document
setKey("Ctrl+P");           // Ctrl+P, e.g. to print document
```

By default, this property contains an empty key sequence.

PythonQt.Qt.QShowEvent.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

There are two kinds of show events: show events caused by the window system
(spontaneous), and internal show events. Spontaneous
([QEvent::spontaneous](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qevent.html#spontaneous)())
show events are sent just after the window system shows the window; they are also sent
when a top-level window is redisplayed after being iconified. Internal show events are
delivered just before the widget becomes visible.

### void QSignalBlocker::reblock()

Re-blocks signals after a previous
[unblock](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsignalblocker.html#unblock)().

The numbers of reblock() and
[unblock](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsignalblocker.html#unblock)() calls are
not counted, so every reblock() undoes any number of
[unblock](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsignalblocker.html#unblock)() calls.

## Detailed Description

PythonQt.Qt.QSize.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

A size is specified by a [width](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsize.html#width)()
and a [height](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsize.html#height)(). It can be set in
the constructor and changed using the
[setWidth](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsize.html#setWidth)(),
[setHeight](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsize.html#setHeight)(), or
[scale](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsize.html#scale)() functions, or using
arithmetic operators. A size can also be manipulated directly by retrieving references
to the width and height using the
[rwidth](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsize.html#rwidth)() and
[rheight](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsize.html#rheight)() functions. Finally,
the width and height can be swapped using the
[transpose](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsize.html#transpose)() function.

The [isValid](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsize.html#isValid)() function
determines if a size is valid (a valid size has both width and height greater than or
equal to zero). The [isEmpty](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsize.html#isEmpty)()
function returns `true` if either of the width and height is less than, or equal to,
zero, while the [isNull](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsize.html#isNull)()
function returns `true` only if both the width and the height is zero.

Use the [expandedTo](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsize.html#expandedTo)()
function to retrieve a size which holds the maximum height and width of *this* size and
a given size. Similarly, the
[boundedTo](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsize.html#boundedTo)() function returns
a size which holds the minimum height and width of *this* size and a given size.

QSize objects can be streamed as well as compared.

a size which holds the minimum height and width of this size and a given size.

The QSizeF class also provides the
[toSize](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsizef.html#toSize)() function returning a
[QSize](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsize.html) copy of this size, constructed by
rounding the width and height to the nearest integers.

QSizeF objects can be streamed as well as compared.

## Detailed Description

This widget works like the standard Windows resize handle. In the X11 version this
resize handle generally works differently from the one provided by the system if the X11
window manager does not support necessary modern post-ICCCM specifications.

Put this widget anywhere in a widget tree and the user can use it to resize the
top-level window or any widget with the
[Qt::SubWindow](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#WindowType-enum) flag set.
Generally, this should be in the lower right-hand corner.

Note that [QStatusBar](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstatusbar.html) already uses
this widget, so if you have a status bar (e.g., you are using
[QMainWindow](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmainwindow.html)), then you don't need
to use this widget explicitly. The same goes for
[QDialog](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdialog.html), for which you can just call
[QDialog::setSizeGripEnabled()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdialog.html#sizeGripEnabled-prop).

On some platforms the size grip automatically hides itself when the window is shown full
screen or maximised.

| Screenshot of a Fusion style size grip | A size grip widget at the bottom-right corner of a main window, shown in the [Fusion widget style](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/gallery.html). |
| --- | --- |

The QSizeGrip class inherits [QWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html)
and reimplements the
[mousePressEvent()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#mousePressEvent) and
[mouseMoveEvent()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#mouseMoveEvent)
functions to feature the resize functionality, and the
[paintEvent()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#paintEvent) function to
render the size grip widget.

Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

The size policy of a widget is an expression of its willingness to be resized in various
ways, and affects how the widget is treated by the [layout
engine](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/layout.html). Each widget returns a
QSizePolicy that describes the horizontal and vertical resizing policy it prefers when
being laid out. You can change this for a specific widget by changing its
[QWidget::sizePolicy](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#sizePolicy-prop)
property.

QSizePolicy contains two independent
[QSizePolicy::Policy](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsizepolicy.html#Policy-enum)
values and two stretch factors; one describes the widgets's horizontal size policy, and
the other describes its vertical size policy. It also contains a flag to indicate
whether the height and width of its preferred size are related.

The horizontal and vertical policies can be set in the constructor, and altered using
the
[setHorizontalPolicy](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsizepolicy.html#setHorizontalPolicy)()
and
[setVerticalPolicy](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsizepolicy.html#setVerticalPolicy)()
functions. The stretch factors can be set using the
[setHorizontalStretch](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsizepolicy.html#setHorizontalStretch)()
and
[setVerticalStretch](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsizepolicy.html#setVerticalStretch)()
functions. The flag indicating whether the widget's
[sizeHint()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#sizeHint-prop) is
width-dependent (such as a menu bar or a word-wrapping label) can be set using the
[setHeightForWidth](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsizepolicy.html#setHeightForWidth)()
function.

The current size policies and stretch factors be retrieved using the
[horizontalPolicy](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsizepolicy.html#horizontalPolicy)(),
[verticalPolicy](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsizepolicy.html#verticalPolicy)(),
[horizontalStretch](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsizepolicy.html#horizontalStretch)()
and
[verticalStretch](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsizepolicy.html#verticalStretch)()
functions. Alternatively, use the
[transpose](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsizepolicy.html#transpose)() function to
swap the horizontal and vertical policies and stretches. The
[hasHeightForWidth](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsizepolicy.html#hasHeightForWidth)()
function returns the current status of the flag indicating the size hint dependencies.

Use the
[expandingDirections](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsizepolicy.html#expandingDirections)()
function to determine whether the associated widget can make use of more space than its
[sizeHint()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#sizeHint-prop) function
indicates, as well as find out in which directions it can expand.

Finally, the QSizePolicy class provides operators comparing this size policy to a given
policy, as well as a [QVariant](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qvariant.html)
operator storing this QSizePolicy as a
[QVariant](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qvariant.html) object.

### void QSizePolicy::setControlType([QSizePolicy::ControlType](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsizepolicy.html#ControlType-enum) *type*)

Sets the control type associated with the widget for which this size policy applies to
*type*.

The control type specifies the type of the widget for which this size policy applies. It
is used by some styles, notably QMacStyle, to insert proper spacing between widgets. For
example, the macOS Aqua guidelines specify that push buttons should be separated by 12
pixels, whereas vertically stacked radio buttons only require 6 pixels.

### void QSizePolicy::setHorizontalStretch(int *stretchFactor*)

Sets the horizontal stretch factor of the size policy to the given *stretchFactor*.
*stretchFactor* must be in the range \[0,255\].

When two widgets are adjacent to each other in a horizontal layout, setting the
horizontal stretch factor of the widget on the left to 2 and the factor of widget on the
right to 1 will ensure that the widget on the left will always be twice the size of the
one on the right.

**See also**
[horizontalStretch](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsizepolicy.html#horizontalStretch)(),
[setVerticalStretch](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsizepolicy.html#setVerticalStretch)(),
and
[setHorizontalPolicy](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsizepolicy.html#setHorizontalPolicy)().

Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

![](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/images/windows-slider.png)

The slider is the classic widget for controlling a bounded value. It lets the user move
a slider handle along a horizontal or vertical groove and translates the handle's
position into an integer value within the legal range.

QSlider has very few of its own functions; most of the functionality is in
[QAbstractSlider](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html). The most
useful functions are
[setValue](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html#value-prop)() to set
the slider directly to some value;
[triggerAction](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html#triggerAction)()
to simulate the effects of clicking (useful for shortcut keys);
[setSingleStep](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html#singleStep-prop)(),
[setPageStep](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html#pageStep-prop)()
to set the steps; and
[setMinimum](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html#minimum-prop)() and
[setMaximum](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html#maximum-prop)() to
define the range of the scroll bar.

QSlider provides methods for controlling tickmarks. You can use
[setTickPosition](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qslider.html#tickPosition-prop)()
to indicate where you want the tickmarks to be,
[setTickInterval](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qslider.html#tickInterval-prop)()
to indicate how many of them you want. the currently set tick position and interval can
be queried using the
[tickPosition](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qslider.html#tickPosition-prop)() and
[tickInterval](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qslider.html#tickInterval-prop)()
functions, respectively.

QSlider inherits a comprehensive set of signals:

| Signal | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [valueChanged](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html#valueChanged)() | Emitted when the slider's value has changed. The tracking() determines whether this signal is emitted during user interaction. |
| [sliderPressed](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html#sliderPressed)() | Emitted when the user starts to drag the slider. |
| [sliderMoved](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html#sliderMoved)() | Emitted when the user drags the slider. |
| [sliderReleased](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html#sliderReleased)() | Emitted when the user releases the slider. |

QSlider only provides integer ranges. Note that although QSlider handles very large
numbers, it becomes difficult for users to use a slider accurately for very large
ranges.

A slider accepts focus on Tab and provides both a mouse wheel and a keyboard interface.
The keyboard interface is the following:

- Left/Right move a horizontal slider by one single step.
- Up/Down move a vertical slider by one single step.
- PageUp moves up one page.
- PageDown moves down one page.
- Home moves to the start (minimum).
- End moves to the end (maximum).

PythonQt.Qt.QSocketNotifier.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

The QSocketNotifier makes it possible to integrate Qt's event loop with other event
loops based on file descriptors. File descriptor action is detected in Qt's main event
loop
([QCoreApplication::exec](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcoreapplication.html#exec)()).

Once you have opened a device using a low-level (usually platform-specific) API, you can
create a socket notifier to monitor the file descriptor. The socket notifier is enabled
by default, i.e. it emits the
[activated](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsocketnotifier.html#activated)() signal
whenever a socket event corresponding to its type occurs. Connect the
[activated](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsocketnotifier.html#activated)() signal
to the slot you want to be called when an event corresponding to your socket notifier's
type occurs.

There are three types of socket notifiers: read, write, and exception. The type is
described by the
[Type](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsocketnotifier.html#Type-enum) enum, and must
be specified when constructing the socket notifier. After construction it can be
determined using the
[type](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsocketnotifier.html#type)() function. Note
that if you need to monitor both reads and writes for the same file descriptor, you must
create two socket notifiers. Note also that it is not possible to install two socket
notifiers of the same type
([Read](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsocketnotifier.html#Type-enum),
[Write](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsocketnotifier.html#Type-enum),
[Exception](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsocketnotifier.html#Type-enum)) on the
same socket.

The [setEnabled](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsocketnotifier.html#setEnabled)()
function allows you to disable as well as enable the socket notifier. It is generally
advisable to explicitly enable or disable the socket notifier, especially for write
notifiers. A disabled notifier ignores socket events (the same effect as not creating
the socket notifier). Use the
[isEnabled](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsocketnotifier.html#isEnabled)()
function to determine the notifier's current status.

Finally, you can use the
[socket](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsocketnotifier.html#socket)() function to
retrieve the socket identifier. Although the class is called QSocketNotifier, it is
normally used for other types of devices than sockets.
[QTcpSocket](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtcpsocket.html) and
[QUdpSocket](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qudpsocket.html) provide notification
through signals, so there is normally no need to use a QSocketNotifier on them.

PythonQt.Qt.QSocketNotifier.activated.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

### `[signal]` void QSocketNotifier::activated(QSocketDescriptor *socket*, [QSocketNotifier::Type](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsocketnotifier.html#Type-enum) *type*)

This signal is emitted whenever the socket notifier is enabled and a socket event
corresponding to its *type* occurs.

The socket identifier is passed in the *socket* parameter.

**Note:** This is a private signal. It can be used in signal connections but cannot be
emitted by the user.

**Note:** Signal *activated* is overloaded in this class. To connect to this signal by
using the function pointer syntax, Qt provides a convenient helper for obtaining the
function pointer as shown in this example:

```
connect(socketNotifier, QOverload<QSocketDescriptor, QSocketNotifier::Type>::of(&QSocketNotifier::activated),
    [=](QSocketDescriptor socket, QSocketNotifier::Type type){ /* ... */ });
```

This function was introduced in Qt 5.15.

**See also** [type](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsocketnotifier.html#type)() and
[socket](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsocketnotifier.html#socket)().

PythonQt.Qt.QSortFilterProxyModel.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

QSortFilterProxyModel can be used for sorting items, filtering out items, or both. The
model transforms the structure of a source model by mapping the model indexes it
supplies to new indexes, corresponding to different locations, for views to use. This
approach allows a given source model to be restructured as far as views are concerned
without requiring any transformations on the underlying data, and without duplicating
the data in memory.

Let's assume that we want to sort and filter the items provided by a custom model. The
code to set up the model and the view, *without* sorting and filtering, would look like
this:

```
        QTreeView *treeView = new QTreeView;
        MyItemModel *model = new MyItemModel(this);

        treeView->setModel(model);
```

To add sorting and filtering support to `MyItemModel`, we need to create a
QSortFilterProxyModel, call
[setSourceModel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsortfilterproxymodel.html#setSourceModel)()
with the `MyItemModel` as argument, and install the QSortFilterProxyModel on the view:

```
        QTreeView *treeView = new QTreeView;
        MyItemModel *sourceModel = new MyItemModel(this);
        QSortFilterProxyModel *proxyModel = new QSortFilterProxyModel(this);

        proxyModel->setSourceModel(sourceModel);
        treeView->setModel(proxyModel);
```

At this point, neither sorting nor filtering is enabled; the original data is displayed
in the view. Any changes made through the QSortFilterProxyModel are applied to the
original model.

The QSortFilterProxyModel acts as a wrapper for the original model. If you need to
convert source [QModelIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmodelindex.html)es to
sorted/filtered model indexes or vice versa, use
[mapToSource](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsortfilterproxymodel.html#mapToSource)(),
[mapFromSource](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsortfilterproxymodel.html#mapFromSource)(),
[mapSelectionToSource](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsortfilterproxymodel.html#mapSelectionToSource)(),
and
[mapSelectionFromSource](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsortfilterproxymodel.html#mapSelectionFromSource)().

**Note:** By default, the model dynamically re-sorts and re-filters data whenever the
original model changes. This behavior can be changed by setting the
[dynamicSortFilter](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsortfilterproxymodel.html#dynamicSortFilter-prop)
property.

The [Basic Sort/Filter
Model](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtwidgets-itemviews-basicsortfiltermodel-example.html)
and [Custom Sort/Filter
Model](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtwidgets-itemviews-customsortfiltermodel-example.html)
examples illustrate how to use QSortFilterProxyModel to perform basic sorting and
filtering and how to subclass it to implement custom behavior.

### Sorting

[QTableView](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtableview.html) and
[QTreeView](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtreeview.html) have a
[sortingEnabled](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtreeview.html#sortingEnabled-prop)
property that controls whether the user can sort the view by clicking the view's
horizontal header. For example:

```
        treeView->setSortingEnabled(true);
```

When this feature is on (the default is off), clicking on a header section sorts the
items according to that column. By clicking repeatedly, the user can alternate between
ascending and descending order.

![A sorted
QTreeView](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/images/qsortfilterproxymodel-sorting.png)

Behind the scene, the view calls the
[sort](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsortfilterproxymodel.html#sort)() virtual
function on the model to reorder the data in the model. To make your data sortable, you
can either implement
[sort](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsortfilterproxymodel.html#sort)() in your
model, or use a QSortFilterProxyModel to wrap your model \-- QSortFilterProxyModel
provides a generic
[sort](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsortfilterproxymodel.html#sort)()
reimplementation that operates on the
[sortRole](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsortfilterproxymodel.html#sortRole-prop)()
([Qt::DisplayRole](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#ItemDataRole-enum) by
default) of the items and that understands several data types, including `int`,
[QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html), and
[QDateTime](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdatetime.html). For hierarchical models,
sorting is applied recursively to all child items. String comparisons are case sensitive
by default; this can be changed by setting the
[sortCaseSensitivity](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsortfilterproxymodel.html#sortCaseSensitivity-prop)
property.

Custom sorting behavior is achieved by subclassing QSortFilterProxyModel and
reimplementing
[lessThan](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsortfilterproxymodel.html#lessThan)(),
which is used to compare items. For example:

```
bool MySortFilterProxyModel::lessThan(const QModelIndex &left,
                                      const QModelIndex &right) const
{
    QVariant leftData = sourceModel()->data(left);
    QVariant rightData = sourceModel()->data(right);

    if (leftData.userType() == QMetaType::QDateTime) {
        return leftData.toDateTime() < rightData.toDateTime();
    } else {
        static const QRegularExpression emailPattern("[\\w\\.]*@[\\w\\.]*");

        QString leftString = leftData.toString();
        if (left.column() == 1) {
            const QRegularExpressionMatch match = emailPattern.match(leftString);
            if (match.hasMatch())
                leftString = match.captured(0);
        }
        QString rightString = rightData.toString();
        if (right.column() == 1) {
            const QRegularExpressionMatch match = emailPattern.match(rightString);
            if (match.hasMatch())
                rightString = match.captured(0);
        }

        return QString::localeAwareCompare(leftString, rightString) < 0;
    }
}
```

(This code snippet comes from the [Custom Sort/Filter
Model](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtwidgets-itemviews-customsortfiltermodel-example.html)
example.)

An alternative approach to sorting is to disable sorting on the view and to impose a
certain order to the user. This is done by explicitly calling
[sort](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsortfilterproxymodel.html#sort)() with the
desired column and order as arguments on the QSortFilterProxyModel (or on the original
model if it implements
[sort](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsortfilterproxymodel.html#sort)()). For
example:

```
        proxyModel->sort(2, Qt::AscendingOrder);
```

QSortFilterProxyModel can be sorted by column -1, in which case it returns to the sort
order of the underlying source model.

### Filtering

In addition to sorting, QSortFilterProxyModel can be used to hide items that do not
match a certain filter. The filter is specified using a
[QRegExp](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qregexp.html) object and is applied to the
[filterRole](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsortfilterproxymodel.html#filterRole-prop)()
([Qt::DisplayRole](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#ItemDataRole-enum) by
default) of each item, for a given column. The
[QRegExp](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qregexp.html) object can be used to match a
regular expression, a wildcard pattern, or a fixed string. For example:

```
        proxyModel->setFilterRegExp(QRegExp(".png", Qt::CaseInsensitive,
                                            QRegExp::FixedString));
        proxyModel->setFilterKeyColumn(1);
```

For hierarchical models, the filter is applied recursively to all children. If a parent
item doesn't match the filter, none of its children will be shown.

A common use case is to let the user specify the filter regular expression, wildcard
pattern, or fixed string in a
[QLineEdit](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qlineedit.html) and to connect the
[textChanged()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qlineedit.html#textChanged) signal to
[setFilterRegularExpression](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsortfilterproxymodel.html#setFilterRegularExpression)(),
[setFilterWildcard](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsortfilterproxymodel.html#setFilterWildcard)(),
or
[setFilterFixedString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsortfilterproxymodel.html#setFilterFixedString)()
to reapply the filter.

Custom filtering behavior can be achieved by reimplementing the
[filterAcceptsRow](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsortfilterproxymodel.html#filterAcceptsRow)()
and
[filterAcceptsColumn](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsortfilterproxymodel.html#filterAcceptsColumn)()
functions. For example (from the [Custom Sort/Filter
Model](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtwidgets-itemviews-customsortfiltermodel-example.html)
example), the following implementation ignores the
[filterKeyColumn](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsortfilterproxymodel.html#filterKeyColumn-prop)
property and performs filtering on columns 0, 1, and 2:

```
bool MySortFilterProxyModel::filterAcceptsRow(int sourceRow,
                                              const QModelIndex &sourceParent) const
{
    QModelIndex index0 = sourceModel()->index(sourceRow, 0, sourceParent);
    QModelIndex index1 = sourceModel()->index(sourceRow, 1, sourceParent);
    QModelIndex index2 = sourceModel()->index(sourceRow, 2, sourceParent);

    return (sourceModel()->data(index0).toString().contains(filterRegExp())
            || sourceModel()->data(index1).toString().contains(filterRegExp()))
            && dateInRange(sourceModel()->data(index2).toDate());
}
```

(This code snippet comes from the [Custom Sort/Filter
Model](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtwidgets-itemviews-customsortfiltermodel-example.html)
example.)

If you are working with large amounts of filtering and have to invoke
[invalidateFilter](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsortfilterproxymodel.html#invalidateFilter)()
repeatedly, using
[beginResetModel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#beginResetModel)()
/
[endResetModel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#endResetModel)()
may be more efficient, depending on the implementation of your model. However,
[beginResetModel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#beginResetModel)()
/
[endResetModel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#endResetModel)()
returns the proxy model to its original state, losing selection information, and will
cause the proxy model to be repopulated.

### Subclassing

Since [QAbstractProxyModel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractproxymodel.html)
and its subclasses are derived from
[QAbstractItemModel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html), much
of the same advice about subclassing normal models also applies to proxy models. In
addition, it is worth noting that many of the default implementations of functions in
this class are written so that they call the equivalent functions in the relevant source
model. This simple proxying mechanism may need to be overridden for source models with
more complex behavior; for example, if the source model provides a custom
[hasChildren](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsortfilterproxymodel.html#hasChildren)()
implementation, you should also provide one in the proxy model.

**Note:** Some general guidelines for subclassing models are available in the [Model
Subclassing
Reference](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/model-view-programming.html#model-subclassing-reference).

**Note:** With Qt 5, regular expression support has been improved through the
[QRegularExpression](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qregularexpression.html) class.
QSortFilterProxyModel dating back prior to that class creation, it originally supported
only [QRegExp](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qregexp.html). Since Qt 5.12,
[QRegularExpression](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qregularexpression.html) APIs
have been added. Therefore, [QRegExp](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qregexp.html)
APIs should be considered deprecated and the
[QRegularExpression](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qregularexpression.html) version
should be used in place.

**Warning:** Don't mix calls to the getters and setters of different regexp types as
this will lead to unexpected results. For maximum compatibility, the original
implementation has been kept. Therefore, if, for example, a call to
[setFilterRegularExpression](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsortfilterproxymodel.html#setFilterRegularExpression)
is made followed by another one to
[setFilterFixedString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsortfilterproxymodel.html#setFilterFixedString),
the first call will setup a
[QRegularExpression](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qregularexpression.html) object
to use as filter while the second will setup a
[QRegExp](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qregexp.html) in FixedString mode. However,
this is an implementation detail that might change in the future.

### dynamicSortFilter : bool

This property holds whether the proxy model is dynamically sorted and filtered whenever
the contents of the source model change

Note that you should not update the source model through the proxy model when
dynamicSortFilter is true. For instance, if you set the proxy model on a
[QComboBox](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcombobox.html), then using functions
that update the model, e.g.,
[addItem()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcombobox.html#addItem), will not work as
expected. An alternative is to set dynamicSortFilter to false and call
[sort()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsortfilterproxymodel.html#sort) after
adding items to the [QComboBox](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcombobox.html).

The default value is true.

This property was introduced in Qt 4.2.

Qt 5 reference:

### `[virtual protected]` bool QSortFilterProxyModel::lessThan(const [QModelIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmodelindex.html) \&*source\_left*, const [QModelIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmodelindex.html) \&*source\_right*) const

Returns `true` if the value of the item referred to by the given index *source\_left* is
less than the value of the item referred to by the given index *source\_right*,
otherwise returns `false`.

This function is used as the \< operator when sorting, and handles the following
[QVariant](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qvariant.html) types:

- [QMetaType::Int](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmetatype.html#Type-enum)
- [QMetaType::UInt](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmetatype.html#Type-enum)
- [QMetaType::LongLong](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmetatype.html#Type-enum)
- [QMetaType::ULongLong](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmetatype.html#Type-enum)
- [QMetaType::Float](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmetatype.html#Type-enum)
- [QMetaType::Double](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmetatype.html#Type-enum)
- [QMetaType::QChar](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmetatype.html#Type-enum)
- [QMetaType::QDate](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmetatype.html#Type-enum)
- [QMetaType::QTime](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmetatype.html#Type-enum)
- [QMetaType::QDateTime](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmetatype.html#Type-enum)
- [QMetaType::QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmetatype.html#Type-enum)

Any other type will be converted to a
[QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html) using
[QVariant::toString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qvariant.html#toString)().

Comparison of [QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html)s is case
sensitive by default; this can be changed using the
[sortCaseSensitivity](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsortfilterproxymodel.html#sortCaseSensitivity-prop)
property.

By default, the
[Qt::DisplayRole](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#ItemDataRole-enum)
associated with the [QModelIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmodelindex.html)es
is used for comparisons. This can be changed by setting the

## Detailed Description

QSourceLocation is a simple value based class that has three properties,
[uri](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsourcelocation.html#uri)(),
[line](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsourcelocation.html#line)(), and
[column](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsourcelocation.html#column)(), that, taken
together, identify a certain point in a resource, e.g., a file or an in-memory document.

[line](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsourcelocation.html#line)() and
[column](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsourcelocation.html#column)() refer to
character counts (not byte counts), and they both start from 1, as opposed to 0\.

### void QSpacerItem::changeSize(int *w*, int *h*, [QSizePolicy::Policy](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsizepolicy.html#Policy-enum) *hPolicy* \= QSizePolicy::Minimum, [QSizePolicy::Policy](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsizepolicy.html#Policy-enum) *vPolicy* \= QSizePolicy::Minimum)

Changes this spacer item to have preferred width *w*, preferred height *h*, horizontal
size policy *hPolicy* and vertical size policy *vPolicy*.

The default values provide a gap that is able to stretch if nothing else wants the
space.

Note that if changeSize() is called after the spacer item has been added to a layout, it
is necessary to invalidate the layout in order for the spacer item's new size to take
effect.

PythonQt.Qt.QSpinBox.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

![](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/images/windows-spinbox.png)

QSpinBox is designed to handle integers and discrete sets of values (e.g., month names);
use [QDoubleSpinBox](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdoublespinbox.html) for
floating point values.

QSpinBox allows the user to choose a value by clicking the up/down buttons or pressing
up/down on the keyboard to increase/decrease the value currently displayed. The user can
also type the value in manually. The spin box supports integer values but can be
extended to use different strings with
[validate](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qspinbox.html#validate)(),
[textFromValue](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qspinbox.html#textFromValue)() and
[valueFromText](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qspinbox.html#valueFromText)().

Every time the value changes QSpinBox emits
[valueChanged](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qspinbox.html#valueChanged)() and
[textChanged](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qspinbox.html#textChanged)() signals,
the former providing a int and the latter a
[QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html). The
[textChanged](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qspinbox.html#textChanged)() signal
provides the value with both
[prefix](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qspinbox.html#prefix-prop)() and
[suffix](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qspinbox.html#suffix-prop)(). The current
value can be fetched with
[value](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qspinbox.html#value-prop)() and set with
[setValue](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qspinbox.html#value-prop)().

Clicking the up/down buttons or using the keyboard accelerator's up and down arrows will
increase or decrease the current value in steps of size
[singleStep](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qspinbox.html#singleStep-prop)(). If you
want to change this behaviour you can reimplement the virtual function
[stepBy](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractspinbox.html#stepBy)(). The minimum
and maximum value and the step size can be set using one of the constructors, and can be
changed later with
[setMinimum](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qspinbox.html#minimum-prop)(),
[setMaximum](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qspinbox.html#maximum-prop)() and
[setSingleStep](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qspinbox.html#singleStep-prop)().

Most spin boxes are directional, but QSpinBox can also operate as a circular spin box,
i.e. if the range is 0-99 and the current value is 99, clicking "up" will give 0 if
[wrapping](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractspinbox.html#wrapping-prop)() is
set to true. Use
[setWrapping](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractspinbox.html#wrapping-prop)()
if you want circular behavior.

The displayed value can be prepended and appended with arbitrary strings indicating, for
example, currency or the unit of measurement. See
[setPrefix](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qspinbox.html#prefix-prop)() and
[setSuffix](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qspinbox.html#suffix-prop)(). The text in
the spin box is retrieved with
[text](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractspinbox.html#text-prop)() (which
includes any [prefix](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qspinbox.html#prefix-prop)()
and [suffix](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qspinbox.html#suffix-prop)()), or with
[cleanText](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qspinbox.html#cleanText-prop)() (which
has no [prefix](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qspinbox.html#prefix-prop)(), no
[suffix](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qspinbox.html#suffix-prop)() and no leading
or trailing whitespace).

It is often desirable to give the user a special (often default) choice in addition to
the range of numeric values. See
[setSpecialValueText](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractspinbox.html#specialValueText-prop)()
for how to do this with QSpinBox.

### Subclassing QSpinBox

If using [prefix](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qspinbox.html#prefix-prop)(),
[suffix](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qspinbox.html#suffix-prop)(), and
[specialValueText](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractspinbox.html#specialValueText-prop)()
don't provide enough control, you subclass QSpinBox and reimplement
[valueFromText](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qspinbox.html#valueFromText)() and
[textFromValue](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qspinbox.html#textFromValue)(). For
example, here's the code for a custom spin box that allows the user to enter icon sizes
(e.g., "32 x 32"):

```
int IconSizeSpinBox::valueFromText(const QString &text) const
{
    static const QRegularExpression regExp(tr("(\\d+)(\\s*[xx]\\s*\\d+)?"));
    Q_ASSERT(regExp.isValid());

    const QRegularExpressionMatch match = regExp.match(text);
    if (match.isValid())
        return match.captured(1).toInt();
    return 0;
}

QString IconSizeSpinBox::textFromValue(int value) const
{
    return tr("%1 x %1").arg(value);
}
```

See the [Icons](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtwidgets-widgets-icons-example.html)
example for the full source code.

### prefix : [QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html)

This property holds the spin box's prefix

The prefix is prepended to the start of the displayed value. Typical use is to display a
unit of measurement or a currency symbol. For example:

```
sb->setPrefix("$");
```

To turn off the prefix display, set this property to an empty string. The default is no
prefix. The prefix is not displayed when
[value](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qspinbox.html#value-prop)() \=\=
[minimum](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qspinbox.html#minimum-prop)() and
[specialValueText](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractspinbox.html#specialValueText-prop)()
is set.

If no prefix is set, prefix() returns an empty string.

**Access functions:**

**See also** [suffix](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qspinbox.html#suffix-prop)(),

Qt 5 reference:

### `[virtual protected]` [QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html) QSpinBox::textFromValue(int *value*) const

This virtual function is used by the spin box whenever it needs to display the given
*value*. The default implementation returns a string containing *value* printed in the
standard way using
[QWidget::locale](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#locale-prop)().toString(),
but with the thousand separator removed unless
[setGroupSeparatorShown](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractspinbox.html#showGroupSeparator-prop)()
is set. Reimplementations may return anything. (See the example in the detailed
description.)

Note: [QSpinBox](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qspinbox.html) does not call this
function for
[specialValueText](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractspinbox.html#specialValueText-prop)()
and that neither
[prefix](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qspinbox.html#prefix-prop)() nor
[suffix](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qspinbox.html#suffix-prop)() should be
included in the return value.

If you reimplement this, you may also need to reimplement
[valueFromText](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qspinbox.html#valueFromText)() and
[validate](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qspinbox.html#validate)()

**See also**
[valueFromText](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qspinbox.html#valueFromText)(),
[validate](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qspinbox.html#validate)(), and
[QLocale::groupSeparator](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qlocale.html#groupSeparator)().

### `[signal]` void QSpinBox::valueChanged(int *i*)

This signal is emitted whenever the spin box's value is changed. The new value's integer
value is passed in *i*.

**Note:** Notifier signal for property
[value](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qspinbox.html#value-prop).

**Note:** Signal *valueChanged* is overloaded in this class. To connect to this signal
by using the function pointer syntax, Qt provides a convenient helper for obtaining the
function pointer as shown in this example:

```
connect(spinBox, QOverload<int>::of(&QSpinBox::valueChanged),
    [=](int i){ /* ... */ });
```

PythonQt.Qt.QSplitter.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

A splitter lets the user control the size of child widgets by dragging the boundary
between them. Any number of widgets may be controlled by a single splitter. The typical
use of a QSplitter is to create several widgets and add them using
[insertWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsplitter.html#insertWidget)() or
[addWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsplitter.html#addWidget)().

The following example will show a
[QListView](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qlistview.html),
[QTreeView](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtreeview.html), and
[QTextEdit](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html) side by side, with two
splitter handles:

```
    QSplitter *splitter = new QSplitter(parent);
    QListView *listview = new QListView;
    QTreeView *treeview = new QTreeView;
    QTextEdit *textedit = new QTextEdit;
    splitter->addWidget(listview);
    splitter->addWidget(treeview);
    splitter->addWidget(textedit);
```

If a widget is already inside a QSplitter when
[insertWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsplitter.html#insertWidget)() or
[addWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsplitter.html#addWidget)() is called, it
will move to the new position. This can be used to reorder widgets in the splitter
later. You can use
[indexOf](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsplitter.html#indexOf)(),
[widget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsplitter.html#widget)(), and
[count](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsplitter.html#count)() to get access to the
widgets inside the splitter.

A default QSplitter lays out its children horizontally (side by side); you can use
[setOrientation](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsplitter.html#orientation-prop)([Qt::Vertical](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#Orientation-enum))
to lay its children out vertically.

By default, all widgets can be as large or as small as the user wishes, between the
[minimumSizeHint](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsplitter.html#minimumSizeHint)()
(or [minimumSize](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#minimumSize-prop)())
and [maximumSize](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#maximumSize-prop)() of
the widgets.

QSplitter resizes its children dynamically by default. If you would rather have
QSplitter resize the children only at the end of a resize operation, call
[setOpaqueResize](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsplitter.html#opaqueResize-prop)(false).

The initial distribution of size between the widgets is determined by multiplying the
initial size with the stretch factor. You can also use
[setSizes](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsplitter.html#setSizes)() to set the
sizes of all the widgets. The function
[sizes](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsplitter.html#sizes)() returns the sizes set
by the user. Alternatively, you can save and restore the sizes of the widgets from a
[QByteArray](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qbytearray.html) using
[saveState](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsplitter.html#saveState)() and
[restoreState](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsplitter.html#restoreState)()
respectively.

When you [hide](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#hide)() a child, its
space will be distributed among the other children. It will be reinstated when you
[show](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#show)() it again.

**Note:** Adding a [QLayout](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qlayout.html) to a
QSplitter is not supported (either through
[setLayout](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#setLayout)() or making the
QSplitter a parent of the [QLayout](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qlayout.html));
use [addWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsplitter.html#addWidget)() instead
(see example above).

### [QSplitterHandle](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsplitterhandle.html) \*QSplitter::handle(int *index*) const

Returns the handle to the left of (or above) the item in the splitter's layout at the
given *index*, or `nullptr` if there is no such item. The handle at index 0 is always
hidden.

For right-to-left languages such as Arabic and Hebrew, the layout of horizontal
splitters is reversed. The handle will be to the right of the widget at *index*.

**See also** [count](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsplitter.html#count)(),
[widget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsplitter.html#widget)(),

[createHandle](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsplitter.html#createHandle)(), and

### int QSplitter::indexOf([QWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#QWidget) \**widget*) const

Returns the index in the splitter's layout of the specified *widget*, or -1 if *widget*
is not found. This also works for handles.

Handles are numbered from 0\. There are as many handles as there are child widgets, but
the handle at position 0 is always hidden.

**See also** [count](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsplitter.html#count)() and

### bool QSplitter::restoreState(const [QByteArray](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qbytearray.html) \&*state*)

Restores the splitter's layout to the *state* specified. Returns `true` if the state is
restored; otherwise returns `false`.

Typically this is used in conjunction with
[QSettings](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsettings.html) to restore the size from
a past session. Here is an example:

Restore the splitter's state:

```
    QSettings settings;
    splitter->restoreState(settings.value("splitterSizes").toByteArray());
```

A failure to restore the splitter's layout may result from either invalid or out-of-date
data in the supplied byte array.

**See also** [saveState](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsplitter.html#saveState)().

Typically this is used in conjunction with
[QSettings](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsettings.html) to remember the size for
a future session. A version number is stored as part of the data. Here is an example:

```
    QSettings settings;
    settings.setValue("splitterSizes", splitter->saveState());
```

**See also**
[restoreState](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsplitter.html#restoreState)().

### void QSplitter::setCollapsible(int *index*, bool *collapse*)

Sets whether the child widget at *index* is collapsible to *collapse*.

By default, children are collapsible, meaning that the user can resize them down to size
0, even if they have a non-zero
[minimumSize](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#minimumSize-prop)() or
[minimumSizeHint](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsplitter.html#minimumSizeHint)().
This behavior can be changed on a per-widget basis by calling this function, or globally
for all the widgets in the splitter by setting the
[childrenCollapsible](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsplitter.html#childrenCollapsible-prop)
property.

**See also**
[isCollapsible](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsplitter.html#isCollapsible)() and
[childrenCollapsible](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsplitter.html#childrenCollapsible-prop).

### void QSplitter::setSizes(const [QList](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qlist.html)\<int\> \&*list*)

Sets the child widgets' respective sizes to the values given in the *list*.

If the splitter is horizontal, the values set the width of each widget in pixels, from
left to right. If the splitter is vertical, the height of each widget is set, from top
to bottom.

Extra values in the *list* are ignored. If *list* contains too few values, the result is
undefined, but the program will still be well-behaved.

The overall size of the splitter widget is not affected. Instead, any additional/missing
space is distributed amongst the widgets according to the relative weight of the sizes.

If you specify a size of 0, the widget will be invisible. The size policies of the
widgets are preserved. That is, a value smaller than the minimal size hint of the
respective widget will be replaced by the value of the hint.

**See also** [sizes](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsplitter.html#sizes)().

signatures: setStretchFactor(self, index: int, stretch: int) -> None

If the splitter's orientation is horizontal, the list contains the widgets width in
pixels, from left to right; if the orientation is vertical, the list contains the

Giving the values to another splitter's
[setSizes](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsplitter.html#setSizes)() function will
produce a splitter with the same layout as this one.

Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

QSslCertificate stores an X509 certificate, and is commonly used to verify the identity
and store information about the local host, a remotely connected peer, or a trusted
third party Certificate Authority.

There are many ways to construct a QSslCertificate. The most common way is to call
[QSslSocket::peerCertificate](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsslsocket.html#peerCertificate)(),
which returns a QSslCertificate object, or
[QSslSocket::peerCertificateChain](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsslsocket.html#peerCertificateChain)(),
which returns a list of them. You can also load certificates from a DER (binary) or PEM
(Base64) encoded bundle, typically stored as one or more local files, or in a Qt
Resource.

You can call [isNull](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsslcertificate.html#isNull)()
to check if your certificate is null. By default, QSslCertificate constructs a null
certificate. A null certificate is invalid, but an invalid certificate is not
necessarily null. If you want to reset all contents in a certificate, call
[clear](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsslcertificate.html#clear)().

After loading a certificate, you can find information about the certificate, its
subject, and its issuer, by calling one of the many accessor functions, including
[version](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsslcertificate.html#version)(),
[serialNumber](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsslcertificate.html#serialNumber)(),
[issuerInfo](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsslcertificate.html#issuerInfo)() and
[subjectInfo](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsslcertificate.html#subjectInfo)().
You can call
[effectiveDate](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsslcertificate.html#effectiveDate)()
and [expiryDate](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsslcertificate.html#expiryDate)()
to check when the certificate starts being effective and when it expires. The
[publicKey](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsslcertificate.html#publicKey)()
function returns the certificate subject's public key as a
[QSslKey](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsslkey.html). You can call
[issuerInfo](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsslcertificate.html#issuerInfo)() or
[subjectInfo](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsslcertificate.html#subjectInfo)() to
get detailed information about the certificate issuer and its subject.

Internally, QSslCertificate is stored as an X509 structure. You can access this handle
by calling [handle](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsslcertificate.html#handle)(),
but the results are likely to not be portable.

### `[static]` bool QSslCertificate::importPkcs12([QIODevice](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qiodevice.html) \**device*, [QSslKey](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsslkey.html) \**key*, [QSslCertificate](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsslcertificate.html#QSslCertificate) \**certificate*, [QList](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qlist.html)\<[QSslCertificate](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsslcertificate.html#QSslCertificate)\> \**caCertificates* \= nullptr, const [QByteArray](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qbytearray.html) \&*passPhrase* \= QByteArray())

Imports a PKCS#12 (pfx) file from the specified *device*. A PKCS#12 file is a bundle
that can contain a number of certificates and keys. This method reads a single *key*,
its *certificate* and any associated *caCertificates* from the bundle. If a *passPhrase*
is specified then this will be used to decrypt the bundle. Returns `true` if the PKCS#12
file was successfully loaded.

**Note:** The *device* must be open and ready to be read from.

This function was introduced in Qt 5.4.

PythonQt.Qt.QSslCertificateExtension.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

QSslCertificateExtension provides access to an extension stored in an X509 certificate.
The information available depends on the type of extension being accessed.

All X509 certificate extensions have the following properties:

| Property | Description |
| --- | --- |
| name | The human readable name of the extension, eg. 'basicConstraints'. |
| criticality | This is a boolean value indicating if the extension is critical to correctly interpreting the certificate. |
| oid | The ASN.1 object identifier that specifies which extension this is. |
| supported | If this is true the structure of the extension's value will not change between Qt versions. |
| value | A [QVariant](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qvariant.html) with a structure dependent on the type of extension. |

Whilst this class provides access to any type of extension, only some are guaranteed to
be returned in a format that will remain unchanged between releases. The
[isSupported](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsslcertificateextension.html#isSupported)()
method returns `true` for extensions where this is the case.

The extensions currently supported, and the structure of the value returned are as
follows:

| Name | OID | Details |
| --- | --- | --- |
| basicConstraints | 2.5.29.19 | Returned as a [QVariantMap](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qvariant.html#QVariantMap-typedef). The key 'ca' contains a boolean value, the optional key 'pathLenConstraint' contains an integer. |
| authorityInfoAccess | 1.3.6.1.5.5.7.1.1 | Returned as a [QVariantMap](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qvariant.html#QVariantMap-typedef). There is a key for each access method, with the value being a URI. |
| subjectKeyIdentifier | 2.5.29.14 | Returned as a [QVariant](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qvariant.html) containing a [QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html). The string is the key identifier. |
| authorityKeyIdentifier | 2.5.29.35 | Returned as a [QVariantMap](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qvariant.html#QVariantMap-typedef). The optional key 'keyid' contains the key identifier as a hex string stored in a [QByteArray](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qbytearray.html). The optional key 'serial' contains the authority key serial number as a qlonglong. Currently there is no support for the general names field of this extension. |

In addition to the supported extensions above, many other common extensions will be
returned in a reasonably structured way. Extensions that the SSL backend has no support
for at all will be returned as a
[QByteArray](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qbytearray.html).

Further information about the types of extensions certificates can contain can be found
in RFC 5280\.

PythonQt.Qt.QSslConfiguration.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

QSslConfiguration is used by Qt networking classes to relay information about an open
SSL connection and to allow the application to control certain features of that
connection.

The settings that QSslConfiguration currently supports are:

- The SSL/TLS protocol to be used
- The certificate to be presented to the peer during connection and its associated private key
- The ciphers allowed to be used for encrypting the connection
- The list of Certificate Authorities certificates that are used to validate the peer's certificate

These settings are applied only during the connection handshake. Setting them after the
connection has been established has no effect.

The state that QSslConfiguration supports are:

- The certificate the peer presented during handshake, along with the chain leading to a CA certificate
- The cipher used to encrypt this session

The state can only be obtained once the SSL connection starts, but not necessarily
before it's done. Some settings may change during the course of the SSL connection
without need to restart it (for instance, the cipher can be changed over time).

State in QSslConfiguration objects cannot be changed.

QSslConfiguration can be used with
[QSslSocket](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsslsocket.html) and the Network Access
API.

Note that changing settings in QSslConfiguration is not enough to change the settings in
the related SSL connection. You must call setSslConfiguration on a modified
QSslConfiguration object to achieve that. The following example illustrates how to
change the protocol to TLSv1\_0 in a
[QSslSocket](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsslsocket.html) object:

```
QSslConfiguration config = sslSocket.sslConfiguration();
config.setProtocol(QSsl::TlsV1_0);
sslSocket.setSslConfiguration(config);
```

### [QList](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qlist.html)\<[QSslCipher](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsslcipher.html)\> QSslConfiguration::ciphers() const

Returns this connection's current cryptographic cipher suite. This list is used during
the handshake phase for choosing a session cipher. The returned list of ciphers is
ordered by descending preference. (i.e., the first cipher in the list is the most
preferred cipher). The session cipher will be the first one in the list that is also
supported by the peer.

By default, the handshake phase can choose any of the ciphers supported by this system's
SSL libraries, which may vary from system to system. The list of ciphers supported by
this system's SSL libraries is returned by QSslSocket::supportedCiphers(). You can
restrict the list of ciphers used for choosing the session cipher for this socket by
calling
[setCiphers](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsslconfiguration.html#setCiphers)()
with a subset of the supported ciphers. You can revert to using the entire set by
calling
[setCiphers](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsslconfiguration.html#setCiphers)()
with the list returned by QSslSocket::supportedCiphers().

**Note:** This is not currently supported in the Schannel backend.

**See also**
[setCiphers](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsslconfiguration.html#setCiphers)() and
[QSslSocket::supportedCiphers](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsslsocket-obsolete.html#supportedCiphers)().

Qt 5 reference:

### [QSslCertificate](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsslcertificate.html) QSslConfiguration::peerCertificate() const

Returns the peer's digital certificate (i.e., the immediate certificate of the host you
are connected to), or a null certificate, if the peer has not assigned a certificate.

The peer certificate is checked automatically during the handshake phase, so this
function is normally used to fetch the certificate for display or for connection
diagnostic purposes. It contains information about the peer, including its host name,
the certificate issuer, and the peer's public key.

Because the peer certificate is set during the handshake phase, it is safe to access the
peer certificate from a slot connected to the QSslSocket::sslErrors() signal,
[QNetworkReply::sslErrors](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qnetworkreply.html#sslErrors)()
signal, or the
[QSslSocket::encrypted](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsslsocket.html#encrypted)()
signal.

If a null certificate is returned, it can mean the SSL handshake failed, or it can mean
the host you are connected to doesn't have a certificate, or it can mean there is no
connection.

If you want to check the peer's complete chain of certificates, use
[peerCertificateChain](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsslconfiguration.html#peerCertificateChain)()
to get them all at once.

**See also**
[peerCertificateChain](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsslconfiguration.html#peerCertificateChain)(),
[QSslSocket::sslErrors](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsslsocket-obsolete.html#sslErrors)(),
[QSslSocket::ignoreSslErrors](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsslsocket.html#ignoreSslErrors)(),
[QNetworkReply::sslErrors](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qnetworkreply.html#sslErrors)(),
and
[QNetworkReply::ignoreSslErrors](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qnetworkreply.html#ignoreSslErrors)().

### void QSslConfiguration::setPeerVerifyDepth(int *depth*)

Sets the maximum number of certificates in the peer's certificate chain to be checked
during the SSL handshake phase, to *depth*. Setting a depth of 0 means that no maximum
depth is set, indicating that the whole certificate chain should be checked.

The certificates are checked in issuing order, starting with the peer's own certificate,
then its issuer's certificate, and so on.

## Detailed Description

The class QSslEllipticCurve represents an elliptic curve for use by elliptic-curve
cipher algorithms.

Elliptic curves can be constructed from a "short name" (SN)
([fromShortName](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsslellipticcurve.html#fromShortName)()),
and by a call to
[QSslConfiguration::supportedEllipticCurves](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsslconfiguration.html#supportedEllipticCurves)().

QSslEllipticCurve instances can be compared for equality and can be used as keys in
[QHash](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qhash-proxy.html) and
[QSet](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qset.html). They cannot be used as key in a
[QMap](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmap.html).

**Note:** This class is currently only supported in OpenSSL.

## Detailed Description

The QSslPreSharedKeyAuthenticator class is used by an SSL socket to provide the required
authentication data in a pre shared key (PSK) ciphersuite.

In a PSK handshake, the client must derive a key, which must match the key set on the
server. The exact algorithm of deriving the key depends on the application; however, for
this purpose, the server may send an *identity hint* to the client. This hint, combined
with other information (for instance a passphrase), is then used by the client to
construct the shared key.

The QSslPreSharedKeyAuthenticator provides means to client applications for completing
the PSK handshake. The client application needs to connect a slot to the
[QSslSocket::preSharedKeyAuthenticationRequired](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsslsocket.html#preSharedKeyAuthenticationRequired)()
signal:

```
    connect(socket, &QSslSocket::preSharedKeyAuthenticationRequired,
            this, &AuthManager::handlePreSharedKeyAuthentication);
```

The signal carries a QSslPreSharedKeyAuthenticator object containing the identity hint
the server sent to the client, and which must be filled with the corresponding client
identity and the derived key:

```
    void AuthManager::handlePreSharedKeyAuthentication(QSslPreSharedKeyAuthenticator *authenticator)
    {
        authenticator->setIdentity("My Qt App");

        const QByteArray key = deriveKey(authenticator->identityHint(), passphrase);
        authenticator->setPreSharedKey(key);
    }
```

**Note:** PSK ciphersuites are supported only when using OpenSSL 1.0.1 (or greater) as
the SSL backend.

**Note:** PSK is currently only supported in OpenSSL.
