PythonQt.Qt.QTableWidget.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

![](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/images/windows-tableview.png)

Table widgets provide standard table display facilities for applications. The items in a
QTableWidget are provided by
[QTableWidgetItem](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtablewidgetitem.html).

If you want a table that uses your own data model you should use
[QTableView](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtableview.html) rather than this class.

Table widgets can be constructed with the required numbers of rows and columns:

```
    tableWidget = new QTableWidget(12, 3, this);
```

Alternatively, tables can be constructed without a given size and resized later:

```
    tableWidget = new QTableWidget(this);
    tableWidget->setRowCount(10);
    tableWidget->setColumnCount(5);
```

Items are created outside the table (with no parent widget) and inserted into the table
with [setItem](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtablewidget.html#setItem)():

```
    QTableWidgetItem *newItem = new QTableWidgetItem(tr("%1").arg(
        (row+1)*(column+1)));
    tableWidget->setItem(row, column, newItem);
```

If you want to enable sorting in your table widget, do so after you have populated it
with items, otherwise sorting may interfere with the insertion order (see
[setItem](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtablewidget.html#setItem)() for details).

Tables can be given both horizontal and vertical headers. The simplest way to create the
headers is to supply a list of strings to the
[setHorizontalHeaderLabels](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtablewidget.html#setHorizontalHeaderLabels)()
and
[setVerticalHeaderLabels](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtablewidget.html#setVerticalHeaderLabels)()
functions. These will provide simple textual headers for the table's columns and rows.
More sophisticated headers can be created from existing table items that are usually
constructed outside the table. For example, we can construct a table item with an icon
and aligned text, and use it as the header for a particular column:

```
    QTableWidgetItem *cubesHeaderItem = new QTableWidgetItem(tr("Cubes"));
    cubesHeaderItem->setIcon(QIcon(QPixmap(":/Images/cubed.png")));
    cubesHeaderItem->setTextAlignment(Qt::AlignVCenter);
```

The number of rows in the table can be found with
[rowCount](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtablewidget.html#rowCount)(), and the
number of columns with
[columnCount](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtablewidget.html#columnCount)(). The
table can be cleared with the
[clear](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtablewidget.html#clear)() function.

### void QTableWidget::setItem(int *row*, int *column*, [QTableWidgetItem](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtablewidgetitem.html) \**item*)

Sets the item for the given *row* and *column* to *item*.

The table takes ownership of the item.

Note that if sorting is enabled (see
[sortingEnabled](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtableview.html#sortingEnabled-prop))
and *column* is the current sort column, the *row* will be moved to the sorted position
determined by *item*.

If you want to set several items of a particular row (say, by calling setItem() in a
loop), you may want to turn off sorting before doing so, and turn it back on afterwards;
this will allow you to use the same *row* argument for all items in the same row (i.e.
setItem() will not move the row).

**See also** [item](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtablewidget.html#item)() and
[takeItem](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtablewidget.html#takeItem)().

PythonQt.Qt.QTableWidgetItem.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

Table items are used to hold pieces of information for table widgets. Items usually
contain text, icons, or checkboxes

The QTableWidgetItem class is a convenience class that replaces the `QTableItem` class
in Qt 3\. It provides an item for use with the
[QTableWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtablewidget.html) class.

Top-level items are constructed without a parent then inserted at the position specified
by a pair of row and column numbers:

```
    QTableWidgetItem *newItem = new QTableWidgetItem(tr("%1").arg(
        pow(row, column+1)));
    tableWidget->setItem(row, column, newItem);
```

Each item can have its own background brush which is set with the
[setBackground](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtablewidgetitem.html#setBackground)()
function. The current background brush can be found with
[background](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtablewidgetitem.html#background)(). The
text label for each item can be rendered with its own font and brush. These are
specified with the
[setFont](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtablewidgetitem.html#setFont)() and
[setForeground](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtablewidgetitem.html#setForeground)()
functions, and read with
[font](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtablewidgetitem.html#font)() and
[foreground](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtablewidgetitem.html#foreground)().

By default, items are enabled, editable, selectable, checkable, and can be used both as
the source of a drag and drop operation and as a drop target. Each item's flags can be
changed by calling
[setFlags](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtablewidgetitem.html#setFlags)() with the
appropriate value (see
[Qt::ItemFlags](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#ItemFlag-enum)). Checkable
items can be checked and unchecked with the
[setCheckState](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtablewidgetitem.html#setCheckState)()
function. The corresponding
[checkState](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtablewidgetitem.html#checkState)()
function indicates whether the item is currently checked.

### Subclassing

When subclassing QTableWidgetItem to provide custom items, it is possible to define new
types for them so that they can be distinguished from standard items. The constructors
for subclasses that require this feature need to call the base class constructor with a
new type value equal to or greater than
[UserType](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtablewidgetitem.html#ItemType-enum).

## Detailed Description

The QTableWidgetSelectionRange class stores the top left and bottom right rows and
columns of a selection range in a table. The selections in the table may consist of
several selection ranges.

**Note:** If the item within the selection range is marked as not selectable, e.g.,
`itemFlags() & Qt::ItemIsSelectable == 0` then it will not appear in the selection
range.

## Detailed Description

*Tablet events* are generated from tablet peripherals such as Wacom tablets and various
other brands, and electromagnetic stylus devices included with some types of tablet
computers. (It is not the same as
[QTouchEvent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtouchevent.html) which a touchscreen
generates, even when a passive stylus is used on a touchscreen.)

Tablet events are similar to mouse events; for example, the
[x](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtabletevent.html#x)(),
[y](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtabletevent.html#y)(),
[pos](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtabletevent.html#pos)(),
[globalX](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtabletevent.html#globalX)(),
[globalY](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtabletevent.html#globalY)(), and
[globalPos](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtabletevent.html#globalPos)() accessors
provide the cursor position, and you can see which
[buttons](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtabletevent.html#buttons)() are pressed
(pressing the stylus tip against the tablet surface is equivalent to a left mouse
button). But tablet events also pass through some extra information that the tablet
device driver provides; for example, you might want to do subpixel rendering with higher
resolution coordinates
([globalPosF](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtabletevent.html#globalPosF)()),
adjust color brightness based on the
[pressure](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtabletevent.html#pressure)() of the tool
against the tablet surface, use different brushes depending on the type of tool in use
([deviceType](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtabletevent.html#deviceType)()),
modulate the brush shape in some way according to the X-axis and Y-axis tilt of the tool
with respect to the tablet surface
([xTilt](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtabletevent.html#xTilt)() and
[yTilt](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtabletevent.html#yTilt)()), and use a
virtual eraser instead of a brush if the user switches to the other end of a
double-ended stylus
([pointerType](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtabletevent.html#pointerType)()).

Every event contains an accept flag that indicates whether the receiver wants the event.
You should call
[QTabletEvent::accept](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qevent.html#accept)() if you
handle the tablet event; otherwise it will be sent to the parent widget. The exception
are [TabletEnterProximity](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qevent.html#Type-enum) and
[TabletLeaveProximity](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qevent.html#Type-enum) events:
these are only sent to
[QApplication](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qapplication.html) and do not check
whether or not they are accepted.

The
[QWidget::setEnabled](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#enabled-prop)()
function can be used to enable or disable mouse, tablet and keyboard events for a
widget.

The event handler
[QWidget::tabletEvent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#tabletEvent)()
receives [TabletPress](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qevent.html#Type-enum),
[TabletRelease](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qevent.html#Type-enum) and
[TabletMove](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qevent.html#Type-enum) events. Qt will
first send a tablet event, then if it is not accepted by any widget, it will send a
mouse event. This allows users of applications that are not designed for tablets to use
a tablet like a mouse. However high-resolution drawing applications should handle the
tablet events, because they can occur at a higher frequency, which is a benefit for
smooth and accurate drawing. If the tablet events are rejected, the synthetic mouse
events may be compressed for efficiency.

New in Qt 5.4: QTabletEvent includes all information available from the device,
including
[QTabletEvent::buttons](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtabletevent.html#buttons)().
Previously it was not possible to accept all tablet events and also know which stylus
buttons were pressed.

Note that pressing the stylus button while the stylus hovers over the tablet will
generate a button press on some types of tablets, while on other types it will be
necessary to press the stylus against the tablet surface in order to register the
simultaneous stylus button press.

### Notes for X11 Users

If the tablet is configured in xorg.conf to use the Wacom driver, there will be separate
XInput "devices" for the stylus, eraser, and (optionally) cursor and touchpad. Qt
recognizes these by their names. Otherwise, if the tablet is configured to use the evdev
driver, there will be only one device and applications may not be able to distinguish
the stylus from the eraser.

### Notes for Windows Users

Tablet support currently requires the WACOM windows driver providing the DLL
`wintab32.dll` to be installed. It is contained in older packages, for example
`pentablet_5.3.5-3.exe`.

### [qreal](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtglobal.html#qreal-typedef) QTabletEvent::rotation() const

Returns the rotation of the current tool in degrees, where zero means the tip of the
stylus is pointing towards the top of the tablet, a positive value means it's turned to
the right, and a negative value means it's turned to the left. This can be given by a 4D
Mouse or a rotation-capable stylus (such as the Wacom Art Pen or the Apple Pencil). If
the device does not support rotation, this value is always 0.0.

PythonQt.Qt.QTabletEvent.tangentialPress.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

### [qreal](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtglobal.html#qreal-typedef) QTabletEvent::tangentialPressure() const

Returns the tangential pressure for the device. This is typically given by a finger
wheel on an airbrush tool. The range is from -1.0 to 1.0. 0.0 indicates a neutral
position. Current airbrushes can only move in the positive direction from the neutrual
position. If the device does not support tangential pressure, this value is always 0.0.

**See also**
[pressure](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtabletevent.html#pressure)().

PythonQt.Qt.QTabletEvent.uniqueId.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

### [qint64](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtglobal.html#qint64-typedef) QTabletEvent::uniqueId() const

Returns a unique ID for the current device, making it possible to differentiate between
multiple devices being used at the same time on the tablet.

Support of this feature is dependent on the tablet.

Values for the same device may vary from OS to OS.

Later versions of the Wacom driver for Linux will now report the ID information. If you
have a tablet that supports unique ID and are not getting the information on Linux,
consider upgrading your driver.

As of Qt 4.2, the unique ID is the same regardless of the orientation of the pen.
Earlier versions would report a different value when using the eraser-end versus the
pen-end of the stylus on some OS's.

**See also**
[pointerType](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtabletevent.html#pointerType)().

PythonQt.Qt.QTcpServer.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

This class makes it possible to accept incoming TCP connections. You can specify the
port or have QTcpServer pick one automatically. You can listen on a specific address or
on all the machine's addresses.

Call [listen](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtcpserver.html#listen)() to have the
server listen for incoming connections. The
[newConnection](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtcpserver.html#newConnection)()
signal is then emitted each time a client connects to the server.

Call
[nextPendingConnection](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtcpserver.html#nextPendingConnection)()
to accept the pending connection as a connected
[QTcpSocket](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtcpsocket.html). The function returns a
pointer to a [QTcpSocket](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtcpsocket.html) in
[QAbstractSocket::ConnectedState](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#SocketState-enum)
that you can use for communicating with the client.

If an error occurs,
[serverError](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtcpserver.html#serverError)() returns
the type of error, and
[errorString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtcpserver.html#errorString)() can be
called to get a human readable description of what happened.

When listening for connections, the address and port on which the server is listening
are available as
[serverAddress](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtcpserver.html#serverAddress)() and
[serverPort](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtcpserver.html#serverPort)().

Calling [close](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtcpserver.html#close)() makes
QTcpServer stop listening for incoming connections.

Although QTcpServer is mostly designed for use with an event loop, it's possible to use
it without one. In that case, you must use
[waitForNewConnection](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtcpserver.html#waitForNewConnection)(),
which blocks until either a connection is available or a timeout expires.

PythonQt.Qt.QTcpServer.incomingConnectio.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

### `[virtual protected]` void QTcpServer::incomingConnection([qintptr](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtglobal.html#qintptr-typedef) *socketDescriptor*)

This virtual function is called by
[QTcpServer](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtcpserver.html) when a new connection
is available. The *socketDescriptor* argument is the native socket descriptor for the
accepted connection.

The base implementation creates a
[QTcpSocket](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtcpsocket.html), sets the socket
descriptor and then stores the
[QTcpSocket](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtcpsocket.html) in an internal list of
pending connections. Finally
[newConnection](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtcpserver.html#newConnection)() is
emitted.

Reimplement this function to alter the server's behavior when a connection is available.

If this server is using
[QNetworkProxy](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qnetworkproxy.html) then the
*socketDescriptor* may not be usable with native socket functions, and should only be
used with
[QTcpSocket::setSocketDescriptor](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#setSocketDescriptor)().

**Note:** If another socket is created in the reimplementation of this method, it needs
to be added to the Pending Connections mechanism by calling
[addPendingConnection](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtcpserver.html#addPendingConnection)().

**Note:** If you want to handle an incoming connection as a new
[QTcpSocket](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtcpsocket.html) object in another
thread you have to pass the
[socketDescriptor](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtcpserver.html#socketDescriptor)
to the other thread and create the
[QTcpSocket](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtcpsocket.html) object there and use
its
[setSocketDescriptor](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtcpserver.html#setSocketDescriptor)()
method.

**See also**
[newConnection](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtcpserver.html#newConnection)(),
[nextPendingConnection](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtcpserver.html#nextPendingConnection)(),
and
[addPendingConnection](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtcpserver.html#addPendingConnection)().

PythonQt.Qt.QTcpServer.listen.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

### bool QTcpServer::listen(const [QHostAddress](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qhostaddress.html) \&*address* \= QHostAddress::Any, [quint16](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtglobal.html#quint16-typedef) *port* \= 0\)

Tells the server to listen for incoming connections on address *address* and port
*port*. If *port* is 0, a port is chosen automatically. If *address* is
[QHostAddress::Any](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qhostaddress.html#SpecialAddress-enum),
the server will listen on all network interfaces.

Returns `true` on success; otherwise returns `false`.

**See also**

### bool QTcpServer::waitForNewConnection(int *msec* \= 0, bool \**timedOut* \= nullptr)

Waits for at most *msec* milliseconds or until an incoming connection is available.
Returns `true` if a connection is available; otherwise returns `false`. If the operation
timed out and *timedOut* is not `nullptr`, \**timedOut* will be set to true.

This is a blocking function call. Its use is disadvised in a single-threaded GUI
application, since the whole application will stop responding until the function
returns. waitForNewConnection() is mostly useful when there is no event loop available.

The non-blocking alternative is to connect to the
[newConnection](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtcpserver.html#newConnection)()
signal.

If msec is -1, this function will not time out.

**See also**
[hasPendingConnections](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtcpserver.html#hasPendingConnections)()
and
[nextPendingConnection](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtcpserver.html#nextPendingConnection)().

## Detailed Description

TCP (Transmission Control Protocol) is a reliable, stream-oriented, connection-oriented
transport protocol. It is especially well suited for continuous transmission of data.

QTcpSocket is a convenience subclass of
[QAbstractSocket](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html) that allows
you to establish a TCP connection and transfer streams of data. See the
[QAbstractSocket](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html) documentation
for details.

**Note:** TCP sockets cannot be opened in
[QIODevice::Unbuffered](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qiodevice.html#OpenModeFlag-enum)
mode.

## Detailed Description

QTemporaryDir is used to create unique temporary directories safely. The directory
itself is created by the constructor. The name of the temporary directory is guaranteed
to be unique (i.e., you are guaranteed to not overwrite an existing directory), and the
directory will subsequently be removed upon destruction of the QTemporaryDir object. The
directory name is either auto-generated, or created based on a template, which is passed
to QTemporaryDir's constructor.

Example:

```
    // Within a function/method...

    QTemporaryDir dir;
    if (dir.isValid()) {
        // dir.path() returns the unique directory path
    }

    // The QTemporaryDir destructor removes the temporary directory
    // as it goes out of scope.
```

It is very important to test that the temporary directory could be created, using
[isValid](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtemporarydir.html#isValid)(). Do not use
[exists()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdir.html#exists-1), since a
default-constructed [QDir](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdir.html) represents the
current directory, which exists.

The path to the temporary directory can be found by calling
[path](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtemporarydir.html#path)().

A temporary directory will have some static part of the name and some part that is
calculated to be unique. The default path will be determined from
[QCoreApplication::applicationName](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcoreapplication.html#applicationName-prop)()
(otherwise `qt_temp`) and will be placed into the temporary path as returned by
[QDir::tempPath](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdir.html#tempPath)(). If you
specify your own path, a relative path will not be placed in the temporary directory by
default, but be relative to the current working directory. In all cases, a random string
will be appended to the path in order to make it unique.

## Detailed Description

QTemporaryFile is used to create unique temporary files safely. The file itself is
created by calling
[open](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtemporaryfile.html#open)(). The name of the
temporary file is guaranteed to be unique (i.e., you are guaranteed to not overwrite an
existing file), and the file will subsequently be removed upon destruction of the
QTemporaryFile object. This is an important technique that avoids data corruption for
applications that store data in temporary files. The file name is either auto-generated,
or created based on a template, which is passed to QTemporaryFile's constructor.

Example:

```
    // Within a function/method...

    QTemporaryFile file;
    if (file.open()) {
        // file.fileName() returns the unique file name
    }

    // The QTemporaryFile destructor removes the temporary file
    // as it goes out of scope.
```

Reopening a QTemporaryFile after calling
[close](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledevice.html#close)() is safe. For as
long as the QTemporaryFile object itself is not destroyed, the unique temporary file
will exist and be kept open internally by QTemporaryFile.

The file name of the temporary file can be found by calling
[fileName](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtemporaryfile.html#fileName)(). Note that
this is only defined after the file is first opened; the function returns an empty
string before this.

A temporary file will have some static part of the name and some part that is calculated
to be unique. The default filename will be determined from
[QCoreApplication::applicationName](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcoreapplication.html#applicationName-prop)()
(otherwise `qt_temp`) and will be placed into the temporary path as returned by
[QDir::tempPath](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdir.html#tempPath)(). If you
specify your own filename, a relative file path will not be placed in the temporary
directory by default, but be relative to the current working directory. It is important
to specify the correct directory if the
[rename](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtemporaryfile.html#rename)() function will
be called, as QTemporaryFile can only rename files within the same volume / filesystem
as the temporary file itself was created on.

Specified filenames can contain the following template `XXXXXX` (six upper case "X"
characters), which will be replaced by the auto-generated portion of the filename. Note
that the template is case sensitive. If the template is not present in the filename,
QTemporaryFile appends the generated part to the filename given. Only the last
occurrence of `"XXXXXX"` will be considered.

**Note:** On Linux, QTemporaryFile will attempt to create unnamed temporary files. If
that succeeds, [open](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtemporaryfile.html#open)()
will return true but exists() will be false. If you call
[fileName](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtemporaryfile.html#fileName)() or any
function that calls it, QTemporaryFile will give the file a name, so most applications
will not see a difference.

### `[static]` [QTemporaryFile](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtemporaryfile.html#QTemporaryFile) \*QTemporaryFile::createNativeFile(QFile \&*file*)

### bool QTemporaryFile::rename(const [QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html) \&*newName*)

Renames the current temporary file to *newName* and returns true if it succeeded.

This function has an important difference compared to QFile::rename(): it will not
perform a copy\+delete if the low-level system call to rename the file fails, something
that could happen if *newName* specifies a file in a different volume or filesystem than
the temporary file was created on. In other words,
[QTemporaryFile](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtemporaryfile.html) only supports
atomic file renaming.

This functionality is intended to support materializing the destination file with all
contents already present, so another process cannot see an incomplete file in the
process of being written. The
[QSaveFile](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsavefile.html) class can be used for a
similar purpose too, particularly if the destination file is not temporary.

**See also** [QSaveFile](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsavefile.html),
[QSaveFile::commit](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsavefile.html#commit)(), and
QFile::rename().

### void QTemporaryFile::setAutoRemove(bool *b*)

Sets the [QTemporaryFile](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtemporaryfile.html) into
auto-remove mode if *b* is `true`.

Auto-remove is on by default.

If you set this property to `false`, ensure the application provides a way to remove the
file once it is no longer needed, including passing the responsibility on to another
process. Always use the
[fileName](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtemporaryfile.html#fileName)() function
to obtain the name and never try to guess the name that
[QTemporaryFile](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtemporaryfile.html) has generated.

On some systems, if
[fileName](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtemporaryfile.html#fileName)() is not
called before closing the file, the temporary file may be removed regardless of the
state of this property. This behavior should not be relied upon, so application code
should either call
[fileName](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtemporaryfile.html#fileName)() or leave
the auto removal functionality enabled.

**See also**
[autoRemove](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtemporaryfile.html#autoRemove)() and

## Detailed Description

A text block encapsulates a block or paragraph of text in a
[QTextDocument](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html). QTextBlock
provides read-only access to the block/paragraph structure of QTextDocuments. It is
mainly of use if you want to implement your own layouts for the visual representation of
a [QTextDocument](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html), or if you want
to iterate over a document and write out the contents in your own custom format.

Text blocks are created by their parent documents. If you need to create a new text
block, or modify the contents of a document while examining its contents, use the
cursor-based interface provided by
[QTextCursor](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcursor.html) instead.

Each text block is located at a specific
[position](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextblock.html#position)() in a
[document](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextblock.html#document)(). The contents
of the block can be obtained by using the
[text](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextblock.html#text)() function. The
[length](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextblock.html#length)() function
determines the block's size within the document (including formatting characters). The
visual properties of the block are determined by its text
[layout](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextblock.html#layout)(), its
[charFormat](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextblock.html#charFormat)(), and its
[blockFormat](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextblock.html#blockFormat)().

The [next](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextblock.html#next)() and
[previous](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextblock.html#previous)() functions
enable iteration over consecutive valid blocks in a document under the condition that
the document is not modified by other means during the iteration process. Note that,
although blocks are returned in sequence, adjacent blocks may come from different places
in the document structure. The validity of a block can be determined by calling
[isValid](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextblock.html#isValid)().

QTextBlock provides comparison operators to make it easier to work with blocks:
[operator\=\=](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextblock.html#operator-eq-eq)()
compares two block for equality,
[operator!\=](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextblock.html#operator-not-eq)()
compares two blocks for inequality, and
[operator\<](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextblock.html#operator-lt)()
determines whether a block precedes another in the same document.

Qt 5 reference:

### void QTextBlock::setUserData([QTextBlockUserData](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextblockuserdata.html) \**data*)

Attaches the given *data* object to the text block.

[QTextBlockUserData](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextblockuserdata.html) can be
used to store custom settings. The ownership is passed to the underlying text document,
i.e. the provided
[QTextBlockUserData](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextblockuserdata.html) object
will be deleted if the corresponding text block gets deleted. The user data object is
not stored in the undo history, so it will not be available after undoing the deletion
of a text block.

For example, if you write a programming editor in an IDE, you may want to let your user
set breakpoints visually in your code for an integrated debugger. In a programming
editor a line of text usually corresponds to one
[QTextBlock](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextblock.html). The
[QTextBlockUserData](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextblockuserdata.html)
interface allows the developer to store data for each
[QTextBlock](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextblock.html), like for example in
which lines of the source code the user has a breakpoint set. Of course this could also
be stored externally, but by storing it inside the
[QTextDocument](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html), it will for
example be automatically deleted when the user deletes the associated line. It's really
just a way to store custom information in the
[QTextDocument](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html) without using
custom properties in [QTextFormat](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextformat.html)
which would affect the undo/redo stack.

This function was introduced in Qt 4.1.

**See also** [userData](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextblock.html#userData)().

PythonQt.Qt.QTextBlockFormat.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

A document is composed of a list of blocks, represented by
[QTextBlock](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextblock.html) objects. Each block can
contain an item of some kind, such as a paragraph of text, a table, a list, or an image.
Every block has an associated QTextBlockFormat that specifies its characteristics.

To cater for left-to-right and right-to-left languages you can set a block's direction
with
[setLayoutDirection](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextformat.html#setLayoutDirection)().
Paragraph alignment is set with
[setAlignment](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextblockformat.html#setAlignment)().
Margins are controlled by
[setTopMargin](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextblockformat.html#setTopMargin)(),
[setBottomMargin](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextblockformat.html#setBottomMargin)(),
[setLeftMargin](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextblockformat.html#setLeftMargin)(),
[setRightMargin](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextblockformat.html#setRightMargin)().
Overall indentation is set with
[setIndent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextblockformat.html#setIndent)(), the
indentation of the first line with
[setTextIndent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextblockformat.html#setTextIndent)().

Line spacing is set with
[setLineHeight](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextblockformat.html#setLineHeight)()
and retrieved via
[lineHeight](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextblockformat.html#lineHeight-1)()
and
[lineHeightType](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextblockformat.html#lineHeightType)().
The types of line spacing available are in the
[LineHeightTypes](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextblockformat.html#LineHeightTypes-enum)
enum.

Line breaking can be enabled and disabled with
[setNonBreakableLines](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextblockformat.html#setNonBreakableLines)().

The brush used to paint the paragraph's background is set with
[setBackground()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextformat.html#setBackground),
and other aspects of the text's appearance can be customized by using the
[setProperty()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextformat.html#setProperty)
function with the `OutlinePen`, `ForegroundBrush`, and `BackgroundBrush`
[QTextFormat::Property](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextformat.html#Property-enum)
values.

If a text block is part of a list, it can also have a list format that is accessible
with the listFormat() function.

PythonQt.Qt.QTextBlockFormat.lineHeight.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

### [qreal](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtglobal.html#qreal-typedef) QTextBlockFormat::lineHeight([qreal](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtglobal.html#qreal-typedef) *scriptLineHeight*, [qreal](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtglobal.html#qreal-typedef) *scaling* \= 1.0) const

Returns the height of the lines in the paragraph based on the height of the script line
given by *scriptLineHeight* and the specified *scaling* factor.

The value that is returned is also dependent on the given
[LineHeightType](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextformat.html#Property-enum) of
the paragraph as well as the
[LineHeight](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextformat.html#Property-enum) setting
that has been set for the paragraph.

The scaling is needed for heights that include a fixed number of pixels, to scale them
appropriately for printing.

This function was introduced in Qt 4.8.

**See also**
[LineHeightTypes](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextblockformat.html#LineHeightTypes-enum),
[setLineHeight](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextblockformat.html#setLineHeight)(),
and
[lineHeightType](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextblockformat.html#lineHeightType)().

## Detailed Description

Block groups can be used to organize blocks of text within a document. They maintain an
up-to-date list of the text blocks that belong to them, even when text blocks are being
edited.

Each group has a parent document which is specified when the group is constructed.

Text blocks can be inserted into a group with
[blockInserted](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextblockgroup.html#blockInserted)(),
and removed with
[blockRemoved](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextblockgroup.html#blockRemoved)().
If a block's format is changed,
[blockFormatChanged](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextblockgroup.html#blockFormatChanged)()
is called.

The list of blocks in the group is returned by
[blockList](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextblockgroup.html#blockList)(). Note
that the blocks in the list are not necessarily adjacent elements in the document; for
example, the top-level items in a multi-level list will be separated by the items in
lower levels of the list.

## Detailed Description

QTextBlockUserData provides an abstract interface for container classes that are used to
associate application-specific user data with text blocks in a
[QTextDocument](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html).

Generally, subclasses of this class provide functions to allow data to be stored and
retrieved, and instances are attached to blocks of text using
[QTextBlock::setUserData](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextblock.html#setUserData)().
This makes it possible to store additional data per text block in a way that can be
retrieved safely by the application.

Each subclass should provide a reimplementation of the destructor to ensure that any
private data is automatically cleaned up when user data objects are deleted.

## Detailed Description

QTextBoundaryFinder allows to find Unicode text boundaries in a string, accordingly to
the Unicode text boundary specification (see [Unicode Standard Annex
#14](https://www.unicode.org/reports/tr14/) and [Unicode Standard Annex
#29](https://www.unicode.org/reports/tr29/)).

QTextBoundaryFinder can operate on a
[QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html) in four possible modes
depending on the value of *BoundaryType*.

Units of Unicode characters that make up what the user thinks of as a character or basic
unit of the language are here called Grapheme clusters. The two unicode characters 'A'
\+ diaeresis do for example form one grapheme cluster as the user thinks of them as one
character, yet it is in this case represented by two unicode code points (see
<https://www.unicode.org/reports/tr29/#Grapheme_Cluster_Boundaries>).

Word boundaries are there to locate the start and end of what a language considers to be
a word (see <https://www.unicode.org/reports/tr29/#Word_Boundaries>).

Line break boundaries give possible places where a line break might happen and sentence
boundaries will show the beginning and end of whole sentences (see
<https://www.unicode.org/reports/tr29/#Sentence_Boundaries> and
<https://www.unicode.org/reports/tr14/>).

The first position in a string is always a valid boundary and refers to the position
before the first character. The last position at the length of the string is also valid
and refers to the position after the last character.

Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

This class extends [QTextEdit](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html) (in
read-only mode), adding some navigation functionality so that users can follow links in
hypertext documents.

If you want to provide your users with an editable rich text editor, use
[QTextEdit](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html). If you want a text
browser without hypertext navigation use
[QTextEdit](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html), and use
[QTextEdit::setReadOnly](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html#readOnly-prop)()
to disable editing. If you just need to display a small piece of rich text use
[QLabel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qlabel.html).

### Document Source and Contents

The contents of [QTextEdit](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html) are set
with [setHtml](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html#html-prop)() or
[setPlainText](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html#setPlainText)(), but
QTextBrowser also implements the
[setSource](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextbrowser.html#source-prop)()
function, making it possible to use a named document as the source text. The name is
looked up in a list of search paths and in the directory of the current document
factory.

If a document name ends with an anchor (for example, "`#anchor"`), the text browser
automatically scrolls to that position (using
[scrollToAnchor](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html#scrollToAnchor)()).
When the user clicks on a hyperlink, the browser will call
[setSource](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextbrowser.html#source-prop)() itself
with the link's `href` value as argument. You can track the current source by connecting
to the
[sourceChanged](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextbrowser.html#sourceChanged)()
signal.

### Navigation

QTextBrowser provides
[backward](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextbrowser.html#backward)() and
[forward](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextbrowser.html#forward)() slots which
you can use to implement Back and Forward buttons. The
[home](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextbrowser.html#home)() slot sets the text
to the very first document displayed. The
[anchorClicked](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextbrowser.html#anchorClicked)()
signal is emitted when the user clicks an anchor. To override the default navigation
behavior of the browser, call the
[setSource](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextbrowser.html#source-prop)() function
to supply new document text in a slot connected to this signal.

If you want to load documents stored in the Qt resource system use `qrc` as the scheme
in the URL to load. For example, for the document resource path `:/docs/index.html` use
`qrc:/docs/index.html` as the URL with
[setSource](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextbrowser.html#source-prop)().

PythonQt.Qt.QTextBrowser.loadResource.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

### `[override virtual]` [QVariant](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qvariant.html) QTextBrowser::loadResource(int *type*, const [QUrl](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qurl.html) \&*name*)

Reimplements:
[QTextEdit::loadResource](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html#loadResource)(int
type, const QUrl \&name).

This function is called when the document is loaded and for each image in the document.
The *type* indicates the type of resource to be loaded. An invalid
[QVariant](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qvariant.html) is returned if the resource
cannot be loaded.

The default implementation ignores *type* and tries to locate the resources by
interpreting *name* as a file name. If it is not an absolute path it tries to find the
file in the paths of the
[searchPaths](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextbrowser.html#searchPaths-prop)
property and in the same directory as the current source. On success, the result is a
[QVariant](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qvariant.html) that stores a
[QByteArray](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qbytearray.html) with the contents of
the file.

If you reimplement this function, you can return other
[QVariant](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qvariant.html) types. The table below
shows which variant types are supported depending on the resource type:

| ResourceType | QVariant::Type |
| --- | --- |
| [QTextDocument::HtmlResource](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html#ResourceType-enum) | [QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html) or [QByteArray](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qbytearray.html) |
| [QTextDocument::ImageResource](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html#ResourceType-enum) | [QImage](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qimage.html), [QPixmap](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpixmap.html) or [QByteArray](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qbytearray.html) |
| [QTextDocument::StyleSheetResource](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html#ResourceType-enum) | [QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html) or [QByteArray](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qbytearray.html) |
| [QTextDocument::MarkdownResource](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html#ResourceType-enum) | [QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html) or [QByteArray](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qbytearray.html) |
signatures: loadResource(self, type: int, name: PySide2.QtCore.QUrl) -> typing.Any

### `[slot]` void QTextBrowser::setSource(const [QUrl](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qurl.html) \&*url*, [QTextDocument::ResourceType](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html#ResourceType-enum) *type*)

Attempts to load the document at the given *url* with the specified *type*.

If *type* is
[UnknownResource](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html#ResourceType-enum)
(the default), the document type will be detected: that is, if the url ends with an
extension of `.md`, `.mkd` or `.markdown`, the document will be loaded via
[QTextDocument::setMarkdown](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html#setMarkdown)();
otherwise it will be loaded via
[QTextDocument::setHtml](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html#setHtml)().
This detection can be bypassed by specifying the *type* explicitly.

**Note:** Setter function for property
[source](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextbrowser.html#source-prop).

Qt 5 reference:

### source : [QUrl](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qurl.html)

This property holds the name of the displayed document.

This is a an invalid url if no document is displayed or if the source is unknown.

When setting this property
[QTextBrowser](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextbrowser.html) tries to find a
document with the specified name in the paths of the
[searchPaths](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextbrowser.html#searchPaths-prop)
property and directory of the current source, unless the value is an absolute file path.
It also checks for optional anchors and scrolls the document accordingly

If the first tag in the document is `<qt type=detail>`, the document is displayed as a
popup rather than as new document in the browser window itself. Otherwise, the document
is displayed normally in the text browser with the text set to the contents of the named
document with
[QTextDocument::setHtml](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html#setHtml)()
or
[QTextDocument::setMarkdown](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html#setMarkdown)(),
depending on whether the filename ends with any of the known Markdown file extensions.

If you would like to avoid automatic type detection and specify the type explicitly,
call setSource() rather than setting this property.

By default, this property contains an empty URL.

**Access functions:**

| --- | --- |

PythonQt.Qt.QTextCharFormat.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

The character format of text in a document specifies the visual properties of the text,
as well as information about its role in a hypertext document.

The font used can be set by supplying a font to the
[setFont](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcharformat.html#setFont)() function,
and each aspect of its appearance can be adjusted to give the desired effect.
[setFontFamily](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcharformat.html#setFontFamily)()
and
[setFontPointSize](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcharformat.html#setFontPointSize)()
define the font's family (e.g. Times) and printed size;
[setFontWeight](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcharformat.html#setFontWeight)()
and
[setFontItalic](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcharformat.html#setFontItalic)()
provide control over the style of the font.
[setFontUnderline](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcharformat.html#setFontUnderline)(),
[setFontOverline](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcharformat.html#setFontOverline)(),
[setFontStrikeOut](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcharformat.html#setFontStrikeOut)(),
and
[setFontFixedPitch](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcharformat.html#setFontFixedPitch)()
provide additional effects for text.

The color is set with
[setForeground](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextformat.html#setForeground)(). If
the text is intended to be used as an anchor (for hyperlinks), this can be enabled with
[setAnchor](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcharformat.html#setAnchor)(). The
[setAnchorHref](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcharformat.html#setAnchorHref)()
and
[setAnchorNames](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcharformat.html#setAnchorNames)()
functions are used to specify the information about the hyperlink's destination and the
anchor's name.

### void QTextCharFormat::setFontStretch(int *factor*)

Sets the stretch factor for the font to *factor*.

The stretch factor changes the width of all characters in the font by factor percent.
For example, setting *factor* to 150 results in all characters in the font being 1.5
times (ie. 150%) wider. The default stretch factor is 100\. The minimum stretch factor
is 1, and the maximum stretch factor is 4000\.

The stretch factor is only applied to outline fonts. The stretch factor is ignored for
bitmap fonts.

This function was introduced in Qt 5.0.

**See also**
[fontStretch](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcharformat.html#fontStretch)().

Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

Qt uses Unicode to store, draw and manipulate strings. In many situations you may wish
to deal with data that uses a different encoding. For example, most Japanese documents
are still stored in Shift-JIS or ISO 2022-JP, while Russian users often have their
documents in KOI8-R or Windows-1251.

Qt provides a set of QTextCodec classes to help with converting non-Unicode formats to
and from Unicode. You can also create your own codec classes.

The supported encodings are:

- [Big5](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/codec-big5.html)
- [Big5-HKSCS](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/codec-big5hkscs.html)
- CP949
- [EUC-JP](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/codec-eucjp.html)
- [EUC-KR](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/codec-euckr.html)
- [GB18030](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/codec-gbk.html)
- HP-ROMAN8
- IBM 850
- IBM 866
- IBM 874
- [ISO 2022-JP](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/codecs-jis.html)
- ISO 8859-1 to 10
- ISO 8859-13 to 16
- Iscii-Bng, Dev, Gjr, Knd, Mlm, Ori, Pnj, Tlg, and Tml
- KOI8-R
- KOI8-U
- Macintosh
- [Shift-JIS](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/codec-sjis.html)
- TIS-620
- [TSCII](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/codec-tscii.html)
- UTF-8
- UTF-16
- UTF-16BE
- UTF-16LE
- UTF-32
- UTF-32BE
- UTF-32LE
- Windows-1250 to 1258

If Qt is compiled with ICU support enabled, most codecs supported by ICU will also be
available to the application.

[QTextCodec](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcodec.html)s can be used as follows
to convert some locally encoded string to Unicode. Suppose you have some string encoded
in Russian KOI8-R encoding, and want to convert it to Unicode. The simple way to do it
is like this:

```
QByteArray encodedString = "...";
QTextCodec *codec = QTextCodec::codecForName("KOI8-R");
QString string = codec->toUnicode(encodedString);
```

After this, `string` holds the text converted to Unicode. Converting a string from
Unicode to the local encoding is just as easy:

```
QString string = "...";
QTextCodec *codec = QTextCodec::codecForName("KOI8-R");
QByteArray encodedString = codec->fromUnicode(string);
```

To read or write files in various encodings, use
[QTextStream](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextstream.html) and its
[setCodec()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextstream.html#setCodec) function. See
the [Codecs](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtwidgets-tools-codecs-example.html)
example for an application of QTextCodec to file I/O.

Some care must be taken when trying to convert the data in chunks, for example, when
receiving it over a network. In such cases it is possible that a multi-byte character
will be split over two chunks. At best this might result in the loss of a character and
at worst cause the entire conversion to fail.

The approach to use in these situations is to create a
[QTextDecoder](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdecoder.html) object for the
codec and use this [QTextDecoder](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdecoder.html)
for the whole decoding process, as shown below:

```
QTextCodec *codec = QTextCodec::codecForName("Shift-JIS");
QTextDecoder *decoder = codec->makeDecoder();

QString string;
while (new_data_available()) {
    QByteArray chunk = get_new_data();
    string += decoder->toUnicode(chunk);
}
delete decoder;
```

The [QTextDecoder](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdecoder.html) object
maintains state between chunks and therefore works correctly even if a multi-byte
character is split between chunks.

### Creating Your Own Codec Class

Support for new text encodings can be added to Qt by creating QTextCodec subclasses.

The pure virtual functions describe the encoder to the system and the coder is used as
required in the different text file formats supported by
[QTextStream](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextstream.html), and under X11, for
the locale-specific character input and output.

To add support for another encoding to Qt, make a subclass of QTextCodec and implement
the functions listed in the table below.

| Function | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [name](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcodec.html#name)() | Returns the official name for the encoding. If the encoding is listed in the [IANA character-sets encoding file](http://www.iana.org/assignments/character-sets/character-sets.xml), the name should be the preferred MIME name for the encoding. |
| [aliases](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcodec.html#aliases)() | Returns a list of alternative names for the encoding. QTextCodec provides a default implementation that returns an empty list. For example, "ISO-8859-1" has "latin1", "CP819", "IBM819", and "iso-ir-100" as aliases. |
| [mibEnum()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcodec.html#mibEnum) | Return the MIB enum for the encoding if it is listed in the [IANA character-sets encoding file](http://www.iana.org/assignments/character-sets/character-sets.xml). |
| [convertToUnicode](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcodec.html#convertToUnicode)() | Converts an 8-bit character string to Unicode. |
| [convertFromUnicode](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcodec.html#convertFromUnicode)() | Converts a Unicode string to an 8-bit character string. |

## Detailed Description

Text cursors are objects that are used to access and modify the contents and underlying
structure of text documents via a programming interface that mimics the behavior of a
cursor in a text editor. QTextCursor contains information about both the cursor's
position within a [QTextDocument](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html)
and any selection that it has made.

QTextCursor is modeled on the way a text cursor behaves in a text editor, providing a
programmatic means of performing standard actions through the user interface. A document
can be thought of as a single string of characters. The cursor's current
[position](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcursor.html#position)() then is
always either *between* two consecutive characters in the string, or else *before* the
very first character or *after* the very last character in the string. Documents can
also contain tables, lists, images, and other objects in addition to text but, from the
developer's point of view, the document can be treated as one long string. Some portions
of that string can be considered to lie within particular blocks (e.g. paragraphs), or
within a table's cell, or a list's item, or other structural elements. When we refer to
"current character" we mean the character immediately *before* the cursor
[position](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcursor.html#position)() in the
document. Similarly, the "current block" is the block that contains the cursor
[position](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcursor.html#position)().

A QTextCursor also has an
[anchor](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcursor.html#anchor)() position. The
text that is between the
[anchor](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcursor.html#anchor)() and the
[position](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcursor.html#position)() is the
selection. If [anchor](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcursor.html#anchor)()
\=\= [position](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcursor.html#position)() there is
no selection.

The cursor position can be changed programmatically using
[setPosition](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcursor.html#setPosition)() and
[movePosition](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcursor.html#movePosition)(); the
latter can also be used to select text. For selections see
[selectionStart](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcursor.html#selectionStart)(),
[selectionEnd](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcursor.html#selectionEnd)(),
[hasSelection](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcursor.html#hasSelection)(),
[clearSelection](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcursor.html#clearSelection)(),
and
[removeSelectedText](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcursor.html#removeSelectedText)().

If the [position](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcursor.html#position)() is at
the start of a block,
[atBlockStart](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcursor.html#atBlockStart)()
returns `true`; and if it is at the end of a block,
[atBlockEnd](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcursor.html#atBlockEnd)() returns
true. The format of the current character is returned by
[charFormat](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcursor.html#charFormat)(), and the
format of the current block is returned by
[blockFormat](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcursor.html#blockFormat)().

Formatting can be applied to the current text document using the
[setCharFormat](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcursor.html#setCharFormat)(),
[mergeCharFormat](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcursor.html#mergeCharFormat)(),
[setBlockFormat](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcursor.html#setBlockFormat)()
and
[mergeBlockFormat](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcursor.html#mergeBlockFormat)()
functions. The 'set' functions will replace the cursor's current character or block
format, while the 'merge' functions add the given format properties to the cursor's
current format. If the cursor has a selection, the given format is applied to the
current selection. Note that when only a part of a block is selected, the block format
is applied to the entire block. The text at the current character position can be turned
into a list using
[createList](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcursor.html#createList)().

Deletions can be achieved using
[deleteChar](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcursor.html#deleteChar)(),
[deletePreviousChar](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcursor.html#deletePreviousChar)(),
and
[removeSelectedText](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcursor.html#removeSelectedText)().

Text strings can be inserted into the document with the
[insertText](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcursor.html#insertText)() function,
blocks (representing new paragraphs) can be inserted with
[insertBlock](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcursor.html#insertBlock)().

Existing fragments of text can be inserted with
[insertFragment](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcursor.html#insertFragment)()
but, if you want to insert pieces of text in various formats, it is usually still easier
to use [insertText](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcursor.html#insertText)()
and supply a character format.

Various types of higher-level structure can also be inserted into the document with the
cursor:

- Lists are ordered sequences of block elements that are decorated with bullet points or symbols. These are inserted in a specified format with [insertList](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcursor.html#insertList)().
- Tables are inserted with the [insertTable](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcursor.html#insertTable)() function, and can be given an optional format. These contain an array of cells that can be traversed using the cursor.
- Inline images are inserted with [insertImage](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcursor.html#insertImage)(). The image to be used can be specified in an image format, or by name.
- Frames are inserted by calling [insertFrame](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcursor.html#insertFrame)() with a specified format.

Actions can be grouped (i.e. treated as a single action for undo/redo) using
[beginEditBlock](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcursor.html#beginEditBlock)()
and [endEditBlock](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcursor.html#endEditBlock)().

Cursor movements are limited to valid cursor positions. In Latin writing this is between
any two consecutive characters in the text, before the first character, or after the
last character. In some other writing systems cursor movements are limited to "clusters"
(e.g. a syllable in Devanagari, or a base letter plus diacritics). Functions such as
[movePosition](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcursor.html#movePosition)() and
[deleteChar](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcursor.html#deleteChar)() limit
cursor movement to these valid positions.

### int QTextCursor::anchor() const

Returns the anchor position; this is the same as
[position](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcursor.html#position)() unless there
is a selection in which case

### void QTextCursor::insertText(const [QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html) \&*text*)

Inserts *text* at the current position, using the current character format.

If there is a selection, the selection is deleted and replaced by *text*, for example:

```
cursor.clearSelection();
cursor.movePosition(QTextCursor::NextWord, QTextCursor::KeepAnchor);
cursor.insertText("Hello World");
```

This clears any existing selection, selects the word at the cursor (i.e. from
[position](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcursor.html#position)() forward), and
replaces the selection with the phrase "Hello World".

Any ASCII linefeed characters (\\n) in the inserted text are transformed into unicode
block separators, corresponding to
[insertBlock](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcursor.html#insertBlock)() calls.

**See also**
[charFormat](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcursor.html#charFormat)() and
[hasSelection](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcursor.html#hasSelection)().

### bool QTextCursor::movePosition([QTextCursor::MoveOperation](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcursor.html#MoveOperation-enum) *operation*, [QTextCursor::MoveMode](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcursor.html#MoveMode-enum) *mode* \= MoveAnchor, int *n* \= 1\)

Moves the cursor by performing the given *operation* *n* times, using the specified
*mode*, and returns `true` if all operations were completed successfully; otherwise
returns `false`.

For example, if this function is repeatedly used to seek to the end of the next word, it
will eventually fail when the end of the document is reached.

By default, the move operation is performed once (*n* \= 1).

If *mode* is `KeepAnchor`, the cursor selects the text it moves over. This is the same
effect that the user achieves when they hold down the Shift key and move the cursor with
the cursor keys.

**See also**
[setVisualNavigation](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcursor.html#setVisualNavigation)().

[QChar](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qchar.html) objects, i.e. 16-bit Unicode
characters, and the position is considered an index into this string. This does not
necessarily correspond to individual graphemes in the writing system, as a single
grapheme may be represented by multiple Unicode characters, such as in the case of
surrogate pairs, linguistic ligatures or diacritics.

### void QTextCursor::setKeepPositionOnInsert(bool *b*)

Defines whether the cursor should keep its current position when text gets inserted at
the current position of the cursor.

If *b* is true, the cursor keeps its current position when text gets inserted at the
positing of the cursor. If *b* is false, the cursor moves along with the inserted text.

The default is false.

Note that a cursor always moves when text is inserted before the current position of the
cursor, and it always keeps its position when text is inserted after the current
position of the cursor.

This function was introduced in Qt 4.7.

**See also**
[keepPositionOnInsert](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcursor.html#keepPositionOnInsert)().

### void QTextCursor::setVerticalMovementX(int *x*)

Sets the visual x position for vertical cursor movements to *x*.

The vertical movement x position is cleared automatically when the cursor moves
horizontally, and kept unchanged when the cursor moves vertically. The mechanism allows
the cursor to move up and down on a visually straight line with proportional fonts, and
to gently "jump" over short lines.

A value of -1 indicates no predefined x position. It will then be set automatically the
next time the cursor moves up or down.

This function was introduced in Qt 4.7.

[verticalMovementX](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcursor.html#verticalMovementX)().

PythonQt.Qt.QTextDocument.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

QTextDocument is a container for structured rich text documents, providing support for
styled text and various types of document elements, such as lists, tables, frames, and
images. They can be created for use in a
[QTextEdit](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html), or used independently.

Each document element is described by an associated format object. Each format object is
treated as a unique object by QTextDocuments, and can be passed to
[objectForFormat](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html#objectForFormat)()
to obtain the document element that it is applied to.

A QTextDocument can be edited programmatically using a
[QTextCursor](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcursor.html), and its contents can
be examined by traversing the document structure. The entire document structure is
stored as a hierarchy of document elements beneath the root frame, found with the
[rootFrame](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html#rootFrame)() function.
Alternatively, if you just want to iterate over the textual contents of the document you
can use [begin](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html#begin)(),
[end](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html#end)(), and
[findBlock](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html#findBlock)() to
retrieve text blocks that you can examine and iterate over.

The layout of a document is determined by the
[documentLayout](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html#documentLayout)();
you can create your own
[QAbstractTextDocumentLayout](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstracttextdocumentlayout.html)
subclass and set it using
[setDocumentLayout](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html#setDocumentLayout)()
if you want to use your own layout logic. The document's title and other
meta-information can be obtained by calling the
[metaInformation](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html#metaInformation)()
function. For documents that are exposed to users through the
[QTextEdit](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html) class, the document title
is also available via the
[QTextEdit::documentTitle](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html#documentTitle-prop)()
function.

The [toPlainText](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html#toPlainText)()
and [toHtml](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html#toHtml)() convenience
functions allow you to retrieve the contents of the document as plain text and HTML. The
document's text can be searched using the
[find](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html#find)() functions.

Undo/redo of operations performed on the document can be controlled using the
[setUndoRedoEnabled](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html#undoRedoEnabled-prop)()
function. The undo/redo system can be controlled by an editor widget through the
[undo](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html#undo-1)() and
[redo](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html#redo-1)() slots; the
document also provides
[contentsChanged](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html#contentsChanged)(),
[undoAvailable](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html#undoAvailable)(),
and
[redoAvailable](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html#redoAvailable)()
signals that inform connected editor widgets about the state of the undo/redo system.
The following are the undo/redo operations of a QTextDocument:

- Insertion or removal of characters. A sequence of insertions or removals within the same text block are regarded as a single undo/redo operation.
- Insertion or removal of text blocks. Sequences of insertion or removals in a single operation (e.g., by selecting and then deleting text) are regarded as a single undo/redo operation.
- Text character format changes.
- Text block format changes.
- Text block group format changes.

PythonQt.Qt.QTextDocument.addResource.doc: Qt 5 reference: ### void QTextDocument::addResource(int *type*, const [QUrl](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qurl.html) \&*name*, const [QVariant](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qvariant.html) \&*resource*) Adds the resource *resource* to the resource cache, using *type* and *name* as identifiers. *type* should be a value from [QTextDocument::ResourceType](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html#ResourceType-enum). For example, you can add an image as a resource in order to reference it from within the document: ``` document->addResource(QTextDocument::ImageResource, QUrl("mydata://image.png"), QVariant(image)); ``` The image can be inserted into the document using the [QTextCursor](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcursor.html) API: ``` QTextImageFormat imageFormat; imageFormat.setName("mydata://image.png"); cursor.insertImage(imageFormat); ``` Alternatively, you can insert images using the HTML `img` tag: ``` editor->append(""); ```

Qt 5 reference:

### baseUrl : [QUrl](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qurl.html)

This property holds the base URL used to resolve relative resource URLs within the
document.

Resource URLs are resolved to be within the same directory as the target of the base URL
meaning any portion of the path after the last '/' will be ignored.

| Base URL | Relative URL | Resolved URL |
| --- | --- | --- |
| file:///path/to/content | images/logo.png | file:///path/to/images/logo.png |
| file:///path/to/content/ | images/logo.png | file:///path/to/content/images/logo.png |
| file:///path/to/content/index.html | images/logo.png | file:///path/to/content/images/logo.png |
| file:///path/to/content/images/ | ../images/logo.png | file:///path/to/content/images/logo.png |

This property was introduced in Qt 5.3.

**Access functions:**

| QUrl | **baseUrl**() const |
| --- | --- |
| void | **setBaseUrl**(const QUrl \&*url*) |

**Notifier signal:**

| void | **baseUrlChanged**(const QUrl \&*url*) |
| --- | --- |

### `[signal]` void QTextDocument::contentsChange(int *position*, int *charsRemoved*, int *charsAdded*)

This signal is emitted whenever the document's content changes; for example, when text
is inserted or deleted, or when formatting is applied.

Information is provided about the *position* of the character in the document where the
change occurred, the number of characters removed (*charsRemoved*), and the number of
characters added (*charsAdded*).

The signal is emitted before the document's layout manager is notified about the change.
This hook allows you to implement syntax highlighting for the document.

**See also**
[QAbstractTextDocumentLayout::documentChanged](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstracttextdocumentlayout.html#documentChanged)()
and
[contentsChanged](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html#contentsChanged)().

### [QTextBlock](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextblock.html) QTextDocument::end() const

This function returns a block to test for the end of the document while iterating over
it.

```
    for (QTextBlock it = doc->begin(); it != doc->end(); it = it.next())
        cout << it.text().toStdString() << Qt::endl;
```

The block returned is invalid and represents the block after the last block in the
document. You can use
[lastBlock](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html#lastBlock)() to
retrieve the last valid block of the document.

**See also**
[lastBlock](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html#lastBlock)().

### [QTextCursor](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcursor.html) QTextDocument::find(const [QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html) \&*subString*, const [QTextCursor](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcursor.html) \&*cursor*, [QTextDocument::FindFlags](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html#FindFlag-enum) *options* \= FindFlags()) const

Finds the next occurrence of the string, *subString*, in the document. The search starts
at the position of the given *cursor*, and proceeds forwards through the document unless
specified otherwise in the search options. The *options* control the type of search
performed.

Returns a cursor with the match selected if *subString* was found; otherwise returns a
null cursor.

If the given *cursor* has a selection, the search begins after the selection; otherwise
it begins at the cursor's position.

By default the search is case insensitive, and can match text anywhere in the document.

otherwise in the search options. The *options* control the type of search performed.

### `[virtual protected]` [QVariant](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qvariant.html) QTextDocument::loadResource(int *type*, const [QUrl](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qurl.html) \&*name*)

Loads data of the specified *type* from the resource with the given *name*.

This function is called by the rich text engine to request data that isn't directly
stored by [QTextDocument](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html), but
still associated with it. For example, images are referenced indirectly by the name
attribute of a
[QTextImageFormat](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextimageformat.html) object.

When called by Qt, *type* is one of the values of
[QTextDocument::ResourceType](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html#ResourceType-enum).

If the [QTextDocument](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html) is a child
object of a [QObject](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qobject.html) that has an
invokable loadResource method such as
[QTextEdit](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html),
[QTextBrowser](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextbrowser.html) or a
[QTextDocument](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html) itself then the
default implementation tries to retrieve the data from the parent.

**Note:** This function can be invoked via the meta-object system and from QML. See
[Q\_INVOKABLE](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qobject.html#Q_INVOKABLE).
signatures: loadResource(self, type: int, name: PySide2.QtCore.QUrl) -> typing.Any

### maximumBlockCount : int

Specifies the limit for blocks in the document.

Specifies the maximum number of blocks the document may have. If there are more blocks
in the document that specified with this property blocks are removed from the beginning
of the document.

A negative or zero value specifies that the document may contain an unlimited amount of
blocks.

The default value is 0\.

Note that setting this property will apply the limit immediately to the document
contents.

Setting this property also disables the undo redo history.

This property is undefined in documents with tables or frames.

This property was introduced in Qt 4.2.

### `[signal]` void QTextDocument::modificationChanged(bool *changed*)

This signal is emitted whenever the content of the document changes in a way that
affects the modification state. If *changed* is true, the document has been modified;
otherwise it is false.

For example, calling
[setModified](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html#modified-prop)(false)
on a document and then inserting text causes the signal to get emitted. If you undo that
operation, causing the document to return to its original unmodified state, the signal
will get emitted again.

Qt 5 reference:

### void QTextDocument::print([QPagedPaintDevice](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpagedpaintdevice.html) \**printer*) const

Prints the document to the given *printer*. The
[QPagedPaintDevice](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpagedpaintdevice.html) must be
set up before being used with this function.

This is only a convenience method to print the whole document to the printer.

If the document is already paginated through a specified height in the
[pageSize](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html#pageSize-prop)()
property it is printed as-is.

If the document is not paginated, like for example a document used in a
[QTextEdit](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html), then a temporary copy of
the document is created and the copy is broken into multiple pages according to the size
of the paint device's paperRect(). By default a 2 cm margin is set around the document
contents. In addition the current page number is printed at the bottom of each page.

**See also**
[QTextEdit::print](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html#print)().

### textWidth : [qreal](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtglobal.html#qreal-typedef)

The text width specifies the preferred width for text in the document. If the text (or
content in general) is wider than the specified with it is broken into multiple lines
and grows vertically. If the text cannot be broken into multiple lines to fit into the
specified text width it will be larger and the
[size](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html#size-prop)() and the
[idealWidth](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html#idealWidth)()
property will reflect that.

If the text width is set to -1 then the text will not be broken into multiple lines
unless it is enforced through an explicit line break or a new paragraph.

The default value is -1.

Setting the text width will also set the page height to -1, causing the document to grow
or shrink vertically in a continuous way. If you want the document layout to break the
text into multiple pages then you have to set the
[pageSize](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html#pageSize-prop) property
instead.

This property was introduced in Qt 4.2.

**Access functions:**

| qreal | **textWidth**() const |
| --- | --- |
| void | **setTextWidth**(qreal *width*) |

**See also** [size](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html#size-prop)(),
[idealWidth](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html#idealWidth)(), and
[pageSize](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html#pageSize-prop)().
