### [QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html) QTextDocument::toHtml(const [QByteArray](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qbytearray.html) \&*encoding* \= QByteArray()) const

Returns a string containing an HTML representation of the document.

The *encoding* parameter specifies the value for the charset attribute in the html
header. For example if 'utf-8' is specified then the beginning of the generated html
will look like this:

```
<html><head><meta http-equiv="Content-Type" content="text/html; charset=utf-8"></head><body>...
```

If no encoding is specified then no such meta information is generated.

If you later on convert the returned html string into a byte array for transmission over
a network or when saving to disk you should specify the encoding you're going to use for
the conversion to a byte array here.

**See also** [Supported HTML
Subset](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/richtext-html-subset.html).

Qt 5 reference:

### [QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html) QTextDocument::toPlainText() const

Returns the plain text contained in the document. If you want formatting information use
a [QTextCursor](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcursor.html) instead.

This function returns the same as
[toRawText](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html#toRawText)(), but will
replace some unicode characters with ASCII alternatives. In particular, no-break space
(U\+00A0) is replaced by a regular space (U\+0020), and both paragraph (U\+2029) and
line (U\+2028) separators are replaced by line feed (U\+000A). If you need the precise
contents of the document, use
[toRawText](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html#toRawText)() instead.

**Note:** Embedded objects, such as images, are represented by a Unicode value U\+FFFC
(OBJECT REPLACEMENT CHARACTER).

**See also** [toHtml](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html#toHtml)().

### useDesignMetrics : bool

This property holds whether the document uses design metrics of fonts to improve the
accuracy of text layout

If this property is set to true, the layout will use design metrics. Otherwise, the
metrics of the paint device as set on
[QAbstractTextDocumentLayout::setPaintDevice](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstracttextdocumentlayout.html#setPaintDevice)()
will be used.

Using design metrics makes a layout have a width that is no longer dependent on hinting
and pixel-rounding. This means that WYSIWYG text layout becomes possible because the
width scales much more linearly based on paintdevice metrics than it would otherwise.

By default, this property is `false`.

This property was introduced in Qt 4.1.

## Detailed Description

A QTextDocumentFragment is a fragment of rich text, that can be inserted into a
[QTextDocument](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html). A document
fragment can be created from a
[QTextDocument](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html), from a
[QTextCursor](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcursor.html)'s selection, or from
another document fragment. Document fragments can also be created by the static
functions,
[fromPlainText](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocumentfragment.html#fromPlainText)()
and
[fromHtml](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocumentfragment.html#fromHtml)().

The contents of a document fragment can be obtained as plain text by using the
[toPlainText](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocumentfragment.html#toPlainText)()
function, or it can be obtained as HTML with
[toHtml](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocumentfragment.html#toHtml)().

## Detailed Description

To write a document, construct a QTextDocumentWriter object with either a file name or a
device object, and specify the document format to be written. You can construct a writer
and set the format using
[setFormat](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocumentwriter.html#setFormat)()
later.

Call [write](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocumentwriter.html#write)() to
write the document to the device. If the document is successfully written, this function
returns `true`. However, if an error occurs when writing the document, it will return
false.

Call
[supportedDocumentFormats](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocumentwriter.html#supportedDocumentFormats)()
for a list of formats that QTextDocumentWriter can write.

Since the capabilities of the supported output formats vary considerably, the writer
simply outputs the appropriate subset of objects for each format. This typically
includes the formatted text and images contained in a document.

### void QTextDocumentWriter::setFormat(const [QByteArray](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qbytearray.html) \&*format*)

Sets the format used to write documents to the *format* specified. *format* is a case
insensitive text string. For example:

```
        QTextDocumentWriter writer;
        writer.setFormat("odf"); // same as writer.setFormat("ODF");

PythonQt.Qt.QTextEdit.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

### Introduction and Concepts

QTextEdit is an advanced WYSIWYG viewer/editor supporting rich text formatting using
HTML-style tags, or Markdown format. It is optimized to handle large documents and to
respond quickly to user input.

QTextEdit works on paragraphs and characters. A paragraph is a formatted string which is
word-wrapped to fit into the width of the widget. By default when reading plain text,
one newline signifies a paragraph. A document consists of zero or more paragraphs. The
words in the paragraph are aligned in accordance with the paragraph's alignment.
Paragraphs are separated by hard line breaks. Each character within a paragraph has its
own attributes, for example, font and color.

QTextEdit can display images, lists and tables. If the text is too large to view within
the text edit's viewport, scroll bars will appear. The text edit can load both plain
text and rich text files. Rich text can be described using a subset of HTML 4 markup;
refer to the [Supported HTML
Subset](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/richtext-html-subset.html) page for more
information.

If you just need to display a small piece of rich text use
[QLabel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qlabel.html).

The rich text support in Qt is designed to provide a fast, portable and efficient way to
add reasonable online help facilities to applications, and to provide a basis for rich
text editors. If you find the HTML support insufficient for your needs you may consider
the use of Qt WebKit, which provides a full-featured web browser widget.

The shape of the mouse cursor on a QTextEdit is
[Qt::IBeamCursor](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#CursorShape-enum) by
default. It can be changed through the
[viewport](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractscrollarea.html#viewport)()'s
cursor property.

### Using QTextEdit as a Display Widget

QTextEdit can display a large HTML subset, including tables and images.

The text can be set or replaced using
[setHtml](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html#html-prop)() which deletes
any existing text and replaces it with the text passed in the
[setHtml](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html#html-prop)() call. If you
call [setHtml](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html#html-prop)() with
legacy HTML, and then call
[toHtml](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html#html-prop)(), the text that
is returned may have different markup, but will render the same. The entire text can be
deleted with [clear](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html#clear)().

Text can also be set or replaced using
[setMarkdown](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html#markdown-prop)(), and
the same caveats apply: if you then call
[toMarkdown](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html#markdown-prop)(), the
text that is returned may be different, but the meaning is preserved as much as
possible. Markdown with some embedded HTML can be parsed, with the same limitations that
[setHtml](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html#html-prop)() has; but
[toMarkdown](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html#markdown-prop)() only
writes "pure" Markdown, without any embedded HTML.

Text itself can be inserted using the
[QTextCursor](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcursor.html) class or using the
convenience functions
[insertHtml](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html#insertHtml)(),
[insertPlainText](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html#insertPlainText)(),
[append](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html#append)() or
[paste](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html#paste)().
[QTextCursor](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcursor.html) is also able to
insert complex objects like tables or lists into the document, and it deals with
creating selections and applying changes to selected text.

By default the text edit wraps words at whitespace to fit within the text edit widget.
The
[setLineWrapMode](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html#lineWrapMode-prop)()
function is used to specify the kind of line wrap you want, or
[NoWrap](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html#LineWrapMode-enum) if you
don't want any wrapping. Call
[setLineWrapMode](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html#lineWrapMode-prop)()
to set a fixed pixel width
[FixedPixelWidth](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html#LineWrapMode-enum),
or character column (e.g. 80 column)
[FixedColumnWidth](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html#LineWrapMode-enum)
with the pixels or columns specified with
[setLineWrapColumnOrWidth](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html#lineWrapColumnOrWidth-prop)().
If you use word wrap to the widget's width
[WidgetWidth](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html#LineWrapMode-enum), you
can specify whether to break on whitespace or anywhere with
[setWordWrapMode](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html#wordWrapMode-prop)().

The [find](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html#find)() function can be
used to find and select a given string within the text.

If you want to limit the total number of paragraphs in a QTextEdit, as for example it is
often useful in a log viewer, then you can use
[QTextDocument](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html)'s
maximumBlockCount property for that.

#### Read-only Key Bindings

When QTextEdit is used read-only the key bindings are limited to navigation, and text
may only be selected with the mouse:

| Keypresses | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Up | Moves one line up. |
| Down | Moves one line down. |
| Left | Moves one character to the left. |
| Right | Moves one character to the right. |
| PageUp | Moves one (viewport) page up. |
| PageDown | Moves one (viewport) page down. |
| Home | Moves to the beginning of the text. |
| End | Moves to the end of the text. |
| Alt\+Wheel | Scrolls the page horizontally (the Wheel is the mouse wheel). |
| Ctrl\+Wheel | Zooms the text. |
| Ctrl\+A | Selects all text. |

The text edit may be able to provide some meta-information. For example, the
[documentTitle](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html#documentTitle-prop)()
function will return the text from within HTML `<title>` tags.

**Note:** Zooming into HTML documents only works if the font-size is not set to a fixed
size.

### Using QTextEdit as an Editor

All the information about using QTextEdit as a display widget also applies here.

The current char format's attributes are set with
[setFontItalic](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html#setFontItalic)(),
[setFontWeight](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html#setFontWeight)(),
[setFontUnderline](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html#setFontUnderline)(),
[setFontFamily](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html#setFontFamily)(),
[setFontPointSize](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html#setFontPointSize)(),
[setTextColor](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html#setTextColor)() and
[setCurrentFont](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html#setCurrentFont)().
The current paragraph's alignment is set with
[setAlignment](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html#setAlignment)().

Selection of text is handled by the
[QTextCursor](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcursor.html) class, which provides
functionality for creating selections, retrieving the text contents or deleting
selections. You can retrieve the object that corresponds with the user-visible cursor
using the [textCursor](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html#textCursor)()
method. If you want to set a selection in QTextEdit just create one on a
[QTextCursor](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcursor.html) object and then make
that cursor the visible cursor using
[setTextCursor](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html#setTextCursor)(). The
selection can be copied to the clipboard with
[copy](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html#copy)(), or cut to the
clipboard with [cut](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html#cut)(). The
entire text can be selected using
[selectAll](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html#selectAll)().

When the cursor is moved and the underlying formatting attributes change, the
[currentCharFormatChanged](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html#currentCharFormatChanged)()
signal is emitted to reflect the new attributes at the new cursor position.

The [textChanged](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html#textChanged)()
signal is emitted whenever the text changes (as a result of
[setText](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html#setText)() or through the
editor itself).

QTextEdit holds a [QTextDocument](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html)
object which can be retrieved using the
[document](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html#document-prop)() method.
You can also set your own document object using
[setDocument](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html#document-prop)().

[QTextDocument](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html) provides an
[isModified()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html#modified-prop)
function which will return true if the text has been modified since it was either loaded
or since the last call to setModified with false as argument. In addition it provides
methods for undo and redo.

#### Drag and Drop

QTextEdit also supports custom drag and drop behavior. By default, QTextEdit will insert
plain text, HTML and rich text when the user drops data of these MIME types onto a
document. Reimplement
[canInsertFromMimeData](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html#canInsertFromMimeData)()
and
[insertFromMimeData](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html#insertFromMimeData)()
to add support for additional MIME types.

For example, to allow the user to drag and drop an image onto a QTextEdit, you could the
implement these functions in the following way:

```
bool TextEdit::canInsertFromMimeData( const QMimeData *source ) const
{
    if (source->hasImage())
        return true;
    else
        return QTextEdit::canInsertFromMimeData(source);
}
```

We add support for image MIME types by returning true. For all other MIME types, we use
the default implementation.

```
void TextEdit::insertFromMimeData( const QMimeData *source )
{
    if (source->hasImage())
    {
        QImage image = qvariant_cast<QImage>(source->imageData());
        QTextCursor cursor = this->textCursor();
        QTextDocument *document = this->document();
        document->addResource(QTextDocument::ImageResource, QUrl("image"), image);
        cursor.insertImage("image");
    }
}
```

We unpack the image from the
[QVariant](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qvariant.html) held by the MIME source and
insert it into the document as a resource.

#### Editing Key Bindings

The list of key bindings which are implemented for editing:

| Keypresses | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Backspace | Deletes the character to the left of the cursor. |
| Delete | Deletes the character to the right of the cursor. |
| Ctrl\+C | Copy the selected text to the clipboard. |
| Ctrl\+Insert | Copy the selected text to the clipboard. |
| Ctrl\+K | Deletes to the end of the line. |
| Ctrl\+V | Pastes the clipboard text into text edit. |
| Shift\+Insert | Pastes the clipboard text into text edit. |
| Ctrl\+X | Deletes the selected text and copies it to the clipboard. |
| Shift\+Delete | Deletes the selected text and copies it to the clipboard. |
| Ctrl\+Z | Undoes the last operation. |
| Ctrl\+Y | Redoes the last operation. |
| Left | Moves the cursor one character to the left. |
| Ctrl\+Left | Moves the cursor one word to the left. |
| Right | Moves the cursor one character to the right. |
| Ctrl\+Right | Moves the cursor one word to the right. |
| Up | Moves the cursor one line up. |
| Down | Moves the cursor one line down. |
| PageUp | Moves the cursor one page up. |
| PageDown | Moves the cursor one page down. |
| Home | Moves the cursor to the beginning of the line. |
| Ctrl\+Home | Moves the cursor to the beginning of the text. |
| End | Moves the cursor to the end of the line. |
| Ctrl\+End | Moves the cursor to the end of the text. |
| Alt\+Wheel | Scrolls the page horizontally (the Wheel is the mouse wheel). |

To select (mark) text hold down the Shift key whilst pressing one of the movement
keystrokes, for example, *Shift\+Right* will select the character to the right, and
*Shift\+Ctrl\+Right* will select the word to the right, etc.

void MyTextEdit::contextMenuEvent(QContextMenuEvent *event)

### `[signal]` void QTextEdit::copyAvailable(bool *yes*)

This signal is emitted when text is selected or de-selected in the text edit.

When text is selected this signal will be emitted with *yes* set to true. If no text has
been selected or if the selected text is de-selected this signal is emitted with *yes*
set to false.

If *yes* is true then [copy](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html#copy)()
can be used to copy the selection to the clipboard. If *yes* is false then
[copy](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html#copy)() does nothing.

**See also**
[selectionChanged](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html#selectionChanged)().

This is an overloaded function.

Finds the next occurrence, matching the regular expression, *exp*, using the given
*options*. The
[QTextDocument::FindCaseSensitively](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html#FindFlag-enum)
option is ignored for this overload, use
[QRegExp::caseSensitivity](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qregexp.html#caseSensitivity)

otherwise returns `false`.

*options*.

otherwise returns `false`.

ignored. Instead, the *options* are used to determine if the search is case sensitive or
not.

PythonQt.Qt.QTextEdit.html.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

### html : [QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html)

This property provides an HTML interface to the text of the text edit.

toHtml() returns the text of the text edit as html.

setHtml() changes the text of the text edit. Any previous text is removed and the
undo/redo history is cleared. The input text is interpreted as rich text in html format.
[currentCharFormat](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html#currentCharFormat)()
is also reset, unless
[textCursor](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html#textCursor)() is already
at the beginning of the document.

**Note:** It is the responsibility of the caller to make sure that the text is correctly
decoded when a [QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html) containing
HTML is created and passed to setHtml().

By default, for a newly-created, empty document, this property contains text to describe
an HTML 4.0 document with no body text.

| --- | --- |
| void | **setHtml**(const QString \&*text*) |

**Notifier signal:**

| void | **[textChanged](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html#textChanged)**() |
| --- | --- |

**See also** [Supported HTML
Subset](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/richtext-html-subset.html) and
[plainText](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html#plainText-prop).

### lineWrapMode : [LineWrapMode](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html#LineWrapMode-enum)

This property holds the line wrap mode

The default mode is
[WidgetWidth](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html#LineWrapMode-enum) which
causes words to be wrapped at the right edge of the text edit. Wrapping occurs at
whitespace, keeping whole words intact. If you want wrapping to occur within words use
[setWordWrapMode](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html#wordWrapMode-prop)().
If you set a wrap mode of
[FixedPixelWidth](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html#LineWrapMode-enum)
or
[FixedColumnWidth](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html#LineWrapMode-enum)
you should also call
[setLineWrapColumnOrWidth](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html#lineWrapColumnOrWidth-prop)()

PythonQt.Qt.QTextEdit.markdown.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

### markdown : [QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html)

This property provides a Markdown interface to the text of the text edit.

`toMarkdown()` returns the text of the text edit as "pure" Markdown, without any
embedded HTML formatting. Some features that
[QTextDocument](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html) supports (such as
the use of specific colors and named fonts) cannot be expressed in "pure" Markdown, and
they will be omitted.

`setMarkdown()` changes the text of the text edit. Any previous text is removed and the
undo/redo history is cleared. The input text is interpreted as rich text in Markdown
format.

Parsing of HTML included in the *markdown* string is handled in the same way as in
[setHtml](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html#html-prop); however,
Markdown formatting inside HTML blocks is not supported.

Some features of the parser can be enabled or disabled via the *features* argument:

| Constant | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `MarkdownNoHTML` | Any HTML tags in the Markdown text will be discarded |
| `MarkdownDialectCommonMark` | The parser supports only the features standardized by CommonMark |
| `MarkdownDialectGitHub` | The parser supports the GitHub dialect |

The default is `MarkdownDialectGitHub`.

This property was introduced in Qt 5.14.

**Access functions:**

| QString | **toMarkdown**(QTextDocument::MarkdownFeatures *features* \= QTextDocument::MarkdownDialectGitHub) const |
| --- | --- |
| void | **setMarkdown**(const QString \&*markdown*) |

**Notifier signal:**

| void | **[textChanged](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html#textChanged)**() |
| --- | --- |

**See also**
[plainText](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html#plainText-prop),
[html](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html#html-prop),
[QTextDocument::toMarkdown](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html#toMarkdown)(),

### overwriteMode : bool

This property holds whether text entered by the user will overwrite existing text

As with many text editors, the text editor widget can be configured to insert or
overwrite existing text with new text entered by the user.

If this property is `true`, existing text is overwritten, character-for-character by new
text; otherwise, text is inserted at the cursor position, displacing existing text.

By default, this property is `false` (new text does not overwrite existing text).

This property was introduced in Qt 4.1.

### `[slot]` void QTextEdit::paste()

Pastes the text from the clipboard into the text edit at the current cursor position.

If there is no text in the clipboard nothing happens.

PythonQt.Qt.QTextFormat.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

A QTextFormat is a generic class used for describing the format of parts of a
[QTextDocument](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html). The derived
classes [QTextCharFormat](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcharformat.html),
[QTextBlockFormat](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextblockformat.html),
[QTextListFormat](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextlistformat.html), and
[QTextTableFormat](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtexttableformat.html) are usually
more useful, and describe the formatting that is applied to specific parts of the
document.

A format has a `FormatType` which specifies the kinds of text item it can format; e.g. a
block of text, a list, a table, etc. A format also has various properties (some specific
to particular format types), as described by the Property enum. Every property has a
corresponding Property.

The format type is given by
[type](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextformat.html#type)(), and the format can
be tested with
[isCharFormat](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextformat.html#isCharFormat)(),
[isBlockFormat](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextformat.html#isBlockFormat)(),
[isListFormat](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextformat.html#isListFormat)(),
[isTableFormat](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextformat.html#isTableFormat)(),
[isFrameFormat](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextformat.html#isFrameFormat)(),
and
[isImageFormat](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextformat.html#isImageFormat)(). If
the type is determined, it can be retrieved with
[toCharFormat](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextformat.html#toCharFormat)(),
[toBlockFormat](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextformat.html#toBlockFormat)(),
[toListFormat](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextformat.html#toListFormat)(),
[toTableFormat](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextformat.html#toTableFormat)(),
[toFrameFormat](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextformat.html#toFrameFormat)(),
and
[toImageFormat](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextformat.html#toImageFormat)().

A format's properties can be set with the
[setProperty](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextformat.html#setProperty)()
functions, and retrieved with
[boolProperty](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextformat.html#boolProperty)(),
[intProperty](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextformat.html#intProperty)(),
[doubleProperty](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextformat.html#doubleProperty)(),
and
[stringProperty](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextformat.html#stringProperty)()
as appropriate. All the property IDs used in the format can be retrieved with
allPropertyIds(). One format can be merged into another using
[merge](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextformat.html#merge)().

A format's object index can be set with
[setObjectIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextformat.html#setObjectIndex)(),
and retrieved with
[objectIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextformat.html#objectIndex)(). These
methods can be used to associate the format with a
[QTextObject](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextobject.html). It is used to
represent lists, frames, and tables inside the document.

## Detailed Description

A text fragment describes a piece of text that is stored with a single character format.
Text in which the character format changes can be represented by sequences of text
fragments with different formats.

If the user edits the text in a fragment and introduces a different character format,
the fragment's text will be split at each point where the format changes, and new
fragments will be created. For example, changing the style of some text in the middle of
a sentence will cause the fragment to be broken into three separate fragments: the first
and third with the same format as before, and the second with the new style. The first
fragment will contain the text from the beginning of the sentence, the second will
contain the text from the middle, and the third takes the text from the end of the
sentence.

![](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/images/qtextfragment-split.png)

A fragment's text and character format can be obtained with the
[text](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextfragment.html#text)() and
[charFormat](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextfragment.html#charFormat)()
functions. The [length](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextfragment.html#length)()
function gives the length of the text in the fragment.
[position](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextfragment.html#position)() gives the
position in the document of the start of the fragment. To determine whether the fragment
contains a particular position within the document, use the
[contains](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextfragment.html#contains)() function.

## Detailed Description

Text frames provide structure for the text in a document. They are used as generic
containers for other document elements. Frames are usually created by using
[QTextCursor::insertFrame](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcursor.html#insertFrame)().

Frames can be used to create hierarchical structures in rich text documents. Each
document has a root frame
([QTextDocument::rootFrame](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html#rootFrame)()),
and each frame beneath the root frame has a parent frame and a (possibly empty) list of
child frames. The parent frame can be found with
[parentFrame](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextframe.html#parentFrame)(), and the
[childFrames](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextframe.html#childFrames)() function
provides a list of child frames.

Each frame contains at least one text block to enable text cursors to insert new
document elements within. As a result, the
[QTextFrame::iterator](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextframe-iterator.html)
class is used to traverse both the blocks and child frames within a given frame. The
first and last child elements in the frame can be found with
[begin](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextframe.html#begin)() and
[end](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextframe.html#end)().

A frame also has a format (specified using
[QTextFrameFormat](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextframeformat.html)) which can
be set with [setFormat](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextobject.html#setFormat)()
and read with [format](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextobject.html#format)().

Text cursors can be obtained that point to the first and last valid cursor positions
within a frame; use the
[firstCursorPosition](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextframe.html#firstCursorPosition)()
and
[lastCursorPosition](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextframe.html#lastCursorPosition)()
functions for this. The frame's extent in the document can be found with
[firstPosition](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextframe.html#firstPosition)() and
[lastPosition](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextframe.html#lastPosition)().

You can iterate over a frame's contents using the
[QTextFrame::iterator](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextframe-iterator.html)
class: this provides read-only access to its internal list of text blocks and child
frames.

## Detailed Description

A text frame groups together one or more blocks of text, providing a layer of structure
larger than the paragraph. The format of a frame specifies how it is rendered and
positioned on the screen. It does not directly specify the behavior of the text
formatting within, but provides constraints on the layout of its children.

The frame format defines the
[width](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextframeformat.html#width)() and
[height](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextframeformat.html#height)() of the frame
on the screen. Each frame can have a
[border](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextframeformat.html#border)() that
surrounds its contents with a rectangular box. The border is surrounded by a
[margin](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextframeformat.html#margin)() around the
frame, and the contents of the frame are kept separate from the border by the frame's
[padding](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextframeformat.html#padding)(). This
scheme is similar to the box model used by Cascading Style Sheets for HTML pages.

![](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/images/qtextframe-style.png)

The [position](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextframeformat.html#position)() of a
frame is set using
[setPosition](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextframeformat.html#setPosition)()
and determines how it is located relative to the surrounding text.

The validity of a QTextFrameFormat object can be determined with the
[isValid](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextframeformat.html#isValid)() function.

## Detailed Description

Inline images are represented by a Unicode value U\+FFFC (OBJECT REPLACEMENT CHARACTER)
which has an associated QTextImageFormat. The image format specifies a name with
[setName](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextimageformat.html#setName)() that is
used to locate the image. The size of the rectangle that the image will occupy is
specified in pixels using
[setWidth](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextimageformat.html#setWidth)() and
[setHeight](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextimageformat.html#setHeight)(). The
desired image quality may be set with

## Detailed Description

Normally, you do not need to create a QTextInlineObject. It is used by
[QAbstractTextDocumentLayout](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstracttextdocumentlayout.html)
to handle inline objects when implementing a custom layout.

The inline object has various attributes that can be set, for example using,
[setWidth](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextinlineobject.html#setWidth)(),
[setAscent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextinlineobject.html#setAscent)(), and
[setDescent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextinlineobject.html#setDescent)().
The rectangle it occupies is given by
[rect](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextinlineobject.html#rect)(), and its
direction by
[textDirection](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextinlineobject.html#textDirection)().
Its position in the text layout is given by
[textPosition](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextinlineobject.html#textPosition)(),
and its format is given by
[format](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextinlineobject.html#format)().

PythonQt.Qt.QTextLayout.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

It offers many features expected from a modern text layout engine, including Unicode
compliant rendering, line breaking and handling of cursor positioning. It can also
produce and render device independent layout, something that is important for WYSIWYG
applications.

The class has a rather low level API and unless you intend to implement your own text
rendering for some specialized widget, you probably won't need to use it directly.

QTextLayout can be used with both plain and rich text.

QTextLayout can be used to create a sequence of
[QTextLine](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextline.html) instances with given
widths and can position them independently on the screen. Once the layout is done, these
lines can be drawn on a paint device.

The text to be laid out can be provided in the constructor or set with
[setText](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextlayout.html#setText)().

The layout can be seen as a sequence of
[QTextLine](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextline.html) objects; use
[createLine](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextlayout.html#createLine)() to create
a [QTextLine](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextline.html) instance, and
[lineAt](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextlayout.html#lineAt)() or
[lineForTextPosition](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextlayout.html#lineForTextPosition)()
to retrieve created lines.

Here is a code snippet that demonstrates the layout phase:

```
int leading = fontMetrics.leading();
qreal height = 0;
textLayout.setCacheEnabled(true);
textLayout.beginLayout();
while (1) {
    QTextLine line = textLayout.createLine();
    if (!line.isValid())
        break;

    line.setLineWidth(lineWidth);
    height += leading;
    line.setPosition(QPointF(0, height));
    height += line.height();
}
textLayout.endLayout();
```

The text can then be rendered by calling the layout's
[draw](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextlayout.html#draw)() function:

```
QPainter painter(this);
textLayout.draw(&painter, QPoint(0, 0));
```

For a given position in the text you can find a valid cursor position with
[isValidCursorPosition](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextlayout.html#isValidCursorPosition)(),
[nextCursorPosition](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextlayout.html#nextCursorPosition)(),
and
[previousCursorPosition](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextlayout.html#previousCursorPosition)().

The QTextLayout itself can be positioned with
[setPosition](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextlayout.html#setPosition)(); it has
a [boundingRect](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextlayout.html#boundingRect)(),
and a [minimumWidth](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextlayout.html#minimumWidth)()
and a
[maximumWidth](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextlayout.html#maximumWidth)().

PythonQt.Qt.QTextLayout.createLine.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

### [QTextLine](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextline.html) QTextLayout::createLine()

Returns a new text line to be laid out if there is text to be inserted into the layout;
otherwise returns an invalid text line.

The text layout creates a new line object that starts after the last line in the layout,
or at the beginning if the layout is empty. The layout maintains an internal cursor, and
each line is filled with text from the cursor position onwards when the
[QTextLine::setLineWidth](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextline.html#setLineWidth)()
function is called.

Once
[QTextLine::setLineWidth](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextline.html#setLineWidth)()
is called, a new line can be created and filled with text. Repeating this process will
lay out the whole block of text contained in the
[QTextLayout](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextlayout.html). If there is no text
left to be inserted into the layout, the
[QTextLine](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextline.html) returned will not be
valid (isValid() will return false).

PythonQt.Qt.QTextLayout.isValidCursorPos.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

### bool QTextLayout::isValidCursorPosition(int *pos*) const

/ Returns `true` if position *pos* is a valid cursor position.

In a Unicode context some positions in the text are not valid cursor positions, because
the position is inside a Unicode surrogate or a grapheme cluster.

A grapheme cluster is a sequence of two or more Unicode characters that form one
indivisible entity on the screen. For example the latin character \`Ä' can be
represented in Unicode by two characters, \`A' (0x41), and the combining diaresis
(0x308). A text cursor can only validly be positioned before or after these two
characters, never between them since that wouldn't make sense. In indic languages every
syllable forms a grapheme cluster.

## Detailed Description

When we specify a value for the length of an element in a text document, we often need
to provide some other information so that the length is used in the way we expect. For
example, when we specify a table width, the value can represent a fixed number of
pixels, or it can be a percentage value. This information changes both the meaning of
the value and the way it is used.

Generally, this class is used to specify table widths. These can be specified either as
a fixed amount of pixels, as a percentage of the containing frame's width, or by a
variable width that allows it to take up just the space it requires.

[QTextLength::FixedLength](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextlength.html#Type-enum)
then that fixed amount is returned. For variable lengths, zero is returned.

PythonQt.Qt.QTextLine.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

A text line is usually created by
[QTextLayout::createLine](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextlayout.html#createLine)().

After being created, the line can be filled using the
[setLineWidth](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextline.html#setLineWidth)() or
[setNumColumns](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextline.html#setNumColumns)()
functions. A line has a number of attributes including the rectangle it occupies,
[rect](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextline.html#rect)(), its coordinates,
[x](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextline.html#x)() and
[y](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextline.html#y)(), its
[textLength](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextline.html#textLength)(),
[width](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextline.html#width)() and
[naturalTextWidth](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextline.html#naturalTextWidth)(),
and its [ascent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextline.html#ascent)() and
[descent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextline.html#descent)() relative to the
text. The position of the cursor in terms of the line is available from
[cursorToX](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextline.html#cursorToX)() and its
inverse from [xToCursor](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextline.html#xToCursor)().
A line can be moved with
[setPosition](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextline.html#setPosition)().

### QList\<[QGlyphRun](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qglyphrun.html)\> QTextLine::glyphRuns(int *from* \= -1, int *length* \= -1) const

Returns the glyph indexes and positions for all glyphs in this
[QTextLine](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextline.html) for characters in the
range defined by *from* and *length*. The *from* index is relative to the beginning of
the text in the containing
[QTextLayout](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextlayout.html), and the range must
be within the range of [QTextLine](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextline.html) as
given by functions
[textStart](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextline.html#textStart)() and
[textLength](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextline.html#textLength)().

If *from* is negative, it will default to
[textStart](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextline.html#textStart)(), and if
*length* is negative it will default to the return value of
[textLength](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextline.html#textLength)().

This function was introduced in Qt 5.0.

**See also**
[QTextLayout::glyphRuns](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextlayout.html#glyphRuns)().

Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

A list contains a sequence of text blocks, each of which is marked with a bullet point
or other symbol. Multiple levels of lists can be used, and the automatic numbering
feature provides support for ordered numeric and alphabetical lists.

Lists are created by using a text cursor to insert an empty list at the current position
or by moving existing text into a new list. The
[QTextCursor::insertList](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcursor.html#insertList)()
function inserts an empty block into the document at the cursor position, and makes it
the first item in a list.

```
    QTextListFormat listFormat;
    if (list) {
        listFormat = list->format();
        listFormat.setIndent(listFormat.indent() + 1);
    }

    listFormat.setStyle(QTextListFormat::ListDisc);
    cursor.insertList(listFormat);
```

The
[QTextCursor::createList](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcursor.html#createList)()
function takes the contents of the cursor's current block and turns it into the first
item of a new list.

The cursor's current list is found with
[QTextCursor::currentList](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcursor.html#currentList)().

The number of items in a list is given by
[count](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextlist.html#count)(). Each item can be
obtained by its index in the list with the
[item](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextlist.html#item)() function. Similarly,
the index of a given item can be found with
[itemNumber](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextlist.html#itemNumber)(). The text
of each item can be found with the
[itemText](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextlist.html#itemText)() function.

Note that the items in the list may not be adjacent elements in the document. For
example, the top-level items in a multi-level list will be separated by the items in
lower levels of the list.

List items can be deleted by index with the
[removeItem](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextlist.html#removeItem)() function.
[remove](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextlist.html#remove)() deletes the
specified item in the list.

The list's format is set with
[setFormat](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextlist.html#setFormat)() and read with
[format](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextlist.html#format)(). The format
describes the decoration of the list itself, and not the individual items.

PythonQt.Qt.QTextListFormat.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

A list is composed of one or more items, represented as text blocks. The list's format
specifies the appearance of items in the list. In particular, it determines the
indentation and the style of each item.

The indentation of the items is an integer value that causes each item to be offset from
the left margin by a certain amount. This value is read with
[indent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextlistformat.html#indent)() and set with
[setIndent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextlistformat.html#setIndent)().

The style used to decorate each item is set with
[setStyle](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextlistformat.html#setStyle)() and can
be read with the
[style](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextlistformat.html#style)() function. The
style controls the type of bullet points and numbering scheme used for items in the
list. Note that lists that use the decimal numbering scheme begin counting at 1 rather
than 0\.

Style properties can be set to further configure the appearance of list items; for
example, the
[ListNumberPrefix](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextformat.html#Property-enum)
and
[ListNumberSuffix](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextformat.html#Property-enum)
properties can be used to customize the numbers used in an ordered list so that they
appear as (1), (2), (3), etc.:

```
QTextListFormat listFormat;

listFormat.setStyle(QTextListFormat::ListDecimal);
listFormat.setNumberPrefix("(");
listFormat.setNumberSuffix(")");

cursor.insertList(listFormat);
```

## Detailed Description

The common grouping text objects are lists
([QTextList](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextlist.html)), frames
([QTextFrame](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextframe.html)), and tables
([QTextTable](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtexttable.html)). A text object has an
associated [format](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextobject.html#format)() and
[document](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextobject.html#document)().

There are essentially two kinds of text objects: those that are used with blocks (block
formats), and those that are used with characters (character formats). The first kind
are derived from
[QTextBlockGroup](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextblockgroup.html), and the
second kind from [QTextFrame](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextframe.html).

You rarely need to use this class directly. When creating custom text objects, you will
also need to reimplement
[QTextDocument::createObject](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html#createObject)()
which acts as a factory method for creating text objects.

## Detailed Description

QTextStream can operate on a
[QIODevice](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qiodevice.html), a
[QByteArray](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qbytearray.html) or a
[QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html). Using QTextStream's
streaming operators, you can conveniently read and write words, lines and numbers. For
generating text, QTextStream supports formatting options for field padding and
alignment, and formatting of numbers. Example:

```
QFile data("output.txt");
if (data.open(QFile::WriteOnly | QFile::Truncate)) {
    QTextStream out(&data);
    out << "Result: " << qSetFieldWidth(10) << left << 3.14 << 2.7;
    // writes "Result: 3.14      2.7       "
}
```

It's also common to use QTextStream to read console input and write console output.
QTextStream is locale aware, and will automatically decode standard input using the
correct codec. Example:

```
QTextStream stream(stdin);
QString line;
while (stream.readLineInto(&line)) {
    ...
}
```

Besides using QTextStream's constructors, you can also set the device or string
QTextStream operates on by calling
[setDevice](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextstream.html#setDevice)() or
[setString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextstream.html#setString)(). You can
seek to a position by calling
[seek](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextstream.html#seek)(), and
[atEnd](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextstream.html#atEnd)() will return true
when there is no data left to be read. If you call
[flush](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextstream.html#flush)(), QTextStream will
empty all data from its write buffer into the device and call
[flush](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextstream.html#flush)() on the device.

Internally, QTextStream uses a Unicode based buffer, and
[QTextCodec](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcodec.html) is used by QTextStream
to automatically support different character sets. By default,
[QTextCodec::codecForLocale](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcodec.html#codecForLocale)()
is used for reading and writing, but you can also set the codec by calling
[setCodec](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextstream.html#setCodec)(). Automatic
Unicode detection is also supported. When this feature is enabled (the default
behavior), QTextStream will detect the UTF-16 or the UTF-32 BOM (Byte Order Mark) and
switch to the appropriate UTF codec when reading. QTextStream does not write a BOM by
default, but you can enable this by calling
[setGenerateByteOrderMark](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextstream.html#setGenerateByteOrderMark)(true).
When QTextStream operates on a
[QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html) directly, the codec is
disabled.

There are three general ways to use QTextStream when reading text files:

- Chunk by chunk, by calling [readLine](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextstream.html#readLine)() or [readAll](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextstream.html#readAll)().
- Word by word. QTextStream supports streaming into [QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html)s, [QByteArray](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qbytearray.html)s and char\* buffers. Words are delimited by space, and leading white space is automatically skipped.
- Character by character, by streaming into [QChar](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qchar.html) or char types. This method is often used for convenient input handling when parsing files, independent of character encoding and end-of-line semantics. To skip white space, call [skipWhiteSpace](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextstream.html#skipWhiteSpace)().

Since the text stream uses a buffer, you should not read from the stream using the
implementation of a superclass. For instance, if you have a
[QFile](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfile.html) and read from it directly using
[QFile::readLine](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qiodevice.html#readLine)() instead
of using the stream, the text stream's internal position will be out of sync with the
file's position.

By default, when reading numbers from a stream of text, QTextStream will automatically
detect the number's base representation. For example, if the number starts with "0x", it
is assumed to be in hexadecimal form. If it starts with the digits 1-9, it is assumed to
be in decimal form, and so on. You can set the integer base, thereby disabling the
automatic detection, by calling
[setIntegerBase](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextstream.html#setIntegerBase)().
Example:

```
QTextStream in("0x50 0x20");
int firstNumber, secondNumber;

in >> firstNumber;             // firstNumber == 80
in >> dec >> secondNumber;     // secondNumber == 0

char ch;
in >> ch;                      // ch == 'x'
```

QTextStream supports many formatting options for generating text. You can set the field
width and pad character by calling
[setFieldWidth](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextstream.html#setFieldWidth)() and
[setPadChar](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextstream.html#setPadChar)(). Use
[setFieldAlignment](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextstream.html#setFieldAlignment)()
to set the alignment within each field. For real numbers, call
[setRealNumberNotation](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextstream.html#setRealNumberNotation)()
and
[setRealNumberPrecision](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextstream.html#setRealNumberPrecision)()
to set the notation
([SmartNotation](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextstream.html#RealNumberNotation-enum),
[ScientificNotation](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextstream.html#RealNumberNotation-enum),
[FixedNotation](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextstream.html#RealNumberNotation-enum))
and precision in digits of the generated number. Some extra number formatting options
are also available through
[setNumberFlags](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextstream.html#setNumberFlags)().

### [qint64](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtglobal.html#qint64-typedef) QTextStream::pos() const

Returns the device position corresponding to the current position of the stream, or -1
if an error occurs (e.g., if there is no device or string, or if there's a device
error).

Because [QTextStream](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextstream.html) is buffered,
this function may have to seek the device to reconstruct a valid device position. This
operation can be expensive, so you may want to avoid calling this function in a tight
loop.

This function was introduced in Qt 4.2.

**See also** [seek](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextstream.html#seek)().

### [QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html) QTextStream::readAll()

Reads the entire content of the stream, and returns it as a
[QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html). Avoid this function when
working on large files, as it will consume a significant amount of memory.

Calling [readLine()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextstream.html#readLine) is

PythonQt.Qt.QTextStream.readLine.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

### [QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html) QTextStream::readLine([qint64](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtglobal.html#qint64-typedef) *maxlen* \= 0\)

Reads one line of text from the stream, and returns it as a
[QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html). The maximum allowed line
length is set to *maxlen*. If the stream contains lines longer than this, then the lines
will be split after *maxlen* characters and returned in parts.

If *maxlen* is 0, the lines can be of any length.

The returned line has no trailing end-of-line characters ("\\n" or "\\r\\n"), so calling
[QString::trimmed](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html#trimmed)() can be
unnecessary.

If the stream has read to the end of the file, readLine() will return a null
[QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html). For strings, or for devices
that support it, you can explicitly test for the end of the stream using
[atEnd](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextstream.html#atEnd)().

**See also** [readAll](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextstream.html#readAll)()
and [QIODevice::readLine](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qiodevice.html#readLine)().

PythonQt.Qt.QTextStream.readLineInto.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

### bool QTextStream::readLineInto([QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html) \**line*, [qint64](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtglobal.html#qint64-typedef) *maxlen* \= 0\)

Reads one line of text from the stream into *line*. If *line* is `nullptr`, the read
line is not stored.

The maximum allowed line length is set to *maxlen*. If the stream contains lines longer
than this, then the lines will be split after *maxlen* characters and returned in parts.

If *maxlen* is 0, the lines can be of any length.

The resulting line has no trailing end-of-line characters ("\\n" or "\\r\\n"), so
calling [QString::trimmed](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html#trimmed)()
can be unnecessary.

If *line* has sufficient capacity for the data that is about to be read, this function
may not need to allocate new memory. Because of this, it can be faster than
[readLine](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextstream.html#readLine)().

Returns `false` if the stream has read to the end of the file or an error has occurred;
otherwise returns `true`. The contents in *line* before the call are discarded in any
case.

This function was introduced in Qt 5.5.

**See also** [readAll](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextstream.html#readAll)()
and [QIODevice::readLine](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qiodevice.html#readLine)().

### void QTextStream::setAutoDetectUnicode(bool *enabled*)

If *enabled* is true, [QTextStream](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextstream.html)
will attempt to detect Unicode encoding by peeking into the stream data to see if it can
find the UTF-8, UTF-16, or UTF-32 Byte Order Mark (BOM). If this mark is found,
[QTextStream](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextstream.html) will replace the
current codec with the UTF codec.

This function can be used together with
[setCodec](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextstream.html#setCodec)(). It is common
to set the codec to UTF-8, and then enable UTF-16 detection.

**See also**
[autoDetectUnicode](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextstream.html#autoDetectUnicode)(),
[setCodec](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextstream.html#setCodec)(), and
[QTextCodec::codecForUtfText](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcodec.html#codecForUtfText)().

PythonQt.Qt.QTextStream.setCodec.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

### void QTextStream::setCodec([QTextCodec](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcodec.html) \**codec*)

Sets the codec for this stream to *codec*. The codec is used for decoding any data that
is read from the assigned device, and for encoding any data that is written. By default,
[QTextCodec::codecForLocale](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcodec.html#codecForLocale)()
is used, and automatic unicode detection is enabled.

If [QTextStream](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextstream.html) operates on a
string, this function does nothing.

**Warning:** If you call this function while the text stream is reading from an open
sequential socket, the internal buffer may still contain text decoded using the old
codec.

**See also** [codec](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextstream.html#codec)(),
[setAutoDetectUnicode](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextstream.html#setAutoDetectUnicode)(),
and [setLocale](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextstream.html#setLocale)().

### void QTextStream::setCodec(const char \**codecName*)

Sets the codec for this stream to the
[QTextCodec](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcodec.html) for the encoding
specified by *codecName*. Common values for `codecName` include "ISO 8859-1", "UTF-8",
and "UTF-16". If the encoding isn't recognized, nothing happens.

Example:

```
QTextStream out(&file);
out.setCodec("UTF-8");
```

**See also**
[QTextCodec::codecForName](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcodec.html#codecForName)()
and [setLocale](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextstream.html#setLocale)().

### void QTextStream::setFieldWidth(int *width*)

Sets the current field width to *width*. If *width* is 0 (the default), the field width
is equal to the length of the generated text.

**Note:** The field width applies to every element appended to this stream after this
function has been called (e.g., it also pads endl). This behavior is different from
similar classes in the STL, where the field width only applies to the next element.

[fieldWidth](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextstream.html#fieldWidth)() and

### void QTextStream::setIntegerBase(int *base*)

Sets the base of integers to *base*, both for reading and for generating numbers. *base*
can be either 2 (binary), 8 (octal), 10 (decimal) or 16 (hexadecimal). If *base* is 0,
[QTextStream](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextstream.html) will attempt to
detect the base by inspecting the data on the stream. When generating numbers,
[QTextStream](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextstream.html) assumes base is 10
unless the base has been set explicitly.

**See also**
[integerBase](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextstream.html#integerBase)(),
[QString::number](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html#number)(), and

### void QTextStream::setPadChar([QChar](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qchar.html) *ch*)

Sets the pad character to *ch*. The default value is the ASCII space character (' '), or
[QChar](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qchar.html)(0x20). This character is used to
fill in the space in fields when generating text.

Example:

```
QString s;
QTextStream out(&s);
out.setFieldWidth(10);
out.setFieldAlignment(QTextStream::AlignCenter);
out.setPadChar('-');
out << "Qt" << "rocks!";
```

The string `s` contains:

```
----Qt------rocks!--
```

**See also** [padChar](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextstream.html#padChar)()
and
[setFieldWidth](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextstream.html#setFieldWidth)().

PythonQt.Qt.QTextTable.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

A table is a group of cells ordered into rows and columns. Each table contains at least
one row and one column. Each cell contains a block, and is surrounded by a frame.

Tables are usually created and inserted into a document with the
[QTextCursor::insertTable](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcursor.html#insertTable)()
function. For example, we can insert a table with three rows and two columns at the
current cursor position in an editor using the following lines of code:

```
    QTextCursor cursor(editor->textCursor());
    cursor.movePosition(QTextCursor::Start);

    QTextTable *table = cursor.insertTable(rows, columns, tableFormat);
```

The table format is either defined when the table is created or changed later with
[setFormat](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtexttable.html#setFormat)().

The table currently being edited by the cursor is found with
[QTextCursor::currentTable](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcursor.html#currentTable)().
This allows its format or dimensions to be changed after it has been inserted into a
document.

A table's size can be changed with
[resize](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtexttable.html#resize)(), or by using
[insertRows](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtexttable.html#insertRows)(),
[insertColumns](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtexttable.html#insertColumns)(),
[removeRows](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtexttable.html#removeRows)(), or
[removeColumns](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtexttable.html#removeColumns)(). Use
[cellAt](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtexttable.html#cellAt)() to retrieve table
cells.

The starting and ending positions of table rows can be found by moving a cursor within a
table, and using the
[rowStart](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtexttable.html#rowStart)() and
[rowEnd](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtexttable.html#rowEnd)() functions to
obtain cursors at the start and end of each row.

Rows and columns within a QTextTable can be merged and split using the
[mergeCells](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtexttable.html#mergeCells)() and
[splitCell](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtexttable.html#splitCell)() functions.
However, only cells that span multiple rows or columns can be split. (Merging or
splitting does not increase or decrease the number of rows and columns.)

Note that if you have merged multiple columns and rows into one cell, you will not be
able to split the merged cell into new cells spanning over more than one row or column.
To be able to split cells spanning over several rows and columns you need to do this
over several iterations.

| Original Table | Suppose we have a 2x3 table of names and addresses. To merge both columns in the first row we invoke [mergeCells](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtexttable.html#mergeCells)() with *row* \= 0, *column* \= 0, *numRows* \= 1 and *numColumns* \= 2\. ```     table->mergeCells(0, 0, 1, 2); ``` |
| --- | --- |
|  | This gives us the following table. To split the first row of the table back into two cells, we invoke the [splitCell](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtexttable.html#splitCell)() function with *numRows* and *numCols* \= 1\. ```     table->splitCell(0, 0, 1, 1); ``` |
| Split Table | This results in the original table. |

## Detailed Description

Table cells are pieces of document structure that belong to a table. The table orders
cells into particular rows and columns; cells can also span multiple columns and rows.

Cells are usually created when a table is inserted into a document with
[QTextCursor::insertTable](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcursor.html#insertTable)(),
but they are also created and destroyed when a table is resized.

Cells contain information about their location in a table; you can obtain the
[row](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtexttablecell.html#row)() and
[column](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtexttablecell.html#column)() numbers of a
cell, and its
[rowSpan](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtexttablecell.html#rowSpan)() and
[columnSpan](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtexttablecell.html#columnSpan)().

The [format](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtexttablecell.html#format)() of a cell
describes the default character format of its contents. The
[firstCursorPosition](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtexttablecell.html#firstCursorPosition)()
and
[lastCursorPosition](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtexttablecell.html#lastCursorPosition)()
functions are used to obtain the extent of the cell in the document.

PythonQt.Qt.QTextTableFormat.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

A table is a group of cells ordered into rows and columns. Each table contains at least
one row and one column. Each cell contains a block. Tables in rich text documents are
formatted using the properties defined in this class.

Tables are horizontally justified within their parent frame according to the table's
alignment. This can be read with the
[alignment](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtexttableformat.html#alignment)()
function and set with
[setAlignment](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtexttableformat.html#setAlignment)().

Cells within the table are separated by cell spacing. The number of pixels between cells
is set with
[setCellSpacing](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtexttableformat.html#setCellSpacing)()
and read with
[cellSpacing](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtexttableformat.html#cellSpacing)().
The contents of each cell is surrounded by cell padding. The number of pixels between
each cell edge and its contents is set with
[setCellPadding](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtexttableformat.html#setCellPadding)()
and read with
[cellPadding](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtexttableformat.html#cellPadding)().

![](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/images/qtexttableformat-cell.png)

The table's background color can be read with the
[background](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextformat.html#background)() function,
and can be specified with
[setBackground](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextformat.html#setBackground)().
The background color of each cell can be set independently, and will control the color
of the cell within the padded area.

The table format also provides a way to constrain the widths of the columns in the
table. Columns can be assigned a fixed width, a variable width, or a percentage of the
available width (see
[QTextLength](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextlength.html)). The
[columns](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtexttableformat.html#columns)() function
returns the number of columns with constraints, and the
[columnWidthConstraints](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtexttableformat.html#columnWidthConstraints)()
function returns the constraints defined for the table. These quantities can also be set
by calling
[setColumnWidthConstraints](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtexttableformat.html#setColumnWidthConstraints)()
with a vector containing new constraints. If no constraints are required,
[clearColumnWidthConstraints](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtexttableformat.html#clearColumnWidthConstraints)()
can be used to remove them.

## Detailed Description

QThreadPool manages and recycles individual
[QThread](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qthread.html) objects to help reduce thread
creation costs in programs that use threads. Each Qt application has one global
QThreadPool object, which can be accessed by calling
[globalInstance](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qthreadpool.html#globalInstance)().

To use one of the QThreadPool threads, subclass
[QRunnable](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qrunnable.html) and implement the run()
virtual function. Then create an object of that class and pass it to
[QThreadPool::start](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qthreadpool.html#start)().

```
class HelloWorldTask : public QRunnable
{
    void run() override
    {
        qDebug() << "Hello world from thread" << QThread::currentThread();
    }
};

HelloWorldTask *hello = new HelloWorldTask();
// QThreadPool takes ownership and deletes 'hello' automatically
QThreadPool::globalInstance()->start(hello);
```

QThreadPool deletes the [QRunnable](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qrunnable.html)
automatically by default. Use
[QRunnable::setAutoDelete](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qrunnable.html#setAutoDelete)()
to change the auto-deletion flag.

QThreadPool supports executing the same
[QRunnable](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qrunnable.html) more than once by calling
tryStart(this) from within
[QRunnable::run](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qrunnable.html#run)(). If autoDelete
is enabled the [QRunnable](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qrunnable.html) will be
deleted when the last thread exits the run function. Calling
[start](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qthreadpool.html#start)() multiple times with
the same [QRunnable](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qrunnable.html) when autoDelete
is enabled creates a race condition and is not recommended.

Threads that are unused for a certain amount of time will expire. The default expiry
timeout is 30000 milliseconds (30 seconds). This can be changed using
[setExpiryTimeout](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qthreadpool.html#expiryTimeout-prop)().
Setting a negative expiry timeout disables the expiry mechanism.

Call
[maxThreadCount](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qthreadpool.html#maxThreadCount-prop)()
to query the maximum number of threads to be used. If needed, you can change the limit
with
[setMaxThreadCount](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qthreadpool.html#maxThreadCount-prop)().
The default
[maxThreadCount](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qthreadpool.html#maxThreadCount-prop)()
is
[QThread::idealThreadCount](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qthread.html#idealThreadCount)().
The
[activeThreadCount](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qthreadpool.html#activeThreadCount-prop)()
function returns the number of threads currently doing work.

The reserveThread() function reserves a thread for external use. Use releaseThread()
when your are done with the thread, so that it may be reused. Essentially, these
functions temporarily increase or reduce the active thread count and are useful when
implementing time-consuming operations that are not visible to the QThreadPool.

Note that QThreadPool is a low-level class for managing threads, see the Qt Concurrent
module for higher level alternatives.

### expiryTimeout : int

Threads that are unused for *expiryTimeout* milliseconds are considered to have expired
and will exit. Such threads will be restarted as needed. The default *expiryTimeout* is
30000 milliseconds (30 seconds). If *expiryTimeout* is negative, newly created threads
will not expire, e.g., they will not exit until the thread pool is destroyed.

Note that setting *expiryTimeout* has no effect on already running threads. Only newly
created threads will use the new *expiryTimeout*. We recommend setting the
*expiryTimeout* immediately after creating the thread pool, but before calling
[start](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qthreadpool.html#start)().

### void QThreadPool::start([QRunnable](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qrunnable.html) \**runnable*, int *priority* \= 0\)

Reserves a thread and uses it to run *runnable*, unless this thread will make the
current thread count exceed
[maxThreadCount](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qthreadpool.html#maxThreadCount-prop)().
In that case, *runnable* is added to a run queue instead. The *priority* argument can be
used to control the run queue's order of execution.

Note that the thread pool takes ownership of the *runnable* if
[runnable-\>autoDelete()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qrunnable.html#autoDelete)
returns `true`, and the *runnable* will be deleted automatically by the thread pool
after the [runnable-\>run()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qrunnable.html#run)
returns. If
[runnable-\>autoDelete()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qrunnable.html#autoDelete)
returns `false`, ownership of *runnable* remains with the caller. Note that changing the
auto-deletion on *runnable* after calling this functions results in undefined behavior.

PythonQt.Qt.QTime.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

A QTime object contains a clock time, which it can express as the numbers of hours,
minutes, seconds, and milliseconds since midnight. It provides functions for comparing
times and for manipulating a time by adding a number of milliseconds.

QTime uses the 24-hour clock format; it has no concept of AM/PM. Unlike
[QDateTime](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdatetime.html), QTime knows nothing
about time zones or daylight-saving time (DST).

A QTime object is typically created either by giving the number of hours, minutes,
seconds, and milliseconds explicitly, or by using the static function
[currentTime](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtime.html#currentTime)(), which
creates a QTime object that represents the system's local time.

The [hour](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtime.html#hour)(),
[minute](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtime.html#minute)(),
[second](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtime.html#second)(), and
[msec](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtime.html#msec)() functions provide access to
the number of hours, minutes, seconds, and milliseconds of the time. The same
information is provided in textual format by the
[toString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtime.html#toString)() function.

The [addSecs](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtime.html#addSecs)() and
[addMSecs](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtime.html#addMSecs)() functions provide
the time a given number of seconds or milliseconds later than a given time.
Correspondingly, the number of seconds or milliseconds between two times can be found
using [secsTo](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtime.html#secsTo)() or
[msecsTo](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtime.html#msecsTo)().

QTime provides a full set of operators to compare two QTime objects; an earlier time is
considered smaller than a later one; if
A.[msecsTo](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtime.html#msecsTo)(B) is positive, then
A \< B.

### QTime QTime::addMSecs(int *ms*) const

Returns a [QTime](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtime.html) object containing a
time *ms* milliseconds later than the time of this object (or earlier if *ms* is
negative).

Note that the time will wrap if it passes midnight. See
[addSecs](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtime.html#addSecs)() for an example.

Returns a null time if this time is invalid.

**See also** [addSecs](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtime.html#addSecs)(),
[msecsTo](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtime.html#msecsTo)(), and

PythonQt.Qt.QTime.addSecs.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

### QTime QTime::addSecs(int *s*) const

Returns a [QTime](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtime.html) object containing a
time *s* seconds later than the time of this object (or earlier if *s* is negative).

Note that the time will wrap if it passes midnight.

Returns a null time if this time is invalid.

Example:

```
QTime n(14, 0, 0);                // n == 14:00:00
QTime t;
t = n.addSecs(70);                // t == 14:01:10
t = n.addSecs(-70);               // t == 13:58:50
t = n.addSecs(10 * 60 * 60 + 5);  // t == 00:00:05
t = n.addSecs(-15 * 60 * 60);     // t == 23:00:00
```

**See also** [addMSecs](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtime.html#addMSecs)(),
[secsTo](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtime.html#secsTo)(), and
[QDateTime::addSecs](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdatetime.html#addSecs)().

### `[static]` QTime QTime::currentTime()

Returns the current time as reported by the system clock.

Note that the accuracy depends on the accuracy of the underlying operating system; not
all systems provide 1-millisecond accuracy.

Furthermore, currentTime() only increases within each day; it shall drop by 24 hours
each time midnight passes; and, beside this, changes in it may not correspond to elapsed
time, if a daylight-saving transition intervenes.

**See also**
[QDateTime::currentDateTime](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdatetime.html#currentDateTime)()
and
[QDateTime::currentDateTimeUtc](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdatetime.html#currentDateTimeUtc)().
