Qt 5 reference:

### [QColor](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcolor.html#QColor) QColor::darker(int *factor* \= 200\) const

Returns a darker (or lighter) color, but does not change this object.

If the *factor* is greater than 100, this functions returns a darker color. Setting
*factor* to 300 returns a color that has one-third the brightness. If the *factor* is
less than 100, the return color is lighter, but we recommend using the
[lighter](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcolor.html#lighter)() function for this
purpose. If the *factor* is 0 or negative, the return value is unspecified.

The function converts the current color to HSV, divides the value (V) component by
*factor* and converts the color back to it's original color spec.

This function was introduced in Qt 4.3.

**See also** [lighter](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcolor.html#lighter)() and
[isValid](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcolor.html#isValid)().

Qt 5 reference:

### [QColor](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcolor.html#QColor) QColor::lighter(int *factor* \= 150\) const

Returns a lighter (or darker) color, but does not change this object.

If the *factor* is greater than 100, this functions returns a lighter color. Setting
*factor* to 150 returns a color that is 50% brighter. If the *factor* is less than 100,
the return color is darker, but we recommend using the
[darker](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcolor.html#darker)() function for this
purpose. If the *factor* is 0 or negative, the return value is unspecified.

The function converts the current color to HSV, multiplies the value (V) component by
*factor* and converts the color back to it's original color spec.

This function was introduced in Qt 4.3.

**See also** [darker](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcolor.html#darker)() and
[isValid](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcolor.html#isValid)().

### void QColor::setNamedColor(const [QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html) \&*name*)

Sets the RGB value of this [QColor](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcolor.html) to
*name*, which may be in one of these formats:

- #RGB (each of R, G, and B is a single hex digit)
- #RRGGBB
- #AARRGGBB (Since 5.2)
- #RRRGGGBBB
- #RRRRGGGGBBBB
- A name from the list of colors defined in the list of [SVG color keyword names](https://www.w3.org/TR/SVG11/types.html#ColorKeywords) provided by the World Wide Web Consortium; for example, "steelblue" or "gainsboro". These color names work on all platforms. Note that these color names are *not* the same as defined by the [Qt::GlobalColor](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#GlobalColor-enum) enums, e.g. "green" and [Qt::green](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#GlobalColor-enum) does not refer to the same color.
- `transparent` \- representing the absence of a color.

The color is invalid if *name* cannot be parsed.

**See also** [QColor](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcolor.html#QColor)(),
[name](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcolor.html#name)(), and

PythonQt.QtGui.QColorDialog.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

The color dialog's function is to allow users to choose colors. For example, you might
use this in a drawing program to allow the user to set the brush color.

The static functions provide modal color dialogs.

The static [getColor](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcolordialog.html#getColor)()
function shows the dialog, and allows the user to specify a color. This function can
also be used to let users choose a color with a level of transparency: pass the
[ShowAlphaChannel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcolordialog.html#ColorDialogOption-enum)
option as an additional argument.

The user can store
[customCount](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcolordialog.html#customCount)()
different custom colors. The custom colors are shared by all color dialogs, and
remembered during the execution of the program. Use
[setCustomColor](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcolordialog.html#setCustomColor)()
to set the custom colors, and use
[customColor](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcolordialog.html#customColor)() to get
them.

When pressing the "Pick Screen Color" button, the cursor changes to a haircross and the
colors on the screen are scanned. The user can pick up one by clicking the mouse or the
Enter button. Pressing Escape restores the last color selected before entering this
mode.

The [Standard
Dialogs](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtwidgets-dialogs-standarddialogs-example.html)
example shows how to use QColorDialog as well as other built-in Qt dialogs.

![A color dialog in the Fusion widget
style.](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/images/fusion-colordialog.png)

## Detailed Description

QColumnView displays a model in a number of QListViews, one for each hierarchy in the
tree. This is sometimes referred to as a cascading list.

The QColumnView class is one of the [Model/View
Classes](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/model-view-programming.html#model-view-classes)
and is part of Qt's [model/view
framework](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/model-view-programming.html).

QColumnView implements the interfaces defined by the
[QAbstractItemView](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemview.html) class to
allow it to display data provided by models derived from the
[QAbstractItemModel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html) class.

![](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/images/qcolumnview.png)

PythonQt.QtGui.QComboBox.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

![](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/images/windows-combobox.png)

A QComboBox provides a means of presenting a list of options to the user in a way that
takes up the minimum amount of screen space.

A combobox is a selection widget that displays the current item, and can pop up a list
of selectable items. A combobox may be editable, allowing the user to modify each item
in the list.

Comboboxes can contain pixmaps as well as strings; the
[insertItem](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcombobox.html#insertItem)() and
[setItemText](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcombobox.html#setItemText)() functions
are suitably overloaded. For editable comboboxes, the function
[clearEditText](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcombobox.html#clearEditText)() is
provided, to clear the displayed string without changing the combobox's contents.

There are three signals emitted if the current item of a combobox changes,
[currentIndexChanged](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcombobox.html#currentIndexChanged)(),
[currentTextChanged](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcombobox.html#currentTextChanged)()
and [activated](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcombobox.html#activated)().
[currentIndexChanged](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcombobox.html#currentIndexChanged)()
and
[currentTextChanged](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcombobox.html#currentTextChanged)()
are always emitted regardless if the change was done programmatically or by user
interaction, while
[activated](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcombobox.html#activated)() is only
emitted when the change is caused by user interaction. The
[highlighted](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcombobox.html#highlighted)() signal is
emitted when the user highlights an item in the combobox popup list. All three signals
exist in two versions, one with a
[QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html) argument and one with an
`int` argument. If the user selects or highlights a pixmap, only the `int` signals are
emitted. Whenever the text of an editable combobox is changed the
[editTextChanged](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcombobox.html#editTextChanged)()
signal is emitted.

When the user enters a new string in an editable combobox, the widget may or may not
insert it, and it can insert it in several locations. The default policy is
[InsertAtBottom](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcombobox.html#InsertPolicy-enum)
but you can change this using
[setInsertPolicy](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcombobox.html#insertPolicy-prop)().

It is possible to constrain the input to an editable combobox using
[QValidator](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qvalidator.html); see
[setValidator](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcombobox.html#setValidator)(). By
default, any input is accepted.

A combobox can be populated using the insert functions,
[insertItem](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcombobox.html#insertItem)() and
[insertItems](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcombobox.html#insertItems)() for
example. Items can be changed with
[setItemText](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcombobox.html#setItemText)(). An item
can be removed with
[removeItem](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcombobox.html#removeItem)() and all
items can be removed with
[clear](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcombobox.html#clear)(). The text of the
current item is returned by
[currentText](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcombobox.html#currentText-prop)(), and
the text of a numbered item is returned with text(). The current item can be set with
[setCurrentIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcombobox.html#currentIndex-prop)().
The number of items in the combobox is returned by
[count](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcombobox.html#count-prop)(); the maximum
number of items can be set with
[setMaxCount](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcombobox.html#maxCount-prop)(). You
can allow editing using
[setEditable](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcombobox.html#editable-prop)(). For
editable comboboxes you can set auto-completion using
[setCompleter](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcombobox.html#setCompleter)() and
whether or not the user can add duplicates is set with
[setDuplicatesEnabled](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcombobox.html#duplicatesEnabled-prop)().

QComboBox uses the [model/view
framework](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/model-view-programming.html) for its popup
list and to store its items. By default a
[QStandardItemModel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstandarditemmodel.html) stores
the items and a [QListView](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qlistview.html) subclass
displays the popuplist. You can access the model and view directly (with
[model](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcombobox.html#model)() and
[view](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcombobox.html#view)()), but QComboBox also
provides functions to set and get item data (e.g.,
[setItemData](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcombobox.html#setItemData)() and
[itemText](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcombobox.html#itemText)()). You can also
set a new model and view (with
[setModel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcombobox.html#setModel)() and
[setView](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcombobox.html#setView)()). For the text
and icon in the combobox label, the data in the model that has the
[Qt::DisplayRole](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#ItemDataRole-enum) and
[Qt::DecorationRole](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#ItemDataRole-enum) is
used. Note that you cannot alter the
[SelectionMode](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemview.html#SelectionMode-enum)
of the [view](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcombobox.html#view)(), e.g., by using
[setSelectionMode()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemview.html#selectionMode-prop).

### currentText : [QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html)

[currentIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcombobox.html#currentIndex-prop) is

PythonQt.QtGui.QCommandLinkButton.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

The command link is a new control that was introduced by Windows Vista. Its intended use
is similar to that of a radio button in that it is used to choose between a set of
mutually exclusive options. Command link buttons should not be used by themselves but
rather as an alternative to radio buttons in Wizards and dialogs and makes pressing the
"next" button redundant. The appearance is generally similar to that of a flat
pushbutton, but it allows for a descriptive text in addition to the normal button text.
By default it will also carry an arrow icon, indicating that pressing the control will
open another window or page.

PythonQt.QtGui.QCompleter.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

You can use QCompleter to provide auto completions in any Qt widget, such as
[QLineEdit](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qlineedit.html) and
[QComboBox](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcombobox.html). When the user starts
typing a word, QCompleter suggests possible ways of completing the word, based on a word
list. The word list is provided as a
[QAbstractItemModel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html). (For
simple applications, where the word list is static, you can pass a
[QStringList](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstringlist.html) to QCompleter's
constructor.)

### Basic Usage

A QCompleter is used typically with a
[QLineEdit](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qlineedit.html) or
[QComboBox](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcombobox.html). For example, here's how
to provide auto completions from a simple word list in a
[QLineEdit](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qlineedit.html):

```
QStringList wordList;
wordList << "alpha" << "omega" << "omicron" << "zeta";

QLineEdit *lineEdit = new QLineEdit(this);

QCompleter *completer = new QCompleter(wordList, this);
completer->setCaseSensitivity(Qt::CaseInsensitive);
lineEdit->setCompleter(completer);
```

A [QFileSystemModel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfilesystemmodel.html) can be
used to provide auto completion of file names. For example:

```
QCompleter *completer = new QCompleter(this);
completer->setModel(new QFileSystemModel(completer));
lineEdit->setCompleter(completer);
```

To set the model on which QCompleter should operate, call
[setModel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcompleter.html#setModel)(). By default,
QCompleter will attempt to match the [completion
prefix](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcompleter.html#completionPrefix-prop) (i.e.,
the word that the user has started typing) against the
[Qt::EditRole](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#ItemDataRole-enum) data stored
in column 0 in the model case sensitively. This can be changed using
[setCompletionRole](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcompleter.html#completionRole-prop)(),
[setCompletionColumn](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcompleter.html#completionColumn-prop)(),
and
[setCaseSensitivity](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcompleter.html#caseSensitivity-prop)().

If the model is sorted on the column and role that are used for completion, you can call
[setModelSorting](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcompleter.html#modelSorting-prop)()
with either
[QCompleter::CaseSensitivelySortedModel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcompleter.html#ModelSorting-enum)
or
[QCompleter::CaseInsensitivelySortedModel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcompleter.html#ModelSorting-enum)
as the argument. On large models, this can lead to significant performance improvements,
because QCompleter can then use binary search instead of linear search. The binary
search only works when the
[filterMode](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcompleter.html#filterMode-prop) is
[Qt::MatchStartsWith](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#MatchFlag-enum).

The model can be a [list
model](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractlistmodel.html), a [table
model](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstracttablemodel.html), or a [tree
model](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html). Completion on tree
models is slightly more involved and is covered in the [Handling Tree
Models](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcompleter.html#handling-tree-models) section
below.

The
[completionMode](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcompleter.html#completionMode-prop)()
determines the mode used to provide completions to the user.

### Iterating Through Completions

To retrieve a single candidate string, call
[setCompletionPrefix](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcompleter.html#completionPrefix-prop)()
with the text that needs to be completed and call
[currentCompletion](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcompleter.html#currentCompletion)().
You can iterate through the list of completions as below:

```
for (int i = 0; completer->setCurrentRow(i); i++)
    qDebug() << completer->currentCompletion() << " is match number " << i;
```

[completionCount](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcompleter.html#completionCount)()
returns the total number of completions for the current prefix.
[completionCount](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcompleter.html#completionCount)()
should be avoided when possible, since it requires a scan of the entire model.

### The Completion Model

[completionModel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcompleter.html#completionModel)()
return a list model that contains all possible completions for the current completion
prefix, in the order in which they appear in the model. This model can be used to
display the current completions in a custom view. Calling
[setCompletionPrefix](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcompleter.html#completionPrefix-prop)()
automatically refreshes the completion model.

### Handling Tree Models

QCompleter can look for completions in tree models, assuming that any item (or sub-item
or sub-sub-item) can be unambiguously represented as a string by specifying the path to
the item. The completion is then performed one level at a time.

Let's take the example of a user typing in a file system path. The model is a
(hierarchical)
[QFileSystemModel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfilesystemmodel.html). The
completion occurs for every element in the path. For example, if the current text is
`C:\Wind`, QCompleter might suggest `Windows` to complete the current path element.
Similarly, if the current text is `C:\Windows\Sy`, QCompleter might suggest `System`.

For this kind of completion to work, QCompleter needs to be able to split the path into
a list of strings that are matched at each level. For `C:\Windows\Sy`, it needs to be
split as "C:", "Windows" and "Sy". The default implementation of
[splitPath](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcompleter.html#splitPath)(), splits the
[completionPrefix](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcompleter.html#completionPrefix-prop)
using [QDir::separator](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdir.html#separator)() if the
model is a [QFileSystemModel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfilesystemmodel.html).

To provide completions, QCompleter needs to know the path from an index. This is
provided by
[pathFromIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcompleter.html#pathFromIndex)(). The
default implementation of
[pathFromIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcompleter.html#pathFromIndex)(),
returns the data for the [edit
role](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#ItemDataRole-enum) for list models and
the absolute file path if the mode is a
[QFileSystemModel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfilesystemmodel.html).

### `[signal]` void QCompleter::activated(const [QModelIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmodelindex.html) \&*index*)

This signal is sent when an item in the
[popup](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcompleter.html#popup)() is activated by the
user. (by clicking or pressing return). The item's *index* in the
[completionModel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcompleter.html#completionModel)()
is given.

**Note:** Signal *activated* is overloaded in this class. To connect to this signal by
using the function pointer syntax, Qt provides a convenient helper for obtaining the
function pointer as shown in this example:

```
connect(completer, QOverload<const QModelIndex &>::of(&QCompleter::activated),
    [=](const QModelIndex &index){ /* ... */ });
```

### `[signal]` void QCompleter::activated(const [QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html) \&*text*)

This signal is sent when an item in the
[popup](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcompleter.html#popup)() is activated by the
user (by clicking or pressing return). The item's *text* is given.

**Note:** Signal *activated* is overloaded in this class. To connect to this signal by
using the function pointer syntax, Qt provides a convenient helper for obtaining the
function pointer as shown in this example:

```
connect(completer, QOverload<const QString &>::of(&QCompleter::activated),
    [=](const QString &text){ /* ... */ });
```

### `[slot]` void QCompleter::complete(const [QRect](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qrect.html) \&*rect* \= QRect())

For
[QCompleter::PopupCompletion](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcompleter.html#CompletionMode-enum)
and QCompletion::UnfilteredPopupCompletion modes, calling this function displays the
popup displaying the current completions. By default, if *rect* is not specified, the
popup is displayed on the bottom of the
[widget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcompleter.html#widget)(). If *rect* is
specified the popup is displayed on the left edge of the rectangle.

For
[QCompleter::InlineCompletion](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcompleter.html#CompletionMode-enum)
mode, the
[highlighted](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcompleter.html#highlighted)() signal
is fired with the current completion.

contains all the possible matches for the current completion prefix. The completion
model is auto-updated to reflect the current completions.

[QAbstractItemModel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html) purely

[QAbstractProxyModel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractproxymodel.html)
subclass.

### filterMode : [Qt::MatchFlags](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#MatchFlag-enum)

This property controls how filtering is performed.

If filterMode is set to
[Qt::MatchStartsWith](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#MatchFlag-enum), only
those entries that start with the typed characters will be displayed.
[Qt::MatchContains](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#MatchFlag-enum) will
display the entries that contain the typed characters, and
[Qt::MatchEndsWith](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#MatchFlag-enum) the ones
that end with the typed characters.

Setting filterMode to any other
[Qt::MatchFlag](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#MatchFlag-enum) will issue a
warning, and no action will be performed. Because of this, the `Qt::MatchCaseSensitive`
flag has no effect. Use the
[caseSensitivity](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcompleter.html#caseSensitivity-prop)
property to control case sensitivity.

The default mode is
[Qt::MatchStartsWith](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#MatchFlag-enum).

This property was introduced in Qt 5.2.

**Access functions:**

### modelSorting : [ModelSorting](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcompleter.html#ModelSorting-enum)

This property holds the way the model is sorted

By default, no assumptions are made about the order of the items in the model that
provides the completions.

If the model's data for the
[completionColumn](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcompleter.html#completionColumn-prop)()
and
[completionRole](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcompleter.html#completionRole-prop)()
is sorted in ascending order, you can set this property to
[CaseSensitivelySortedModel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcompleter.html#ModelSorting-enum)
or
[CaseInsensitivelySortedModel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcompleter.html#ModelSorting-enum).
On large models, this can lead to significant performance improvements because the
completer object can then use a binary search algorithm instead of linear search
algorithm.

The sort order (i.e ascending or descending order) of the model is determined
dynamically by inspecting the contents of the model.

**Note:** The performance improvements described above cannot take place when the
completer's
[caseSensitivity](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcompleter.html#caseSensitivity-prop)
is different to the case sensitivity used by the model's when sorting.

**Access functions:**

| QCompleter::ModelSorting | **modelSorting**() const |
| --- | --- |

PythonQt.QtGui.QConicalGradient.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

Conical gradients interpolate interpolate colors counter-clockwise around a center
point.

![](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/images/qconicalgradient.png)

The colors in a gradient is defined using stop points of the
[QGradientStop](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgradient.html#QGradientStop-typedef)
type, i.e. a position and a color. Use the
[QGradient::setColorAt](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgradient.html#setColorAt)()
or the
[QGradient::setStops](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgradient.html#setStops)()
function to define the stop points. It is the gradient's complete set of stop points
that describes how the gradient area should be filled. If no stop points have been
specified, a gradient of black at 0 to white at 1 is used.

In addition to the functions inherited from
[QGradient](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgradient.html), the QConicalGradient
class provides the
[angle](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qconicalgradient.html#angle)() and
[center](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qconicalgradient.html#center)() functions
returning the start angle and center of the gradient.

Note that the [setSpread](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgradient.html#setSpread)()
function has no effect for conical gradients. The reason is that the conical gradient is
closed by definition, i.e. the conical gradient fills the entire circle from 0 \- 360
degrees, while the boundary of a radial or a linear gradient can be specified through
its radius or final stop points, respectively.

## Detailed Description

Context menu events are sent to widgets when a user performs an action associated with
opening a context menu. The actions required to open context menus vary between
platforms; for example, on Windows, pressing the menu button or clicking the right mouse
button will cause this event to be sent.

When this event occurs it is customary to show a
[QMenu](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmenu.html) with a context menu, if this is
relevant to the context.

Context menu events contain a special accept flag that indicates whether the receiver
accepted the event. If the event handler does not accept the event then, if possible,
whatever triggered the event will be handled as a regular input event.

Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

This class is mainly used to create mouse cursors that are associated with particular
widgets and to get and set the position of the mouse cursor.

Qt has a number of standard cursor shapes, but you can also make custom cursor shapes
based on a [QBitmap](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qbitmap.html), a mask and a
hotspot.

To associate a cursor with a widget, use
[QWidget::setCursor](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#cursor-prop)(). To
associate a cursor with all widgets (normally for a short period of time), use
[QGuiApplication::setOverrideCursor](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qguiapplication.html#setOverrideCursor)().

To set a cursor shape use
[QCursor::setShape](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcursor.html#setShape)() or use
the QCursor constructor which takes the shape as argument, or you can use one of the
predefined cursors defined in the
[Qt::CursorShape](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#CursorShape-enum) enum.

If you want to create a cursor with your own bitmap, either use the QCursor constructor
which takes a bitmap and a mask or the constructor which takes a pixmap as arguments.

To set or get the position of the mouse cursor use the static methods
[QCursor::pos](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcursor.html#pos)() and
[QCursor::setPos](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcursor.html#setPos)().

**Note:** It is possible to create a QCursor before
[QGuiApplication](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qguiapplication.html), but it is
not useful except as a place-holder for a real QCursor created after
[QGuiApplication](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qguiapplication.html). Attempting
to use a QCursor that was created before
[QGuiApplication](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qguiapplication.html) will result

[QWidget::mapToGlobal](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#mapToGlobal)() to

PythonQt.QtGui.QDataWidgetMapper.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

QDataWidgetMapper can be used to create data-aware widgets by mapping them to sections
of an item model. A section is a column of a model if the orientation is horizontal (the
default), otherwise a row.

Every time the current index changes, each widget is updated with data from the model
via the property specified when its mapping was made. If the user edits the contents of
a widget, the changes are read using the same property and written back to the model. By
default, each widget's [user
property](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qobject.html#Q_PROPERTY) is used to
transfer data between the model and the widget. Since Qt 4.3, an additional
[addMapping](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdatawidgetmapper.html#addMapping)()
function enables a named property to be used instead of the default user property.

It is possible to set an item delegate to support custom widgets. By default, a
[QItemDelegate](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qitemdelegate.html) is used to
synchronize the model with the widgets.

Let us assume that we have an item model named `model` with the following contents:

| 1 | Qt Norway | Oslo |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2 | Qt Australia | Brisbane |
| 3 | Qt USA | Palo Alto |
| 4 | Qt China | Beijing |
| 5 | Qt Germany | Berlin |

The following code will map the columns of the model to widgets called `mySpinBox`,
`myLineEdit` and `myCountryChooser`:

```
QDataWidgetMapper *mapper = new QDataWidgetMapper;
mapper->setModel(model);
mapper->addMapping(mySpinBox, 0);
mapper->addMapping(myLineEdit, 1);
mapper->addMapping(myCountryChooser, 2);
mapper->toFirst();
```

After the call to
[toFirst](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdatawidgetmapper.html#toFirst)(),
`mySpinBox` displays the value `1`, `myLineEdit` displays `Qt Norway` and
`myCountryChooser` displays `Oslo`. The navigational functions
[toFirst](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdatawidgetmapper.html#toFirst)(),
[toNext](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdatawidgetmapper.html#toNext)(),
[toPrevious](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdatawidgetmapper.html#toPrevious)(),
[toLast](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdatawidgetmapper.html#toLast)() and
[setCurrentIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdatawidgetmapper.html#currentIndex-prop)()
can be used to navigate in the model and update the widgets with contents from the
model.

The
[setRootIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdatawidgetmapper.html#setRootIndex)()
function enables a particular item in a model to be specified as the root index \-
children of this item will be mapped to the relevant widgets in the user interface.

QDataWidgetMapper supports two submit policies, `AutoSubmit` and `ManualSubmit`.
`AutoSubmit` will update the model as soon as the current widget loses focus,
`ManualSubmit` will not update the model unless
[submit](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdatawidgetmapper.html#submit)() is called.
`ManualSubmit` is useful when displaying a dialog that lets the user cancel all
modifications. Also, other views that display the model won't update until the user
finishes all their modifications and submits.

Note that QDataWidgetMapper keeps track of external modifications. If the contents of
the model are updated in another module of the application, the widgets are updated as
well.

### void QDataWidgetMapper::addMapping([QWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html) \**widget*, int *section*)

Adds a mapping between a *widget* and a *section* from the model. The *section* is a
column in the model if the orientation is horizontal (the default), otherwise a row.

For the following example, we assume a model `myModel` that has two columns: the first
one contains the names of people in a group, and the second column contains their ages.
The first column is mapped to the
[QLineEdit](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qlineedit.html) `nameLineEdit`, and the
second is mapped to the [QSpinBox](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qspinbox.html)
`ageSpinBox`:

```
QDataWidgetMapper *mapper = new QDataWidgetMapper;
mapper->setModel(myModel);
mapper->addMapping(nameLineEdit, 0);
mapper->addMapping(ageSpinBox, 1);
```

**Notes:**

- If the *widget* is already mapped to a section, the old mapping will be replaced by the new one.
- Only one-to-one mappings between sections and widgets are allowed. It is not possible to map a single section to multiple widgets, or to map a single widget to multiple sections.

**See also**
[removeMapping](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdatawidgetmapper.html#removeMapping)(),
[mappedSection](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdatawidgetmapper.html#mappedSection)(),
and
[clearMapping](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdatawidgetmapper.html#clearMapping)().

### orientation : [Qt::Orientation](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#Orientation-enum)

This property holds the orientation of the model

If the orientation is
[Qt::Horizontal](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#Orientation-enum) (the
default), a widget is mapped to a column of a data model. The widget will be populated
with the model's data from its mapped column and the row that
[currentIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdatawidgetmapper.html#currentIndex-prop)()
points at.

Use [Qt::Horizontal](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#Orientation-enum) for
tabular data that looks like this:

| 1 | Qt Norway | Oslo |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2 | Qt Australia | Brisbane |
| 3 | Qt USA | Silicon Valley |
| 4 | Qt China | Beijing |
| 5 | Qt Germany | Berlin |

If the orientation is set to
[Qt::Vertical](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#Orientation-enum), a widget is
mapped to a row. Calling
[setCurrentIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdatawidgetmapper.html#currentIndex-prop)()
will change the current column. The widget will be populates with the model's data from
its mapped row and the column that
[currentIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdatawidgetmapper.html#currentIndex-prop)()
points at.

Use [Qt::Vertical](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#Orientation-enum) for
tabular data that looks like this:

| 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Qt Norway | Qt Australia | Qt USA | Qt China | Qt Germany |
| Oslo | Brisbane | Silicon Valley | Beijing | Berlin |

Changing the orientation clears all existing mappings.

| --- | --- |
| void | **setOrientation**(Qt::Orientation *aOrientation*) |

Sets the current index to the row of the *index* if the orientation is horizontal (the
default), otherwise to the column of the *index*.

Calls
[setCurrentIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdatawidgetmapper.html#currentIndex-prop)()
internally. This convenience slot can be connected to the signal
[currentRowChanged()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qitemselectionmodel.html#currentRowChanged)
or
[currentColumnChanged()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qitemselectionmodel.html#currentColumnChanged)
of another view's [selection
model](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qitemselectionmodel.html).

The following example illustrates how to update all widgets with new data whenever the
selection of a [QTableView](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtableview.html) named
`myTableView` changes:

```
QDataWidgetMapper *mapper = new QDataWidgetMapper;
connect(myTableView->selectionModel(), &QItemSelectionModel::currentRowChanged,
        mapper, &QDataWidgetMapper::setCurrentModelIndex);
```

**See also**
[currentIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdatawidgetmapper.html#currentIndex-prop)().

### void QDataWidgetMapper::setItemDelegate([QAbstractItemDelegate](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemdelegate.html) \**delegate*)

Sets the item delegate to *delegate*. The delegate will be used to write data from the
model into the widget and from the widget to the model, using
[QAbstractItemDelegate::setEditorData](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemdelegate.html#setEditorData)()
and
[QAbstractItemDelegate::setModelData](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemdelegate.html#setModelData)().

The delegate also decides when to apply data and when to change the editor, using
[QAbstractItemDelegate::commitData](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemdelegate.html#commitData)()
and
[QAbstractItemDelegate::closeEditor](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemdelegate.html#closeEditor)().

**Warning:** You should not share the same instance of a delegate between widget mappers
or views. Doing so can cause incorrect or unintuitive editing behavior since each view
connected to a given delegate may receive the
[closeEditor()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemdelegate.html#closeEditor)
signal, and attempt to access, modify or close an editor that has already been closed.

**See also**
[itemDelegate](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdatawidgetmapper.html#itemDelegate)().

### `[slot]` bool QDataWidgetMapper::submit()

Submits all changes from the mapped widgets to the model.

For every mapped section, the item delegate reads the current value from the widget and
sets it in the model. Finally, the model's
[submit()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#submit) method is
invoked.

Returns `true` if all the values were submitted, otherwise false.

Note: For database models,
[QSqlQueryModel::lastError](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsqlquerymodel.html#lastError)()
can be used to retrieve the last error.

**See also**
[revert](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdatawidgetmapper.html#revert)() and
[setSubmitPolicy](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdatawidgetmapper.html#submitPolicy-prop)().

## Detailed Description

![](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/images/windows-dateedit.png)

Many of the properties and functions provided by QDateEdit are implemented in
[QDateTimeEdit](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdatetimeedit.html). These are the
relevant properties of this class:

- [date](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdatetimeedit.html#date) holds the date displayed by the widget.
- [minimumDate](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdatetimeedit.html#minimumDate-prop) defines the minimum (earliest) date that can be set by the user.
- [maximumDate](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdatetimeedit.html#maximumDate-prop) defines the maximum (latest) date that can be set by the user.
- [displayFormat](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdatetimeedit.html#displayFormat-prop) contains a string that is used to format the date displayed in the widget.

PythonQt.QtGui.QDateTimeEdit.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

![](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/images/windows-datetimeedit.png)

QDateTimeEdit allows the user to edit dates by using the keyboard or the arrow keys to
increase and decrease date and time values. The arrow keys can be used to move from
section to section within the QDateTimeEdit box. Dates and times appear in accordance
with the format set; see
[setDisplayFormat](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdatetimeedit.html#displayFormat-prop)().

```
QDateTimeEdit *dateEdit = new QDateTimeEdit(QDate::currentDate());
dateEdit->setMinimumDate(QDate::currentDate().addDays(-365));
dateEdit->setMaximumDate(QDate::currentDate().addDays(365));
dateEdit->setDisplayFormat("yyyy.MM.dd");
```

Here we've created a new QDateTimeEdit object initialized with today's date, and
restricted the valid date range to today plus or minus 365 days. We've set the order to
month, day, year.

The range of valid values for a QDateTimeEdit is controlled by the properties
[minimumDateTime](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdatetimeedit.html#minimumDateTime-prop),
[maximumDateTime](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdatetimeedit.html#maximumDateTime-prop),
and their respective date and time components. By default, any date-time from the start
of 100 CE to the end of 9999 CE is valid.

### Using a Pop-up Calendar Widget

QDateTimeEdit can be configured to allow a
[QCalendarWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcalendarwidget.html) to be used to
select dates. This is enabled by setting the
[calendarPopup](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdatetimeedit.html#calendarPopup-prop)
property. Additionally, you can supply a custom calendar widget for use as the calendar
pop-up by calling the
[setCalendarWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdatetimeedit.html#setCalendarWidget)()
function. The existing calendar widget can be retrieved with
[calendarWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdatetimeedit.html#calendarWidget)().

### Keyboard Tracking

When [keyboard
tracking](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractspinbox.html#keyboardTracking-prop)
is enabled (the default), every keystroke of editing a field triggers signals for value
changes.

When the allowed
[range](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdatetimeedit.html#setDateTimeRange) is
narrower than some time interval whose end it straddles, keyboard tracking prevents the
user editing the date or time to access the later part of the interval. For example, for
a range from 29.04.2020 to 02.05.2020 and an initial date of 30.04.2020, the user can
change neither the month (May 30th is outside the range) nor the day (April 2nd is
outside the range).

When keyboard tracking is disabled, changes are only signalled when focus leaves the
text field after edits have modified the content. This allows the user to edit via an
invalid date-time to reach a valid one.

### displayFormat : [QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html)

This property holds the format used to display the time/date of the date time edit.

This format is described in
[QDateTime::toString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdatetime.html#toString)() and
[QDateTime::fromString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdatetime.html#fromString)()

Example format strings (assuming that the date is 2nd of July 1969):

| Format | Result |
| --- | --- |
| dd.MM.yyyy | 02.07.1969 |
| MMM d yy | Jul 2 69 |
| MMMM d yy | July 2 69 |

Note that if you specify a two digit year, it will be interpreted to be in the century
in which the date time edit was initialized. The default century is the 21st
(2000-2099).

If you specify an invalid format the format will not be set.

### maximumDate : [QDate](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdate.html)

This property holds the maximum date of the date time edit.

Changing this property updates the date of the
[maximumDateTime](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdatetimeedit.html#maximumDateTime-prop)
property while preserving the
[maximumTime](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdatetimeedit.html#maximumTime-prop)
property. When setting this property, the
[minimumDate](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdatetimeedit.html#minimumDate-prop) is
adjusted, if necessary, to ensure that the range remains valid. When this happens, the
[minimumTime](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdatetimeedit.html#minimumTime-prop)
property is also adjusted if it is greater than the
[maximumTime](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdatetimeedit.html#maximumTime-prop)
property. Otherwise, changes to this property preserve the
[minimumDateTime](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdatetimeedit.html#minimumDateTime-prop)
property.

This property can only be set to a valid
[QDate](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdate.html) object describing a date on which
the current
[maximumTime](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdatetimeedit.html#maximumTime-prop)
property makes a valid [QDateTime](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdatetime.html)
object. The latest date that setMaximumDate() accepts is the end of 9999 CE. This is the
default for this property. This default can be restored with
[clearMaximumDateTime](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdatetimeedit.html#maximumDateTime-prop)().

### void QDateTimeEdit::setDateRange(const [QDate](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdate.html) \&*min*, const [QDate](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdate.html) \&*max*)

Set the range of allowed dates for the date time edit.

This convenience function sets the
[minimumDate](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdatetimeedit.html#minimumDate-prop)
and
[maximumDate](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdatetimeedit.html#maximumDate-prop)
properties.

```
setDateRange(min, max);
```

is analogous to:

```
setMinimumDate(min);
setMaximumDate(max);
```

If either *min* or *max* is invalid, this function does nothing. This function preserves
the
[minimumTime](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdatetimeedit.html#minimumTime-prop)
property. If *max* is less than *min*, the new
[maximumDateTime](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdatetimeedit.html#maximumDateTime-prop)
property shall be the new
[minimumDateTime](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdatetimeedit.html#minimumDateTime-prop)
property. If *max* is equal to *min* and the
[maximumTime](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdatetimeedit.html#maximumTime-prop)
property was less then the
[minimumTime](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdatetimeedit.html#minimumTime-prop)
property, the
[maximumTime](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdatetimeedit.html#maximumTime-prop)
property is set to the
[minimumTime](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdatetimeedit.html#minimumTime-prop)
property. Otherwise, this preserves the
[maximumTime](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdatetimeedit.html#maximumTime-prop)
property.

If the range is narrower then a time interval whose end it spans, for example a week
that spans the end of a month, users can only edit the date to one in the later part of
the range if keyboard-tracking is disabled.

**See also**
[minimumDate](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdatetimeedit.html#minimumDate-prop),
[maximumDate](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdatetimeedit.html#maximumDate-prop),

[maximumTime](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdatetimeedit.html#maximumTime-prop)

and
[maximumDate](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdatetimeedit.html#maximumDate-prop).
When these date properties do not coincide, times after *max* are allowed on dates
before
[maximumDate](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdatetimeedit.html#maximumDate-prop)
and times before *min* are allowed on dates after
[minimumDate](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdatetimeedit.html#minimumDate-prop).

```

```

is analogous to:

```

```

If either *min* or *max* is invalid, this function does nothing. This function preserves

[minimumDate](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdatetimeedit.html#minimumDate-prop)
and
[maximumDate](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdatetimeedit.html#maximumDate-prop)
properties. If those properties coincide and *max* is less than *min*, *min* is used as
*max*.

If the range is narrower then a time interval whose end it spans, for example the
interval from ten to an hour to ten past the same hour, users can only edit the time to
one in the later part of the range if keyboard-tracking is disabled.

## Detailed Description

Many desktop environments provide services that can be used by applications to perform
common tasks, such as opening a web page, in a way that is both consistent and takes
into account the user's application preferences.

This class contains functions that provide simple interfaces to these services that
indicate whether they succeeded or failed.

The [openUrl](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdesktopservices.html#openUrl)()
function is used to open files located at arbitrary URLs in external applications. For
URLs that correspond to resources on the local filing system (where the URL scheme is
"file"), a suitable application will be used to open the file; otherwise, a web browser
will be used to fetch and display the file.

The user's desktop settings control whether certain executable file types are opened for
browsing, or if they are executed instead. Some desktop environments are configured to
prevent users from executing files obtained from non-local URLs, or to ask the user's
permission before doing so.

### URL Handlers

The behavior of the
[openUrl](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdesktopservices.html#openUrl)() function
can be customized for individual URL schemes to allow applications to override the
default handling behavior for certain types of URLs.

The dispatch mechanism allows only one custom handler to be used for each URL scheme;
this is set using the
[setUrlHandler](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdesktopservices.html#setUrlHandler)()
function. Each handler is implemented as a slot which accepts only a single
[QUrl](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qurl.html) argument.

The existing handlers for each scheme can be removed with the
[unsetUrlHandler](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdesktopservices.html#unsetUrlHandler)()
function. This returns the handling behavior for the given scheme to the default
behavior.

This system makes it easy to implement a help system, for example. Help could be
provided in labels and text browsers using **help://myapplication/mytopic** URLs, and by
registering a handler it becomes possible to display the help text inside the
application:

```
class MyHelpHandler : public QObject
{
    Q_OBJECT
public:
    ...
public slots:
    void showHelp(const QUrl &url);
};

QDesktopServices::setUrlHandler("help", helpInstance, "showHelp");
```

If inside the handler you decide that you can't open the requested URL, you can just
call
[QDesktopServices::openUrl](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdesktopservices.html#openUrl)()
again with the same argument, and it will try to open the URL using the appropriate
mechanism for the user's desktop environment.

Combined with platform specific settings, the schemes registered by the
[openUrl](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdesktopservices.html#openUrl)() function
can also be exposed to other applications, opening up for application deep linking or a
very basic URL-based IPC mechanism.

**Note:** Since Qt 5, storageLocation() and displayName() are replaced by functionality
provided by the [QStandardPaths](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstandardpaths.html)
class.

PythonQt.QtGui.QDesktopServices.openUrl.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

### `[static]` bool QDesktopServices::openUrl(const [QUrl](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qurl.html) \&*url*)

Opens the given *url* in the appropriate Web browser for the user's desktop environment,
and returns `true` if successful; otherwise returns `false`.

If the URL is a reference to a local file (i.e., the URL scheme is "file") then it will
be opened with a suitable application instead of a Web browser.

The following example opens a file on the Windows file system residing on a path that
contains spaces:

```
QDesktopServices::openUrl(QUrl("file:///C:/Program Files", QUrl::TolerantMode));
```

If a `mailto` URL is specified, the user's e-mail client will be used to open a composer
window containing the options specified in the URL, similar to the way `mailto` links
are handled by a Web browser.

For example, the following URL contains a recipient (`user@foo.com`), a subject
(`Test`), and a message body (`Just a test`):

```
mailto:user@foo.com?subject=Test&body=Just a test
```

**Warning:** Although many e-mail clients can send attachments and are Unicode-aware,
the user may have configured their client without these features. Also, certain e-mail
clients (e.g., Lotus Notes) have problems with long URLs.

**Warning:** A return value of `true` indicates that the application has successfully
requested the operating system to open the URL in an external application. The external
application may still fail to launch or fail to open the requested URL. This result will
not be reported back to the application.

**Warning:** URLs passed to this function on iOS will not load unless their schemes are
listed in the `LSApplicationQueriesSchemes` key of the application's Info.plist file.
For more information, see the Apple Developer Documentation for
[canOpenURL(\_:)](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/uikit/uiapplication/1622952-canopenurl).
For example, the following lines enable URLs with the HTTPS scheme:

```
<key>LSApplicationQueriesSchemes</key>
<array>
    <string>https</string>
</array>
```

**See also**
[setUrlHandler](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdesktopservices.html#setUrlHandler)().

PythonQt.QtGui.QDesktopServices.setUrlHa.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

### `[static]` void QDesktopServices::setUrlHandler(const [QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html) \&*scheme*, [QObject](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qobject.html) \**receiver*, const char \**method*)

Sets the handler for the given *scheme* to be the handler *method* provided by the
*receiver* object.

This function provides a way to customize the behavior of
[openUrl](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdesktopservices.html#openUrl)(). If
[openUrl](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdesktopservices.html#openUrl)() is called
with a URL with the specified *scheme* then the given *method* on the *receiver* object
is called instead of
[QDesktopServices](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdesktopservices.html) launching
an external application.

The provided method must be implemented as a slot that only accepts a single
[QUrl](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qurl.html) argument.

```
class MyHelpHandler : public QObject
{
    Q_OBJECT
public:
    ...
public slots:
    void showHelp(const QUrl &url);
};

QDesktopServices::setUrlHandler("help", helpInstance, "showHelp");
```

To use this function for receiving data from other apps on iOS you also need to add the
custom scheme to the `CFBundleURLSchemes` list in your Info.plist file:

```
<key>CFBundleURLTypes</key>
<array>
    <dict>
        <key>CFBundleURLSchemes</key>
        <array>
            <string>myapp</string>
        </array>
    </dict>
</array>
```

For more information, see the Apple Developer Documentation for [Communicating with
Other Apps Using Custom
URLs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/uikit/core_app/allowing_apps_and_websites_to_link_to_your_content/communicating_with_other_apps_using_custom_urls?language=objc).

**Warning:** It is not possible to claim support for some well known URL schemes,
including http and https. This is only allowed for Universal Links.

To claim support for http and https the above entry in the Info.plist file is not
allowed. This is only possible when you add your domain to the Entitlements file:

```
<key>com.apple.developer.associated-domains</key>
<array>
    <string>applinks:your.domain.com</string>
</array>
```

iOS will search for /.well-known/apple-app-site-association on your domain, when the
application is installed. If you want to listen to
https://your.domain.com/help?topic\=ABCDEF you need to provide the following content
there:

```
{
    "applinks": {
        "apps": [],
        "details": [{
            "appIDs" : [ "ABCDE12345.com.example.app" ],
            "components": [{
                "/": "/help",
                "?": { "topic": "?*"}
            }]
        }]
    }
}
```

For more information, see the Apple Developer Documentation for
<https://developer.apple.com/documentation/safariservices/supporting_associated_domains_in_your_app>\[Supporting
Associated Domains}.

If setUrlHandler() is used to set a new handler for a scheme which already has a
handler, the existing handler is simply replaced with the new one. Since
[QDesktopServices](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdesktopservices.html) does not
take ownership of handlers, no objects are deleted when a handler is replaced.

Note that the handler will always be called from within the same thread that calls
[QDesktopServices::openUrl](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdesktopservices.html#openUrl)().

You must call
[unsetUrlHandler](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdesktopservices.html#unsetUrlHandler)()
before destroying the handler object, so the destruction of the handler object does not
overlap with concurrent invocations of
[openUrl](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdesktopservices.html#openUrl)() using it.

**See also**
[openUrl](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdesktopservices.html#openUrl)() and
[unsetUrlHandler](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdesktopservices.html#unsetUrlHandler)().
signatures: setUrlHandler(scheme: str, receiver: PySide2.QtCore.QObject, method: str) -> None

### `[static]` void QDesktopServices::unsetUrlHandler(const [QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html) \&*scheme*)

## Detailed Description

Systems with more than one graphics card and monitor can manage the physical screen
space available either as multiple desktops, or as a large virtual desktop.

This class provides information about the user's desktop, such as its total size, number
of screens, the geometry of each screen, and whether they are configured as separate
desktops or a single virtual desktop.

Widgets provided by Qt use this class to place tooltips, menus and dialog boxes on the
correct screen for their parent or application widgets. Applications can use this class
to obtain information that can be used to save window positions, or to place child
widgets and dialogs on one particular screen.

### Obtaining a Desktop Widget

The
[QApplication::desktop](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qapplication-obsolete.html#desktop)()
function is used to get an instance of QDesktopWidget.

The widget's
[screenGeometry](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdesktopwidget-obsolete.html#screenGeometry)()
function provides information about the geometry of the available screens with. The
number of screens available is returned by
[screenCount](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdesktopwidget-obsolete.html#screenCount-prop),
and the
[screenCountChanged](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdesktopwidget-obsolete.html#screenCountChanged)()
signal is emitted when screens are added or removed. The screen number that a particular
point or widget is located in is returned by
[screenNumber](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdesktopwidget.html#screenNumber)().

### Screen Geometry

To obtain the dimensions of a particular screen, call the
[screenGeometry](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdesktopwidget-obsolete.html#screenGeometry)()
function. On some desktop environments, not all of the screen is available for
applications to use; for example, an application dock or menu bar may take up some
space. Use the
[availableGeometry](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdesktopwidget-obsolete.html#availableGeometry)()
function to obtain the available area for applications.

QDesktopWidget also inherits the
[QWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html) properties,
[width](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#width-prop)() and
[height](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#height-prop)(), which specify
the size of the desktop. However, for desktops with multiple screens, the size of the
desktop is the union of all the screen sizes, so
[width](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#width-prop)() and
[height](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#height-prop)() should *not* be
used for computing the size of a widget to be placed on one of the screens.

On systems that are configured to use the available screens as a single, large virtual
desktop, the
[virtualDesktop](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdesktopwidget-obsolete.html#virtualDesktop-prop)
property will be set to true. In this case, the widget's size is usually the size of the
bounding rectangle of all the screens.

### Use of the Primary Screen

For an application, the screen where the main widget resides is the primary screen. This
is stored in the
[primaryScreen](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdesktopwidget-obsolete.html#primaryScreen-prop)
property. All windows opened in the context of the application should be constrained to
the boundaries of the primary screen; for example, it would be inconvenient if a dialog
box popped up on a different screen, or split over two screens.

![Managing Multiple
Screens](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/images/qdesktopwidget.png)

In the illustration above, Application One's primary screen is screen 0, and App Two's
primary screen is screen 1\.

## Detailed Description

![](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/images/windows-dial.png)

QDial is used when the user needs to control a value within a program-definable range,
and the range either wraps around (for example, with angles measured from 0 to 359
degrees) or the dialog layout needs a square widget.

Since QDial inherits from
[QAbstractSlider](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html), the dial
behaves in a similar way to a [slider](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qslider.html).
When [wrapping](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdial.html#wrapping-prop)() is false
(the default setting) there is no real difference between a slider and a dial. They both
share the same signals, slots and member functions. Which one you use depends on the
expectations of your users and on the type of application.

The dial initially emits
[valueChanged](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html#valueChanged)()
signals continuously while the slider is being moved; you can make it emit the signal
less often by disabling the
[tracking](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html#tracking-prop)
property. The
[sliderMoved](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html#sliderMoved)()
signal is emitted continuously even when tracking is disabled.

The dial also emits
[sliderPressed](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html#sliderPressed)()
and
[sliderReleased](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html#sliderReleased)()
signals when the mouse button is pressed and released. Note that the dial's value can
change without these signals being emitted since the keyboard and wheel can also be used
to change the value.

Unlike the slider, QDial attempts to draw a "nice" number of notches rather than one per
line step. If possible, the number of notches drawn is one per line step, but if there
aren't enough pixels to draw every one, QDial will skip notches to try and draw a
uniform set (e.g. by drawing every second or third notch).

Like the slider, the dial makes the
[QAbstractSlider](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html) function
[setValue](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html#value-prop)()
available as a slot.

The dial's keyboard interface is fairly simple: The **left**/**up** and
**right**/**down** arrow keys adjust the dial's
[value](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html#value-prop) by the
defined
[singleStep](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html#singleStep-prop),
**Page Up** and **Page Down** by the defined
[pageStep](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html#pageStep-prop), and
the **Home** and **End** keys set the value to the defined
[minimum](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html#minimum-prop) and
[maximum](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html#maximum-prop) values.

If you are using the mouse wheel to adjust the dial, the increment value is determined
by the lesser value of
[wheelScrollLines](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qapplication.html#wheelScrollLines-prop)
multiplied by
[singleStep](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html#singleStep-prop),
and [pageStep](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html#pageStep-prop).

### wrapping : bool

This property holds whether wrapping is enabled

If true, wrapping is enabled; otherwise some space is inserted at the bottom of the dial
to separate the ends of the range of valid values.

If enabled, the arrow can be oriented at any angle on the dial. If disabled, the arrow
will be restricted to the upper part of the dial; if it is rotated into the space at the
bottom of the dial, it will be clamped to the closest end of the valid range of values.

By default this property is `false`.

## Detailed Description

A dialog window is a top-level window mostly used for short-term tasks and brief
communications with the user. QDialogs may be modal or modeless. QDialogs can provide a
[return value](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdialog.html#return), and they can
have [default buttons](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdialog.html#default).
QDialogs can also have a [QSizeGrip](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsizegrip.html)
in their lower-right corner, using
[setSizeGripEnabled](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdialog.html#sizeGripEnabled-prop)().

Note that QDialog (and any other widget that has type `Qt::Dialog`) uses the parent
widget slightly differently from other classes in Qt. A dialog is always a top-level
widget, but if it has a parent, its default location is centered on top of the parent's
top-level widget (if it is not top-level itself). It will also share the parent's
taskbar entry.

Use the overload of the
[QWidget::setParent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#setParent)()
function to change the ownership of a QDialog widget. This function allows you to
explicitly set the window flags of the reparented widget; using the overloaded function
will clear the window flags specifying the window-system properties for the widget (in
particular it will reset the
[Qt::Dialog](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#WindowType-enum) flag).

**Note:** The parent relationship of the dialog does *not* imply that the dialog will
always be stacked on top of the parent window. To ensure that the dialog is always on
top, make the dialog modal. This also applies for child windows of the dialog itself. To
ensure that child windows of the dialog stay on top of the dialog, make the child
windows modal as well.

### Modal Dialogs

A **modal** dialog is a dialog that blocks input to other visible windows in the same
application. Dialogs that are used to request a file name from the user or that are used
to set application preferences are usually modal. Dialogs can be [application
modal](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#WindowModality-enum) (the default) or
[window modal](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#WindowModality-enum).

When an application modal dialog is opened, the user must finish interacting with the
dialog and close it before they can access any other window in the application. Window
modal dialogs only block access to the window associated with the dialog, allowing the
user to continue to use other windows in an application.

The most common way to display a modal dialog is to call its
[exec](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdialog.html#exec)() function. When the user
closes the dialog, [exec](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdialog.html#exec)() will
provide a useful [return value](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdialog.html#return).
To close the dialog and return the appropriate value, you must connect a default button,
e.g. an **OK** button to the
[accept](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdialog.html#accept)() slot and a **Cancel**
button to the [reject](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdialog.html#reject)() slot.
Alternatively, you can call the
[done](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdialog.html#done)() slot with `Accepted` or
`Rejected`.

An alternative is to call
[setModal](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdialog.html#modal-prop)(true) or
[setWindowModality](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#windowModality-prop)(),
then [show](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#show)(). Unlike
[exec](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdialog.html#exec)(),
[show](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#show)() returns control to the
caller immediately. Calling
[setModal](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdialog.html#modal-prop)(true) is
especially useful for progress dialogs, where the user must have the ability to interact
with the dialog, e.g. to cancel a long running operation. If you use
[show](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#show)() and
[setModal](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdialog.html#modal-prop)(true) together to
perform a long operation, you must call
[QCoreApplication::processEvents](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcoreapplication.html#processEvents)()
periodically during processing to enable the user to interact with the dialog. (See
[QProgressDialog](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qprogressdialog.html).)

### Modeless Dialogs

A **modeless** dialog is a dialog that operates independently of other windows in the
same application. Find and replace dialogs in word-processors are often modeless to
allow the user to interact with both the application's main window and with the dialog.

Modeless dialogs are displayed using
[show](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#show)(), which returns control to
the caller immediately.

If you invoke the [show()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#show)
function after hiding a dialog, the dialog will be displayed in its original position.
This is because the window manager decides the position for windows that have not been
explicitly placed by the programmer. To preserve the position of a dialog that has been
moved by the user, save its position in your
[closeEvent()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#closeEvent) handler and
then move the dialog to that position, before showing it again.

### Default Button

A dialog's *default* button is the button that's pressed when the user presses Enter
(Return). This button is used to signify that the user accepts the dialog's settings and
wants to close the dialog. Use
[QPushButton::setDefault](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpushbutton.html#default-prop)(),
[QPushButton::isDefault](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpushbutton.html#default-prop)()
and
[QPushButton::autoDefault](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpushbutton.html#autoDefault-prop)()
to set and control the dialog's default button.

### Escape Key

If the user presses the Esc key in a dialog,
[QDialog::reject](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdialog.html#reject)() will be
called. This will cause the window to close: The [close
event](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcloseevent.html) cannot be
[ignored](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qevent.html#ignore).

### Extensibility

Extensibility is the ability to show the dialog in two ways: a partial dialog that shows
the most commonly used options, and a full dialog that shows all the options. Typically
an extensible dialog will initially appear as a partial dialog, but with a **More**
toggle button. If the user presses the **More** button down, the dialog is expanded. The
[Extension
Example](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtwidgets-dialogs-extension-example.html)
shows how to achieve extensible dialogs using Qt.

### Return Value (Modal Dialogs)

Modal dialogs are often used in situations where a return value is required, e.g. to
indicate whether the user pressed **OK** or **Cancel**. A dialog can be closed by
calling the [accept](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdialog.html#accept)() or the
[reject](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdialog.html#reject)() slots, and
[exec](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdialog.html#exec)() will return `Accepted` or
`Rejected` as appropriate. The
[exec](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdialog.html#exec)() call returns the result
of the dialog. The result is also available from
[result](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdialog.html#result)() if the dialog has not
been destroyed.

In order to modify your dialog's close behavior, you can reimplement the functions
[accept](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdialog.html#accept)(),
[reject](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdialog.html#reject)() or
[done](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdialog.html#done)(). The
[closeEvent()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#closeEvent) function
should only be reimplemented to preserve the dialog's position or to override the
standard close or reject behavior.

### Code Examples

A modal dialog:

```
void EditorWindow::countWords()
{
    WordCountDialog dialog(this);
    dialog.setWordCount(document().wordCount());
    dialog.exec();
}
```

A modeless dialog:

```
void EditorWindow::find()
{
    if (!findDialog) {
        findDialog = new FindDialog(this);
        connect(findDialog, &FindDialog::findNext,
                this, &EditorWindow::findNext);
    }

    findDialog->show();
    findDialog->raise();
    findDialog->activateWindow();
}
```

### `[virtual slot]` void QDialog::done(int *r*)

Closes the dialog and sets its result code to *r*. The
[finished](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdialog.html#finished)() signal will emit
*r*; if *r* is
[QDialog::Accepted](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdialog.html#DialogCode-enum) or
[QDialog::Rejected](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdialog.html#DialogCode-enum),
the [accepted](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdialog.html#accepted)() or the
[rejected](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdialog.html#rejected)() signals will also
be emitted, respectively.

If this dialog is shown with
[exec](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdialog.html#exec)(), done() also causes the
local event loop to finish, and
[exec](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdialog.html#exec)() to return *r*.

As with [QWidget::close](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#close)(),
done() deletes the dialog if the
[Qt::WA\_DeleteOnClose](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#WidgetAttribute-enum)
flag is set. If the dialog is the application's main widget, the application terminates.
If the dialog is the last window closed, the
[QApplication::lastWindowClosed](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qguiapplication.html#lastWindowClosed)()
signal is emitted.

**See also** [accept](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdialog.html#accept)(),
[reject](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdialog.html#reject)(),
[QApplication::activeWindow](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qapplication.html#activeWindow)(),
and
[QCoreApplication::quit](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcoreapplication.html#quit)().

### `[virtual slot]` int QDialog::exec()

Shows the dialog as a [modal
dialog](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdialog.html#modal-dialogs), blocking until
the user closes it. The function returns a
[DialogCode](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdialog.html#DialogCode-enum) result.

If the dialog is [application
modal](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#WindowModality-enum), users cannot
interact with any other window in the same application until they close the dialog. If
the dialog is [window
modal](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#WindowModality-enum), only interaction
with the parent window is blocked while the dialog is open. By default, the dialog is
application modal.

**Note:** Avoid using this function; instead, use `open()`. Unlike exec(),
[open](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdialog.html#open)() is asynchronous, and does
not spin an additional event loop. This prevents a series of dangerous bugs from
happening (e.g. deleting the dialog's parent while the dialog is open via exec()). When
using [open](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdialog.html#open)() you can connect to
the [finished](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdialog.html#finished)() signal of
[QDialog](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdialog.html) to be notified when the
dialog is closed.

**See also** [open](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdialog.html#open)(),
[show](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#show)(),
[result](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdialog.html#result)(), and
[setWindowModality](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#windowModality-prop)().
