Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

Dialogs and message boxes typically present buttons in a layout that conforms to the
interface guidelines for that platform. Invariably, different platforms have different
layouts for their dialogs. QDialogButtonBox allows a developer to add buttons to it and
will automatically use the appropriate layout for the user's desktop environment.

Most buttons for a dialog follow certain roles. Such roles include:

- Accepting or rejecting the dialog.
- Asking for help.
- Performing actions on the dialog itself (such as resetting fields or applying changes).

There can also be alternate ways of dismissing the dialog which may cause destructive
results.

Most dialogs have buttons that can almost be considered standard (e.g. **OK** and
**Cancel** buttons). It is sometimes convenient to create these buttons in a standard
way.

There are a couple ways of using QDialogButtonBox. One ways is to create the buttons (or
button texts) yourself and add them to the button box, specifying their role.

```
    findButton = new QPushButton(tr("&Find"));
    findButton->setDefault(true);

    moreButton = new QPushButton(tr("&More"));
    moreButton->setCheckable(true);
    moreButton->setAutoDefault(false);
```

Alternatively, QDialogButtonBox provides several standard buttons (e.g. OK, Cancel,
Save) that you can use. They exist as flags so you can OR them together in the
constructor.

```
    buttonBox = new QDialogButtonBox(QDialogButtonBox::Ok
                                     | QDialogButtonBox::Cancel);

    connect(buttonBox, &QDialogButtonBox::accepted, this, &QDialog::accept);
    connect(buttonBox, &QDialogButtonBox::rejected, this, &QDialog::reject);
```

You can mix and match normal buttons and standard buttons.

Currently the buttons are laid out in the following way if the button box is horizontal:

| GnomeLayout Horizontal | Button box laid out in horizontal [GnomeLayout](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdialogbuttonbox.html#ButtonLayout-enum) |
| --- | --- |
| KdeLayout Horizontal | Button box laid out in horizontal [KdeLayout](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdialogbuttonbox.html#ButtonLayout-enum) |
| MacLayout Horizontal | Button box laid out in horizontal [MacLayout](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdialogbuttonbox.html#ButtonLayout-enum) |
| WinLayout Horizontal | Button box laid out in horizontal [WinLayout](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdialogbuttonbox.html#ButtonLayout-enum) |

The buttons are laid out the following way if the button box is vertical:

| [GnomeLayout](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdialogbuttonbox.html#ButtonLayout-enum) | [KdeLayout](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdialogbuttonbox.html#ButtonLayout-enum) | [MacLayout](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdialogbuttonbox.html#ButtonLayout-enum) | [WinLayout](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdialogbuttonbox.html#ButtonLayout-enum) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GnomeLayout Vertical | KdeLayout Vertical | MacLayout Vertical | WinLayout Vertical |

Additionally, button boxes that contain only buttons with
[ActionRole](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdialogbuttonbox.html#ButtonRole-enum)
or [HelpRole](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdialogbuttonbox.html#ButtonRole-enum)
can be considered modeless and have an alternate look on macOS:

| modeless horizontal [MacLayout](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdialogbuttonbox.html#ButtonLayout-enum) | Screenshot of modeless horizontal MacLayout |
| --- | --- |
| modeless vertical [MacLayout](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdialogbuttonbox.html#ButtonLayout-enum) | Screenshot of modeless vertical MacLayout |

When a button is clicked in the button box, the
[clicked](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdialogbuttonbox.html#clicked)() signal is
emitted for the actual button is that is pressed. For convenience, if the button has an
[AcceptRole](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdialogbuttonbox.html#ButtonRole-enum),
[RejectRole](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdialogbuttonbox.html#ButtonRole-enum),
or [HelpRole](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdialogbuttonbox.html#ButtonRole-enum),
the [accepted](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdialogbuttonbox.html#accepted)(),
[rejected](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdialogbuttonbox.html#rejected)(), or
[helpRequested](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdialogbuttonbox.html#helpRequested)()
signals are emitted respectively.

If you want a specific button to be default you need to call
[QPushButton::setDefault](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpushbutton.html#default-prop)()
on it yourself. However, if there is no default button set and to preserve which button
is the default button across platforms when using the
[QPushButton::autoDefault](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpushbutton.html#autoDefault-prop)
property, the first push button with the accept role is made the default button when the
QDialogButtonBox is shown,

Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

The usage of QDirModel is not recommended anymore. The
[QFileSystemModel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfilesystemmodel.html) class is a
more performant alternative.

This class provides access to the local filesystem, providing functions for renaming and
removing files and directories, and for creating new directories. In the simplest case,
it can be used with a suitable display widget as part of a browser or filer.

QDirModel keeps a cache with file information. The cache needs to be updated with
[refresh](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdirmodel.html#refresh)().

QDirModel can be accessed using the standard interface provided by
[QAbstractItemModel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html), but it
also provides some convenience functions that are specific to a directory model. The
[fileInfo](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdirmodel.html#fileInfo)() and
[isDir](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdirmodel.html#isDir)() functions provide
information about the underlying files and directories related to items in the model.

Directories can be created and removed using
[mkdir](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdirmodel.html#mkdir)(),
[rmdir](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdirmodel.html#rmdir)(), and the model will
be automatically updated to take the changes into account.

**Note:** QDirModel requires an instance of
[QApplication](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qapplication.html).

PythonQt.QtGui.QDockWidget.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

QDockWidget provides the concept of dock widgets, also know as tool palettes or utility
windows. Dock windows are secondary windows placed in the *dock widget area* around the
[central widget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmainwindow.html#centralWidget) in a
[QMainWindow](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmainwindow.html).

![](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/images/mainwindow-docks.png)

Dock windows can be moved inside their current area, moved into new areas and floated
(e.g., undocked) by the end-user. The QDockWidget API allows the programmer to restrict
the dock widgets ability to move, float and close, as well as the areas in which they
can be placed.

### Appearance

A QDockWidget consists of a title bar and the content area. The title bar displays the
dock widgets [window
title](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#windowTitle-prop), a *float*
button and a *close* button. Depending on the state of the QDockWidget, the *float* and
*close* buttons may be either disabled or not shown at all.

The visual appearance of the title bar and buttons is dependent on the
[style](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstyle.html) in use.

A QDockWidget acts as a wrapper for its child widget, set with
[setWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdockwidget.html#setWidget)(). Custom
size hints, minimum and maximum sizes and size policies should be implemented in the
child widget. QDockWidget will respect them, adjusting its own constraints to include
the frame and title. Size constraints should not be set on the QDockWidget itself,
because they change depending on whether it is docked; a docked QDockWidget has no frame
and a smaller title bar.

**Note:** On macOS, if the QDockWidget has a native window handle (for example, if
[winId](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#winId)() is called on it or the
child widget), then due to a limitation it will not be possible to drag the dock widget
when undocking. Starting the drag will undock the dock widget, but a second drag will be
needed to move the dock widget itself.

### void QDockWidget::setTitleBarWidget([QWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#QWidget) \**widget*)

Sets an arbitrary *widget* as the dock widget's title bar. If *widget* is `nullptr`, any
custom title bar widget previously set on the dock widget is removed, but not deleted,
and the default title bar will be used instead.

If a title bar widget is set,
[QDockWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdockwidget.html) will not use native
window decorations when it is floated.

Here are some tips for implementing custom title bars:

- Mouse events that are not explicitly handled by the title bar widget must be ignored by calling [QMouseEvent::ignore](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qevent.html#ignore)(). These events then propagate to the [QDockWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdockwidget.html) parent, which handles them in the usual manner, moving when the title bar is dragged, docking and undocking when it is double-clicked, etc.
- When [DockWidgetVerticalTitleBar](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdockwidget.html#DockWidgetFeature-enum) is set on [QDockWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdockwidget.html), the title bar widget is repositioned accordingly. In [resizeEvent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#resizeEvent)(), the title bar should check what orientation it should assume:

  ```
  QDockWidget *dockWidget = qobject_cast<QDockWidget*>(parentWidget());
  if (dockWidget->features() & QDockWidget::DockWidgetVerticalTitleBar) {
      // I need to be vertical
  } else {
      // I need to be horizontal
  }
  ```
- The title bar widget must have a valid [QWidget::sizeHint](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#sizeHint-prop)() and [QWidget::minimumSizeHint](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#minimumSizeHint-prop)(). These functions should take into account the current orientation of the title bar.
- It is not possible to remove a title bar from a dock widget. However, a similar effect can be achieved by setting a default constructed [QWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html) as the title bar widget.

Using [qobject\_cast](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qobject.html#qobject_cast)() as
shown above, the title bar widget has full access to its parent
[QDockWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdockwidget.html). Hence it can perform
such operations as docking and hiding in response to user actions.

This function was introduced in Qt 4.3.

**See also**
[titleBarWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdockwidget.html#titleBarWidget)()
and
[DockWidgetVerticalTitleBar](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdockwidget.html#DockWidgetFeature-enum).

PythonQt.QtGui.QDoubleSpinBox.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

QDoubleSpinBox allows the user to choose a value by clicking the up and down buttons or
by pressing Up or Down on the keyboard to increase or decrease the value currently
displayed. The user can also type the value in manually. The spin box supports double
values but can be extended to use different strings with
[validate](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdoublespinbox.html#validate)(),
[textFromValue](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdoublespinbox.html#textFromValue)()
and
[valueFromText](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdoublespinbox.html#valueFromText)().

Every time the value changes QDoubleSpinBox emits
[valueChanged](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdoublespinbox.html#valueChanged)()
and [textChanged](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdoublespinbox.html#textChanged)()
signals, the former providing a double and the latter a
[QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html). The
[textChanged](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdoublespinbox.html#textChanged)()
signal provides the value with both
[prefix](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdoublespinbox.html#prefix-prop)() and
[suffix](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdoublespinbox.html#suffix-prop)(). The
current value can be fetched with
[value](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdoublespinbox.html#value-prop)() and set
with [setValue](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdoublespinbox.html#value-prop)().

Note: QDoubleSpinBox will round numbers so they can be displayed with the current
precision. In a QDoubleSpinBox with decimals set to 2, calling
[setValue](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdoublespinbox.html#value-prop)(2.555)
will cause [value](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdoublespinbox.html#value-prop)()
to return 2.56.

Clicking the up and down buttons or using the keyboard accelerator's Up and Down arrows
will increase or decrease the current value in steps of size
[singleStep](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdoublespinbox.html#singleStep-prop)().
If you want to change this behavior you can reimplement the virtual function
[stepBy](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractspinbox.html#stepBy)(). The minimum
and maximum value and the step size can be set using one of the constructors, and can be
changed later with
[setMinimum](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdoublespinbox.html#minimum-prop)(),
[setMaximum](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdoublespinbox.html#maximum-prop)() and
[setSingleStep](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdoublespinbox.html#singleStep-prop)().
The spinbox has a default precision of 2 decimal places but this can be changed using
[setDecimals](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdoublespinbox.html#decimals-prop)().

Most spin boxes are directional, but QDoubleSpinBox can also operate as a circular spin
box, i.e. if the range is 0.0-99.9 and the current value is 99.9, clicking "up" will
give 0 if
[wrapping](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractspinbox.html#wrapping-prop)() is
set to true. Use
[setWrapping](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractspinbox.html#wrapping-prop)()
if you want circular behavior.

The displayed value can be prepended and appended with arbitrary strings indicating, for
example, currency or the unit of measurement. See
[setPrefix](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdoublespinbox.html#prefix-prop)() and
[setSuffix](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdoublespinbox.html#suffix-prop)(). The
text in the spin box is retrieved with
[text](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractspinbox.html#text-prop)() (which
includes any
[prefix](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdoublespinbox.html#prefix-prop)() and
[suffix](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdoublespinbox.html#suffix-prop)()), or with
[cleanText](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdoublespinbox.html#cleanText-prop)()
(which has no
[prefix](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdoublespinbox.html#prefix-prop)(), no
[suffix](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdoublespinbox.html#suffix-prop)() and no
leading or trailing whitespace).

It is often desirable to give the user a special (often default) choice in addition to
the range of numeric values. See
[setSpecialValueText](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractspinbox.html#specialValueText-prop)()
for how to do this with QDoubleSpinBox.

**Note:** The displayed value of the QDoubleSpinBox is limited to 18 characters in
addition to eventual prefix and suffix content. This limitation is used to keep the
double spin box usable even with extremely large values.

Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

QDoubleValidator provides an upper bound, a lower bound, and a limit on the number of
digits after the decimal point. It does not provide a
[fixup](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qvalidator.html#fixup)() function.

You can set the acceptable range in one call with
[setRange](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdoublevalidator.html#setRange)(), or with
[setBottom](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdoublevalidator.html#bottom-prop)() and
[setTop](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdoublevalidator.html#top-prop)(). Set the
number of decimal places with
[setDecimals](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdoublevalidator.html#decimals-prop)().
The [validate](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdoublevalidator.html#validate)()
function returns the validation state.

QDoubleValidator uses its
[locale](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qvalidator.html#locale)() to interpret the
number. For example, in the German locale, "1,234" will be accepted as the fractional
number 1.234. In Arabic locales, QDoubleValidator will accept Arabic digits.

**Note:** The
[QLocale::NumberOptions](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qlocale.html#NumberOption-enum)
set on the [locale](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qvalidator.html#locale)() also
affect the way the number is interpreted. For example, since
[QLocale::RejectGroupSeparator](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qlocale.html#NumberOption-enum)
is not set by default, the validator will accept group separators. It is thus
recommended to use
[QLocale::toDouble](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qlocale.html#toDouble)() to
obtain the numeric value.

### `[override virtual]` [QValidator::State](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qvalidator.html#State-enum) QDoubleValidator::validate([QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html) \&*input*, int \&*pos*) const

Reimplements:
[QValidator::validate](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qvalidator.html#validate)(QString
\&input, int \&pos) const.

Returns [Acceptable](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qvalidator.html#State-enum) if
the string *input* contains a double that is within the valid range and is in the
correct format.

Returns [Intermediate](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qvalidator.html#State-enum) if
*input* contains a double that is outside the range or is in the wrong format; e.g. is
empty.

Returns [Invalid](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qvalidator.html#State-enum) if the
*input* is not a double or with too many digits after the decimal point.

Note: If the valid range consists of just positive doubles (e.g. 0.0 to 100.0) and
*input* is a negative double then
[Invalid](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qvalidator.html#State-enum) is returned. If
[notation](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdoublevalidator.html#notation-prop)() is
set to
[StandardNotation](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdoublevalidator.html#Notation-enum),
and the input contains more digits before the decimal point than a double in the valid
range may have, [Invalid](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qvalidator.html#State-enum)
is returned. If
[notation](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdoublevalidator.html#notation-prop)() is
[ScientificNotation](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdoublevalidator.html#Notation-enum),
and the input is not in the valid range,
[Intermediate](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qvalidator.html#State-enum) is
returned. The value may yet become valid by changing the exponent.

By default, the *pos* parameter is not used by this validator.
signatures: validate(self, arg__1: str, arg__2: int) -> PySide2.QtGui.QValidator.State

## Detailed Description

Drag and drop is an intuitive way for users to copy or move data around in an
application, and is used in many desktop environments as a mechanism for copying data
between applications. Drag and drop support in Qt is centered around the QDrag class
that handles most of the details of a drag and drop operation.

The data to be transferred by the drag and drop operation is contained in a
[QMimeData](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmimedata.html) object. This is specified
with the [setMimeData](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdrag.html#setMimeData)()
function in the following way:

```
        QDrag *drag = new QDrag(this);
        QMimeData *mimeData = new QMimeData;

        mimeData->setText(commentEdit->toPlainText());
        drag->setMimeData(mimeData);
```

Note that [setMimeData](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdrag.html#setMimeData)()
assigns ownership of the [QMimeData](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmimedata.html)
object to the QDrag object. The QDrag must be constructed on the heap with a parent
[QObject](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qobject.html) to ensure that Qt can clean
up after the drag and drop operation has been completed.

A pixmap can be used to represent the data while the drag is in progress, and will move
with the cursor to the drop target. This pixmap typically shows an icon that represents
the MIME type of the data being transferred, but any pixmap can be set with
[setPixmap](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdrag.html#setPixmap)(). The cursor's hot
spot can be given a position relative to the top-left corner of the pixmap with the
[setHotSpot](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdrag.html#setHotSpot)() function. The
following code positions the pixmap so that the cursor's hot spot points to the center
of its bottom edge:

```
    drag->setHotSpot(QPoint(drag->pixmap().width()/2,
                            drag->pixmap().height()));
```

**Note:** On X11, the pixmap may not be able to keep up with the mouse movements if the
hot spot causes the pixmap to be displayed directly under the cursor.

The source and target widgets can be found with
[source](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdrag.html#source)() and
[target](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdrag.html#target)(). These functions are
often used to determine whether drag and drop operations started and finished at the
same widget, so that special behavior can be implemented.

QDrag only deals with the drag and drop operation itself. It is up to the developer to
decide when a drag operation begins, and how a QDrag object should be constructed and
used. For a given widget, it is often necessary to reimplement
[mousePressEvent()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#mousePressEvent) to
determine whether the user has pressed a mouse button, and reimplement
[mouseMoveEvent()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#mouseMoveEvent) to
check whether a QDrag is required.

PythonQt.QtGui.QDrag.exec.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

### [Qt::DropAction](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#DropAction-enum) QDrag::exec([Qt::DropActions](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#DropAction-enum) *supportedActions* \= Qt::MoveAction)

Starts the drag and drop operation and returns a value indicating the requested drop
action when it is completed. The drop actions that the user can choose from are
specified in *supportedActions*. The default proposed action will be selected among the
allowed actions in the following order: Move, Copy and Link.

**Note:** On Linux and macOS, the drag and drop operation can take some time, but this
function does not block the event loop. Other events are still delivered to the
application while the operation is performed. On Windows, the Qt event loop is blocked
during the operation.

This function was introduced in Qt 4.3.

**See also** [cancel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdrag.html#cancel)().

### [Qt::DropAction](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#DropAction-enum) QDrag::exec([Qt::DropActions](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#DropAction-enum) *supportedActions*, [Qt::DropAction](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#DropAction-enum) *defaultDropAction*)

Starts the drag and drop operation and returns a value indicating the requested drop
action when it is completed. The drop actions that the user can choose from are
specified in *supportedActions*.

The *defaultDropAction* determines which action will be proposed when the user performs
a drag without using modifier keys.

**Note:** On Linux and macOS, the drag and drop operation can take some time, but this
function does not block the event loop. Other events are still delivered to the
application while the operation is performed. On Windows, the Qt event loop is blocked
during the operation. However,
[QDrag::exec](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdrag.html#exec)() on Windows causes
processEvents() to be called frequently to keep the GUI responsive. If any loops or
operations are called while a drag operation is active, it will block the drag
operation.

This function was introduced in Qt 4.3.

## Detailed Description

A widget must accept this event in order to receive the [drag move
events](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdragmoveevent.html) that are sent while the
drag and drop action is in progress. The drag enter event is always immediately followed
by a drag move event.

QDragEnterEvent inherits most of its functionality from
[QDragMoveEvent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdragmoveevent.html), which in turn
inherits most of its functionality from
[QDropEvent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdropevent.html).

PythonQt.QtGui.QDragLeaveEvent.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

This event is always preceded by a
[QDragEnterEvent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdragenterevent.html) and a series
of [QDragMoveEvent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdragmoveevent.html)s. It is not
sent if a [QDropEvent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdropevent.html) is sent
instead.

PythonQt.QtGui.QDragMoveEvent.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

A widget will receive drag move events repeatedly while the drag is within its
boundaries, if it accepts [drop
events](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#acceptDrops-prop) and [enter
events](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#dragEnterEvent). The widget
should examine the event to see what kind of
[data](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdropevent.html#mimeData) it provides, and
call the [accept](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdragmoveevent.html#accept-1)()
function to accept the drop if appropriate.

The rectangle supplied by the
[answerRect](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdragmoveevent.html#answerRect)()
function can be used to restrict drops to certain parts of the widget. For example, we
can check whether the rectangle intersects with the geometry of a certain child widget
and only call
[acceptProposedAction()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdropevent.html#acceptProposedAction)
if that is the case.

Note that this class inherits most of its functionality from
[QDropEvent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdropevent.html).

### void QDragMoveEvent::accept(const [QRect](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qrect.html) \&*rectangle*)

The same as accept(), but also notifies that future moves will also be acceptable if
they remain within the *rectangle* given on the widget. This can improve performance,
but may also be ignored by the underlying system.

If the rectangle is empty, drag move events will be sent continuously. This is useful if
the source is scrolling in a timer event.

### void QDragMoveEvent::accept()

This is an overloaded function.

Calls [QDropEvent::accept](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qevent.html#accept)().

PythonQt.QtGui.QDropEvent.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

When a widget [accepts drop
events](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#acceptDrops-prop), it will
receive this event if it has accepted the most recent
[QDragEnterEvent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdragenterevent.html) or
[QDragMoveEvent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdragmoveevent.html) sent to it.

The drop event contains a proposed action, available from
[proposedAction](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdropevent.html#proposedAction)(),
for the widget to either accept or ignore. If the action can be handled by the widget,
you should call the
[acceptProposedAction](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdropevent.html#acceptProposedAction)()
function. Since the proposed action can be a combination of
[Qt::DropAction](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#DropAction-enum) values, it
may be useful to either select one of these values as a default action or ask the user
to select their preferred action.

If the proposed drop action is not suitable, perhaps because your custom widget does not
support that action, you can replace it with any of the [possible drop
actions](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdropevent.html#possibleActions) by calling
[setDropAction](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdropevent.html#setDropAction)() with
your preferred action. If you set a value that is not present in the bitwise OR
combination of values returned by
[possibleActions](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdropevent.html#possibleActions)(),
the default copy action will be used. Once a replacement drop action has been set, call
[accept](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qevent.html#accept)() instead of
[acceptProposedAction](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdropevent.html#acceptProposedAction)()
to complete the drop operation.

The [mimeData](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdropevent.html#mimeData)() function
provides the data dropped on the widget in a
[QMimeData](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmimedata.html) object. This contains
information about the MIME type of the data in addition to the data itself.

PythonQt.QtGui.QErrorMessage.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

An error message widget consists of a text label and a checkbox. The checkbox lets the
user control whether the same error message will be displayed again in the future,
typically displaying the text, "Show this message again" translated into the appropriate
local language.

For production applications, the class can be used to display messages which the user
only needs to see once. To use QErrorMessage like this, you create the dialog in the
usual way, and show it by calling the
[showMessage](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qerrormessage.html#showMessage)() slot
or connecting signals to it.

The static
[qtHandler](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qerrormessage.html#qtHandler)() function
installs a message handler using
[qInstallMessageHandler](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtglobal.html#qInstallMessageHandler)()
and creates a QErrorMessage that displays
[qDebug](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtglobal.html#qDebug)(),
[qWarning](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtglobal.html#qWarning)() and
[qFatal](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtglobal.html#qFatal)() messages. This is
most useful in environments where no console is available to display warnings and error
messages.

In both cases QErrorMessage will queue pending messages and display them in order, with
each new message being shown as soon as the user has accepted the previous message. Once
the user has specified that a message is not to be shown again it is automatically
skipped, and the dialog will show the next appropriate message in the queue.

The [Standard

## Detailed Description

Expose events are sent to windows when an area of the window is invalidated, for example
when window exposure in the windowing system changes.

A Window with a client area that is completely covered by another window, or is
otherwise not visible may be considered obscured by Qt and may in such cases not receive
expose events.

The event handler
[QWindow::exposeEvent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwindow.html#exposeEvent)()
receives expose events.

PythonQt.QtGui.QFileDialog.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

The QFileDialog class enables a user to traverse the file system in order to select one
or many files or a directory.

The easiest way to create a QFileDialog is to use the static functions.

```
fileName = QFileDialog::getOpenFileName(this,
    tr("Open Image"), "/home/jana", tr("Image Files (*.png *.jpg *.bmp)"));
```

In the above example, a modal QFileDialog is created using a static function. The dialog
initially displays the contents of the "/home/jana" directory, and displays files
matching the patterns given in the string "Image Files (\*.png \*.jpg \*.bmp)". The
parent of the file dialog is set to *this*, and the window title is set to "Open Image".

If you want to use multiple filters, separate each one with *two* semicolons. For
example:

```
"Images (*.png *.xpm *.jpg);;Text files (*.txt);;XML files (*.xml)"
```

You can create your own QFileDialog without using the static functions. By calling
[setFileMode](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html#fileMode-prop)(), you
can specify what the user must select in the dialog:

```
QFileDialog dialog(this);
dialog.setFileMode(QFileDialog::AnyFile);
```

In the above example, the mode of the file dialog is set to
[AnyFile](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html#FileMode-enum), meaning
that the user can select any file, or even specify a file that doesn't exist. This mode
is useful for creating a "Save As" file dialog. Use
[ExistingFile](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html#FileMode-enum) if the
user must select an existing file, or
[Directory](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html#FileMode-enum) if only a
directory may be selected. See the
[QFileDialog::FileMode](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html#FileMode-enum)
enum for the complete list of modes.

The [fileMode](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html#fileMode-prop)
property contains the mode of operation for the dialog; this indicates what types of
objects the user is expected to select. Use
[setNameFilter](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html#setNameFilter)() to
set the dialog's file filter. For example:

```
dialog.setNameFilter(tr("Images (*.png *.xpm *.jpg)"));
```

In the above example, the filter is set to `"Images (*.png *.xpm *.jpg)"`, this means
that only files with the extension `png`, `xpm`, or `jpg` will be shown in the
QFileDialog. You can apply several filters by using
[setNameFilters](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html#setNameFilters)().
Use
[selectNameFilter](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html#selectNameFilter)()
to select one of the filters you've given as the file dialog's default filter.

The file dialog has two view modes:
[List](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html#ViewMode-enum) and
[Detail](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html#ViewMode-enum).
[List](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html#ViewMode-enum) presents the
contents of the current directory as a list of file and directory names.
[Detail](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html#ViewMode-enum) also
displays a list of file and directory names, but provides additional information
alongside each name, such as the file size and modification date. Set the mode with
[setViewMode](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html#viewMode-prop)():

```
dialog.setViewMode(QFileDialog::Detail);
```

The last important function you will need to use when creating your own file dialog is
[selectedFiles](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html#selectedFiles)().

```
QStringList fileNames;
if (dialog.exec())
    fileNames = dialog.selectedFiles();
```

In the above example, a modal file dialog is created and shown. If the user clicked OK,
the file they selected is put in `fileName`.

The dialog's working directory can be set with
[setDirectory](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html#setDirectory)(). Each
file in the current directory can be selected using the
[selectFile](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html#selectFile)() function.

The [Standard
Dialogs](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtwidgets-dialogs-standarddialogs-example.html)
example shows how to use QFileDialog as well as other built-in Qt dialogs.

By default, a platform-native file dialog will be used if the platform has one. In that
case, the widgets which would otherwise be used to construct the dialog will not be
instantiated, so related accessors such as
[layout](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#layout)() and
[itemDelegate](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html#itemDelegate)() will
return null. Also, not all platforms show file dialogs with a title bar, so be aware
that the caption text might not be visible to the user. You can set the
[DontUseNativeDialog](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html#Option-enum)
option to ensure that the widget-based implementation will be used instead of the native
dialog.

Qt 5 reference:

### `[static]` [QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html) QFileDialog::getExistingDirectory([QWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#QWidget) \**parent* \= nullptr, const [QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html) \&*caption* \= QString(), const [QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html) \&*dir* \= QString(), [QFileDialog::Options](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html#Option-enum) *options* \= ShowDirsOnly)

This is a convenience static function that will return an existing directory selected by
the user.

```
QString dir = QFileDialog::getExistingDirectory(this, tr("Open Directory"),
                                                "/home",
                                                QFileDialog::ShowDirsOnly
                                                | QFileDialog::DontResolveSymlinks);
```

This function creates a modal file dialog with the given *parent* widget. If *parent* is
not `nullptr`, the dialog will be shown centered over the parent widget.

The dialog's working directory is set to *dir*, and the caption is set to *caption*.
Either of these may be an empty string in which case the current directory and a default
caption will be used respectively.

The *options* argument holds various options about how to run the dialog, see the
[QFileDialog::Option](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html#Option-enum)
enum for more information on the flags you can pass. To ensure a native file dialog,
[ShowDirsOnly](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html#Option-enum) must be
set.

On Windows and macOS, this static function will use the native file dialog and not a
[QFileDialog](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html). However, the native
Windows file dialog does not support displaying files in the directory chooser. You need
to pass
[DontUseNativeDialog](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html#Option-enum)
to display files using a
[QFileDialog](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html).

Note that the macOS native file dialog does not show a title bar.

On Unix/X11, the normal behavior of the file dialog is to resolve and follow symlinks.
For example, if `/usr/tmp` is a symlink to `/var/tmp`, the file dialog will change to
`/var/tmp` after entering `/usr/tmp`. If *options* includes
[DontResolveSymlinks](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html#Option-enum),
the file dialog will treat symlinks as regular directories.

On Windows, the dialog will spin a blocking modal event loop that will not dispatch any
QTimers, and if *parent* is not `nullptr` then it will position the dialog just below
the parent's title bar.

**Warning:** Do not delete *parent* during the execution of the dialog. If you want to
do this, you should create the dialog yourself using one of the
[QFileDialog](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html) constructors.

**See also**
[getOpenFileName](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html#getOpenFileName)(),
[getOpenFileNames](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html#getOpenFileNames)(),
and
[getSaveFileName](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html#getSaveFileName)().

### `[static]` [QUrl](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qurl.html) QFileDialog::getExistingDirectoryUrl([QWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#QWidget) \**parent* \= nullptr, const [QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html) \&*caption* \= QString(), const [QUrl](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qurl.html) \&*dir* \= QUrl(), [QFileDialog::Options](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html#Option-enum) *options* \= ShowDirsOnly, const [QStringList](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstringlist.html) \&*supportedSchemes* \= QStringList())

This is a convenience static function that will return an existing directory selected by
the user. If the user presses Cancel, it returns an empty url.

The function is used similarly to
[QFileDialog::getExistingDirectory](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html#getExistingDirectory)().
In particular *parent*, *caption*, *dir* and *options* are used in the exact same way.

The main difference with
[QFileDialog::getExistingDirectory](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html#getExistingDirectory)()
comes from the ability offered to the user to select a remote directory. That's why the
return type and the type of *dir* is
[QUrl](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qurl.html).

The *supportedSchemes* argument allows to restrict the type of URLs the user will be
able to select. It is a way for the application to declare the protocols it will support
to fetch the file content. An empty list means that no restriction is applied (the
default). Supported for local files ("file" scheme) is implicit and always enabled; it
is not necessary to include it in the restriction.

When possible, this static function will use the native file dialog and not a
[QFileDialog](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html). On platforms which
don't support selecting remote files, Qt will allow to select only local files.

This function was introduced in Qt 5.2.

**See also**
[getExistingDirectory](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html#getExistingDirectory)(),
[getOpenFileUrl](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html#getOpenFileUrl)(),
[getOpenFileUrls](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html#getOpenFileUrls)(),

### `[static]` [QStringList](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstringlist.html) QFileDialog::getOpenFileNames([QWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#QWidget) \**parent* \= nullptr, const [QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html) \&*caption* \= QString(), const [QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html) \&*dir* \= QString(), const [QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html) \&*filter* \= QString(), [QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html) \**selectedFilter* \= nullptr, [QFileDialog::Options](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html#Option-enum) *options* \= Options())

This is a convenience static function that will return one or more existing files
selected by the user.

```
QStringList files = QFileDialog::getOpenFileNames(
                        this,
                        "Select one or more files to open",
                        "/home",
                        "Images (*.png *.xpm *.jpg)");
```

This function creates a modal file dialog with the given *parent* widget. If *parent* is
not `nullptr`, the dialog will be shown centered over the parent widget.

The file dialog's working directory will be set to *dir*. If *dir* includes a file name,
the file will be selected. The filter is set to *filter* so that only those files which
match the filter are shown. The filter selected is set to *selectedFilter*. The
parameters *dir*, *selectedFilter* and *filter* may be empty strings. If you need
multiple filters, separate them with ';;', for instance:

```
"Images (*.png *.xpm *.jpg);;Text files (*.txt);;XML files (*.xml)"
```

The dialog's caption is set to *caption*. If *caption* is not specified then a default
caption will be used.

On Windows, and macOS, this static function will use the native file dialog and not a
[QFileDialog](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html). Note that the macOS
native file dialog does not show a title bar.

On Windows the dialog will spin a blocking modal event loop that will not dispatch any
QTimers, and if *parent* is not `nullptr` then it will position the dialog just below
the parent's title bar.

On Unix/X11, the normal behavior of the file dialog is to resolve and follow symlinks.
For example, if `/usr/tmp` is a symlink to `/var/tmp`, the file dialog will change to
`/var/tmp` after entering `/usr/tmp`. The *options* argument holds various options about
how to run the dialog, see the
[QFileDialog::Option](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html#Option-enum)
enum for more information on the flags you can pass.

**Warning:** Do not delete *parent* during the execution of the dialog. If you want to
do this, you should create the dialog yourself using one of the
[QFileDialog](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html) constructors.

**See also**
[getOpenFileName](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html#getOpenFileName)(),
[getSaveFileName](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html#getSaveFileName)(),
and
[getExistingDirectory](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html#getExistingDirectory)().
signatures: getOpenFileNames(parent: typing.Optional[PySide2.QtWidgets.QWidget]=..., caption: str=..., dir: str=..., filter: str=..., options: PySide2.QtWidgets.QFileDialog.Options=...) -> typing.Tuple[typing.List[str], str]

### `[static]` [QUrl](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qurl.html) QFileDialog::getOpenFileUrl([QWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#QWidget) \**parent* \= nullptr, const [QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html) \&*caption* \= QString(), const [QUrl](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qurl.html) \&*dir* \= QUrl(), const [QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html) \&*filter* \= QString(), [QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html) \**selectedFilter* \= nullptr, [QFileDialog::Options](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html#Option-enum) *options* \= Options(), const [QStringList](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstringlist.html) \&*supportedSchemes* \= QStringList())

This is a convenience static function that returns an existing file selected by the
user. If the user presses Cancel, it returns an empty url.

The function is used similarly to
[QFileDialog::getOpenFileName](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html#getOpenFileName)().
In particular *parent*, *caption*, *dir*, *filter*, *selectedFilter* and *options* are
used in the exact same way.

The main difference with
[QFileDialog::getOpenFileName](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html#getOpenFileName)()
comes from the ability offered to the user to select a remote file. That's why the
return type and the type of *dir* is
[QUrl](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qurl.html).

The *supportedSchemes* argument allows to restrict the type of URLs the user will be
able to select. It is a way for the application to declare the protocols it will support
to fetch the file content. An empty list means that no restriction is applied (the
default). Supported for local files ("file" scheme) is implicit and always enabled; it
is not necessary to include it in the restriction.

When possible, this static function will use the native file dialog and not a
[QFileDialog](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html). On platforms which
don't support selecting remote files, Qt will allow to select only local files.

This function was introduced in Qt 5.2.

**See also**
[getOpenFileName](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html#getOpenFileName)(),
[getOpenFileUrls](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html#getOpenFileUrls)(),
[getSaveFileUrl](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html#getSaveFileUrl)(),
and
[getExistingDirectoryUrl](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html#getExistingDirectoryUrl)().

### `[static]` [QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html) QFileDialog::getSaveFileName([QWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#QWidget) \**parent* \= nullptr, const [QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html) \&*caption* \= QString(), const [QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html) \&*dir* \= QString(), const [QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html) \&*filter* \= QString(), [QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html) \**selectedFilter* \= nullptr, [QFileDialog::Options](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html#Option-enum) *options* \= Options())

This is a convenience static function that will return a file name selected by the user.
The file does not have to exist.

It creates a modal file dialog with the given *parent* widget. If *parent* is not
`nullptr`, the dialog will be shown centered over the parent widget.

```
QString fileName = QFileDialog::getSaveFileName(this, tr("Save File"),
                           "/home/jana/untitled.png",
                           tr("Images (*.png *.xpm *.jpg)"));
```

The file dialog's working directory will be set to *dir*. If *dir* includes a file name,
the file will be selected. Only files that match the *filter* are shown. The filter
selected is set to *selectedFilter*. The parameters *dir*, *selectedFilter*, and
*filter* may be empty strings. Multiple filters are separated with ';;'. For instance:

```
"Images (*.png *.xpm *.jpg);;Text files (*.txt);;XML files (*.xml)"
```

The *options* argument holds various options about how to run the dialog, see the
[QFileDialog::Option](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html#Option-enum)
enum for more information on the flags you can pass.

The default filter can be chosen by setting *selectedFilter* to the desired value.

The dialog's caption is set to *caption*. If *caption* is not specified, a default
caption will be used.

On Windows, and macOS, this static function will use the native file dialog and not a
[QFileDialog](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html).

On Windows the dialog will spin a blocking modal event loop that will not dispatch any
QTimers, and if *parent* is not `nullptr` then it will position the dialog just below
the parent's title bar. On macOS, with its native file dialog, the filter argument is
ignored.

On Unix/X11, the normal behavior of the file dialog is to resolve and follow symlinks.
For example, if `/usr/tmp` is a symlink to `/var/tmp`, the file dialog will change to
`/var/tmp` after entering `/usr/tmp`. If *options* includes
[DontResolveSymlinks](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html#Option-enum)
the file dialog will treat symlinks as regular directories.

**Warning:** Do not delete *parent* during the execution of the dialog. If you want to
do this, you should create the dialog yourself using one of the
[QFileDialog](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html) constructors.

**See also**
[getOpenFileName](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html#getOpenFileName)(),
[getOpenFileNames](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html#getOpenFileNames)(),
and
[getExistingDirectory](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html#getExistingDirectory)().

### void QFileDialog::open([QObject](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qobject.html#QObject) \**receiver*, const char \**member*)

This function connects one of its signals to the slot specified by *receiver* and
*member*. The specific signal depends is
[filesSelected](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html#filesSelected)() if
[fileMode](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html#fileMode-prop) is
[ExistingFiles](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html#FileMode-enum) and
[fileSelected](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html#fileSelected)() if
[fileMode](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html#fileMode-prop) is
anything else.

The signal will be disconnected from the slot when the dialog is closed.

This function was introduced in Qt 4.5.

### options : [Options](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html#Option-enum)

This property holds the various options that affect the look and feel of the dialog

By default, all options are disabled.

Options (particularly the DontUseNativeDialogs option) should be set before changing
dialog properties or showing the dialog.

Setting options while the dialog is visible is not guaranteed to have an immediate
effect on the dialog (depending on the option and on the platform).

Setting options after changing other properties may cause these values to have no
effect.

This property was introduced in Qt 4.5.

### void QFileDialog::setDirectoryUrl(const [QUrl](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qurl.html) \&*directory*)

Sets the file dialog's current *directory* url.

**Note:** The non-native
[QFileDialog](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html) supports only local
files.

**Note:** On Windows, it is possible to pass URLs representing one of the *virtual
folders*, such as "Computer" or "Network". This is done by passing a
[QUrl](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qurl.html) using the scheme `clsid` followed
by the CLSID value with the curly braces removed. For example the URL
`clsid:374DE290-123F-4565-9164-39C4925E467B` denotes the download location. For a
complete list of possible values, see the MSDN documentation on
[KNOWNFOLDERID](https://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/windows/desktop/dd378457.aspx).
This feature was added in Qt 5.5.

This function was introduced in Qt 5.2.

**See also**
[directoryUrl](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html#directoryUrl)() and
[QUuid](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/quuid.html).

### void QFileDialog::setItemDelegate([QAbstractItemDelegate](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemdelegate.html) \**delegate*)

Sets the item delegate used to render items in the views in the file dialog to the given
*delegate*.

**Warning:** You should not share the same instance of a delegate between views. Doing
so can cause incorrect or unintuitive editing behavior since each view connected to a
given delegate may receive the
[closeEditor()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemdelegate.html#closeEditor)
signal, and attempt to access, modify or close an editor that has already been closed.

Note that the model used is
[QFileSystemModel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfilesystemmodel.html). It has
custom item data roles, which is described by the
[Roles](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfilesystemmodel.html#Roles-enum) enum. You
can use a [QFileIconProvider](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfileiconprovider.html)
if you only want custom icons.

Qt 5 reference:

### void QFileDialog::setMimeTypeFilters(const [QStringList](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstringlist.html) \&*filters*)

Sets the *filters* used in the file dialog, from a list of MIME types.

Convenience method for
[setNameFilters](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html#setNameFilters)().
Uses [QMimeType](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmimetype.html) to create a name
filter from the glob patterns and description defined in each MIME type.

Use application/octet-stream for the "All files (\*)" filter, since that is the base
MIME type for all files.

Calling setMimeTypeFilters overrides any previously set name filters, and changes the
return value of
[nameFilters](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html#nameFilters)().

```
QStringList mimeTypeFilters({"image/jpeg", // will show "JPEG image (*.jpeg *.jpg *.jpe)
                             "image/png",  // will show "PNG image (*.png)"
                             "application/octet-stream" // will show "All files (*)"
                            });

QFileDialog dialog(this);
dialog.setMimeTypeFilters(mimeTypeFilters);
dialog.exec();
```

This function was introduced in Qt 5.2.

**See also**
[mimeTypeFilters](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html#mimeTypeFilters)().

PythonQt.QtGui.QFileDialog.setNameFilter.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

### void QFileDialog::setNameFilter(const [QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html) \&*filter*)

Sets the filter used in the file dialog to the given *filter*.

If *filter* contains a pair of parentheses containing one or more filename-wildcard
patterns, separated by spaces, then only the text contained in the parentheses is used
as the filter. This means that these calls are all equivalent:

```
dialog.setNameFilter("All C++ files (*.cpp *.cc *.C *.cxx *.c++)");
dialog.setNameFilter("*.cpp *.cc *.C *.cxx *.c++");
```

**Note:** With Android's native file dialog, the mime type matching the given name
filter is used because only mime types are supported.

This function was introduced in Qt 4.4.

**See also**
[setMimeTypeFilters](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html#setMimeTypeFilters)()
and
[setNameFilters](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html#setNameFilters)().

Qt 5 reference:

### void QFileDialog::setNameFilters(const [QStringList](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstringlist.html) \&*filters*)

Sets the *filters* used in the file dialog.

Note that the filter **\*.\*** is not portable, because the historical assumption that
the file extension determines the file type is not consistent on every operating system.
It is possible to have a file with no dot in its name (for example, `Makefile`). In a
native Windows file dialog, **\*.\*** will match such files, while in other types of
file dialogs it may not. So it is better to use **\*** if you mean to select any file.

```
const QStringList filters({"Image files (*.png *.xpm *.jpg)",
                           "Text files (*.txt)",
                           "Any files (*)"
                          });
QFileDialog dialog(this);
dialog.setNameFilters(filters);
dialog.exec();
```

[setMimeTypeFilters](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html#setMimeTypeFilters)()
has the advantage of providing all possible name filters for each file type. For
example, JPEG images have three possible extensions; if your application can open such
files, selecting the `image/jpeg` mime type as a filter will allow you to open all of
them.

This function was introduced in Qt 4.4.

**See also**
[nameFilters](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html#nameFilters)().

### void QFileDialog::setOption([QFileDialog::Option](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfiledialog.html#Option-enum) *option*, bool *on* \= true)

Sets the given *option* to be enabled if *on* is true; otherwise, clears the given
*option*.

Options (particularly the DontUseNativeDialogs option) should be set before changing
dialog properties or showing the dialog.

Setting options while the dialog is visible is not guaranteed to have an immediate
effect on the dialog (depending on the option and on the platform).

Setting options after changing other properties may cause these values to have no
effect.

This function was introduced in Qt 4.5.

This property holds the URL schemes that the file dialog should allow navigating to.

select. It is a way for the application to declare the protocols it will support to
fetch the file content. An empty list means that no restriction is applied (the
default). Supported for local files ("file" scheme) is implicit and always enabled; it
is not necessary to include it in the restriction.

PythonQt.QtGui.QFileOpenEvent.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

File open events will be sent to the
[QApplication::instance](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcoreapplication.html#instance)()
when the operating system requests that a file or URL should be opened. This is a
high-level event that can be caused by different user actions depending on the user's
desktop environment; for example, double clicking on an file icon in the Finder on
macOS.

This event is only used to notify the application of a request. It may be safely
ignored.

**Note:** This class is currently supported for macOS only.

### macOS Example

In order to trigger the event on macOS, the application must be configured to let the OS
know what kind of file(s) it should react on.

For example, the following `Info.plist` file declares that the application can act as a
viewer for files with a PNG extension:

```
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
<plist version="1.0">
<dict>
    <key>CFBundleDocumentTypes</key>
    <array>
        <dict>
            <key>CFBundleTypeExtensions</key>
            <array>
                <string>png</string>
            </array>
            <key>CFBundleTypeRole</key>
            <string>Viewer</string>
        </dict>
    </array>
</dict>
</plist>
```

The following implementation of a
[QApplication](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qapplication.html) subclass prints the
path to the file that was, for example, dropped on the Dock icon of the application.

```
#include <QApplication>
#include <QFileOpenEvent>
#include <QtDebug>

class MyApplication : public QApplication
{
public:
    MyApplication(int &argc, char **argv)
        : QApplication(argc, argv)
    {
    }

    bool event(QEvent *event) override
    {
        if (event->type() == QEvent::FileOpen) {
            QFileOpenEvent *openEvent = static_cast<QFileOpenEvent *>(event);
            qDebug() << "Open file" << openEvent->file();
        }

        return QApplication::event(event);
    }
};
```

PythonQt.QtGui.QFileSystemModel.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

This class provides access to the local filesystem, providing functions for renaming and
removing files and directories, and for creating new directories. In the simplest case,
it can be used with a suitable display widget as part of a browser or filter.

QFileSystemModel can be accessed using the standard interface provided by
[QAbstractItemModel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html), but it
also provides some convenience functions that are specific to a directory model. The
[fileInfo](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfilesystemmodel.html#fileInfo)(),
[isDir](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfilesystemmodel.html#isDir)(),
[fileName](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfilesystemmodel.html#fileName)() and
[filePath](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfilesystemmodel.html#filePath)()
functions provide information about the underlying files and directories related to
items in the model. Directories can be created and removed using
[mkdir](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfilesystemmodel.html#mkdir)(),
[rmdir](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfilesystemmodel.html#rmdir)().

**Note:** QFileSystemModel requires an instance of
[QApplication](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qapplication.html).

### Example Usage

A directory model that displays the contents of a default directory is usually
constructed with a parent object:

```
    QFileSystemModel *model = new QFileSystemModel;
    model->setRootPath(QDir::currentPath());
```

A tree view can be used to display the contents of the model

```
    QTreeView *tree = new QTreeView(splitter);
    tree->setModel(model);
```

and the contents of a particular directory can be displayed by setting the tree view's
root index:

```
    tree->setRootIndex(model->index(QDir::currentPath()));
```

The view's root index can be used to control how much of a hierarchical model is
displayed. QFileSystemModel provides a convenience function that returns a suitable
model index for a path to a directory within the model.

### Caching and Performance

QFileSystemModel will not fetch any files or directories until
[setRootPath](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfilesystemmodel.html#setRootPath)() is
called. This will prevent any unnecessary querying on the file system until that point
such as listing the drives on Windows.

Unlike QDirModel, QFileSystemModel uses a separate thread to populate itself so it will
not cause the main thread to hang as the file system is being queried. Calls to
[rowCount](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfilesystemmodel.html#rowCount)() will
return 0 until the model populates a directory.

QFileSystemModel keeps a cache with file information. The cache is automatically kept up
to date using the
[QFileSystemWatcher](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfilesystemwatcher.html).

system watcher](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfilesystemwatcher.html) on it. Any

## Detailed Description

Focus events are sent to widgets when the keyboard input focus changes. Focus events
occur due to mouse actions, key presses (such as **Tab** or **Backtab**), the window
system, popup menus, keyboard shortcuts, or other application-specific reasons. The
reason for a particular focus event is returned by
[reason](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfocusevent.html#reason)() in the
appropriate event handler.

The event handlers
[QWidget::focusInEvent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#focusInEvent)(),
[QWidget::focusOutEvent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#focusOutEvent)(),
[QGraphicsItem::focusInEvent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsitem.html#focusInEvent)
and
[QGraphicsItem::focusOutEvent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsitem.html#focusOutEvent)()
receive focus events.

## Detailed Description

Normally an application will not need to create its own QFocusFrame as
[QStyle](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstyle.html) will handle this detail for
you. A style writer can optionally use a QFocusFrame to have a focus area outside of the
widget's paintable geometry. In this way space need not be reserved for the widget to
have focus but only set on a [QWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html)
with
[QFocusFrame::setWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfocusframe.html#setWidget).
It is, however, legal to create your own QFocusFrame on a custom widget and set its
geometry manually via

PythonQt.QtGui.QFont.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

QFont can be regarded as a query for one or more fonts on the system.

When you create a QFont object you specify various attributes that you want the font to
have. Qt will use the font with the specified attributes, or if no matching font exists,
Qt will use the closest matching installed font. The attributes of the font that is
actually used are retrievable from a
[QFontInfo](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfontinfo.html) object. If the window
system provides an exact match
[exactMatch](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfont.html#exactMatch)() returns `true`.
Use [QFontMetricsF](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfontmetricsf.html) to get
measurements, e.g. the pixel length of a string using QFontMetrics::width().

Attributes which are not specifically set will not affect the font selection algorithm,
and default values will be preferred instead.

To load a specific physical font, typically represented by a single file, use
[QRawFont](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qrawfont.html) instead.

Note that a [QGuiApplication](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qguiapplication.html)
instance must exist before a QFont can be used. You can set the application's default
font with
[QGuiApplication::setFont](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qguiapplication.html#setFont)().

If a chosen font does not include all the characters that need to be displayed, QFont
will try to find the characters in the nearest equivalent fonts. When a
[QPainter](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpainter.html) draws a character from a
font the QFont will report whether or not it has the character; if it does not,
[QPainter](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpainter.html) will draw an unfilled
square.

Create QFonts like this:

```
QFont serifFont("Times", 10, QFont::Bold);
QFont sansFont("Helvetica [Cronyx]", 12);
```

The attributes set in the constructor can also be set later, e.g.
[setFamily](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfont.html#setFamily)(),
[setPointSize](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfont.html#setPointSize)(),
[setPointSizeF](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfont.html#setPointSizeF)(),
[setWeight](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfont.html#setWeight)() and
[setItalic](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfont.html#setItalic)(). The remaining
attributes must be set after contstruction, e.g.
[setBold](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfont.html#setBold)(),
[setUnderline](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfont.html#setUnderline)(),
[setOverline](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfont.html#setOverline)(),
[setStrikeOut](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfont.html#setStrikeOut)() and
[setFixedPitch](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfont.html#setFixedPitch)().
[QFontInfo](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfontinfo.html) objects should be created
*after* the font's attributes have been set. A
[QFontInfo](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfontinfo.html) object will not change,
even if you change the font's attributes. The corresponding "get" functions, e.g.
[family](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfont.html#family)(),
[pointSize](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfont.html#pointSize)(), etc., return the
values that were set, even though the values used may differ. The actual values are
available from a [QFontInfo](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfontinfo.html) object.

If the requested font family is unavailable you can influence the [font matching
algorithm](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfont.html#fontmatching) by choosing a
particular
[QFont::StyleHint](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfont.html#StyleHint-enum) and
[QFont::StyleStrategy](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfont.html#StyleStrategy-enum)
with [setStyleHint](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfont.html#setStyleHint)(). The
default family (corresponding to the current style hint) is returned by
[defaultFamily](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfont.html#defaultFamily)().

You can provide substitutions for font family names using
[insertSubstitution](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfont.html#insertSubstitution)()
and
[insertSubstitutions](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfont.html#insertSubstitutions)().
Substitutions can be removed with
[removeSubstitutions](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfont.html#removeSubstitutions)().
Use [substitute](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfont.html#substitute)() to retrieve
a family's first substitute, or the family name itself if it has no substitutes. Use
[substitutes](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfont.html#substitutes)() to retrieve a
list of a family's substitutes (which may be empty). After substituting a font, you must
trigger the updating of the font by destroying and re-creating all QFont objects.

Every QFont has a [key](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfont.html#key)() which you
can use, for example, as the key in a cache or dictionary. If you want to store a user's
font preferences you could use
[QSettings](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsettings.html), writing the font
information with [toString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfont.html#toString)()
and reading it back with
[fromString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfont.html#fromString)(). The
operator\<\<() and operator\>\>() functions are also available, but they work on a data
stream.

It is possible to set the height of characters shown on the screen to a specified number
of pixels with
[setPixelSize](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfont.html#setPixelSize)(); however
using [setPointSize](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfont.html#setPointSize)() has a
similar effect and provides device independence.

Loading fonts can be expensive, especially on X11. QFont contains extensive
optimizations to make the copying of QFont objects fast, and to cache the results of the
slow window system functions it depends upon.

The font matching algorithm works as follows:

1. The specified font families (set by [setFamilies](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfont.html#setFamilies)()) are searched for.
2. If not found, then if set the specified font family exists and can be used to represent the writing system in use, it will be selected.
3. If not, a replacement font that supports the writing system is selected. The font matching algorithm will try to find the best match for all the properties set in the QFont. How this is done varies from platform to platform.
4. If no font exists on the system that can support the text, then special "missing character" boxes will be shown in its place.

**Note:** If the selected font, though supporting the writing system in general, is
missing glyphs for one or more specific characters, then Qt will try to find a fallback
font for this or these particular characters. This feature can be disabled using
[QFont::NoFontMerging](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfont.html#StyleStrategy-enum)
style strategy.

In Windows a request for the "Courier" font is automatically changed to "Courier New",
an improved version of Courier that allows for smooth scaling. The older "Courier"
bitmap font can be selected by setting the
[PreferBitmap](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfont.html#StyleStrategy-enum) style
strategy (see
[setStyleStrategy](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfont.html#setStyleStrategy)()).

Once a font is found, the remaining attributes are matched in order of priority:

1. [fixedPitch](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfont.html#fixedPitch)()
2. [pointSize](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfont.html#pointSize)() (see below)
3. [weight](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfont.html#weight)()
4. [style](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfont.html#style)()

If you have a font which matches on family, even if none of the other attributes match,
this font will be chosen in preference to a font which doesn't match on family but which
does match on the other attributes. This is because font family is the dominant search
criteria.

The point size is defined to match if it is within 20% of the requested point size. When
several fonts match and are only distinguished by point size, the font with the closest
point size to the one requested will be chosen.

The actual family, font size, weight and other font attributes used for drawing text
will depend on what's available for the chosen family under the window system. A
[QFontInfo](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfontinfo.html) object can be used to
determine the actual values used for drawing the text.

Examples:

```
QFont f("Helvetica");
```

If you had both an Adobe and a Cronyx Helvetica, you might get either.

```
QFont f("Helvetica [Cronyx]");
```

You can specify the foundry you want in the family name. The font f in the above example
will be set to "Helvetica \[Cronyx\]".

To determine the attributes of the font actually used in the window system, use a
[QFontInfo](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfontinfo.html) object, e.g.

```
QFontInfo info(f1);
QString family = info.family();
```

To find out font metrics use a
[QFontMetrics](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfontmetrics.html) object, e.g.

```
QFontMetrics fm(f1);
int textWidthInPixels = fm.horizontalAdvance("How many pixels wide is this text?");
int textHeightInPixels = fm.height();
```

For more general information on fonts, see the [comp.fonts
FAQ](http://nwalsh.com/comp.fonts/FAQ/). Information on encodings can be found from
[Roman Czyborra's](http://czyborra.com/) page.

### void QFont::setBold(bool *enable*)

If *enable* is true sets the font's weight to
[QFont::Bold](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfont.html#Weight-enum); otherwise sets
the weight to
[QFont::Normal](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfont.html#Weight-enum).

For finer boldness control use
[setWeight](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfont.html#setWeight)().

**Note:** If [styleName](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfont.html#styleName)() is
set, this value may be ignored, or if supported on the platform, the font artificially
embolded.

**See also** [bold](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfont.html#bold)() and
[setWeight](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfont.html#setWeight)().

### void QFont::setFamily(const [QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html) \&*family*)

Sets the family name of the font. The name is case insensitive and may include a foundry
name.

The *family* name may optionally also include a foundry name, e.g. "Helvetica
\[Cronyx\]". If the *family* is available from more than one foundry and the foundry
isn't specified, an arbitrary foundry is chosen. If the family isn't available a family
will be set using the [font matching](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfont.html)
algorithm.

**See also** [family](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfont.html#family)(),
[setStyleHint](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfont.html#setStyleHint)(), and
[QFontInfo](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfontinfo.html).

Qt 5 reference:

### void QFont::setKerning(bool *enable*)

Enables kerning for this font if *enable* is true; otherwise disables it. By default,
kerning is enabled.

When kerning is enabled, glyph metrics do not add up anymore, even for Latin text. In
other words, the assumption that width('a') \+ width('b') is equal to width("ab") is not
necessarily true.

**See also** [kerning](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfont.html#kerning)() and
[QFontMetrics](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfontmetrics.html).

PythonQt.QtGui.QFont.setStretch.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

### void QFont::setStretch(int *factor*)

Sets the stretch factor for the font.

The stretch factor matches a condensed or expanded version of the font or applies a
stretch transform that changes the width of all characters in the font by *factor*
percent. For example, setting *factor* to 150 results in all characters in the font
being 1.5 times (ie. 150%) wider. The minimum stretch factor is 1, and the maximum
stretch factor is 4000\. The default stretch factor is `AnyStretch`, which will accept
any stretch factor and not apply any transform on the font.

The stretch factor is only applied to outline fonts. The stretch factor is ignored for
bitmap fonts.

**Note:** When matching a font with a native non-default stretch factor, requesting a
stretch of 100 will stretch it back to a medium width font.

**See also** [stretch](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfont.html#stretch)() and
[QFont::Stretch](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfont.html#Stretch-enum).

### void QFont::setStyleName(const [QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html) \&*styleName*)

Sets the style name of the font to *styleName*. When set, other style properties like
[style](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfont.html#style)() and
[weight](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfont.html#weight)() will be ignored for

matching by style properties
