### minimumRenderSize : [qreal](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtglobal.html#qreal-typedef)

This property holds the minimal view-transformed size an item must have to be drawn

When the scene is rendered, any item whose width or height, transformed to the target
view, is smaller that minimumRenderSize(), will not be rendered. If an item is not
rendered and it clips its children items they will also not be rendered. Set this value
to speed up rendering of scenes with many objects rendered on a zoomed out view.

The default value is 0\. If unset, or if set to 0 or a negative value, all items will
always be rendered.

For example, setting this property can be especially useful if a scene is rendered by
multiple views, one of which serves as an overview which always displays all items. In
scenes with many items, such a view will use a high scaling factor so that all items can
be shown. Due to the scaling, smaller items will only make an insignificant contribution
to the final rendered scene. To avoid drawing these items and reduce the time necessary
to render the scene, you can call setMinimumRenderSize() with a non-negative value.

**Note:** Items that are not drawn as a result of being too small, are still returned by
methods such as [items](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsscene.html#items)()
and [itemAt](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsscene.html#itemAt)(), and
participate in collision detection and interactions. It is recommended that you set
minimumRenderSize() to a value less than or equal to 1 in order to avoid large
unrendered items that are interactive.

This property was introduced in Qt 5.4.

**Access functions:**

| qreal | **minimumRenderSize**() const |
| --- | --- |
| void | **setMinimumRenderSize**(qreal *minSize*) |

### `[virtual protected]` void QGraphicsScene::mouseDoubleClickEvent([QGraphicsSceneMouseEvent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsscenemouseevent.html) \**mouseEvent*)

This event handler, for event *mouseEvent*, can be reimplemented in a subclass to
receive mouse double-click events for the scene.

If someone doubleclicks on the scene, the scene will first receive a mouse press event,
followed by a release event (i.e., a click), then a double-click event, and finally a
release event. If the double-click event is delivered to a different item than the one
that received the first press and release, it will be delivered as a press event.
However, tripleclick events are not delivered as double-click events in this case.

The default implementation is similar to
[mousePressEvent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsscene.html#mousePressEvent)().

Note: See [items](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsscene.html#items)() for a
definition of which items are considered visible by this function.

**See also**
[QGraphicsItem::mousePressEvent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsitem.html#mousePressEvent)(),
[QGraphicsItem::mouseMoveEvent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsitem.html#mouseMoveEvent)(),
[QGraphicsItem::mouseReleaseEvent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsitem.html#mouseReleaseEvent)(),
and
[QGraphicsItem::setAcceptedMouseButtons](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsitem.html#setAcceptedMouseButtons)().

PythonQt.QtGui.QGraphicsScene.mouseGrabb.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

### [QGraphicsItem](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsitem.html) \*QGraphicsScene::mouseGrabberItem() const

Returns the current mouse grabber item, or `nullptr` if no item is currently grabbing
the mouse. The mouse grabber item is the item that receives all mouse events sent to the
scene.

An item becomes a mouse grabber when it receives and accepts a mouse press event, and it
stays the mouse grabber until either of the following events occur:

- If the item receives a mouse release event when there are no other buttons pressed, it loses the mouse grab.
- If the item becomes invisible (i.e., someone calls `item->setVisible(false)`), or if it becomes disabled (i.e., someone calls `item->setEnabled(false)`), it loses the mouse grab.
- If the item is removed from the scene, it loses the mouse grab.

If the item loses its mouse grab, the scene will ignore all mouse events until a new
item grabs the mouse (i.e., until a new item receives a mouse press event).

### `[virtual protected]` void QGraphicsScene::mouseMoveEvent([QGraphicsSceneMouseEvent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsscenemouseevent.html) \**mouseEvent*)

This event handler, for event *mouseEvent*, can be reimplemented in a subclass to
receive mouse move events for the scene.

The default implementation depends on the mouse grabber state. If there is a mouse
grabber item, the event is sent to the mouse grabber. If there are any items that accept

accepted; otherwise it's ignored.

PythonQt.QtGui.QGraphicsScene.mousePress.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

### `[virtual protected]` void QGraphicsScene::mousePressEvent([QGraphicsSceneMouseEvent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsscenemouseevent.html) \**mouseEvent*)

This event handler, for event *mouseEvent*, can be reimplemented in a subclass to
receive mouse press events for the scene.

The default implementation depends on the state of the scene. If there is a mouse
grabber item, then the event is sent to the mouse grabber. Otherwise, it is forwarded to
the topmost visible item that accepts mouse events at the scene position from the event,
and that item promptly becomes the mouse grabber item.

If there is no item at the given position on the scene, the selection area is reset, any
focus item loses its input focus, and the event is then ignored.

Note: See [items](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsscene.html#items)() for a
definition of which items are considered visible by this function.

**See also**
[QGraphicsItem::mousePressEvent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsitem.html#mousePressEvent)()
and
[QGraphicsItem::setAcceptedMouseButtons](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsitem.html#setAcceptedMouseButtons)().

### palette : [QPalette](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpalette.html)

This property holds the scene's default palette

This property provides the scene's palette. The scene palette defaults to, and resolves
all its entries from,
[QApplication::palette](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qapplication.html#palette).

If the scene's palette changes, either directly through setPalette() or indirectly when
the application palette changes,
[QGraphicsScene](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsscene.html) first sends
itself a [PaletteChange](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qevent.html#Type-enum)
event, and it then sends
[PaletteChange](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qevent.html#Type-enum) events to all
top-level widget items in the scene. These items respond by resolving their own palettes
to the scene, and they then notify their children, who again notify their children, and
so on, until all widget items have updated their palettes.

Changing the scene palette, (directly or indirectly through
[QApplication::setPalette](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qapplication.html#setPalette)(),)
automatically schedules a redraw the entire scene.

This property was introduced in Qt 4.4.

**Access functions:**

| QPalette | **palette**() const |
| --- | --- |

### void QGraphicsScene::render([QPainter](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpainter.html) \**painter*, const [QRectF](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qrectf.html) \&*target* \= QRectF(), const [QRectF](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qrectf.html) \&*source* \= QRectF(), [Qt::AspectRatioMode](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#AspectRatioMode-enum) *aspectRatioMode* \= Qt::KeepAspectRatio)

Renders the *source* rect from scene into *target*, using *painter*. This function is
useful for capturing the contents of the scene onto a paint device, such as a
[QImage](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qimage.html) (e.g., to take a screenshot),
or for printing with QPrinter. For example:

```
QGraphicsScene scene;
scene.addItem(...
...
QPrinter printer(QPrinter::HighResolution);
printer.setPaperSize(QPrinter::A4);

QPainter painter(&printer);
scene.render(&painter);
```

If *source* is a null rect, this function will use
[sceneRect](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsscene.html#sceneRect-prop)() to
determine what to render. If *target* is a null rect, the dimensions of *painter*'s
paint device will be used.

The source rect contents will be transformed according to *aspectRatioMode* to fit into
the target rect. By default, the aspect ratio is kept, and *source* is scaled to fit in
*target*.

**See also**
[QGraphicsView::render](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsview.html#render)().

### sceneRect : [QRectF](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qrectf.html)

This property holds the scene rectangle; the bounding rectangle of the scene

The scene rectangle defines the extent of the scene. It is primarily used by
[QGraphicsView](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsview.html) to determine the
view's default scrollable area, and by
[QGraphicsScene](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsscene.html) to manage item
indexing.

If unset, or if set to a null [QRectF](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qrectf.html),
sceneRect() will return the largest bounding rect of all items on the scene since the
scene was created (i.e., a rectangle that grows when items are added to or moved in the
scene, but never shrinks).

### `[signal]` void QGraphicsScene::selectionChanged()

This signal is emitted by
[QGraphicsScene](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsscene.html) whenever the
selection changes. You can call
[selectedItems](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsscene.html#selectedItems)()
to get the new list of selected items.

The selection changes whenever an item is selected or unselected, a selection area is
set, cleared or otherwise changed, if a preselected item is added to the scene, or if a
selected item is removed from the scene.

[QGraphicsScene](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsscene.html) emits this
signal only once for group selection operations. For example, if you set a selection
area, select or unselect a
[QGraphicsItemGroup](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsitemgroup.html), or if
you add or remove from the scene a parent item that contains several selected items,
selectionChanged() is emitted only once after the operation has completed (instead of
once for each item).

This function was introduced in Qt 4.3.

**See also**
[setSelectionArea](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsscene.html#setSelectionArea)(),
[selectedItems](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsscene.html#selectedItems)(),

### void QGraphicsScene::setFocus([Qt::FocusReason](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#FocusReason-enum) *focusReason* \= Qt::OtherFocusReason)

Sets focus on the scene by sending a
[QFocusEvent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfocusevent.html) to the scene, passing
*focusReason* as the reason. If the scene regains focus after having previously lost it
while an item had focus, the last focus item will receive focus with *focusReason* as
the reason.

If the scene already has focus, this function does nothing.

**See also**
[hasFocus](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsscene.html#hasFocus)(),
[clearFocus](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsscene.html#clearFocus)(), and

Sets the scene's focus item to *item*, with the focus reason *focusReason*, after
removing focus from any previous item that may have had focus.

If *item* is `nullptr`, or if it either does not accept focus (i.e., it does not have
the
[QGraphicsItem::ItemIsFocusable](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsitem.html#GraphicsItemFlag-enum)

any previous focusitem.

If item is not `nullptr`, and the scene does not currently have focus (i.e.,
[hasFocus](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsscene.html#hasFocus)() returns
`false`), this function will call
[setFocus](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsscene.html#setFocus)()

### void QGraphicsScene::setStyle([QStyle](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstyle.html) \**style*)

Sets or replaces the style of the scene to *style*, and reparents the style to this
scene. Any previously assigned style is deleted. The scene's style defaults to
[QApplication::style](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qapplication.html#style)(), and
serves as the default for all
[QGraphicsWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/graphicsview.html#qgraphicswidget)
items in the scene.

Changing the style, either directly by calling this function, or indirectly by calling
[QApplication::setStyle](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qapplication.html#setStyle)(),
will automatically update the style for all widgets in the scene that do not have a
style explicitly assigned to them.

If *style* is `nullptr`,
[QGraphicsScene](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsscene.html) will revert to
[QApplication::style](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qapplication.html#style)().

This function was introduced in Qt 4.4.

**See also** [style](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsscene.html#style)().

### stickyFocus : bool

This property holds whether clicking into the scene background will clear focus

In a [QGraphicsScene](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsscene.html) with
stickyFocus set to true, focus will remain unchanged when the user clicks into the scene
background or on an item that does not accept focus. Otherwise, focus will be cleared.

By default, this property is `false`.

Focus changes in response to a mouse press. You can reimplement
[mousePressEvent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsscene.html#mousePressEvent)()
in a subclass of
[QGraphicsScene](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsscene.html) to toggle this
property based on where the user has clicked.

This property was introduced in Qt 4.6.

This event handler, for event *wheelEvent*, can be reimplemented in a subclass to
receive mouse wheel events for the scene.

By default, the event is delivered to the topmost visible item under the cursor. If
ignored, the event propagates to the item beneath, and again until the event is
accepted, or it reaches the scene. If no items accept the event, it is ignored.

[QGraphicsView](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsview.html) inherits the drag
and drop functionality provided by
[QWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html). When it receives a drag and
drop event, it translates it to a QGraphicsSceneDragDropEvent.

QGraphicsSceneDragDropEvent stores events of type
[GraphicsSceneDragEnter](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qevent.html#Type-enum),
[GraphicsSceneDragLeave](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qevent.html#Type-enum),
[GraphicsSceneDragMove](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qevent.html#Type-enum), or
[GraphicsSceneDrop](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qevent.html#Type-enum).

QGraphicsSceneDragDropEvent contains the position of the mouse cursor in both item,
scene, and screen coordinates; this can be retrieved with
[pos](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsscenedragdropevent.html#pos)(),
[scenePos](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsscenedragdropevent.html#scenePos)(),
and
[screenPos](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsscenedragdropevent.html#screenPos)().

The scene sends the event to the first
[QGraphicsItem](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsitem.html) under the mouse
cursor that accepts drops; a graphics item is set to accept drops with
[setAcceptDrops()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsitem.html#setAcceptDrops).

### void QGraphicsSceneDragDropEvent::acceptProposedAction()

Sets the proposed action as accepted, i.e, the drop action is set to the proposed

## Detailed Description

When a [QGraphicsView](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsview.html) receives
Qt mouse, keyboard, and drag and drop events
([QMouseEvent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmouseevent.html),
[QKeyEvent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qkeyevent.html), QDragEvent, etc.), it
translates them into instances of QGraphicsSceneEvent subclasses and forwards them to
the [QGraphicsScene](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsscene.html) it
displays. The scene then forwards the events to the relevant items.

For example, when a
[QGraphicsView](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsview.html) receives a
[QMouseEvent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmouseevent.html) of type MousePress as
a response to a user click, the view sends a
[QGraphicsSceneMouseEvent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsscenemouseevent.html)
of type
[GraphicsSceneMousePress](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qevent.html#Type-enum) to
the underlying [QGraphicsScene](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsscene.html)
through its
[mousePressEvent()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsscene.html#mousePressEvent)
function. The default
[QGraphicsScene::mousePressEvent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsscene.html#mousePressEvent)()
implementation determines which item was clicked and forwards the event to
[QGraphicsItem::mousePressEvent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsitem.html#mousePressEvent)().

Subclasses such as
[QGraphicsSceneMouseEvent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsscenemouseevent.html)
and
[QGraphicsSceneContextMenuEvent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsscenecontextmenuevent.html)
provide the coordinates from the original
[QEvent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qevent.html) in screen, scene, and item
coordinates (see
[screenPos()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsscenemouseevent.html#screenPos),
[scenePos()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsscenemouseevent.html#scenePos),
and [pos()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsscenemouseevent.html#pos)). The
item coordinates are set by the
[QGraphicsScene](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsscene.html) before it
forwards the event to the event to a
[QGraphicsItem](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsitem.html). The mouse events
also add the possibility to retrieve the coordinates from the last event received by the
view (see
[lastScreenPos()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsscenemouseevent.html#lastScreenPos),
[lastScenePos()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsscenemouseevent.html#lastScenePos),
and
[lastPos()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsscenemouseevent.html#lastPos)).

## Detailed Description

When a [QGraphicsView](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsview.html) receives a
[QEvent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qevent.html) of type
[QEvent::ToolTip](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qevent.html#Type-enum), it creates
a QGraphicsSceneHelpEvent, which is forwarded to the scene. You can set a tooltip on a
[QGraphicsItem](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsitem.html) with
[setToolTip()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsitem.html#setToolTip); by
default [QGraphicsScene](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsscene.html)
displays the tooltip of the
[QGraphicsItem](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsitem.html) with the highest
z-value (i.e, the top-most item) under the mouse position.

[QGraphicsView](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsview.html) does not forward
events when ["What's This"](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwhatsthis.html) and
[status tip](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstatustipevent.html) help is requested.
If you need this, you can reimplement
[QGraphicsView::viewportEvent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsview.html#viewportEvent)()
and forward [QStatusTipEvent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstatustipevent.html)
events and [QEvents](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qevent.html) of type
[QEvent::WhatsThis](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qevent.html#Type-enum) to the
scene.

## Detailed Description

When a [QGraphicsView](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsview.html) receives a
[QMouseEvent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmouseevent.html), it translates it to
a QGraphicsSceneMouseEvent. The event is then forwarded to the
[QGraphicsScene](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsscene.html) associated with
the view. If the event is not handled by the scene, the view may use it, e.g., for the
[DragMode](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsview.html#DragMode-enum).

In addition to containing the item, scene, and screen coordinates of the event (as
[pos](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsscenemouseevent.html#pos)(),
[scenePos](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsscenemouseevent.html#scenePos)(),
and
[screenPos](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsscenemouseevent.html#screenPos)()),
mouse events also contain the coordinates of the previous mouse event received by the
view. These can be retrieved with
[lastPos](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsscenemouseevent.html#lastPos)(),
[lastScreenPos](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsscenemouseevent.html#lastScreenPos)(),
and
[lastScenePos](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsscenemouseevent.html#lastScenePos)().

## Detailed Description

A
[QGraphicsWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/graphicsview.html#qgraphicswidget)
sends itself a QGraphicsSceneMoveEvent immediately when its local position changes. The

[QPointF](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpointf.html) instead of
[QPoint](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpoint.html).

## Detailed Description

To set the item's text, you can either pass a
[QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html) to QGraphicsSimpleTextItem's
constructor, or call
[setText](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicssimpletextitem.html#setText)() to
change the text later. To set the text fill color, call
[setBrush](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractgraphicsshapeitem.html#setBrush)().

The simple text item can have both a fill and an outline;
[setBrush](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractgraphicsshapeitem.html#setBrush)()
will set the text fill (i.e., text color), and
[setPen](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractgraphicsshapeitem.html#setPen)()
sets the pen that will be used to draw the text outline. (The latter can be slow,
especially for complex pens, and items with long text content.) If all you want is to
draw a simple line of text, you should call
[setBrush](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractgraphicsshapeitem.html#setBrush)()
only, and leave the pen unset; QGraphicsSimpleTextItem's pen is by default
[Qt::NoPen](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#PenStyle-enum).

QGraphicsSimpleTextItem uses the text's formatted size and the associated font to
provide a reasonable implementation of
[boundingRect](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicssimpletextitem.html#boundingRect)(),
[shape](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicssimpletextitem.html#shape)(), and
[contains](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicssimpletextitem.html#contains)().
You can set the font by calling
[setFont](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicssimpletextitem.html#setFont)().

QGraphicsSimpleText does not display rich text; instead, you can use
[QGraphicsTextItem](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicstextitem.html), which
provides full text control capabilities.

![](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/images/graphicsview-simpletextitem.png)

Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

If you only need to show plain text in an item, consider using
[QGraphicsSimpleTextItem](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicssimpletextitem.html)
instead.

To set the item's text, pass a
[QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html) to QGraphicsTextItem's
constructor, or call
[setHtml](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicstextitem.html#setHtml)()/[setPlainText](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicstextitem.html#setPlainText)().

QGraphicsTextItem uses the text's formatted size and the associated font to provide a
reasonable implementation of
[boundingRect](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicstextitem.html#boundingRect)(),
[shape](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicstextitem.html#shape)(), and
[contains](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicstextitem.html#contains)(). You
can set the font by calling
[setFont](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicstextitem.html#setFont)().

It is possible to make the item editable by setting the
[Qt::TextEditorInteraction](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#TextInteractionFlag-enum)
flag using
[setTextInteractionFlags](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicstextitem.html#setTextInteractionFlags)().

The item's preferred text width can be set using
[setTextWidth](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicstextitem.html#setTextWidth)()
and obtained using
[textWidth](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicstextitem.html#textWidth)().

**Note:** In order to align HTML text in the center, the item's text width must be set.
Otherwise, you can call
[adjustSize](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicstextitem.html#adjustSize)()
after setting the item's text.

![](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/images/graphicsview-textitem.png)

**Note:** QGraphicsTextItem accepts [hover
events](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsitem.html#acceptHoverEvents) by
default. You can change this with
[setAcceptHoverEvents()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsitem.html#setAcceptHoverEvents).

### void QGraphicsTextItem::setTabChangesFocus(bool *b*)

If *b* is true, the **Tab** key will cause the widget to change focus; otherwise, the
tab key will insert a tab into the document.

In some occasions text edits should not allow the user to input tabulators or change
indentation using the **Tab** key, as this breaks the focus chain. The default is false.

This function was introduced in Qt 4.5.

**See also**
[tabChangesFocus](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicstextitem.html#tabChangesFocus)(),
[ItemIsFocusable](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsitem.html#GraphicsItemFlag-enum),
and
[textInteractionFlags](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicstextitem.html#textInteractionFlags)().

### void QGraphicsTextItem::setTextInteractionFlags([Qt::TextInteractionFlags](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#TextInteractionFlag-enum) *flags*)

Sets the flags *flags* to specify how the text item should react to user input.

The default for a
[QGraphicsTextItem](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicstextitem.html) is
[Qt::NoTextInteraction](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#TextInteractionFlag-enum).
This function also affects the
[ItemIsFocusable](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsitem.html#GraphicsItemFlag-enum)
[QGraphicsItem](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsitem.html) flag by setting
it if *flags* is different from
[Qt::NoTextInteraction](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#TextInteractionFlag-enum)
and clearing it otherwise.

By default, the text is read-only. To transform the item into an editor, set the
[Qt::TextEditable](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#TextInteractionFlag-enum)
flag.

**See also**
[textInteractionFlags](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicstextitem.html#textInteractionFlags)().

Qt 5 reference:

### void QGraphicsTextItem::setTextWidth([qreal](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtglobal.html#qreal-typedef) *width*)

Sets the preferred width for the item's text. If the actual text is wider than the
specified width then it will be broken into multiple lines.

If *width* is set to -1 then the text will not be broken into multiple lines unless it
is enforced through an explicit line break or a new paragraph.

The default value is -1.

Note that [QGraphicsTextItem](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicstextitem.html)
keeps a [QTextDocument](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html)
internally, which is used to calculate the text width.

**See also**
[textWidth](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicstextitem.html#textWidth)() and
[QTextDocument::setTextWidth](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html#textWidth-prop)().

PythonQt.QtGui.QGraphicsTransform.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

As an alternative to
[QGraphicsItem::transform](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsitem.html#transform),
QGraphicsTransform lets you create and control advanced transformations that can be
configured independently using specialized properties.

[QGraphicsItem](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsitem.html) allows you to
assign any number of QGraphicsTransform instances to one
[QGraphicsItem](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsitem.html). Each
QGraphicsTransform is applied in order, one at a time, to the
[QGraphicsItem](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsitem.html) it's assigned to.

QGraphicsTransform is particularly useful for animations. Whereas
[QGraphicsItem::setTransform](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsitem.html#setTransform)()
lets you assign any transform directly to an item, there is no direct way to interpolate
between two different transformations (e.g., when transitioning between two states, each
for which the item has a different arbitrary transform assigned). Using
QGraphicsTransform you can interpolate the property values of each independent
transformation. The resulting operation is then combined into a single transform which
is applied to [QGraphicsItem](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsitem.html).

Transformations are computed in true 3D space using
[QMatrix4x4](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmatrix4x4.html). When the
transformation is applied to a
[QGraphicsItem](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsitem.html), it will be
projected back to a 2D [QTransform](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtransform.html).
When multiple QGraphicsTransform objects are applied to a
[QGraphicsItem](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsitem.html), all of the
transformations are computed in true 3D space, with the projection back to 2D only
occurring after the last QGraphicsTransform is applied. The exception to this is
[QGraphicsRotation](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsrotation.html), which
projects back to 2D after each rotation to preserve the perspective effect around the X
and Y axes.

If you want to create your own configurable transformation, you can create a subclass of
QGraphicsTransform (or any or the existing subclasses), and reimplement the pure virtual
[applyTo](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicstransform.html#applyTo)()
function, which takes a pointer to a
[QMatrix4x4](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmatrix4x4.html). Each operation you
would like to apply should be exposed as properties (e.g.,
customTransform-\>setVerticalShear(2.5)). Inside you reimplementation of
[applyTo](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicstransform.html#applyTo)(), you can
modify the provided transform respectively.

QGraphicsTransform can be used together with
[QGraphicsItem::setTransform](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsitem.html#setTransform)(),
[QGraphicsItem::setRotation](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsitem.html#setRotation)(),
and
[QGraphicsItem::setScale](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsitem.html#setScale)().

PythonQt.QtGui.QGraphicsView.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

QGraphicsView visualizes the contents of a
[QGraphicsScene](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsscene.html) in a scrollable
viewport. To create a scene with geometrical items, see
[QGraphicsScene](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsscene.html)'s
documentation. QGraphicsView is part of the [Graphics View
Framework](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/graphicsview.html).

To visualize a scene, you start by constructing a QGraphicsView object, passing the
address of the scene you want to visualize to QGraphicsView's constructor.
Alternatively, you can call
[setScene](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsview.html#setScene)() to set the
scene at a later point. After you call
[show](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#show)(), the view will by default
scroll to the center of the scene and display any items that are visible at this point.
For example:

```
QGraphicsScene scene;
scene.addText("Hello, world!");

QGraphicsView view(&scene);
view.show();
```

You can explicitly scroll to any position on the scene by using the scroll bars, or by
calling [centerOn](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsview.html#centerOn)(). By
passing a point to
[centerOn](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsview.html#centerOn)(),
QGraphicsView will scroll its viewport to ensure that the point is centered in the view.
An overload is provided for scrolling to a
[QGraphicsItem](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsitem.html), in which case
QGraphicsView will see to that the center of the item is centered in the view. If all
you want is to ensure that a certain area is visible, (but not necessarily centered,)
you can call
[ensureVisible](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsview.html#ensureVisible)()
instead.

QGraphicsView can be used to visualize a whole scene, or only parts of it. The
visualized area is by default detected automatically when the view is displayed for the
first time (by calling
[QGraphicsScene::itemsBoundingRect](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsscene.html#itemsBoundingRect)()).
To set the visualized area rectangle yourself, you can call
[setSceneRect](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsview.html#sceneRect-prop)().
This will adjust the scroll bars' ranges appropriately. Note that although the scene
supports a virtually unlimited size, the range of the scroll bars will never exceed the
range of an integer (INT\_MIN, INT\_MAX).

QGraphicsView visualizes the scene by calling
[render](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsview.html#render)(). By default,
the items are drawn onto the viewport by using a regular
[QPainter](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpainter.html), and using default render
hints. To change the default render hints that QGraphicsView passes to
[QPainter](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpainter.html) when painting items, you
can call
[setRenderHints](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsview.html#renderHints-prop)().

By default, QGraphicsView provides a regular
[QWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html) for the viewport widget. You
can access this widget by calling
[viewport](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractscrollarea.html#viewport)(), or
you can replace it by calling
[setViewport](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractscrollarea.html#setViewport)().
To render using OpenGL, simply call
[setViewport](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractscrollarea.html#setViewport)(new
[QOpenGLWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglwidget.html)). QGraphicsView
takes ownership of the viewport widget.

QGraphicsView supports affine transformations, using
[QTransform](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtransform.html). You can either pass a
matrix to
[setTransform](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsview.html#setTransform)(), or
you can call one of the convenience functions
[rotate](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsview.html#rotate)(),
[scale](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsview.html#scale)(),
[translate](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsview.html#translate)() or
[shear](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsview.html#shear)(). The most two
common transformations are scaling, which is used to implement zooming, and rotation.
QGraphicsView keeps the center of the view fixed during a transformation. Because of the
scene alignment (setAligment()), translating the view will have no visual impact.

You can interact with the items on the scene by using the mouse and keyboard.
QGraphicsView translates the mouse and key events into *scene* events, (events that
inherit
[QGraphicsSceneEvent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicssceneevent.html),),
and forward them to the visualized scene. In the end, it's the individual item that
handles the events and reacts to them. For example, if you click on a selectable item,
the item will typically let the scene know that it has been selected, and it will also
redraw itself to display a selection rectangle. Similarly, if you click and drag the
mouse to move a movable item, it's the item that handles the mouse moves and moves
itself. Item interaction is enabled by default, and you can toggle it by calling
[setInteractive](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsview.html#interactive-prop)().

You can also provide your own custom scene interaction, by creating a subclass of
QGraphicsView, and reimplementing the mouse and key event handlers. To simplify how you
programmatically interact with items in the view, QGraphicsView provides the mapping
functions
[mapToScene](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsview.html#mapToScene)() and
[mapFromScene](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsview.html#mapFromScene)(),
and the item accessors
[items](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsview.html#items)() and
[itemAt](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsview.html#itemAt)(). These
functions allow you to map points, rectangles, polygons and paths between view
coordinates and scene coordinates, and to find items on the scene using view
coordinates.

![](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/images/graphicsview-view.png)

**Note:** Using an OpenGL viewport limits the ability to use
[QGraphicsProxyWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsproxywidget.html).
Not all combinations of widgets and styles can be supported with such a setup. You
should carefully test your UI and make the necessary adjustments.

### alignment : [Qt::Alignment](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#AlignmentFlag-enum)

This property holds the alignment of the scene in the view when the whole scene is
visible.

If the whole scene is visible in the view, (i.e., there are no visible scroll bars,) the
view's alignment will decide where the scene will be rendered in the view. For example,
if the alignment is
[Qt::AlignCenter](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#AlignmentFlag-enum), which
is default, the scene will be centered in the view, and if the alignment is
([Qt::AlignLeft](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#AlignmentFlag-enum) \|
[Qt::AlignTop](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#AlignmentFlag-enum)), the
scene will be rendered in the top-left corner of the view.

PythonQt.QtGui.QGraphicsView.cacheMode.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

### cacheMode : [CacheMode](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsview.html#CacheModeFlag-enum)

This property holds which parts of the view are cached

[QGraphicsView](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsview.html) can cache
pre-rendered content in a [QPixmap](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpixmap.html),
which is then drawn onto the viewport. The purpose of such caching is to speed up the
total rendering time for areas that are slow to render. Texture, gradient and alpha
blended backgrounds, for example, can be notibly slow to render; especially with a
transformed view. The
[CacheBackground](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsview.html#CacheModeFlag-enum)
flag enables caching of the view's background. For example:

```
QGraphicsView view;
view.setBackgroundBrush(QImage(":/images/backgroundtile.png"));
view.setCacheMode(QGraphicsView::CacheBackground);
```

The cache is invalidated every time the view is transformed. However, when scrolling,
only partial invalidation is required.

By default, nothing is cached.

**Access functions:**

| QGraphicsView::CacheMode | **cacheMode**() const |
| --- | --- |
| void | **setCacheMode**(QGraphicsView::CacheMode *mode*) |

**See also**
[resetCachedContent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsview.html#resetCachedContent)()
and [QPixmapCache](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpixmapcache.html).

### void QGraphicsView::fitInView(const [QRectF](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qrectf.html) \&*rect*, [Qt::AspectRatioMode](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#AspectRatioMode-enum) *aspectRatioMode* \= Qt::IgnoreAspectRatio)

Scales the view matrix and scrolls the scroll bars to ensure that the scene rectangle
*rect* fits inside the viewport. *rect* must be inside the scene rect; otherwise,
fitInView() cannot guarantee that the whole rect is visible.

This function keeps the view's rotation, translation, or shear. The view is scaled
according to *aspectRatioMode*. *rect* will be centered in the view if it does not fit
tightly.

It's common to call fitInView() from inside a reimplementation of
[resizeEvent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsview.html#resizeEvent)(), to
ensure that the whole scene, or parts of the scene, scales automatically to fit the new
size of the viewport as the view is resized. Note though, that calling fitInView() from
inside
[resizeEvent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsview.html#resizeEvent)() can
lead to unwanted resize recursion, if the new transformation toggles the automatic state
of the scrollbars. You can toggle the scrollbar policies to always on or always off to
prevent this (see
[horizontalScrollBarPolicy](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractscrollarea.html#horizontalScrollBarPolicy-prop)()
and
[verticalScrollBarPolicy](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractscrollarea.html#verticalScrollBarPolicy-prop)()).

If *rect* is empty, or if the viewport is too small, this function will do nothing.

**See also**
[setTransform](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsview.html#setTransform)(),
[ensureVisible](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsview.html#ensureVisible)(),
and [centerOn](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsview.html#centerOn)().

### void QGraphicsView::fitInView([qreal](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtglobal.html#qreal-typedef) *x*, [qreal](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtglobal.html#qreal-typedef) *y*, [qreal](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtglobal.html#qreal-typedef) *w*, [qreal](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtglobal.html#qreal-typedef) *h*, [Qt::AspectRatioMode](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#AspectRatioMode-enum) *aspectRatioMode* \= Qt::IgnoreAspectRatio)

### [QList](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qlist.html)\<[QGraphicsItem](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsitem.html) \*\> QGraphicsView::items(const [QPoint](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpoint.html) \&*pos*) const

Returns a list of all the items at the position *pos* in the view. The items are listed
in descending stacking order (i.e., the first item in the list is the uppermost item,
and the last item is the lowermost item). *pos* is in viewport coordinates.

This function is most commonly called from within mouse event handlers in a subclass in
[QGraphicsView](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsview.html). *pos* is in
untransformed viewport coordinates, just like
[QMouseEvent::pos](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmouseevent.html#pos)().

```
void CustomView::mousePressEvent(QMouseEvent *event)
{
    qDebug() << "There are" << items(event->pos()).size()
             << "items at position" << mapToScene(event->pos());
}
```

### optimizationFlags : [OptimizationFlags](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsview.html#OptimizationFlag-enum)

flags that can be used to tune
[QGraphicsView](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsview.html)'s performance.

[QGraphicsView](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsview.html) uses clipping,
extra bounding rect adjustments, and certain other aids to improve rendering quality and
performance for the common case graphics scene. However, depending on the target
platform, the scene, and the viewport in use, some of these operations can degrade
performance.

The effect varies from flag to flag; see the
[OptimizationFlags](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsview.html#OptimizationFlag-enum)
documentation for details.

By default, no optimization flags are enabled.

This property was introduced in Qt 4.3.

### renderHints : [QPainter::RenderHints](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpainter.html#RenderHint-enum)

This property holds the default render hints for the view

These hints are used to initialize
[QPainter](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpainter.html) before each visible item is
drawn. [QPainter](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpainter.html) uses render hints to
toggle rendering features such as antialiasing and smooth pixmap transformation.

[QPainter::TextAntialiasing](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpainter.html#RenderHint-enum)
is enabled by default.

Example:

```
QGraphicsScene scene;
scene.addRect(QRectF(-10, -10, 20, 20));

QGraphicsView view(&scene);
view.setRenderHints(QPainter::Antialiasing | QPainter::SmoothPixmapTransform);
view.show();
```

### resizeAnchor : [ViewportAnchor](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsview.html#ViewportAnchor-enum)

how the view should position the scene when the view is resized.

[QGraphicsView](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsview.html) uses this
property to decide how to position the scene in the viewport when the viewport widget's
size changes. The default behavior,
[NoAnchor](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsview.html#ViewportAnchor-enum),
leaves the scene's position unchanged during a resize; the top-left corner of the view
will appear to be anchored while resizing.

Note that the effect of this property is noticeable when only a part of the scene is
visible (i.e., when there are scroll bars). Otherwise, if the whole scene fits in the
view, [QGraphicsScene](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsscene.html) uses the
view [alignment](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/stylesheet-reference.html#alignment)
to position the scene in the view.

### sceneRect : [QRectF](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qrectf.html)

This property holds the area of the scene visualized by this view.

The scene rectangle defines the extent of the scene, and in the view's case, this means
the area of the scene that you can navigate using the scroll bars.

If unset, or if a null [QRectF](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qrectf.html) is set,
this property has the same value as
[QGraphicsScene::sceneRect](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsscene.html#sceneRect-prop),
and it changes with
[QGraphicsScene::sceneRect](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsscene.html#sceneRect-prop).
Otherwise, the view's scene rect is unaffected by the scene.

Note that, although the scene supports a virtually unlimited size, the range of the
scroll bars will never exceed the range of an integer (INT\_MIN, INT\_MAX). When the
scene is larger than the scroll bars' values, you can choose to use
[translate](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsview.html#translate)() to
navigate the scene instead.

By default, this property contains a rectangle at the origin with zero width and height.

### void QGraphicsView::setTransform(const [QTransform](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtransform.html) \&*matrix*, bool *combine* \= false)

Sets the view's current transformation matrix to *matrix*.

If *combine* is true, then *matrix* is combined with the current matrix; otherwise,
*matrix* *replaces* the current matrix. *combine* is false by default.

The transformation matrix transforms the scene into view coordinates. Using the default
transformation, provided by the identity matrix, one pixel in the view represents one
unit in the scene (e.g., a 10x10 rectangular item is drawn using 10x10 pixels in the
view). If a 2x2 scaling matrix is applied, the scene will be drawn in 1:2 (e.g., a 10x10
rectangular item is then drawn using 20x20 pixels in the view).

Example:

```
QGraphicsScene scene;
scene.addText("GraphicsView rotated clockwise");

QGraphicsView view(&scene);
view.rotate(90); // the text is rendered with a 90 degree clockwise rotation
view.show();
```

To simplify interation with items using a transformed view,
[QGraphicsView](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsview.html) provides
[mapTo](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#mapTo)... and
[mapFrom](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#mapFrom)... functions that can
translate between scene and view coordinates. For example, you can call
[mapToScene](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsview.html#mapToScene)() to map
a view coordinate to a floating point scene coordinate, or
[mapFromScene](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsview.html#mapFromScene)() to
map from floating point scene coordinates to view coordinates.

**See also**
[transform](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsview.html#transform)(),
[rotate](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsview.html#rotate)(),
[scale](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsview.html#scale)(),
[shear](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsview.html#shear)(), and
[translate](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsview.html#translate)().
signatures: setTransform(self, matrix: PySide2.QtGui.QTransform, combine: bool=...) -> None

### transformationAnchor : [ViewportAnchor](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsview.html#ViewportAnchor-enum)

how the view should position the scene during transformations.

[QGraphicsView](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsview.html) uses this
property to decide how to position the scene in the viewport when the transformation
matrix changes, and the coordinate system of the view is transformed. The default
behavior,
[AnchorViewCenter](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsview.html#ViewportAnchor-enum),
ensures that the scene point at the center of the view remains unchanged during
transformations (e.g., when rotating, the scene will appear to rotate around the center
of the view).

Note that the effect of this property is noticeable when only a part of the scene is
visible (i.e., when there are scroll bars). Otherwise, if the whole scene fits in the
view, [QGraphicsScene](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsscene.html) uses the
view [alignment](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/stylesheet-reference.html#alignment)

Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

QGraphicsWidget is an extended base item that provides extra functionality over
[QGraphicsItem](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsitem.html). It is similar to
[QWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html) in many ways:

- Provides a [palette](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicswidget.html#palette-prop), a [font](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/stylesheet-reference.html#font) and a [style](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicswidget.html#style)().
- Has a defined [geometry](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicslayoutitem.html#geometry)().
- Supports layouts with [setLayout](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicswidget.html#setLayout)() and [layout](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicswidget.html#layout)().
- Supports shortcuts and actions with [grabShortcut](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicswidget.html#grabShortcut)() and [insertAction](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicswidget.html#insertAction)()

Unlike [QGraphicsItem](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsitem.html),
QGraphicsWidget is not an abstract class; you can create instances of a QGraphicsWidget
without having to subclass it. This approach is useful for widgets that only serve the
purpose of organizing child widgets into a layout.

QGraphicsWidget can be used as a base item for your own custom item if you require
advanced input focus handling, e.g., tab focus and activation, or layouts.

Since QGraphicsWidget resembles
[QWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html) and has similar API, it is
easier to port a widget from [QWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html)
to QGraphicsWidget, instead of
[QGraphicsItem](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsitem.html).

**Note:** [QWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html)-based widgets can
be directly embedded into a
[QGraphicsScene](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsscene.html) using
[QGraphicsProxyWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsproxywidget.html).

Noticeable differences between QGraphicsWidget and
[QWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html) are:

| QGraphicsWidget | [QWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html) |
| --- | --- |
| Coordinates and geometry are defined with qreals (doubles or floats, depending on the platform). | [QWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html) uses integer geometry ([QPoint](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpoint.html), [QRect](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qrect.html)). |
| The widget is already visible by default; you do not have to call [show](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsitem.html#show)() to display the widget. | [QWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html) is hidden by default until you call [show](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsitem.html#show)(). |
| A subset of widget attributes are supported. | All widget attributes are supported. |
| A top-level item's style defaults to [QGraphicsScene::style](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsscene.html#style) | A top-level widget's style defaults to [QApplication::style](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qapplication.html#style) |
| Graphics View provides a custom drag and drop framework, different from [QWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html). | Standard drag and drop framework. |
| Widget items do not support modality. | Full modality support. |

QGraphicsWidget supports a subset of Qt's widget attributes,
([Qt::WidgetAttribute](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#WidgetAttribute-enum)),
as shown in the table below. Any attributes not listed in this table are unsupported, or
otherwise unused.

| Widget Attribute | Usage |
| --- | --- |
| [Qt::WA\_SetLayoutDirection](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#WidgetAttribute-enum) | Set by [setLayoutDirection](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicswidget.html#layoutDirection-prop)(), cleared by [unsetLayoutDirection](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicswidget.html#layoutDirection-prop)(). You can test this attribute to check if the widget has been explicitly assigned a [layoutDirection](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicswidget.html#layoutDirection-prop). If the attribute is not set, the [layoutDirection()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicswidget.html#layoutDirection-prop) is inherited. |
| [Qt::WA\_RightToLeft](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#WidgetAttribute-enum) | Toggled by [setLayoutDirection](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicswidget.html#layoutDirection-prop)(). Inherited from the parent/scene. If set, the widget's layout will order horizontally arranged widgets from right to left. |
| [Qt::WA\_SetStyle](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#WidgetAttribute-enum) | Set and cleared by [setStyle](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicswidget.html#setStyle)(). If this attribute is set, the widget has been explicitly assigned a style. If it is unset, the widget will use the scene's or the application's style. |
| [Qt::WA\_Resized](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#WidgetAttribute-enum) | Set by [setGeometry](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicswidget.html#geometry-prop)() and [resize](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicswidget.html#size-prop)(). |
| [Qt::WA\_SetPalette](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#WidgetAttribute-enum) | Set by [setPalette](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicswidget.html#palette-prop)(). |
| [Qt::WA\_SetFont](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#WidgetAttribute-enum) | Set by [setFont](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicswidget.html#font-prop)(). |
| [Qt::WA\_WindowPropagation](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#WidgetAttribute-enum) | Enables propagation to window widgets. |

Although QGraphicsWidget inherits from both
[QObject](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qobject.html) and
[QGraphicsItem](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsitem.html), you should use
the functions provided by
[QGraphicsItem](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsitem.html), *not*
[QObject](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qobject.html), to manage the relationships
between parent and child items. These functions control the stacking order of items as
well as their ownership.

**Note:** The
[QObject::parent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qobject.html#parent)() should
always return `nullptr` for QGraphicsWidgets, but this policy is not strictly defined.

### void QGraphicsWidget::addAction([QAction](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qaction.html) \**action*)

Appends the action *action* to this widget's list of actions.

All QGraphicsWidgets have a list of
[QAction](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qaction.html)s, however they can be
represented graphically in many different ways. The default use of the
[QAction](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qaction.html) list (as returned by
[actions](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicswidget.html#actions)()) is to
create a context [QMenu](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmenu.html).

A

PythonQt.QtGui.QGraphicsWidget.focusNext.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

### `[virtual protected]` bool QGraphicsWidget::focusNextPrevChild(bool *next*)

Finds a new widget to give the keyboard focus to, as appropriate for Tab and Shift\+Tab,
and returns `true` if it can find a new widget; returns `false` otherwise. If *next* is
true, this function searches forward; if *next* is false, it searches backward.

Sometimes, you will want to reimplement this function to provide special focus handling
for your widget and its subwidgets. For example, a web browser might reimplement it to
move its current active link forward or backward, and call the base implementation only
when it reaches the last or first link on the page.

Child widgets call focusNextPrevChild() on their parent widgets, but only the window
that contains the child widgets decides where to redirect focus. By reimplementing this
function for an object, you gain control of focus traversal for all child widgets.

**See also**
[focusPolicy](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicswidget.html#focusPolicy-prop)().

### focusPolicy : [Qt::FocusPolicy](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#FocusPolicy-enum)

This property holds the way the widget accepts keyboard focus

The focus policy is
[Qt::TabFocus](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#FocusPolicy-enum) if the
widget accepts keyboard focus by tabbing,
[Qt::ClickFocus](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#FocusPolicy-enum) if the
widget accepts focus by clicking,
[Qt::StrongFocus](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#FocusPolicy-enum) if it
accepts both, and
[Qt::NoFocus](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#FocusPolicy-enum) (the default)
if it does not accept focus at all.

You must enable keyboard focus for a widget if it processes keyboard events. This is
normally done from the widget's constructor. For instance, the
[QLineEdit](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qlineedit.html) constructor calls
setFocusPolicy([Qt::StrongFocus](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#FocusPolicy-enum)).

If you enable a focus policy (i.e., not
[Qt::NoFocus](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#FocusPolicy-enum)),
[QGraphicsWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/graphicsview.html#qgraphicswidget)
will automatically enable the
[ItemIsFocusable](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsitem.html#GraphicsItemFlag-enum)
flag. Setting [Qt::NoFocus](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#FocusPolicy-enum)
on a widget will clear the
[ItemIsFocusable](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsitem.html#GraphicsItemFlag-enum)
flag. If the widget currently has keyboard focus, the widget will automatically lose
focus.

**Access functions:**

### font : [QFont](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfont.html)

This property holds the widgets' font

This property provides the widget's font.

[QFont](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfont.html) consists of font properties that
have been explicitly defined and properties implicitly inherited from the widget's
parent. Hence, font() can return a different font compared to the one set with
setFont(). This scheme allows you to define single entries in a font without affecting
the font's inherited entries.

When a widget's font changes, it resolves its entries against its parent widget. If the
widget does not have a parent widget, it resolves its entries against the scene. The
widget then sends itself a
[FontChange](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qevent.html#Type-enum) event and
notifies all its descendants so that they can resolve their fonts as well.

By default, this property contains the application's default font.

**Access functions:**

| --- | --- |
| void | **setFont**(const QFont \&*font*) |

Qt 5 reference:

### int QGraphicsWidget::grabShortcut(const [QKeySequence](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qkeysequence.html) \&*sequence*, [Qt::ShortcutContext](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#ShortcutContext-enum) *context* \= Qt::WindowShortcut)

Adds a shortcut to Qt's shortcut system that watches for the given key *sequence* in the
given *context*. If the *context* is
[Qt::ApplicationShortcut](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#ShortcutContext-enum),
the shortcut applies to the application as a whole. Otherwise, it is either local to
this widget,
[Qt::WidgetShortcut](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#ShortcutContext-enum),
or to the window itself,
[Qt::WindowShortcut](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#ShortcutContext-enum).
For widgets that are not part of a window (i.e., top-level widgets and their children),
[Qt::WindowShortcut](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#ShortcutContext-enum)
shortcuts apply to the scene.

If the same key *sequence* has been grabbed by several widgets, when the key *sequence*
occurs a [QEvent::Shortcut](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qevent.html#Type-enum)
event is sent to all the widgets to which it applies in a non-deterministic order, but
with the \`\`ambiguous'' flag set to true.

**Warning:** You should not normally need to use this function; instead create
[QAction](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qaction.html)s with the shortcut key
sequences you require (if you also want equivalent menu options and toolbar buttons), or
create [QShortcut](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qshortcut.html)s if you just need
key sequences. Both [QAction](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qaction.html) and
[QShortcut](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qshortcut.html) handle all the event
filtering for you, and provide signals which are triggered when the user triggers the
key sequence, so are much easier to use than this low-level function.

This function was introduced in Qt 4.5.

**See also**
[releaseShortcut](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicswidget.html#releaseShortcut)(),
[setShortcutEnabled](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicswidget.html#setShortcutEnabled)(),
and
[QWidget::grabShortcut](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#grabShortcut)().
signatures: grabShortcut(self, sequence: PySide2.QtGui.QKeySequence, context: PySide2.QtCore.Qt.ShortcutContext=...) -> int

### `[virtual protected]` void QGraphicsWidget::initStyleOption([QStyleOption](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstyleoption.html) \**option*) const

Populates a style option object for this widget based on its current state, and stores
the output in *option*. The default implementation populates *option* with the following
properties.

| Style Option Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| state \& [QStyle::State\_Enabled](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstyle.html#StateFlag-enum) | Corresponds to [QGraphicsItem::isEnabled](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsitem.html#isEnabled)(). |
| state \& [QStyle::State\_HasFocus](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstyle.html#StateFlag-enum) | Corresponds to [QGraphicsItem::hasFocus](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsitem.html#hasFocus)(). |
| state \& [QStyle::State\_MouseOver](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstyle.html#StateFlag-enum) | Corresponds to [QGraphicsItem::isUnderMouse](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsitem.html#isUnderMouse)(). |
| direction | Corresponds to [QGraphicsWidget::layoutDirection](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicswidget.html#layoutDirection-prop)(). |
| rect | Corresponds to [QGraphicsWidget::rect](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicswidget.html#rect)().toRect(). |
| palette | Corresponds to [QGraphicsWidget::palette](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicswidget.html#palette-prop)(). |
| fontMetrics | Corresponds to [QFontMetrics](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfontmetrics.html)([QGraphicsWidget::font](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicswidget.html#font-prop)()). |

Subclasses of
[QGraphicsWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/graphicsview.html#qgraphicswidget)
should call the base implementation, and then test the type of *option* using
[qstyleoption\_cast](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstyleoption.html#qstyleoption_cast)\<\>()
or test
[QStyleOption::Type](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstyleoption.html#StyleOptionType-enum)
before storing widget-specific options.

For example:

```

### layout : [QGraphicsLayout](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicslayout.html)\*

This property holds the layout of the widget

Any existing layout manager is deleted before the new layout is assigned. If *layout* is
`nullptr`, the widget is left without a layout. Existing subwidgets' geometries will
remain unaffected.

[QGraphicsWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/graphicsview.html#qgraphicswidget)
takes ownership of *layout*.

All widgets that are currently managed by *layout* or all of its sublayouts, are
automatically reparented to this item. The layout is then invalidated, and the child
widget geometries are adjusted according to this item's
[geometry](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicslayoutitem.html#geometry)() and
contentsMargins(). Children who are not explicitly managed by *layout* remain unaffected
by the layout after it has been assigned to this widget.

If no layout is currently managing this widget, layout() will return `nullptr`.

### layoutDirection : [Qt::LayoutDirection](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#LayoutDirection-enum)

This property holds the layout direction for this widget.

This property modifies this widget's and all of its descendants'
[Qt::WA\_RightToLeft](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#WidgetAttribute-enum)
attribute. It also sets this widget's
[Qt::WA\_SetLayoutDirection](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#WidgetAttribute-enum)
attribute.

The widget's layout direction determines the order in which the layout manager
horizontally arranges subwidgets of this widget. The default value depends on the
language and locale of the application, and is typically in the same direction as words
are read and written. With
[Qt::LeftToRight](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#LayoutDirection-enum), the
layout starts placing subwidgets from the left side of this widget towards the right.
[Qt::RightToLeft](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#LayoutDirection-enum) does
the opposite \- the layout will place widgets starting from the right edge moving
towards the left.

Subwidgets inherit their layout direction from the parent. Top-level widget items
inherit their layout direction from QGraphicsScene::layoutDirection. If you change a
widget's layout direction by calling setLayoutDirection(), the widget will send itself a
[LayoutDirectionChange](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qevent.html#Type-enum) event,
and then propagate the new layout direction to all its descendants.

**Access functions:**

| --- | --- |

| void | **unsetLayoutDirection**() |

Qt 5 reference:

### palette : [QPalette](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpalette.html)

This property holds the widget's palette

This property provides the widget's palette. The palette provides colors and brushes for
color groups (e.g.,
[QPalette::Button](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpalette.html#ColorRole-enum)) and
states (e.g.,
[QPalette::Inactive](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpalette.html#ColorGroup-enum)),
loosely defining the general look of the widget and its children.

[QPalette](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpalette.html) consists of color groups
that have been explicitly defined, and groups that are implicitly inherited from the
widget's parent. Because of this, palette() can return a different palette than what has
been set with setPalette(). This scheme allows you to define single entries in a palette
without affecting the palette's inherited entries.

When a widget's palette changes, it resolves its entries against its parent widget, or
if it doesn't have a parent widget, it resolves against the scene. It then sends itself
a [PaletteChange](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qevent.html#Type-enum) event, and
notifies all its descendants so they can resolve their palettes as well.

By default, this property contains the application's default palette.

**Access functions:**

| --- | --- |
| void | **setPalette**(const QPalette \&*palette*) |

**See also**

### void QGraphicsWidget::setLayout([QGraphicsLayout](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicslayout.html) \**layout*)

Sets the layout for this widget to *layout*. Any existing layout manager is deleted
before the new layout is assigned. If *layout* is `nullptr`, the widget is left without
a layout. Existing subwidgets' geometries will remain unaffected.

All widgets that are currently managed by *layout* or all of its sublayouts, are
automatically reparented to this item. The layout is then invalidated, and the child
widget geometries are adjusted according to this item's
[geometry](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicslayoutitem.html#geometry)() and
contentsMargins(). Children who are not explicitly managed by *layout* remain unaffected
by the layout after it has been assigned to this widget.

[QGraphicsWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/graphicsview.html#qgraphicswidget)
takes ownership of *layout*.

**Note:** Setter function for property
[layout](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicswidget.html#layout).

**See also** [layout](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicswidget.html#layout)(),
[QGraphicsLinearLayout::addItem](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicslinearlayout.html#addItem)(),
and
[QGraphicsLayout::invalidate](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicslayout.html#invalidate)().

### void QGraphicsWidget::setStyle([QStyle](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstyle.html) \**style*)

Sets the widget's style to *style*.
[QGraphicsWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/graphicsview.html#qgraphicswidget)
does *not* take ownership of *style*.

If no style is assigned, or *style* is `nullptr`, the widget will use
[QGraphicsScene::style](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsscene.html#style)()

[QApplication::style](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qapplication.html#style)().

This function sets the
[Qt::WA\_SetStyle](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#WidgetAttribute-enum)
attribute if *style* is not `nullptr`; otherwise it clears the attribute.

**See also** [style](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicswidget.html#style)().

PythonQt.QtGui.QGraphicsWidget.setTabOrd.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

### `[static]` void QGraphicsWidget::setTabOrder([QGraphicsWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicswidget.html#QGraphicsWidget) \**first*, [QGraphicsWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicswidget.html#QGraphicsWidget) \**second*)

Moves the *second* widget around the ring of focus widgets so that keyboard focus moves
from the *first* widget to the *second* widget when the Tab key is pressed.

Note that since the tab order of the *second* widget is changed, you should order a
chain like this:

```
setTabOrder(a, b); // a to b
setTabOrder(b, c); // a to b to c
setTabOrder(c, d); // a to b to c to d
```

*not* like this:

```
// WRONG
setTabOrder(c, d); // c to d
setTabOrder(a, b); // a to b AND c to d
setTabOrder(b, c); // a to b to c, but not c to d
```

If *first* is `nullptr`, this indicates that *second* should be the first widget to
receive input focus should the scene gain Tab focus (i.e., the user hits Tab so that
focus passes into the scene). If *second* is `nullptr`, this indicates that *first*
should be the first widget to gain focus if the scene gained BackTab focus.

By default, tab order is defined implicitly using widget creation order.

**See also**
[focusPolicy](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicswidget.html#focusPolicy-prop)
and [Keyboard Focus in Widgets](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/focus.html).

### size : [QSizeF](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsizef.html)

This property holds the size of the widget

Calling resize() resizes the widget to a *size* bounded by
[minimumSize](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicslayoutitem.html#minimumSize)()
and
[maximumSize](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicslayoutitem.html#maximumSize)().
This property only affects the widget's width and height (e.g., its right and bottom
edges); the widget's position and top-left corner remains unaffected.

Resizing a widget triggers the widget to immediately receive a
[GraphicsSceneResize](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qevent.html#Type-enum) event
with the widget's old and new size. If the widget has a layout assigned when this event
arrives, the layout will be activated and it will automatically update any child
widgets's geometry.

This property does not affect any layout of the parent widget. If the widget itself is
managed by a parent layout; e.g., it has a parent widget with a layout assigned, that
layout will not activate.

By default, this property contains a size with zero width and height.

**Access functions:**

| void | **[resize](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicswidget.html#resize-1)**(qreal *w*, qreal *h*) |

**Notifier signal:**

| void | **[geometryChanged](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicswidget.html#geometryChanged)**() |
| --- | --- |

### windowFlags : [Qt::WindowFlags](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#WindowType-enum)

This property holds the widget's window flags

Window flags are a combination of a window type (e.g.,
[Qt::Dialog](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#WindowType-enum)) and several
flags giving hints on the behavior of the window. The behavior is platform-dependent.

By default, this property contains no window flags.

Windows are panels. If you set the
[Qt::Window](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#WindowType-enum) flag, the
[ItemIsPanel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsitem.html#GraphicsItemFlag-enum)
flag will be set automatically. If you clear the
[Qt::Window](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#WindowType-enum) flag, the
[ItemIsPanel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsitem.html#GraphicsItemFlag-enum)
flag is also cleared. Note that the
[ItemIsPanel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsitem.html#GraphicsItemFlag-enum)
flag can be set independently of
[Qt::Window](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#WindowType-enum).
