PythonQt.QtGui.QMenu.exec.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

### [QAction](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qaction.html) \*QMenu::exec()

Executes this menu synchronously.

This is equivalent to `exec(pos())`.

This returns the triggered [QAction](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qaction.html) in
either the popup menu or one of its submenus, or `nullptr` if no item was triggered
(normally because the user pressed Esc).

In most situations you'll want to specify the position yourself, for example, the
current mouse position:

```
exec(QCursor::pos());
```

or aligned to a widget:

```
exec(somewidget.mapToGlobal(QPoint(0,0)));
```

or in reaction to a [QMouseEvent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmouseevent.html)
\*e:

```
exec(e->globalPos());
```

### [QAction](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qaction.html) \*QMenu::exec(const [QPoint](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpoint.html) \&*p*, [QAction](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qaction.html) \**action* \= nullptr)

This is an overloaded function.

Executes this menu synchronously.

Pops up the menu so that the action *action* will be at the specified *global* position
*p*. To translate a widget's local coordinates into global coordinates, use
[QWidget::mapToGlobal](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#mapToGlobal)().

This returns the triggered [QAction](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qaction.html) in
either the popup menu or one of its submenus, or `nullptr` if no item was triggered
(normally because the user pressed Esc).

Note that all signals are emitted as usual. If you connect a
[QAction](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qaction.html) to a slot and call the menu's
exec(), you get the result both via the signal-slot connection and in the return value
of exec().

Common usage is to position the menu at the current mouse position:

```
exec(QCursor::pos());
```

or aligned to a widget:

```
exec(somewidget.mapToGlobal(QPoint(0, 0)));
```

or in reaction to a [QMouseEvent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmouseevent.html)
\*e:

```
exec(e->globalPos());
```

When positioning a menu with exec() or
[popup](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmenu.html#popup)(), bear in mind that you
cannot rely on the menu's current
[size](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#size-prop)(). For performance
reasons, the menu adapts its size only when necessary. So in many cases, the size before
and after the show is different. Instead, use
[sizeHint](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmenu.html#sizeHint)() which calculates
the proper size depending on the menu's current contents.

**See also** [popup](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmenu.html#popup)() and
[QWidget::mapToGlobal](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#mapToGlobal)().

### `[static]` [QAction](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qaction.html) \*QMenu::exec([QList](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qlist.html)\<[QAction](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qaction.html) \*\> *actions*, const [QPoint](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpoint.html) \&*pos*, [QAction](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qaction.html) \**at* \= nullptr, [QWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#QWidget) \**parent* \= nullptr)

This is an overloaded function.

Executes a menu synchronously.

The menu's actions are specified by the list of *actions*. The menu will pop up so that
the specified action, *at*, appears at global position *pos*. If *at* is not specified
then the menu appears at position *pos*. *parent* is the menu's parent widget;
specifying the parent will provide context when *pos* alone is not enough to decide
where the menu should go (e.g., with multiple desktops or when the parent is embedded in
[QGraphicsView](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsview.html)).

The function returns the triggered
[QAction](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qaction.html) in either the popup menu or
one of its submenus, or `nullptr` if no item was triggered (normally because the user
pressed Esc).

This is equivalent to:

```
QMenu menu;
QAction *at = actions[0]; // Assumes actions is not empty
for (QAction *a : qAsConst(actions))
    menu.addAction(a);
menu.exec(pos, at);
```

**See also** [popup](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmenu.html#popup)() and
[QWidget::mapToGlobal](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#mapToGlobal)().

This convenience function creates a new title action, i.e. an action with
[QAction::isSeparator](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qaction.html#isSeparator)()
returning true but also having *text* hint. The function inserts the newly created
action into this menu's list of actions before action *before* and returns it.

The rendering of the hint is style and platform dependent. Widget styles can use the
text information in the rendering for sections, or can choose to ignore it and render
sections like simple separators.

[QAction](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qaction.html).

Normally, you connect each menu action's
[triggered()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qaction.html#triggered) signal to its

PythonQt.QtGui.QMenuBar.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

A menu bar consists of a list of pull-down menu items. You add menu items with
[addMenu](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmenubar.html#addMenu)(). For example,
assuming that `menubar` is a pointer to a QMenuBar and `fileMenu` is a pointer to a
[QMenu](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmenu.html), the following statement inserts
the menu into the menu bar:

```
menubar->addMenu(fileMenu);
```

The ampersand in the menu item's text sets Alt\+F as a shortcut for this menu. (You can
use "\&\&" to get a real ampersand in the menu bar.)

There is no need to lay out a menu bar. It automatically sets its own geometry to the
top of the parent widget and changes it appropriately whenever the parent is resized.

### Usage

In most main window style applications you would use the
[menuBar()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmainwindow.html#menuBar) function
provided in [QMainWindow](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmainwindow.html), adding
[QMenu](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmenu.html)s to the menu bar and adding
[QAction](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qaction.html)s to the pop-up menus.

Example (from the
[Menus](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtwidgets-mainwindows-menus-example.html)
example):

```
    fileMenu = menuBar()->addMenu(tr("&File"));
    fileMenu->addAction(newAct);
```

Menu items may be removed with
[removeAction](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#removeAction)().

Widgets can be added to menus by using instances of the
[QWidgetAction](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidgetaction.html) class to hold
them. These actions can then be inserted into menus in the usual way; see the
[QMenu](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmenu.html) documentation for more details.

### Platform Dependent Look and Feel

Different platforms have different requirements for the appearance of menu bars and
their behavior when the user interacts with them. For example, Windows systems are often
configured so that the underlined character mnemonics that indicate keyboard shortcuts
for items in the menu bar are only shown when the **Alt** key is pressed.

### QMenuBar as a Global Menu Bar

On macOS and on certain Linux desktop environments such as Ubuntu Unity, QMenuBar is a
wrapper for using the system-wide menu bar. If you have multiple menu bars in one dialog
the outermost menu bar (normally inside a widget with widget flag
[Qt::Window](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#WindowType-enum)) will be used
for the system-wide menu bar.

Qt for macOS also provides a menu bar merging feature to make QMenuBar conform more
closely to accepted macOS menu bar layout. The merging functionality is based on string
matching the title of a [QMenu](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmenu.html) entry.
These strings are translated (using
[QObject::tr](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qobject.html#tr)()) in the "QMenuBar"
context. If an entry is moved its slots will still fire as if it was in the original
place. The table below outlines the strings looked for and where the entry is placed if
matched:

| String matches | Placement | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| about.\* | Application Menu \| About \<application name\> | The application name is fetched from the `Info.plist` file (see note below). If this entry is not found no About item will appear in the Application Menu. |
| config, options, setup, settings or preferences | Application Menu \| Preferences | If this entry is not found the Settings item will be disabled |
| quit or exit | Application Menu \| Quit \<application name\> | If this entry is not found a default Quit item will be created to call [QCoreApplication::quit](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcoreapplication.html#quit)() |

You can override this behavior by using the
[QAction::menuRole](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qaction.html#menuRole-prop)()
property.

If you want all windows in a Mac application to share one menu bar, you must create a
menu bar that does not have a parent. Create a parent-less menu bar this way:

```
QMenuBar *menuBar = new QMenuBar(nullptr);
```

**Note:** Do *not* call
[QMainWindow::menuBar](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmainwindow.html#menuBar)() to
create the shared menu bar, because that menu bar will have the
[QMainWindow](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmainwindow.html) as its parent. That
menu bar would only be displayed for the parent
[QMainWindow](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmainwindow.html).

**Note:** The text used for the application name in the macOS menu bar is obtained from
the value set in the `Info.plist` file in the application's bundle. See [Qt for macOS \-
Deployment](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/macos-deployment.html) for more
information.

**Note:** On Linux, if the com.canonical.AppMenu.Registrar service is available on the
D-Bus session bus, then Qt will communicate with it to install the application's menus
into the global menu bar, as described.

### Examples

The [Menus](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtwidgets-mainwindows-menus-example.html)
example shows how to use QMenuBar and
[QMenu](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmenu.html). The other [main window
application examples](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/examples-mainwindow.html) also
provide menus using these classes.

### nativeMenuBar : bool

This property holds whether or not a menubar will be used as a native menubar on
platforms that support it

This property specifies whether or not the menubar should be used as a native menubar on
platforms that support it. The currently supported platforms are macOS, and Linux
desktops which use the com.canonical.dbusmenu D-Bus interface (such as Ubuntu Unity). If
this property is `true`, the menubar is used in the native menubar and is not in the
window of its parent; if `false` the menubar remains in the window. On other platforms,
setting this attribute has no effect, and reading this attribute will always return
`false`.

The default is to follow whether the
[Qt::AA\_DontUseNativeMenuBar](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#ApplicationAttribute-enum)
attribute is set for the application. Explicitly setting this property overrides the
presence (or absence) of the attribute.

This property was introduced in Qt 4.6.

This signal is emitted when an action in a menu belonging to this menubar is triggered
as a result of a mouse click; *action* is the action that caused the signal to be

ownership of the [QMenu](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmenu.html) in order this

Normally, you connect each menu action to a single slot using
[QAction::triggered](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qaction.html#triggered)(), but
sometimes you will want to connect several items to a single slot (most often if the

PythonQt.QtGui.QMessageBox.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

A message box displays a primary
[text](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#text-prop) to alert the user
to a situation, an [informative
text](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#informativeText-prop) to
further explain the alert or to ask the user a question, and an optional [detailed
text](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#detailedText-prop) to provide
even more data if the user requests it. A message box can also display an
[icon](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#icon-prop) and [standard
buttons](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#standardButtons-prop) for
accepting a user response.

Two APIs for using QMessageBox are provided, the property-based API, and the static
functions. Calling one of the static functions is the simpler approach, but it is less
flexible than using the property-based API, and the result is less informative. Using
the property-based API is recommended.

### The Property-based API

To use the property-based API, construct an instance of QMessageBox, set the desired
properties, and call [exec](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#exec)()
to show the message. The simplest configuration is to set only the [message
text](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#text-prop) property.

```
QMessageBox msgBox;
msgBox.setText("The document has been modified.");
msgBox.exec();
```

The user must click the **OK** button to dismiss the message box. The rest of the GUI is
blocked until the message box is dismissed.

![](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/images/msgbox1.png)

A better approach than just alerting the user to an event is to also ask the user what
to do about it. Store the question in the [informative
text](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#informativeText-prop)
property, and set the [standard
buttons](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#standardButtons-prop)
property to the set of buttons you want as the set of user responses. The buttons are
specified by combining values from
[StandardButtons](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#StandardButton-enum)
using the bitwise OR operator. The display order for the buttons is platform-dependent.
For example, on Windows, **Save** is displayed to the left of **Cancel**, whereas on Mac
OS, the order is reversed.

Mark one of your standard buttons to be your [default
button](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#defaultButton).

```
QMessageBox msgBox;
msgBox.setText("The document has been modified.");
msgBox.setInformativeText("Do you want to save your changes?");
msgBox.setStandardButtons(QMessageBox::Save | QMessageBox::Discard | QMessageBox::Cancel);
msgBox.setDefaultButton(QMessageBox::Save);
int ret = msgBox.exec();
```

This is the approach recommended in the [macOS
Guidelines](http://developer.apple.com/library/mac/documentation/UserExperience/Conceptual/AppleHIGuidelines/Windows/Windows.html#//apple_ref/doc/uid/20000961-BABCAJID).
Similar guidelines apply for the other platforms, but note the different ways the
[informative
text](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#informativeText-prop) is
handled for different platforms.

![](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/images/msgbox2.png)

The [exec](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#exec)() slot returns the
[StandardButtons](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#StandardButton-enum)
value of the button that was clicked.

```
switch (ret) {
  case QMessageBox::Save:
      // Save was clicked
      break;
  case QMessageBox::Discard:
      // Don't Save was clicked
      break;
  case QMessageBox::Cancel:
      // Cancel was clicked
      break;
  default:
      // should never be reached
      break;
}
```

To give the user more information to help him answer the question, set the [detailed
text](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#detailedText-prop) property.
If the [detailed
text](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#detailedText-prop) property is
set, the **Show Details...** button will be shown.

![](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/images/msgbox3.png)

Clicking the **Show Details...** button displays the detailed text.

![](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/images/msgbox4.png)

#### Rich Text and the Text Format Property

The [detailed
text](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#detailedText-prop) property is
always interpreted as plain text. The [main
text](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#text-prop) and [informative
text](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#informativeText-prop)
properties can be either plain text or rich text. These strings are interpreted
according to the setting of the [text
format](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#textFormat-prop) property.
The default setting is
[auto-text](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#TextFormat-enum).

Note that for some plain text strings containing XML meta-characters, the auto-text
[rich text detection
test](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt-sub-qtgui.html#mightBeRichText) may fail
causing your plain text string to be interpreted incorrectly as rich text. In these rare
cases, use
[Qt::convertFromPlainText](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt-sub-qtgui.html#convertFromPlainText)()
to convert your plain text string to a visually equivalent rich text string, or set the
[text format](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#textFormat-prop)
property explicitly with
[setTextFormat](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#textFormat-prop)().

#### Severity Levels and the Icon and Pixmap Properties

QMessageBox supports four predefined message severity levels, or message types, which
really only differ in the predefined icon they each show. Specify one of the four
predefined message types by setting the
[icon](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#icon-prop) property to one of
the [predefined icons](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#Icon-enum).
The following rules are guidelines:

|  | [Question](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#Icon-enum) | For asking a question during normal operations. |
| --- | --- | --- |
|  | [Information](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#Icon-enum) | For reporting information about normal operations. |
|  | [Warning](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#Icon-enum) | For reporting non-critical errors. |
|  | [Critical](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#Icon-enum) | For reporting critical errors. |

[Predefined icons](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#Icon-enum) are
not defined by QMessageBox, but provided by the style. The default value is [No
Icon](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#Icon-enum). The message boxes
are otherwise the same for all cases. When using a standard icon, use the one
recommended in the table, or use the one recommended by the style guidelines for your
platform. If none of the standard icons is right for your message box, you can use a
custom icon by setting the [icon
pixmap](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#iconPixmap-prop) property
instead of setting the
[icon](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#icon-prop) property.

In summary, to set an icon, use *either*
[setIcon](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#icon-prop)() for one of
the standard icons, *or*
[setIconPixmap](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#iconPixmap-prop)()
for a custom icon.

### The Static Functions API

Building message boxes with the static functions API, although convenient, is less
flexible than using the property-based API, because the static function signatures lack
parameters for setting the [informative
text](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#informativeText-prop) and
[detailed text](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#detailedText-prop)
properties. One work-around for this has been to use the `title` parameter as the
message box main text and the `text` parameter as the message box informative text.
Because this has the obvious drawback of making a less readable message box, platform
guidelines do not recommend it. The *Microsoft Windows User Interface Guidelines*
recommend using the [application
name](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcoreapplication.html#applicationName-prop) as
the [window's
title](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#setWindowTitle), which means
that if you have an informative text in addition to your main text, you must concatenate
it to the `text` parameter.

Note that the static function signatures have changed with respect to their button
parameters, which are now used to set the [standard
buttons](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#standardButtons-prop) and
the [default button](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#defaultButton).

Static functions are available for creating
[information](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#information)(),
[question](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#question)(),
[warning](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#warning)(), and
[critical](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#critical)() message
boxes.

```
int ret = QMessageBox::warning(this, tr("My Application"),
                               tr("The document has been modified.\n"
                                  "Do you want to save your changes?"),
                               QMessageBox::Save | QMessageBox::Discard
                               | QMessageBox::Cancel,
                               QMessageBox::Save);
```

The [Standard
Dialogs](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtwidgets-dialogs-standarddialogs-example.html)
example shows how to use QMessageBox and the other built-in Qt dialogs.

### Advanced Usage

If the [standard
buttons](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#StandardButton-enum) are
not flexible enough for your message box, you can use the
[addButton](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#addButton)() overload
that takes a text and a
[ButtonRole](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#ButtonRole-enum) to add
custom buttons. The
[ButtonRole](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#ButtonRole-enum) is
used by QMessageBox to determine the ordering of the buttons on screen (which varies
according to the platform). You can test the value of
[clickedButton](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#clickedButton)()
after calling [exec](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#exec)(). For
example,

```
QMessageBox msgBox;
QPushButton *connectButton = msgBox.addButton(tr("Connect"), QMessageBox::ActionRole);
QPushButton *abortButton = msgBox.addButton(QMessageBox::Abort);

msgBox.exec();

if (msgBox.clickedButton() == connectButton) {
    // connect
} else if (msgBox.clickedButton() == abortButton) {
    // abort
}
```

### Default and Escape Keys

The default button (i.e., the button activated when **Enter** is pressed) can be
specified using
[setDefaultButton](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#setDefaultButton)().
If a default button is not specified, QMessageBox tries to find one based on the [button
roles](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#ButtonRole-enum) of the
buttons used in the message box.

The escape button (the button activated when **Esc** is pressed) can be specified using
[setEscapeButton](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#setEscapeButton)().
If an escape button is not specified, QMessageBox tries to find one using these rules:

1. If there is only one button, it is the button activated when **Esc** is pressed.
2. If there is a [Cancel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#StandardButton-enum) button, it is the button activated when **Esc** is pressed.
3. If there is exactly one button having either [the Reject role](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#ButtonRole-enum) or the [the No role](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#ButtonRole-enum), it is the button activated when **Esc** is pressed.

When an escape button can't be determined using these rules, pressing **Esc** has no
effect.

### `[static]` void QMessageBox::about([QWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#QWidget) \**parent*, const [QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html) \&*title*, const [QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html) \&*text*)

Displays a simple about box with title *title* and text *text*. The about box's parent
is *parent*.

about() looks for a suitable icon in four locations:

1. It prefers [parent-\>icon()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#windowIcon-prop) if that exists.
2. If not, it tries the top-level widget containing *parent*.
3. If that fails, it tries the [active window.](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qapplication.html#activeWindow)
4. As a last resort it uses the Information icon.

The about box has a single button labelled "OK". On macOS, the about box is popped up as
a modeless window; on other platforms, it is currently application modal.

**See also**
[QWidget::windowIcon](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#windowIcon-prop)()
and
[QApplication::activeWindow](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qapplication.html#activeWindow)().

Opens a critical message box with the given *title* and *text* in front of the specified
*parent* widget.

The standard *buttons* are added to the message box. *defaultButton* specifies the
button used when **Enter** is pressed. *defaultButton* must refer to a button that was
given in *buttons*. If *defaultButton* is
[QMessageBox::NoButton](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#StandardButton-enum),
[QMessageBox](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html) chooses a suitable
default automatically.

Returns the identity of the standard button that was clicked. If **Esc** was pressed
instead, the [escape
button](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#default-and-escape-keys) is
returned.

The message box is an [application
modal](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#WindowModality-enum) dialog box.

**Warning:** Do not delete *parent* during the execution of the dialog. If you want to
do this, you should create the dialog yourself using one of the
[QMessageBox](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html) constructors.

Qt 5 reference:

### [QAbstractButton](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractbutton.html) \*QMessageBox::escapeButton() const

Returns the button that is activated when escape is pressed.

By default, [QMessageBox](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html) attempts
to automatically detect an escape button as follows:

1. If there is only one button, it is made the escape button.
2. If there is a [Cancel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#StandardButton-enum) button, it is made the escape button.
3. On macOS only, if there is exactly one button with the role [QMessageBox::RejectRole](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#ButtonRole-enum), it is made the escape button.

When an escape button could not be automatically detected, pressing **Esc** has no
effect.

This function was introduced in Qt 4.2.

**See also**
[setEscapeButton](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#setEscapeButton)()
and [addButton](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#addButton)().

### `[override virtual slot]` int QMessageBox::exec()

Reimplements: [QDialog::exec](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdialog.html#exec)().

Shows the message box as a [modal
dialog](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdialog.html#modal-dialogs), blocking until
the user closes it.

When using a [QMessageBox](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html) with
standard buttons, this function returns a
[StandardButton](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#StandardButton-enum)
value indicating the standard button that was clicked. When using
[QMessageBox](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html) with custom buttons,
this function returns an opaque value; use
[clickedButton](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#clickedButton)() to
determine which button was clicked.

**Note:** The [result](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdialog.html#result)()
function returns also
[StandardButton](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#StandardButton-enum)
value instead of
[QDialog::DialogCode](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdialog.html#DialogCode-enum).

Users cannot interact with any other window in the same application until they close the
dialog, either by clicking a button or by using a mechanism provided by the window
system.

**See also** [show](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#show)() and
[result](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdialog.html#result)().

Opens an information message box with the given *title* and *text* in front of the
specified *parent* widget.

The standard *buttons* are added to the message box. *defaultButton* specifies the
button used when **Enter** is pressed. *defaultButton* must refer to a button that was
given in *buttons*. If *defaultButton* is
[QMessageBox::NoButton](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#StandardButton-enum),
[QMessageBox](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html) chooses a suitable
default automatically.

Returns the identity of the standard button that was clicked. If **Esc** was pressed
instead, the [escape
button](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#default-and-escape-keys) is
returned.

The message box is an [application
modal](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#WindowModality-enum) dialog box.

**Warning:** Do not delete *parent* during the execution of the dialog. If you want to
do this, you should create the dialog yourself using one of the
[QMessageBox](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html) constructors.

This function was introduced in Qt 4.2.

**See also** [question](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#question)(),
[warning](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#warning)(), and
[critical](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#critical)().

### `[static]` [QMessageBox::StandardButton](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#StandardButton-enum) QMessageBox::warning([QWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#QWidget) \**parent*, const [QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html) \&*title*, const [QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html) \&*text*, [QMessageBox::StandardButtons](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#StandardButton-enum) *buttons* \= Ok, [QMessageBox::StandardButton](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#StandardButton-enum) *defaultButton* \= NoButton)

Opens a warning message box with the given *title* and *text* in front of the specified
*parent* widget.

The standard *buttons* are added to the message box. *defaultButton* specifies the
button used when **Enter** is pressed. *defaultButton* must refer to a button that was
given in *buttons*. If *defaultButton* is
[QMessageBox::NoButton](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#StandardButton-enum),
[QMessageBox](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html) chooses a suitable
default automatically.

Returns the identity of the standard button that was clicked. If **Esc** was pressed
instead, the [escape
button](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#default-and-escape-keys) is
returned.

The message box is an [application
modal](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#WindowModality-enum) dialog box.

**Warning:** Do not delete *parent* during the execution of the dialog. If you want to
do this, you should create the dialog yourself using one of the
[QMessageBox](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html) constructors.

This function was introduced in Qt 4.2.

**See also** [question](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#question)(),
[information](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#information)(), and
[critical](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmessagebox.html#critical)().

Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

Mouse events occur when a mouse button is pressed or released inside a widget, or when
the mouse cursor is moved.

Mouse move events will occur only when a mouse button is pressed down, unless mouse
tracking has been enabled with
[QWidget::setMouseTracking](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#mouseTracking-prop)().

Qt automatically grabs the mouse when a mouse button is pressed inside a widget; the
widget will continue to receive mouse events until the last mouse button is released.

A mouse event contains a special accept flag that indicates whether the receiver wants
the event. You should call
[ignore](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qevent.html#ignore)() if the mouse event is
not handled by your widget. A mouse event is propagated up the parent widget chain until
a widget accepts it with
[accept](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qevent.html#accept)(), or an event filter
consumes it.

**Note:** If a mouse event is propagated to a
[widget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html) for which
[Qt::WA\_NoMousePropagation](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#WidgetAttribute-enum)
has been set, that mouse event will not be propagated further up the parent widget
chain.

The state of the keyboard modifier keys can be found by calling the
[modifiers()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qinputevent.html#modifiers) function,
inherited from [QInputEvent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qinputevent.html).

The functions [pos](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmouseevent.html#pos)(),
[x](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmouseevent.html#x)(), and
[y](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmouseevent.html#y)() give the cursor position
relative to the widget that receives the mouse event. If you move the widget as a result
of the mouse event, use the global position returned by
[globalPos](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmouseevent.html#globalPos)() to avoid a
shaking motion.

The
[QWidget::setEnabled](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#enabled-prop)()
function can be used to enable or disable mouse and keyboard events for a widget.

Reimplement the [QWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html) event
handlers,
[QWidget::mousePressEvent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#mousePressEvent)(),
[QWidget::mouseReleaseEvent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#mouseReleaseEvent)(),
[QWidget::mouseDoubleClickEvent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#mouseDoubleClickEvent)(),
and
[QWidget::mouseMoveEvent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#mouseMoveEvent)()
to receive mouse events in your own widgets.

### [Qt::MouseButtons](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#MouseButton-enum) QMouseEvent::buttons() const

Returns the button state when the event was generated. The button state is a combination
of [Qt::LeftButton](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#MouseButton-enum),
[Qt::RightButton](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#MouseButton-enum),
[Qt::MiddleButton](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#MouseButton-enum) using
the OR operator. For mouse move events, this is all buttons that are pressed down. For
mouse press and double click events this includes the button that caused the event. For
mouse release events this excludes the button that caused the event.

**See also** [button](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmouseevent.html#button)() and
[Qt::MouseButton](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#MouseButton-enum).

### [QPoint](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpoint.html) QMouseEvent::globalPos() const

[QWidget::mapToGlobal](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#mapToGlobal)([pos](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmouseevent.html#pos)()).

### [Qt::MouseEventSource](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#MouseEventSource-enum) QMouseEvent::source() const

Returns information about the mouse event source.

The mouse event source can be used to distinguish between genuine and artificial mouse
events. The latter are events that are synthesized from touch events by the operating
system or Qt itself.

**Note:** Many platforms provide no such information. On such platforms
[Qt::MouseEventNotSynthesized](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#MouseEventSource-enum)
is returned always.

This function was introduced in Qt 5.3.

**See also**
[Qt::MouseEventSource](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#MouseEventSource-enum)
and
[QGraphicsSceneMouseEvent::source](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qgraphicsscenemouseevent.html#source)().

PythonQt.QtGui.QMovie.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

This class is used to show simple animations without sound. If you want to display video
and media content, use the [Qt
Multimedia](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtmultimedia-index.html) multimedia
framework instead.

First, create a QMovie object by passing either the name of a file or a pointer to a
[QIODevice](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qiodevice.html) containing an animated
image format to QMovie's constructor. You can call
[isValid](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmovie.html#isValid)() to check if the
image data is valid, before starting the movie. To start the movie, call
[start](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmovie.html#start)(). QMovie will enter
[Running](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmovie.html#MovieState-enum) state, and
emit [started](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmovie.html#started)() and
[stateChanged](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmovie.html#stateChanged)(). To get
the current state of the movie, call
[state](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmovie.html#state)().

To display the movie in your application, you can pass your QMovie object to
[QLabel::setMovie](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qlabel.html#setMovie)(). Example:

```
QLabel label;
QMovie *movie = new QMovie("animations/fire.gif");

label.setMovie(movie);
movie->start();
```

Whenever a new frame is available in the movie, QMovie will emit
[updated](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmovie.html#updated)(). If the size of the
frame changes, [resized](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmovie.html#resized)() is
emitted. You can call
[currentImage](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmovie.html#currentImage)() or
[currentPixmap](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmovie.html#currentPixmap)() to get a
copy of the current frame. When the movie is done, QMovie emits
[finished](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmovie.html#finished)(). If any error
occurs during playback (i.e, the image file is corrupt), QMovie will emit
[error](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmovie.html#error)().

You can control the speed of the movie playback by calling
[setSpeed](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmovie.html#speed-prop)(), which takes the
percentage of the original speed as an argument. Pause the movie by calling
[setPaused](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmovie.html#setPaused)(true). QMovie will
then enter [Paused](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmovie.html#MovieState-enum)
state and emit
[stateChanged](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmovie.html#stateChanged)(). If you
call [setPaused](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmovie.html#setPaused)(false),
QMovie will reenter
[Running](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmovie.html#MovieState-enum) state and
start the movie again. To stop the movie, call
[stop](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmovie.html#stop)().

Certain animation formats allow you to set the background color. You can call
[setBackgroundColor](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmovie.html#setBackgroundColor)()
to set the color, or
[backgroundColor](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmovie.html#backgroundColor)() to
retrieve the current background color.

[currentFrameNumber](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmovie.html#currentFrameNumber)()
returns the sequence number of the current frame. The first frame in the animation has
the sequence number 0\.
[frameCount](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmovie.html#frameCount)() returns the
total number of frames in the animation, if the image format supports this. You can call
[loopCount](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmovie.html#loopCount)() to get the
number of times the movie should loop before finishing.
[nextFrameDelay](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmovie.html#nextFrameDelay)()
returns the number of milliseconds the current frame should be displayed.

QMovie can be instructed to cache frames of an animation by calling
[setCacheMode](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmovie.html#cacheMode-prop)().

Call
[supportedFormats](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmovie.html#supportedFormats)()
for a list of formats that QMovie supports.

### cacheMode : [CacheMode](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmovie.html#CacheMode-enum)

This property holds the movie's cache mode

Caching frames can be useful when the underlying animation format handler that
[QMovie](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmovie.html) relies on to decode the
animation data does not support jumping to particular frames in the animation, or even
"rewinding" the animation to the beginning (for looping). Furthermore, if the image data
comes from a sequential device, it is not possible for the underlying animation handler
to seek back to frames whose data has already been read (making looping altogether
impossible).

To aid in such situations, a [QMovie](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmovie.html)
object can be instructed to cache the frames, at the added memory cost of keeping the
frames in memory for the lifetime of the object.

By default, this property is set to
[CacheNone](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmovie.html#CacheMode-enum).

**Access functions:**

| QMovie::CacheMode | **cacheMode**() const |
| --- | --- |
| void | **setCacheMode**(QMovie::CacheMode *mode*) |

**See also**
[QMovie::CacheMode](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmovie.html#CacheMode-enum).

### int QMovie::loopCount() const

Returns the number of times the movie will loop before it finishes. If the movie will
only play once (no looping), loopCount returns 0\. If the movie loops forever, loopCount
returns -1.

Note that, if the image data comes from a sequential device (e.g. a socket),
[QMovie](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmovie.html) can only loop the movie if the
[cacheMode](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmovie.html#cacheMode-prop) is set to
[QMovie::CacheAll](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmovie.html#CacheMode-enum).

### `[slot]` void QMovie::start()

Starts the movie. [QMovie](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmovie.html) will enter
[Running](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmovie.html#MovieState-enum) state, and
start emitting [updated](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmovie.html#updated)() and
[resized](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmovie.html#resized)() as the movie
progresses.

If [QMovie](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmovie.html) is in the
[Paused](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmovie.html#MovieState-enum) state, this
function is equivalent to calling
[setPaused](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmovie.html#setPaused)(false). If
[QMovie](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmovie.html) is already in the
[Running](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmovie.html#MovieState-enum) state, this
function does nothing.

**See also** [stop](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmovie.html#stop)() and
[setPaused](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmovie.html#setPaused)().

Qt 5 reference:

### `[slot]` void QMovie::stop()

Stops the movie. [QMovie](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmovie.html) enters
[NotRunning](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmovie.html#MovieState-enum) state, and
stops emitting [updated](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmovie.html#updated)() and
[resized](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmovie.html#resized)(). If
[start](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmovie.html#start)() is called again, the
movie will restart from the beginning.

If [QMovie](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmovie.html) is already in the
[NotRunning](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmovie.html#MovieState-enum) state, this
function does nothing.

**See also** [start](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmovie.html#start)() and
[setPaused](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmovie.html#setPaused)().

## Detailed Description

Native gesture events are generated by the operating system, typically by interpreting
touch events. Gesture events are high-level events such as zoom or rotate.

| Event Type | Description | Touch sequence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Qt::ZoomNativeGesture](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#NativeGestureType-enum) | Magnification delta in percent. | macOS: Two-finger pinch. |
| [Qt::SmartZoomNativeGesture](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#NativeGestureType-enum) | Boolean magnification state. | macOS: Two-finger douple tap (trackpad) / One-finger douple tap (magic mouse). |
| [Qt::RotateNativeGesture](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#NativeGestureType-enum) | Rotation delta in degrees. | macOS: Two-finger rotate. |

In addition, BeginNativeGesture and EndNativeGesture are sent before and after gesture
event streams:

BeginNativeGesture ZoomNativeGesture ZoomNativeGesture ZoomNativeGesture
EndNativeGesture

PythonQt.QtGui.QOffscreenSurface.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

QOffscreenSurface is intended to be used with
[QOpenGLContext](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglcontext.html) to allow
rendering with OpenGL in an arbitrary thread without the need to create a
[QWindow](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwindow.html).

Even though the surface is typically renderable, the surface's pixels are not
accessible. QOffscreenSurface should only be used to create OpenGL resources such as
textures or framebuffer objects.

An application will typically use QOffscreenSurface to perform some time-consuming tasks
in a separate thread in order to avoid stalling the main rendering thread. Resources
created in the QOffscreenSurface's context can be shared with the main OpenGL context.
Some common use cases are asynchronous texture uploads or rendering into a
[QOpenGLFramebufferObject](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglframebufferobject.html).

How the offscreen surface is implemented depends on the underlying platform, but it will
typically use a pixel buffer (pbuffer). If the platform doesn't implement or support
offscreen surfaces, QOffscreenSurface will use an invisible
[QWindow](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwindow.html) internally.

**Note:** Due to the fact that QOffscreenSurface is backed by a
[QWindow](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwindow.html) on some platforms,
cross-platform applications must ensure that
[create](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qoffscreensurface.html#create)() is only
called on the main (GUI) thread. The QOffscreenSurface is then safe to be used with
[makeCurrent()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglcontext.html#makeCurrent) on
other threads, but the initialization and destruction must always happen on the main
(GUI) thread.

**Note:** In order to create an offscreen surface that is guaranteed to be compatible
with a given context and window, make sure to set the format to the context's or the
window's actual format, that is, the
[QSurfaceFormat](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsurfaceformat.html) returned from
[QOpenGLContext::format](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglcontext.html#format)()
or [QWindow::format](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwindow.html#format)() *after
the context or window has been created*. Passing the format returned from
[QWindow::requestedFormat](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwindow.html#requestedFormat)()
to [setFormat](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qoffscreensurface.html#setFormat)()
may result in an incompatible offscreen surface since the underlying windowing system
interface may offer a different set of configurations for window and pbuffer surfaces.

**Note:** Some platforms may utilize a surfaceless context extension (for example
EGL\_KHR\_surfaceless\_context) when available. In this case there will be no underlying
native surface. For the use cases of QOffscreenSurface (rendering to FBOs, texture
upload) this is not a problem.

PythonQt.QtGui.QOffscreenSurface.create.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

### void QOffscreenSurface::create()

Allocates the platform resources associated with the offscreen surface.

It is at this point that the surface format set using
[setFormat](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qoffscreensurface.html#setFormat)() gets
resolved into an actual native surface.

## Detailed Description

Buffer objects are created in the OpenGL server so that the client application can avoid
uploading vertices, indices, texture image data, etc every time they are needed.

QOpenGLBuffer objects can be copied around as a reference to the underlying OpenGL
buffer object:

```
    QOpenGLBuffer buffer1(QOpenGLBuffer::IndexBuffer);
    buffer1.create();

    QOpenGLBuffer buffer2 = buffer1;
```

QOpenGLBuffer performs a shallow copy when objects are copied in this manner, but does
not implement copy-on-write semantics. The original object will be affected whenever the
copy is modified.

PythonQt.QtGui.QOpenGLContext.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

QOpenGLContext represents the OpenGL state of an underlying OpenGL context. To set up a
context, set its screen and format such that they match those of the surface or surfaces
with which the context is meant to be used, if necessary make it share resources with
other contexts with
[setShareContext](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglcontext.html#setShareContext)(),
and finally call
[create](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglcontext.html#create)(). Use the
return value or
[isValid](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglcontext.html#isValid)() to check if
the context was successfully initialized.

A context can be made current against a given surface by calling
[makeCurrent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglcontext.html#makeCurrent)().
When OpenGL rendering is done, call
[swapBuffers](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglcontext.html#swapBuffers)() to
swap the front and back buffers of the surface, so that the newly rendered content
becomes visible. To be able to support certain platforms, QOpenGLContext requires that
you call
[makeCurrent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglcontext.html#makeCurrent)()
again before starting rendering a new frame, after calling
[swapBuffers](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglcontext.html#swapBuffers)().

If the context is temporarily not needed, such as when the application is not rendering,
it can be useful to delete it in order to free resources. You can connect to the
[aboutToBeDestroyed](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglcontext.html#aboutToBeDestroyed)()
signal to clean up any resources that have been allocated with different ownership from
the QOpenGLContext itself.

Once a QOpenGLContext has been made current, you can render to it in a platform
independent way by using Qt's OpenGL enablers such as
[QOpenGLFunctions](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglfunctions.html),
[QOpenGLBuffer](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglbuffer.html),
[QOpenGLShaderProgram](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglshaderprogram.html),
and
[QOpenGLFramebufferObject](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglframebufferobject.html).
It is also possible to use the platform's OpenGL API directly, without using the Qt
enablers, although potentially at the cost of portability. The latter is necessary when
wanting to use OpenGL 1.x or OpenGL ES 1.x.

For more information about the OpenGL API, refer to the official [OpenGL
documentation](http://www.opengl.org).

For an example of how to use QOpenGLContext see the [OpenGL
Window](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtgui-openglwindow-example.html) example.

### Thread Affinity

QOpenGLContext can be moved to a different thread with
[moveToThread](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qobject.html#moveToThread)(). Do not
call [makeCurrent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglcontext.html#makeCurrent)()
from a different thread than the one to which the QOpenGLContext object belongs. A
context can only be current in one thread and against one surface at a time, and a
thread only has one context current at a time.

### Context Resource Sharing

Resources such as textures and vertex buffer objects can be shared between contexts. Use
[setShareContext](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglcontext.html#setShareContext)()
before calling [create](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglcontext.html#create)()
to specify that the contexts should share these resources. QOpenGLContext internally
keeps track of a
[QOpenGLContextGroup](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglcontextgroup.html)
object which can be accessed with
[shareGroup](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglcontext.html#shareGroup)(), and
which can be used to find all the contexts in a given share group. A share group
consists of all contexts that have been successfully initialized and are sharing with an
existing context in the share group. A non-sharing context has a share group consisting
of a single context.

### Default Framebuffer

On certain platforms, a framebuffer other than 0 might be the default frame buffer
depending on the current surface. Instead of calling glBindFramebuffer(0), it is
recommended that you use
glBindFramebuffer(ctx-\>[defaultFramebufferObject](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglcontext.html#defaultFramebufferObject)()),
to ensure that your application is portable between different platforms. However, if you
use
[QOpenGLFunctions::glBindFramebuffer](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglfunctions.html#glBindFramebuffer)(),
this is done automatically for you.

### bool QOpenGLContext::create()

Attempts to create the OpenGL context with the current configuration.

The current configuration includes the format, the share context, and the screen.

If the OpenGL implementation on your system does not support the requested version of
OpenGL context, then
[QOpenGLContext](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglcontext.html) will try to
create the closest matching version. The actual created context properties can be
queried using the
[QSurfaceFormat](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsurfaceformat.html) returned by the
[format](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglcontext.html#format)() function. For
example, if you request a context that supports OpenGL 4.3 Core profile but the driver
and/or hardware only supports version 3.2 Core profile contexts then you will get a 3.2
Core profile context.

Returns `true` if the native context was successfully created and is ready to be used
with
[makeCurrent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglcontext.html#makeCurrent)(),
[swapBuffers](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglcontext.html#swapBuffers)(),
etc.

**Note:** If the context already exists, this function destroys the existing context
first, and then creates a new one.

**See also**
[makeCurrent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglcontext.html#makeCurrent)() and
[format](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglcontext.html#format)().

### GLuint QOpenGLContext::defaultFramebufferObject() const

Call this to get the default framebuffer object for the current surface.

On some platforms (for instance, iOS) the default framebuffer object depends on the
surface being rendered to, and might be different from 0\. Thus, instead of calling
glBindFramebuffer(0), you should call
glBindFramebuffer(ctx-\>defaultFramebufferObject()) if you want your application to work
across different Qt platforms.

If you use the glBindFramebuffer() in
[QOpenGLFunctions](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglfunctions.html) you do not
have to worry about this, as it automatically binds the current context's
defaultFramebufferObject() when 0 is passed.

**Note:** Widgets that render via framebuffer objects, like
[QOpenGLWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglwidget.html) and
[QQuickWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qquickwidget.html), will override the
value returned from this function when painting is active, because at that time the
correct "default" framebuffer is the widget's associated backing framebuffer, not the
platform-specific one belonging to the top-level window's surface. This ensures the
expected behavior for this function and other classes relying on it (for example,
[QOpenGLFramebufferObject::bindDefault](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglframebufferobject.html#bindDefault)()
or
[QOpenGLFramebufferObject::release](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglframebufferobject.html#release)()).

**See also**
[QOpenGLFramebufferObject](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglframebufferobject.html).

Qt 5 reference:

### [QSurfaceFormat](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsurfaceformat.html) QOpenGLContext::format() const

Returns the format of the underlying platform context, if
[create](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglcontext.html#create)() has been
called.

Otherwise, returns the requested format.

The requested and the actual format may differ. Requesting a given OpenGL version does
not mean the resulting context will target exactly the requested version. It is only
guaranteed that the version/profile/options combination for the created context is
compatible with the request, as long as the driver is able to provide such a context.

For example, requesting an OpenGL version 3.x core profile context may result in an
OpenGL 4.x core profile context. Similarly, a request for OpenGL 2.1 may result in an
OpenGL 3.0 context with deprecated functions enabled. Finally, depending on the driver,
unsupported versions may result in either a context creation failure or in a context for
the highest supported version.

Similar differences are possible in the buffer sizes, for example, the resulting context
may have a larger depth buffer than requested. This is perfectly normal.

**See also**
[setFormat](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglcontext.html#setFormat)().

### bool QOpenGLContext::isValid() const

Returns if this context is valid, i.e. has been successfully created.

On some platforms the return value of `false` for a context that was successfully
created previously indicates that the OpenGL context was lost.

The typical way to handle context loss scenarios in applications is to check via this
function whenever
[makeCurrent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglcontext.html#makeCurrent)()
fails and returns `false`. If this function then returns `false`, recreate the
underlying native OpenGL context by calling
[create](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglcontext.html#create)(), call
[makeCurrent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglcontext.html#makeCurrent)()
again and then reinitialize all OpenGL resources.

On some platforms context loss situations is not something that can avoided. On others
however, they may need to be opted-in to. This can be done by enabling
[ResetNotification](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsurfaceformat.html#FormatOption-enum)
in the [QSurfaceFormat](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsurfaceformat.html). This
will lead to setting `RESET_NOTIFICATION_STRATEGY_EXT` to `LOSE_CONTEXT_ON_RESET_EXT` in
the underlying native OpenGL context.
[QOpenGLContext](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglcontext.html) will then
monitor the status via `glGetGraphicsResetStatusEXT()` in every
[makeCurrent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglcontext.html#makeCurrent)().

**See also** [create](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglcontext.html#create)().

PythonQt.QtGui.QOpenGLContext.makeCurren.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

### bool QOpenGLContext::makeCurrent([QSurface](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsurface.html) \**surface*)

Makes the context current in the current thread, against the given *surface*. Returns
`true` if successful; otherwise returns `false`. The latter may happen if the surface is
not exposed, or the graphics hardware is not available due to e.g. the application being
suspended.

If *surface* is `nullptr` this is equivalent to calling
[doneCurrent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglcontext.html#doneCurrent)().

Avoid calling this function from a different thread than the one the
[QOpenGLContext](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglcontext.html) instance lives
in. If you wish to use
[QOpenGLContext](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglcontext.html) from a
different thread you should first make sure it's not current in the current thread, by
calling
[doneCurrent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglcontext.html#doneCurrent)() if
necessary. Then call
[moveToThread](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qobject.html#moveToThread)(otherThread)
before using it in the other thread.

By default Qt employs a check that enforces the above condition on the thread affinity.
It is still possible to disable this check by setting the
`Qt::AA_DontCheckOpenGLContextThreadAffinity` application attribute. Be sure to
understand the consequences of using QObjects from outside the thread they live in, as
explained in the [QObject thread
affinity](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qobject.html#thread-affinity)
documentation.

**See also**
[functions](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglcontext.html#functions)(),
[doneCurrent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglcontext.html#doneCurrent)(), and
[Qt::AA\_DontCheckOpenGLContextThreadAffinity](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#ApplicationAttribute-enum).

### void QOpenGLContext::setNativeHandle(const [QVariant](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qvariant.html) \&*handle*)

Set the native handles for this context. When
[create](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglcontext.html#create)() is called and
a native handle is set, configuration settings, like
[format](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglcontext.html#format)(), are ignored
since this [QOpenGLContext](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglcontext.html) will
wrap an already created native context instead of creating a new one from scratch.

On some platforms the native context handle is not sufficient and other related handles
(for example, for a window or display) have to be provided in addition. Therefore
*handle* is variant containing a platform-specific value type. These classes can be
found in the
[QtPlatformHeaders](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtplatformheaders-module.html)
module.

When [create](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglcontext.html#create)() is called
with native handles set,
[QOpenGLContext](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglcontext.html) does not take
ownership of the handles, so destroying the
[QOpenGLContext](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglcontext.html) does not
destroy the native context.

**Note:** Some frameworks track the current context and surfaces internally. Making the
adopted [QOpenGLContext](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglcontext.html) current
via Qt will have no effect on such other frameworks' internal state. Therefore a
subsequent
[makeCurrent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglcontext.html#makeCurrent) done
via the other framework may have no effect. It is therefore advisable to make explicit
calls to make no context and surface current to reset the other frameworks' internal
state after performing OpenGL operations via Qt.

**Note:** Using foreign contexts with Qt windows and Qt contexts with windows and
surfaces created by other frameworks may give unexpected results, depending on the
platform, due to potential mismatches in context and window pixel formats. To make sure
this does not happen, avoid making contexts and surfaces from different frameworks
current together. Instead, prefer approaches based on context sharing where OpenGL
resources like textures are accessible both from Qt's and the foreign framework's
contexts.

This function was introduced in Qt 5.4.

**See also**
[nativeHandle](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglcontext.html#nativeHandle)().

## Detailed Description

The QOpenGLFramebufferObject class encapsulates an OpenGL framebuffer object, defined by
the `GL_EXT_framebuffer_object` extension. It provides a rendering surface that can be
painted on with a [QPainter](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpainter.html) with the
help of
[QOpenGLPaintDevice](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglpaintdevice.html), or
rendered to using native OpenGL calls. This surface can be bound and used as a regular
texture in your own OpenGL drawing code. By default, the QOpenGLFramebufferObject class
generates a 2D OpenGL texture (using the `GL_TEXTURE_2D` target), which is used as the
internal rendering target.

**It is important to have a current OpenGL context when creating a
QOpenGLFramebufferObject, otherwise initialization will fail.**

Create the QOpenGLFrameBufferObject instance with the
[CombinedDepthStencil](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglframebufferobject.html#Attachment-enum)
attachment if you want [QPainter](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpainter.html) to
render correctly. Note that you need to create a QOpenGLFramebufferObject with more than
one sample per pixel for primitives to be antialiased when drawing using a
[QPainter](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpainter.html). To create a multisample
framebuffer object you should use one of the constructors that take a
[QOpenGLFramebufferObjectFormat](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglframebufferobjectformat.html)
parameter, and set the
[QOpenGLFramebufferObjectFormat::samples](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglframebufferobjectformat.html#samples)()
property to a non-zero value.

For multisample framebuffer objects a color render buffer is created, otherwise a
texture with the specified texture target is created. The color render buffer or texture
will have the specified internal format, and will be bound to the `GL_COLOR_ATTACHMENT0`
attachment in the framebuffer object.

Multiple render targets are also supported, in case the OpenGL implementation supports
this. Here there will be multiple textures (or, in case of multisampling, renderbuffers)
present and each of them will get attached to `GL_COLOR_ATTACHMENT0`, `1`, `2`, ...

If you want to use a framebuffer object with multisampling enabled as a texture, you
first need to copy from it to a regular framebuffer object using
QOpenGLContext::blitFramebuffer().

It is possible to draw into a QOpenGLFramebufferObject using
[QPainter](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpainter.html) and
[QOpenGLPaintDevice](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglpaintdevice.html) in a
separate thread.

### void QOpenGLFramebufferObject::addColorAttachment(const [QSize](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsize.html) \&*size*, GLenum *internalFormat* \= 0\)

Creates and attaches an additional texture or renderbuffer of *size* width and height.

There is always an attachment at GL\_COLOR\_ATTACHMENT0. Call this function to set up
additional attachments at GL\_COLOR\_ATTACHMENT1, GL\_COLOR\_ATTACHMENT2, ...

When *internalFormat* is not `0`, it specifies the internal format of the texture or
renderbuffer. Otherwise a default of GL\_RGBA or GL\_RGBA8 is used.

**Note:** This is only functional when multiple render targets are supported by the
OpenGL implementation. When that is not the case, the function will not add any
additional color attachments. Call
[QOpenGLFunctions::hasOpenGLFeature](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglfunctions.html#hasOpenGLFeature)()
with
[QOpenGLFunctions::MultipleRenderTargets](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglfunctions.html#OpenGLFeature-enum)
at runtime to check if MRT is supported.

**Note:** The internal format of the color attachments may differ but there may be
limitations on the supported combinations, depending on the drivers.

**Note:** The size of the color attachments may differ but rendering is limited to the
area that fits all the attachments, according to the OpenGL specification. Some drivers
may not be fully conformant in this respect, however.

This function was introduced in Qt 5.6.

### void QOpenGLFramebufferObject::addColorAttachment(int *width*, int *height*, GLenum *internalFormat* \= 0\)

This is an overloaded function.

Creates and attaches an additional texture or renderbuffer of size *width* and *height*.

When *internalFormat* is not `0`, it specifies the internal format of the texture or
renderbuffer. Otherwise a default of GL\_RGBA or GL\_RGBA8 is used.

This function was introduced in Qt 5.6.

### `[static]` void QOpenGLFramebufferObject::blitFramebuffer([QOpenGLFramebufferObject](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglframebufferobject.html#QOpenGLFramebufferObject) \**target*, const [QRect](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qrect.html) \&*targetRect*, [QOpenGLFramebufferObject](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglframebufferobject.html#QOpenGLFramebufferObject) \**source*, const [QRect](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qrect.html) \&*sourceRect*, GLbitfield *buffers*, GLenum *filter*, int *readColorAttachmentIndex*, int *drawColorAttachmentIndex*, [QOpenGLFramebufferObject::FramebufferRestorePolicy](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglframebufferobject.html#FramebufferRestorePolicy-enum) *restorePolicy*)

Blits from the *sourceRect* rectangle in the *source* framebuffer object to the
*targetRect* rectangle in the *target* framebuffer object.

If *source* or *target* is 0, the default framebuffer will be used instead of a
framebuffer object as source or target respectively.

This function will have no effect unless
[hasOpenGLFramebufferBlit](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglframebufferobject.html#hasOpenGLFramebufferBlit)()
returns true.

The *buffers* parameter should be a mask consisting of any combination of
`GL_COLOR_BUFFER_BIT`, `GL_DEPTH_BUFFER_BIT`, and `GL_STENCIL_BUFFER_BIT`. Any buffer
type that is not present both in the source and target buffers is ignored.

The *sourceRect* and *targetRect* rectangles may have different sizes; in this case
*buffers* should not contain `GL_DEPTH_BUFFER_BIT` or `GL_STENCIL_BUFFER_BIT`. The
*filter* parameter should be set to `GL_LINEAR` or `GL_NEAREST`, and specifies whether
linear or nearest interpolation should be used when scaling is performed.

If *source* equals *target* a copy is performed within the same buffer. Results are
undefined if the source and target rectangles overlap and have different sizes. The
sizes must also be the same if any of the framebuffer objects are multisample
framebuffers.

**Note:** The scissor test will restrict the blit area if enabled.

When multiple render targets are in use, *readColorAttachmentIndex* and
*drawColorAttachmentIndex* specify the index of the color attachments in the source and
destination framebuffers.

The *restorePolicy* determines if the framebuffer that was bound prior to calling this
function should be restored, or if the default framebuffer should be bound before
returning, of if the caller is responsible for tracking and setting the bound
framebuffer. Restoring the previous framebuffer can be relatively expensive due to the
call to `glGetIntegerv` which on some OpenGL drivers may imply a pipeline stall.

This function was introduced in Qt 5.7.

**See also**
[hasOpenGLFramebufferBlit](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglframebufferobject.html#hasOpenGLFramebufferBlit)().

### bool QOpenGLFramebufferObject::isValid() const

Returns `true` if the framebuffer object is valid.

The framebuffer can become invalid if the initialization process fails, the user
attaches an invalid buffer to the framebuffer object, or a non-power of two width/height
is specified as the texture size if the texture target is `GL_TEXTURE_2D`. The non-power
of two limitation does not apply if the OpenGL version is 2.0 or higher, or if the
GL\_ARB\_texture\_non\_power\_of\_two extension is present.

[QOpenGLContext](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglcontext.html) that the
framebuffer was created within is destroyed and there are no other shared contexts that
can take over ownership of the framebuffer.

### [QImage](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qimage.html) QOpenGLFramebufferObject::toImage(bool *flipped*) const

Returns the contents of this framebuffer object as a
[QImage](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qimage.html).

If *flipped* is true the image is flipped from OpenGL coordinates to raster coordinates.
If used together with
[QOpenGLPaintDevice](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglpaintdevice.html),
*flipped* should be the opposite of the value of
[QOpenGLPaintDevice::paintFlipped](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglpaintdevice.html#paintFlipped)().

The returned image has a format of premultiplied ARGB32 or RGB32. The latter is used
only when internalTextureFormat() is set to `GL_RGB`. Since Qt 5.2 the function will
fall back to premultiplied RGBA8888 or RGBx8888 when reading to (A)RGB32 is not
supported, and this includes OpenGL ES. Since Qt 5.4 an A2BGR30 image is returned if the
internal format is RGB10\_A2, and since Qt 5.12 a RGBA64 image is return if the internal
format is RGBA16.

If the rendering in the framebuffer was not done with premultiplied alpha in mind,
create a wrapper [QImage](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qimage.html) with a
non-premultiplied format. This is necessary before performing operations like
[QImage::save](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qimage.html#save)() because otherwise
the image data would get unpremultiplied, even though it was not premultiplied in the
first place. To create such a wrapper without performing a copy of the pixel data, do
the following:

```
QImage fboImage(fbo.toImage());
QImage image(fboImage.constBits(), fboImage.width(), fboImage.height(), QImage::Format_ARGB32);
```

For multisampled framebuffer objects the samples are resolved using the
`GL_EXT_framebuffer_blit` extension. If the extension is not available, the contents of
the returned image is undefined.

For singlesampled framebuffers the contents is retrieved via `glReadPixels`. This is a
potentially expensive and inefficient operation. Therefore it is recommended that this
function is used as seldom as possible.

**See also**
[QOpenGLPaintDevice::paintFlipped](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglpaintdevice.html#paintFlipped)().

## Detailed Description

A framebuffer object has several characteristics:

- [Number of samples per pixels.](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglframebufferobjectformat.html#setSamples)
- [Depth and/or stencil attachments.](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglframebufferobjectformat.html#setAttachment)
- [Texture target.](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglframebufferobjectformat.html#setTextureTarget)
- [Internal texture format.](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglframebufferobjectformat.html#setInternalTextureFormat)

Note that the desired attachments or number of samples per pixels might not be supported
by the hardware driver. Call
[QOpenGLFramebufferObject::format](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglframebufferobject.html#format)()
after creating a
[QOpenGLFramebufferObject](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglframebufferobject.html)
to find the exact format that was used to create the frame buffer object.

## Detailed Description

The QOpenGLPaintDevice uses the **current** QOpenGL context to render
[QPainter](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpainter.html) draw commands. The context
is captured upon construction. It requires support for OpenGL (ES) 2.0 or higher.

### Performance

The QOpenGLPaintDevice is almost always hardware accelerated and has the potential of
being much faster than software rasterization. However, it is more sensitive to state
changes, and therefore requires the drawing commands to be carefully ordered to achieve
optimal performance.

### Antialiasing and Quality

Antialiasing in the OpenGL paint engine is done using multisampling. Most hardware
require significantly more memory to do multisampling and the resulting quality is not
on par with the quality of the software paint engine. The OpenGL paint engine's strength
lies in its performance, not its visual rendering quality.

### State Changes

When painting to a QOpenGLPaintDevice using
[QPainter](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpainter.html), the state of the current
OpenGL context will be altered by the paint engine to reflect its needs. Applications
should not rely upon the OpenGL state being reset to its original conditions,
particularly the current shader program, OpenGL viewport, texture units, and drawing
modes.

### Mixing QPainter and OpenGL

When intermixing [QPainter](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpainter.html) and
OpenGL, it is important to notify
[QPainter](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpainter.html) that the OpenGL state may
have been cluttered so it can restore its internal state. This is achieved by calling
[QPainter::beginNativePainting](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpainter.html#beginNativePainting)()
before starting the OpenGL rendering and calling
[QPainter::endNativePainting](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpainter.html#endNativePainting)()
after finishing.
