PythonQt.QtGui.QPalette.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

A palette consists of three color groups: *Active*, *Disabled*, and *Inactive*. All
widgets in Qt contain a palette and use their palette to draw themselves. This makes the
user interface easily configurable and easier to keep consistent.

If you create a new widget we strongly recommend that you use the colors in the palette
rather than hard-coding specific colors.

The color groups:

- The Active group is used for the window that has keyboard focus.
- The Inactive group is used for other windows.
- The Disabled group is used for widgets (not windows) that are disabled for some reason.

Both active and inactive windows can contain disabled widgets. (Disabled widgets are
often called *inaccessible* or *grayed out*.)

In most styles, Active and Inactive look the same.

Colors and brushes can be set for particular roles in any of a palette's color groups
with [setColor](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpalette.html#setColor)() and
[setBrush](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpalette.html#setBrush)(). A color group
contains a group of colors used by widgets for drawing themselves. We recommend that
widgets use color group roles from the palette such as "foreground" and "base" rather
than literal colors like "red" or "turquoise". The color roles are enumerated and
defined in the
[ColorRole](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpalette.html#ColorRole-enum)
documentation.

We strongly recommend that you use the default palette of the current style (returned by
[QGuiApplication::palette](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qguiapplication.html#palette)())
and modify that as necessary. This is done by Qt's widgets when they are drawn.

To modify a color group you call the functions
[setColor](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpalette.html#setColor)() and
[setBrush](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpalette.html#setBrush)(), depending on
whether you want a pure color or a pixmap pattern.

There are also corresponding
[color](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpalette.html#color)() and
[brush](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpalette.html#brush)() getters, and a
commonly used convenience function to get the
[ColorRole](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpalette.html#ColorRole-enum) for the
current [ColorGroup](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpalette.html#ColorGroup-enum):
[window](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpalette.html#window)(),
[windowText](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpalette.html#windowText)(),
[base](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpalette.html#base)(), etc.

You can copy a palette using the copy constructor and test to see if two palettes are
*identical* using
[isCopyOf](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpalette.html#isCopyOf)().

QPalette is optimized by the use of [implicit
sharing](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/implicit-sharing.html), so it is very
efficient to pass QPalette objects as arguments.

**Warning:** Some styles do not use the palette for all drawing, for instance, if they
make use of native theme engines. This is the case for both the Windows Vista and the
macOS styles.

### lastOffset : [QPointF](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpointf.html)

This property holds the last offset recorded for this gesture

The last offset contains the change in position of the user's input as reported in the
[offset](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpangesture.html#offset-prop) property when
a previous gesture event was delivered for this gesture.

gesture object contains information about the first movement in the gesture) then this

### bool QPdfWriter::setPageLayout(const [QPageLayout](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpagelayout.html) \&*newPageLayout*)

Sets the PDF page layout to *newPageLayout*.

You should call this before calling
[QPainter::begin](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpainter.html#begin)(), or
immediately before calling
[newPage](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpdfwriter.html#newPage)() to apply the new
page layout to a new page. You should not call any painting methods between a call to
setPageLayout() and
[newPage](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpdfwriter.html#newPage)() as the wrong
paint metrics may be used.

Returns true if the page layout was successfully set to *newPageLayout*.

This function was introduced in Qt 5.3.

**See also**
[pageLayout](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpdfwriter.html#pageLayout)().

Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

A pen has a [style](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpen.html#style)(),
[width](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpen.html#width)(),
[brush](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpen.html#brush)(),
[capStyle](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpen.html#capStyle)() and
[joinStyle](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpen.html#joinStyle)().

The pen style defines the line type. The brush is used to fill strokes generated with
the pen. Use the [QBrush](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qbrush.html) class to
specify fill styles. The cap style determines the line end caps that can be drawn using
[QPainter](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpainter.html), while the join style
describes how joins between two lines are drawn. The pen width can be specified in both
integer ([width](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpen.html#width)()) and floating
point ([widthF](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpen.html#widthF)()) precision. A
line width of zero indicates a cosmetic pen. This means that the pen width is always
drawn one pixel wide, independent of the
[transformation](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpainter.html#coordinate-transformations)
set on the painter.

The various settings can easily be modified using the corresponding
[setStyle](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpen.html#setStyle)(),
[setWidth](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpen.html#setWidth)(),
[setBrush](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpen.html#setBrush)(),
[setCapStyle](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpen.html#setCapStyle)() and
[setJoinStyle](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpen.html#setJoinStyle)() functions
(note that the painter's pen must be reset when altering the pen's properties).

For example:

```
QPainter painter(this);
QPen pen(Qt::green, 3, Qt::DashDotLine, Qt::RoundCap, Qt::RoundJoin);
painter.setPen(pen);
```

which is equivalent to

```
QPainter painter(this);
QPen pen;  // creates a default pen

pen.setStyle(Qt::DashDotLine);
pen.setWidth(3);
pen.setBrush(Qt::green);
pen.setCapStyle(Qt::RoundCap);
pen.setJoinStyle(Qt::RoundJoin);

painter.setPen(pen);
```

The default pen is a solid black brush with 1 width, square cap style
([Qt::SquareCap](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#PenCapStyle-enum)), and
bevel join style
([Qt::BevelJoin](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#PenJoinStyle-enum)).

In addition QPen provides the
[color](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpen.html#color)() and
[setColor](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpen.html#setColor)() convenience
functions to extract and set the color of the pen's brush, respectively. Pens may also
be compared and streamed.

For more information about painting in general, see the [Paint
System](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/paintsystem.html) documentation.

### Pen Style

Qt provides several built-in styles represented by the
[Qt::PenStyle](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#PenStyle-enum) enum:

|  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Qt::SolidLine](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#PenStyle-enum) | [Qt::DashLine](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#PenStyle-enum) | [Qt::DotLine](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#PenStyle-enum) |
|  |  |  |
| [Qt::DashDotLine](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#PenStyle-enum) | [Qt::DashDotDotLine](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#PenStyle-enum) | [Qt::CustomDashLine](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#PenStyle-enum) |

Simply use the [setStyle](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpen.html#setStyle)()
function to convert the pen style to either of the built-in styles, except the
[Qt::CustomDashLine](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#PenStyle-enum) style
which we will come back to shortly. Setting the style to
[Qt::NoPen](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#PenStyle-enum) tells the painter
to not draw lines or outlines. The default pen style is
[Qt::SolidLine](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#PenStyle-enum).

Since Qt 4.1 it is also possible to specify a custom dash pattern using the
[setDashPattern](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpen.html#setDashPattern)() function
which implicitly converts the style of the pen to
[Qt::CustomDashLine](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#PenStyle-enum). The
pattern argument, a [QVector](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qvector.html), must be
specified as an even number of
[qreal](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtglobal.html#qreal-typedef) entries where
the entries 1, 3, 5... are the dashes and 2, 4, 6... are the spaces. For example, the
custom pattern shown above is created using the following code:

```
QPen pen;
QVector<qreal> dashes;
qreal space = 4;

dashes << 1 << space << 3 << space << 9 << space
           << 27 << space << 9 << space;

pen.setDashPattern(dashes);
```

Note that the dash pattern is specified in units of the pens width, e.g. a dash of
length 5 in width 10 is 50 pixels long.

The currently set dash pattern can be retrieved using the
[dashPattern](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpen.html#dashPattern)() function. Use
the [isSolid](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpen.html#isSolid)() function to
determine whether the pen has a solid fill, or not.

### Cap Style

The cap style defines how the end points of lines are drawn using
[QPainter](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpainter.html). The cap style only apply
to wide lines, i.e. when the width is 1 or greater. The
[Qt::PenCapStyle](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#PenCapStyle-enum) enum
provides the following styles:

|  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Qt::SquareCap](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#PenCapStyle-enum) | [Qt::FlatCap](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#PenCapStyle-enum) | [Qt::RoundCap](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#PenCapStyle-enum) |

The [Qt::SquareCap](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#PenCapStyle-enum) style
is a square line end that covers the end point and extends beyond it by half the line
width. The [Qt::FlatCap](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#PenCapStyle-enum)
style is a square line end that does not cover the end point of the line. And the
[Qt::RoundCap](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#PenCapStyle-enum) style is a
rounded line end covering the end point.

The default is
[Qt::SquareCap](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#PenCapStyle-enum).

Whether or not end points are drawn when the pen width is 0 or 1 depends on the cap
style. Using
[Qt::SquareCap](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#PenCapStyle-enum) or
[Qt::RoundCap](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#PenCapStyle-enum) they are
drawn, using [Qt::FlatCap](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#PenCapStyle-enum)
they are not drawn.

### Join Style

The join style defines how joins between two connected lines can be drawn using
[QPainter](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpainter.html). The join style only apply
to wide lines, i.e. when the width is 1 or greater. The
[Qt::PenJoinStyle](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#PenJoinStyle-enum) enum
provides the following styles:

|  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Qt::BevelJoin](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#PenJoinStyle-enum) | [Qt::MiterJoin](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#PenJoinStyle-enum) | [Qt::RoundJoin](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#PenJoinStyle-enum) |

The [Qt::BevelJoin](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#PenJoinStyle-enum) style
fills the triangular notch between the two lines. The
[Qt::MiterJoin](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#PenJoinStyle-enum) style
extends the lines to meet at an angle. And the
[Qt::RoundJoin](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#PenJoinStyle-enum) style
fills a circular arc between the two lines.

The default is
[Qt::BevelJoin](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#PenJoinStyle-enum).

![](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/images/qpen-miterlimit.png)

When the [Qt::MiterJoin](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#PenJoinStyle-enum)
style is applied, it is possible to use the
[setMiterLimit](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpen.html#setMiterLimit)() function
to specify how far the miter join can extend from the join point. The
[miterLimit](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpen.html#miterLimit)() is used to
reduce artifacts between line joins where the lines are close to parallel.

The [miterLimit](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpen.html#miterLimit)() must be
specified in units of the pens width, e.g. a miter limit of 5 in width 10 is 50 pixels
long. The default miter limit is 2, i.e. twice the pen width in pixels.

|  | **[The Path Stroking Example](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtwidgets-painting-pathstroke-example.html)** The Path Stroking example shows Qt's built-in dash patterns and shows how custom patterns can be used to extend the range of available patterns. |
| --- | --- |

### bool QPen::isCosmetic() const

Returns `true` if the pen is cosmetic; otherwise returns `false`.

Cosmetic pens are used to draw strokes that have a constant width regardless of any
transformations applied to the
[QPainter](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpainter.html) they are used with. Drawing
a shape with a cosmetic pen ensures that its outline will have the same thickness at
different scale factors.

A zero width pen is cosmetic by default.

**See also** [setCosmetic](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpen.html#setCosmetic)()
and [widthF](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpen.html#widthF)().

### void QPen::setDashOffset([qreal](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtglobal.html#qreal-typedef) *offset*)

Sets the dash offset (the starting point on the dash pattern) for this pen to the
*offset* specified. The offset is measured in terms of the units used to specify the
dash pattern.

|  | For example, a pattern where each stroke is four units long, followed by a gap of two units, will begin with the stroke when drawn as a line. However, if the dash offset is set to 4.0, any line drawn will begin with the gap. Values of the offset up to 4.0 will cause part of the stroke to be drawn first, and values of the offset between 4.0 and 6.0 will cause the line to begin with part of the gap. |
| --- | --- |

**Note:** This implicitly converts the style of the pen to
[Qt::CustomDashLine](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#PenStyle-enum).

**See also** [dashOffset](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpen.html#dashOffset)().

### void QPen::setDashPattern(const [QVector](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qvector.html)\<[qreal](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtglobal.html#qreal-typedef)\> \&*pattern*)

Sets the dash pattern for this pen to the given *pattern*. This implicitly converts the
style of the pen to
[Qt::CustomDashLine](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#PenStyle-enum).

The pattern must be specified as an even number of positive entries where the entries 1,
3, 5... are the dashes and 2, 4, 6... are the spaces. For example:

|  | ``` QPen pen; QVector<qreal> dashes; qreal space = 4; dashes << 1 << space << 3 << space << 9 << space            << 27 << space << 9 << space; pen.setDashPattern(dashes); ``` |
| --- | --- |

The dash pattern is specified in units of the pens width; e.g. a dash of length 5 in
width 10 is 50 pixels long. Note that a pen with zero width is equivalent to a cosmetic
pen with a width of 1 pixel.

Each dash is also subject to cap styles so a dash of 1 with square cap set will extend
0.5 pixels out in each direction resulting in a total width of 2\.

Note that the default cap style is
[Qt::SquareCap](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#PenCapStyle-enum), meaning
that a square line end covers the end point and extends beyond it by half the line
width.

**See also** [setStyle](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpen.html#setStyle)(),
[dashPattern](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpen.html#dashPattern)(),
[setCapStyle](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpen.html#setCapStyle)(), and
[setCosmetic](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpen.html#setCosmetic)().

## Detailed Description

A picture serializes painter commands to an IO device in a platform-independent format.
They are sometimes referred to as meta-files.

Qt pictures use a proprietary binary format. Unlike native picture (meta-file) formats
on many window systems, Qt pictures have no limitations regarding their contents.
Everything that can be painted on a widget or pixmap (e.g., fonts, pixmaps, regions,
transformed graphics, etc.) can also be stored in a picture.

QPicture is resolution independent, i.e. a QPicture can be displayed on different
devices (for example svg, pdf, ps, printer and screen) looking the same. This is, for
instance, needed for WYSIWYG print preview. QPicture runs in the default system dpi, and
scales the painter to match differences in resolution depending on the window system.

Example of how to record a picture:

```
        QPicture picture;
        QPainter painter;
        painter.begin(&picture);           // paint in picture
        painter.drawEllipse(10,20, 80,70); // draw an ellipse
        painter.end();                     // painting done
        picture.save("drawing.pic");       // save picture
```

Note that the list of painter commands is reset on each call to the
[QPainter::begin](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpainter.html#begin)() function.

Example of how to replay a picture:

```
        QPicture picture;
        picture.load("drawing.pic");           // load picture
        QPainter painter;
        painter.begin(&myImage);               // paint in myImage
        painter.drawPicture(0, 0, picture);    // draw the picture at (0,0)
        painter.end();                         // painting done
```

Pictures can also be drawn using
[play](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpicture.html#play)(). Some basic data about a
picture is available, for example,
[size](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpicture.html#size)(),
[isNull](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpicture.html#isNull)() and
[boundingRect](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpicture.html#boundingRect)().

## Detailed Description

The picture format plugin is a simple plugin interface that makes it easy to create
custom picture formats that can be used transparently by applications.

Writing an picture format plugin is achieved by subclassing this base class,
reimplementing the pure virtual functions
[loadPicture](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpictureformatplugin.html#loadPicture)(),
[savePicture](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpictureformatplugin.html#savePicture)(),
and
[installIOHandler](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpictureformatplugin.html#installIOHandler)(),
and exporting the class with the
[Q\_PLUGIN\_METADATA](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtplugin.html#Q_PLUGIN_METADATA)()
macro.

The json file containing the metadata should contain one entry with the list of picture
formats supported by the plugin:

```
{ "Keys": [ "mypictureformat" ] }
```

### bool QPictureIO::read()

Reads an picture into memory and returns `true` if the picture was successfully read;
otherwise returns `false`.

Before reading an picture you must set an IO device or a file name. If both an IO device
and a file name have been set, the IO device will be used.

Setting the picture file format string is optional.

Note that this function does *not* set the
[format](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpictureio.html#format) used to read the
picture. If you need that information, use the
[pictureFormat](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpictureio.html#pictureFormat)()
static functions.

Example:

```
        QPictureIO iio;
        QPixmap  pixmap;
        iio.setFileName("vegeburger.pic");
        if (iio.read()) {        // OK
            QPicture picture = iio.picture();
            QPainter painter(&pixmap);
            painter.drawPicture(0, 0, picture);
        }
```

**See also**
[setIODevice](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpictureio.html#setIODevice)(),
[setFileName](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpictureio.html#setFileName)(),
[setFormat](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpictureio.html#setFormat)(),
[write](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpictureio.html#write)(), and
[QPixmap::load](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpixmap.html#load)().

Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

A pinch gesture is a form of touch user input in which the user typically touches two
points on the input device with a thumb and finger, before moving them closer together
or further apart to change the scale factor, zoom, or level of detail of the user
interface.

For an overview of gesture handling in Qt and information on using gestures in your
applications, see the [Gestures in Widgets and Graphics
View](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/gestures-overview.html) document.

![](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/images/pinchgesture.png)

Instead of repeatedly applying the same pinching gesture, the user may continue to touch
the input device in one place, and apply a second touch to a new point, continuing the
gesture. When this occurs, gesture events will continue to be delivered to the target
object, containing an instance of QPinchGesture in the
[Qt::GestureUpdated](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#GestureState-enum)
state.

PythonQt.QtGui.QPixelFormat.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

In Qt there is a often a need to represent the layout of the pixels in a graphics
buffer. Internally QPixelFormat stores everything in a 64 bit datastructure. This gives
performance but also some limitations.

QPixelFormat can describe 5 color channels and 1 alpha channel, each can use 6 bits to
describe the size of the color channel.

The position of the alpha channel is described with a separate enum. This is to make it
possible to describe [QImage](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qimage.html) formats
like ARGB32, and also describe typical OpenGL formats like RBGA8888.

How pixels are suppose to be read is determined by the
[TypeInterpretation](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpixelformat.html#TypeInterpretation-enum)
enum. It describes if color values are suppose to be read byte per byte, or if a pixel
is suppose to be read as a complete int and then masked.

There is no support for describing YUV's macro pixels. Instead a list of YUV formats has
been made. When a QPixelFormat is describing a YUV format, the
[bitsPerPixel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpixelformat.html#bitsPerPixel) value
has been deduced by the YUV Layout enum. Also, the color channels should all be set to
zero except the fifth color channel that should store the
[bitsPerPixel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpixelformat.html#bitsPerPixel) value.

PythonQt.QtGui.QPixmap.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

Qt provides four classes for handling image data:
[QImage](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qimage.html), QPixmap,
[QBitmap](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qbitmap.html) and
[QPicture](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpicture.html).
[QImage](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qimage.html) is designed and optimized for
I/O, and for direct pixel access and manipulation, while QPixmap is designed and
optimized for showing images on screen.
[QBitmap](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qbitmap.html) is only a convenience class
that inherits QPixmap, ensuring a depth of 1\. The
[isQBitmap](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpixmap.html#isQBitmap)() function
returns `true` if a QPixmap object is really a bitmap, otherwise returns `false`.
Finally, the [QPicture](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpicture.html) class is a
paint device that records and replays
[QPainter](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpainter.html) commands.

A QPixmap can easily be displayed on the screen using
[QLabel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qlabel.html) or one of
[QAbstractButton](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractbutton.html)'s subclasses
(such as [QPushButton](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpushbutton.html) and
[QToolButton](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtoolbutton.html)).
[QLabel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qlabel.html) has a pixmap property, whereas
[QAbstractButton](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractbutton.html) has an icon
property.

QPixmap objects can be passed around by value since the QPixmap class uses implicit data
sharing. For more information, see the [Implicit Data
Sharing](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/implicit-sharing.html) documentation.
QPixmap objects can also be streamed.

Note that the pixel data in a pixmap is internal and is managed by the underlying window
system. Because QPixmap is a
[QPaintDevice](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpaintdevice.html) subclass,
[QPainter](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpainter.html) can be used to draw
directly onto pixmaps. Pixels can only be accessed through
[QPainter](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpainter.html) functions or by converting
the QPixmap to a [QImage](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qimage.html). However, the
[fill](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpixmap.html#fill)() function is available for
initializing the entire pixmap with a given color.

There are functions to convert between
[QImage](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qimage.html) and QPixmap. Typically, the
[QImage](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qimage.html) class is used to load an image
file, optionally manipulating the image data, before the
[QImage](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qimage.html) object is converted into a
QPixmap to be shown on screen. Alternatively, if no manipulation is desired, the image
file can be loaded directly into a QPixmap.

QPixmap provides a collection of functions that can be used to obtain a variety of
information about the pixmap. In addition, there are several functions that enables
transformation of the pixmap.

### Reading and Writing Image Files

QPixmap provides several ways of reading an image file: The file can be loaded when
constructing the QPixmap object, or by using the
[load](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpixmap.html#load)() or
[loadFromData](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpixmap.html#loadFromData)() functions
later on. When loading an image, the file name can either refer to an actual file on
disk or to one of the application's embedded resources. See [The Qt Resource
System](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/resources.html) overview for details on how
to embed images and other resource files in the application's executable.

Simply call the [save](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpixmap.html#save)() function
to save a QPixmap object.

The complete list of supported file formats are available through the
[QImageReader::supportedImageFormats](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qimagereader.html#supportedImageFormats)()
and
[QImageWriter::supportedImageFormats](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qimagewriter.html#supportedImageFormats)()
functions. New file formats can be added as plugins. By default, Qt supports the
following formats:

| Format | Description | Qt's support |
| --- | --- | --- |
| BMP | Windows Bitmap | Read/write |
| GIF | Graphic Interchange Format (optional) | Read |
| JPG | Joint Photographic Experts Group | Read/write |
| JPEG | Joint Photographic Experts Group | Read/write |
| PNG | Portable Network Graphics | Read/write |
| PBM | Portable Bitmap | Read |
| PGM | Portable Graymap | Read |
| PPM | Portable Pixmap | Read/write |
| XBM | X11 Bitmap | Read/write |
| XPM | X11 Pixmap | Read/write |

### Pixmap Information

QPixmap provides a collection of functions that can be used to obtain a variety of
information about the pixmap:

|  | Available Functions |
| --- | --- |
| Geometry | The [size](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpixmap.html#size)(), [width](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpixmap.html#width)() and [height](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpixmap.html#height)() functions provide information about the pixmap's size. The [rect](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpixmap.html#rect)() function returns the image's enclosing rectangle. |
| Alpha component | The [hasAlphaChannel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpixmap.html#hasAlphaChannel)() returns `true` if the pixmap has a format that respects the alpha channel, otherwise returns `false`. The [hasAlpha](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpixmap.html#hasAlpha)(), [setMask](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpixmap.html#setMask)() and [mask](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpixmap.html#mask)() functions are legacy and should not be used. They are potentially very slow. The [createHeuristicMask](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpixmap.html#createHeuristicMask)() function creates and returns a 1-bpp heuristic mask (i.e. a [QBitmap](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qbitmap.html)) for this pixmap. It works by selecting a color from one of the corners and then chipping away pixels of that color, starting at all the edges. The [createMaskFromColor](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpixmap.html#createMaskFromColor)() function creates and returns a mask (i.e. a [QBitmap](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qbitmap.html)) for the pixmap based on a given color. |
| Low-level information | The [depth](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpixmap.html#depth)() function returns the depth of the pixmap. The [defaultDepth](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpixmap.html#defaultDepth)() function returns the default depth, i.e. the depth used by the application on the given screen. The [cacheKey](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpixmap.html#cacheKey)() function returns a number that uniquely identifies the contents of the QPixmap object. |

### Pixmap Conversion

A QPixmap object can be converted into a
[QImage](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qimage.html) using the
[toImage](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpixmap.html#toImage)() function. Likewise,
a [QImage](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qimage.html) can be converted into a
QPixmap using the
[fromImage](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpixmap.html#fromImage)(). If this is too
expensive an operation, you can use
[QBitmap::fromImage](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qbitmap.html#fromImage)()
instead.

To convert a QPixmap to and from HICON you can use the QtWinExtras functions
QtWin::toHICON() and QtWin::fromHICON() respectively.

### Pixmap Transformations

QPixmap supports a number of functions for creating a new pixmap that is a transformed
version of the original:

The [scaled](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpixmap.html#scaled)(),
[scaledToWidth](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpixmap.html#scaledToWidth)() and
[scaledToHeight](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpixmap.html#scaledToHeight)()
functions return scaled copies of the pixmap, while the
[copy](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpixmap.html#copy)() function creates a
QPixmap that is a plain copy of the original one.

The [transformed](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpixmap.html#transformed)()
function returns a copy of the pixmap that is transformed with the given transformation
matrix and transformation mode: Internally, the transformation matrix is adjusted to
compensate for unwanted translation, i.e.
[transformed](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpixmap.html#transformed)() returns the
smallest pixmap containing all transformed points of the original pixmap. The static
[trueMatrix](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpixmap.html#trueMatrix)() function
returns the actual matrix used for transforming the pixmap.

Qt 5 reference:

### [QBitmap](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qbitmap.html) QPixmap::createHeuristicMask(bool *clipTight* \= true) const

Creates and returns a heuristic mask for this pixmap.

The function works by selecting a color from one of the corners and then chipping away
pixels of that color, starting at all the edges. If *clipTight* is true (the default)
the mask is just large enough to cover the pixels; otherwise, the mask is larger than
the data pixels.

The mask may not be perfect but it should be reasonable, so you can do things such as
the following:

```
QPixmap myPixmap;
myPixmap.setMask(myPixmap.createHeuristicMask());
```

This function is slow because it involves converting to/from a
[QImage](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qimage.html), and non-trivial computations.

**See also**
[QImage::createHeuristicMask](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qimage.html#createHeuristicMask)()
and
[createMaskFromColor](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpixmap.html#createMaskFromColor)().

successfully loaded; otherwise invalidates the pixmap and returns `false`.

The loader attempts to read the pixmap using the specified *format*. If the *format* is
not specified (which is the default), the loader probes the file for a header to guess
the file format.

The file name can either refer to an actual file on disk or to one of the application's
embedded resources. See the [Resource
System](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/resources.html) overview for details on how
to embed pixmaps and other resource files in the application's executable.

If the data needs to be modified to fit in a lower-resolution result (e.g. converting
from 32-bit to 8-bit), use the *flags* to control the conversion.

Note that QPixmaps are automatically added to the
[QPixmapCache](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpixmapcache.html) when loaded from a
file in main thread; the key used is internal and cannot be acquired.

[loadFromData](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpixmap.html#loadFromData)() and
[Reading and Writing Image
Files](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpixmap.html#reading-and-writing-image-files).

### bool QPixmap::save(const [QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html) \&*fileName*, const char \**format* \= nullptr, int *quality* \= -1) const

Saves the pixmap to the file with the given *fileName* using the specified image file

given *device* using the specified image file *format* and *quality* factor. This can be
used, for example, to save a pixmap directly into a
[QByteArray](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qbytearray.html):

### [QPixmap](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpixmap.html#QPixmap) QPixmap::scaled(const [QSize](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsize.html) \&*size*, [Qt::AspectRatioMode](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#AspectRatioMode-enum) *aspectRatioMode* \= Qt::IgnoreAspectRatio, [Qt::TransformationMode](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#TransformationMode-enum) *transformMode* \= Qt::FastTransformation) const

Scales the pixmap to the given *size*, using the aspect ratio and transformation modes
specified by *aspectRatioMode* and *transformMode*.

![](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/images/qimage-scaling.png)

- If *aspectRatioMode* is [Qt::IgnoreAspectRatio](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#AspectRatioMode-enum), the pixmap is scaled to *size*.
- If *aspectRatioMode* is [Qt::KeepAspectRatio](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#AspectRatioMode-enum), the pixmap is scaled to a rectangle as large as possible inside *size*, preserving the aspect ratio.
- If *aspectRatioMode* is [Qt::KeepAspectRatioByExpanding](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#AspectRatioMode-enum), the pixmap is scaled to a rectangle as small as possible outside *size*, preserving the aspect ratio.

If the given *size* is empty, this function returns a null pixmap.

In some cases it can be more beneficial to draw the pixmap to a painter with a scale set
rather than scaling the pixmap. This is the case when the painter is for instance based
on OpenGL or when the scale factor changes rapidly.

**See also** [isNull](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpixmap.html#isNull)() and
[Pixmap
Transformations](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpixmap.html#pixmap-transformations).

This is an overloaded function.

Returns a copy of the pixmap scaled to a rectangle with the given *width* and *height*
according to the given *aspectRatioMode* and *transformMode*.

If either the *width* or the *height* is zero or negative, this function returns a null
pixmap.

### void QPixmap::setDevicePixelRatio([qreal](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtglobal.html#qreal-typedef) *scaleFactor*)

Sets the device pixel ratio for the pixmap. This is the ratio between image pixels and
device-independent pixels.

The default *scaleFactor* is 1.0. Setting it to something else has two effects:

QPainters that are opened on the pixmap will be scaled. For example, painting on a
200x200 image if with a ratio of 2.0 will result in effective (device-independent)
painting bounds of 100x100.

Code paths in Qt that calculate layout geometry based on the pixmap size will take the
ratio into account: [QSize](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsize.html) layoutSize \=
pixmap.[size](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpixmap.html#size)() /
pixmap.[devicePixelRatio](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpixmap.html#devicePixelRatio)()
The net effect of this is that the pixmap is displayed as high-DPI pixmap rather than a
large pixmap (see [Drawing High Resolution Versions of Pixmaps and
Images](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpainter.html#drawing-high-resolution-versions-of-pixmaps-and-images)).

**See also**
[devicePixelRatio](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpixmap.html#devicePixelRatio)().

### void QPixmap::setMask(const [QBitmap](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qbitmap.html) \&*mask*)

Sets a mask bitmap.

This function merges the *mask* with the pixmap's alpha channel. A pixel value of 1 on
the mask means the pixmap's pixel is unchanged; a value of 0 means the pixel is
transparent. The mask must have the same size as this pixmap.

Setting a null mask resets the mask, leaving the previously transparent pixels black.
The effect of this function is undefined when the pixmap is being painted on.

**Warning:** This is potentially an expensive operation.

**See also** [mask](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpixmap.html#mask)(), [Pixmap
Transformations](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpixmap.html#pixmap-transformations),

PythonQt.QtGui.QPixmapCache.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

This class is a tool for optimized drawing with
[QPixmap](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpixmap.html). You can use it to store
temporary pixmaps that are expensive to generate without using more storage space than
[cacheLimit](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpixmapcache.html#cacheLimit)(). Use
[insert](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpixmapcache.html#insert)() to insert
pixmaps, find() to find them, and
[clear](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpixmapcache.html#clear)() to empty the
cache.

QPixmapCache contains no member data, only static functions to access the global pixmap
cache. It creates an internal [QCache](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcache.html)
object for caching the pixmaps.

The cache associates a pixmap with a user-provided string as a key, or with a
[QPixmapCache::Key](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpixmapcache-key.html) that the
cache generates. Using
[QPixmapCache::Key](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpixmapcache-key.html) for keys
is faster than using strings. The string API is very convenient for complex keys but the
[QPixmapCache::Key](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpixmapcache-key.html) API will
be very efficient and convenient for a one-to-one object-to-pixmap mapping \- in this
case, you can store the keys as members of an object.

If two pixmaps are inserted into the cache using equal keys then the last pixmap will
replace the first pixmap in the cache. This follows the behavior of the
[QHash](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qhash.html#qhash) and
[QCache](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcache.html) classes.

The cache becomes full when the total size of all pixmaps in the cache exceeds
[cacheLimit](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpixmapcache.html#cacheLimit)(). The
initial cache limit is 10240 KB (10 MB); you can change this by calling
[setCacheLimit](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpixmapcache.html#setCacheLimit)()
with the required value. A pixmap takes roughly (*width* \* *height* \* *depth*)/8 bytes
of memory.

The *Qt Quarterly* article [Optimizing with
QPixmapCache](http://doc.qt.io/archives/qq/qq12-qpixmapcache.html) explains how to use
QPixmapCache to speed up applications by caching the results of painting.

**Note:** QPixmapCache is only usable from the application's main thread. Access from
other threads will be ignored and return failure.

### `[static]` bool QPixmapCache::find(const [QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html) \&*key*, [QPixmap](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpixmap.html) \**pixmap*)

Looks for a cached pixmap associated with the given *key* in the cache. If the pixmap is
found, the function sets *pixmap* to that pixmap and returns `true`; otherwise it leaves
*pixmap* alone and returns `false`.

Example:

```
QPixmap pm;
if (!QPixmapCache::find("my_big_image", &pm)) {
    pm.load("bigimage.png");
    QPixmapCache::insert("my_big_image", pm);
}
painter->drawPixmap(0, 0, pm);
```

This function was introduced in Qt 4.6.

### `[static]` bool QPixmapCache::find(const [QPixmapCache::Key](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpixmapcache-key.html) \&*key*, [QPixmap](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpixmap.html) \**pixmap*)

Looks for a cached pixmap associated with the given *key* in the cache. If the pixmap is
found, the function sets *pixmap* to that pixmap and returns `true`; otherwise it leaves
*pixmap* alone and returns `false`. If the pixmap is not found, it means that the *key*
is no longer valid, so it will be released for the next insertion.

This function was introduced in Qt 4.6.

### `[static]` bool QPixmapCache::insert(const [QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html) \&*key*, const [QPixmap](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpixmap.html) \&*pixmap*)

Inserts a copy of the pixmap *pixmap* associated with the *key* into the cache.

All pixmaps inserted by the Qt library have a key starting with "$qt", so your own
pixmap keys should never begin "$qt".

When a pixmap is inserted and the cache is about to exceed its limit, it removes pixmaps
until there is enough room for the pixmap to be inserted.

The oldest pixmaps (least recently accessed in the cache) are deleted when more space is
needed.

The function returns `true` if the object was inserted into the cache; otherwise it
returns `false`.

**See also**
[setCacheLimit](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpixmapcache.html#setCacheLimit)().

When a pixmap is inserted and the cache is about to exceed its limit, it removes pixmaps

The oldest pixmaps (least recently accessed in the cache) are deleted when more space is

## Detailed Description

A QPlainTextDocumentLayout is required for text documents that can be display or edited
in a [QPlainTextEdit](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qplaintextedit.html). See
[QTextDocument::setDocumentLayout](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html#setDocumentLayout)().

QPlainTextDocumentLayout uses the
[QAbstractTextDocumentLayout](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstracttextdocumentlayout.html)
API that [QTextDocument](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html)
requires, but redefines it partially in order to support plain text better. For
instances, it does not operate on vertical pixels, but on paragraphs (called blocks)
instead. The height of a document is identical to the number of paragraphs it contains.
The layout also doesn't support tables or nested frames, or any sort of advanced text
layout that goes beyond a list of paragraphs with syntax highlighting.

## Detailed Description

### Introduction and Concepts

QPlainTextEdit is an advanced viewer/editor supporting plain text. It is optimized to
handle large documents and to respond quickly to user input.

QPlainText uses very much the same technology and concepts as
[QTextEdit](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html), but is optimized for
plain text handling.

QPlainTextEdit works on paragraphs and characters. A paragraph is a formatted string
which is word-wrapped to fit into the width of the widget. By default when reading plain
text, one newline signifies a paragraph. A document consists of zero or more paragraphs.
Paragraphs are separated by hard line breaks. Each character within a paragraph has its
own attributes, for example, font and color.

The shape of the mouse cursor on a QPlainTextEdit is
[Qt::IBeamCursor](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#CursorShape-enum) by
default. It can be changed through the
[viewport](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractscrollarea.html#viewport)()'s
cursor property.

### Using QPlainTextEdit as a Display Widget

The text is set or replaced using
[setPlainText](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qplaintextedit.html#setPlainText)()
which deletes the existing text and replaces it with the text passed to
[setPlainText](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qplaintextedit.html#setPlainText)().

Text can be inserted using the
[QTextCursor](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcursor.html) class or using the
convenience functions
[insertPlainText](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qplaintextedit.html#insertPlainText)(),
[appendPlainText](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qplaintextedit.html#appendPlainText)()
or [paste](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qplaintextedit.html#paste)().

By default, the text edit wraps words at whitespace to fit within the text edit widget.
The
[setLineWrapMode](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qplaintextedit.html#lineWrapMode-prop)()
function is used to specify the kind of line wrap you want,
[WidgetWidth](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qplaintextedit.html#LineWrapMode-enum)
or [NoWrap](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qplaintextedit.html#LineWrapMode-enum) if
you don't want any wrapping. If you use word wrap to the widget's width
[WidgetWidth](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qplaintextedit.html#LineWrapMode-enum),
you can specify whether to break on whitespace or anywhere with
[setWordWrapMode](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qplaintextedit.html#wordWrapMode-prop)().

The [find](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qplaintextedit.html#find)() function can
be used to find and select a given string within the text.

If you want to limit the total number of paragraphs in a QPlainTextEdit, as it is for
example useful in a log viewer, then you can use the
[maximumBlockCount](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qplaintextedit.html#maximumBlockCount-prop)
property. The combination of
[setMaximumBlockCount](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qplaintextedit.html#maximumBlockCount-prop)()
and
[appendPlainText](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qplaintextedit.html#appendPlainText)()
turns QPlainTextEdit into an efficient viewer for log text. The scrolling can be reduced
with the
[centerOnScroll](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qplaintextedit.html#centerOnScroll-prop)()
property, making the log viewer even faster. Text can be formatted in a limited way,
either using a syntax highlighter (see below), or by appending html-formatted text with
[appendHtml](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qplaintextedit.html#appendHtml)(). While
QPlainTextEdit does not support complex rich text rendering with tables and floats, it
does support limited paragraph-based formatting that you may need in a log viewer.

#### Read-only Key Bindings

When QPlainTextEdit is used read-only the key bindings are limited to navigation, and
text may only be selected with the mouse:

| Keypresses | Action |
| --- | --- |
| [Qt::UpArrow](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#ArrowType-enum) | Moves one line up. |
| [Qt::DownArrow](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#ArrowType-enum) | Moves one line down. |
| [Qt::LeftArrow](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#ArrowType-enum) | Moves one character to the left. |
| [Qt::RightArrow](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#ArrowType-enum) | Moves one character to the right. |
| PageUp | Moves one (viewport) page up. |
| PageDown | Moves one (viewport) page down. |
| Home | Moves to the beginning of the text. |
| End | Moves to the end of the text. |
| Alt\+Wheel | Scrolls the page horizontally (the Wheel is the mouse wheel). |
| Ctrl\+Wheel | Zooms the text. |
| Ctrl\+A | Selects all text. |

### Using QPlainTextEdit as an Editor

All the information about using QPlainTextEdit as a display widget also applies here.

Selection of text is handled by the
[QTextCursor](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcursor.html) class, which provides
functionality for creating selections, retrieving the text contents or deleting
selections. You can retrieve the object that corresponds with the user-visible cursor
using the
[textCursor](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qplaintextedit.html#textCursor)()
method. If you want to set a selection in QPlainTextEdit just create one on a
[QTextCursor](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextcursor.html) object and then make
that cursor the visible cursor using
[setCursor](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#cursor-prop)(). The
selection can be copied to the clipboard with
[copy](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qplaintextedit.html#copy)(), or cut to the
clipboard with [cut](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qplaintextedit.html#cut)(). The
entire text can be selected using
[selectAll](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qplaintextedit.html#selectAll)().

QPlainTextEdit holds a
[QTextDocument](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html) object which can
be retrieved using the
[document](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qplaintextedit.html#document)() method.
You can also set your own document object using
[setDocument](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qplaintextedit.html#setDocument)().
[QTextDocument](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html) emits a
[textChanged](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qplaintextedit.html#textChanged)()
signal if the text changes and it also provides a isModified() function which will
return true if the text has been modified since it was either loaded or since the last
call to setModified with false as argument. In addition it provides methods for undo and
redo.

#### Syntax Highlighting

Just like [QTextEdit](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html), QPlainTextEdit
works together with
[QSyntaxHighlighter](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsyntaxhighlighter.html).

#### Editing Key Bindings

The list of key bindings which are implemented for editing:

| Keypresses | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Backspace | Deletes the character to the left of the cursor. |
| Delete | Deletes the character to the right of the cursor. |
| Ctrl\+C | Copy the selected text to the clipboard. |
| Ctrl\+Insert | Copy the selected text to the clipboard. |
| Ctrl\+K | Deletes to the end of the line. |
| Ctrl\+V | Pastes the clipboard text into text edit. |
| Shift\+Insert | Pastes the clipboard text into text edit. |
| Ctrl\+X | Deletes the selected text and copies it to the clipboard. |
| Shift\+Delete | Deletes the selected text and copies it to the clipboard. |
| Ctrl\+Z | Undoes the last operation. |
| Ctrl\+Y | Redoes the last operation. |
| LeftArrow | Moves the cursor one character to the left. |
| Ctrl\+LeftArrow | Moves the cursor one word to the left. |
| RightArrow | Moves the cursor one character to the right. |
| Ctrl\+RightArrow | Moves the cursor one word to the right. |
| UpArrow | Moves the cursor one line up. |
| Ctrl\+UpArrow | Moves the cursor one word up. |
| DownArrow | Moves the cursor one line down. |
| Ctrl\+Down Arrow | Moves the cursor one word down. |
| PageUp | Moves the cursor one page up. |
| PageDown | Moves the cursor one page down. |
| Home | Moves the cursor to the beginning of the line. |
| Ctrl\+Home | Moves the cursor to the beginning of the text. |
| End | Moves the cursor to the end of the line. |
| Ctrl\+End | Moves the cursor to the end of the text. |
| Alt\+Wheel | Scrolls the page horizontally (the Wheel is the mouse wheel). |
| Ctrl\+Wheel | Zooms the text. |

To select (mark) text hold down the Shift key whilst pressing one of the movement
keystrokes, for example, *Shift\+Right Arrow* will select the character to the right,
and *Shift\+Ctrl\+Right Arrow* will select the word to the right, etc.

### Differences to QTextEdit

QPlainTextEdit is a thin class, implemented by using most of the technology that is
behind [QTextEdit](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html) and
[QTextDocument](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html). Its performance
benefits over [QTextEdit](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html) stem mostly
from using a different and simplified text layout called
[QPlainTextDocumentLayout](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qplaintextdocumentlayout.html)
on the text document (see
[QTextDocument::setDocumentLayout](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html#setDocumentLayout)()).
The plain text document layout does not support tables nor embedded frames, and
*replaces a pixel-exact height calculation with a line-by-line respectively
paragraph-by-paragraph scrolling approach*. This makes it possible to handle
significantly larger documents, and still resize the editor with line wrap enabled in
real time. It also makes for a fast log viewer (see
[setMaximumBlockCount](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qplaintextedit.html#maximumBlockCount-prop)()).

### centerOnScroll : bool

This property holds whether the cursor should be centered on screen

If set to true, the plain text edit scrolls the document vertically to make the cursor
visible at the center of the viewport. This also allows the text edit to scroll below
the end of the document. Otherwise, if set to false, the plain text edit scrolls the
smallest amount possible to ensure the cursor is visible. The same algorithm is applied
to any new line appended through
[appendPlainText](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qplaintextedit.html#appendPlainText)().

The default is false.

### `[protected]` [QPointF](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpointf.html) QPlainTextEdit::contentOffset() const

Returns the content's origin in viewport coordinates.

The origin of the content of a plain text edit is always the top left corner of the
first visible text block. The content offset is different from (0,0) when the text has
been scrolled horizontally, or when the first visible block has been scrolled partially
off the screen, i.e. the visible text does not start with the first line of the first
visible block, or when the first visible block is the very first block and the editor
displays a margin.

[firstVisibleBlock](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qplaintextedit.html#firstVisibleBlock)(),

Qt 5 reference:

### `[override virtual protected]` void QPlainTextEdit::contextMenuEvent([QContextMenuEvent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcontextmenuevent.html) \**event*)

Reimplements:
[QAbstractScrollArea::contextMenuEvent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractscrollarea.html#contextMenuEvent)(QContextMenuEvent
\*e).

Shows the standard context menu created with
[createStandardContextMenu](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qplaintextedit.html#createStandardContextMenu)().

If you do not want the text edit to have a context menu, you can set its
[contextMenuPolicy](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#contextMenuPolicy-prop)
to
[Qt::NoContextMenu](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#ContextMenuPolicy-enum).
If you want to customize the context menu, reimplement this function. If you want to
extend the standard context menu, reimplement this function, call
[createStandardContextMenu](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qplaintextedit.html#createStandardContextMenu)()
and extend the menu returned.

Information about the event is passed in the *event* object.

```
void MyQPlainTextEdit::contextMenuEvent(QContextMenuEvent *event)
{
    QMenu *menu = createStandardContextMenu();
    menu->addAction(tr("My Menu Item"));
    //...
    menu->exec(event->globalPos());
    delete menu;
}
```

### `[signal]` void QPlainTextEdit::copyAvailable(bool *yes*)

This signal is emitted when text is selected or de-selected in the text edit.

When text is selected this signal will be emitted with *yes* set to true. If no text has

copy the selection to the clipboard. If *yes* is false then
[copy](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qplaintextedit.html#copy)() does nothing.

This function creates the standard context menu which is shown when the user clicks on

[contextMenuEvent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qplaintextedit.html#contextMenuEvent)()
handler and it takes the *position* in document coordinates where the mouse click was.

Qt 5 reference:

### bool QPlainTextEdit::find(const [QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html) \&*exp*, [QTextDocument::FindFlags](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html#FindFlag-enum) *options* \= QTextDocument::FindFlags())

Finds the next occurrence of the string, *exp*, using the given *options*. Returns
`true` if *exp* was found and changes the cursor to select the match; otherwise returns
`false`.

### bool QPlainTextEdit::find(const [QRegExp](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qregexp.html) \&*exp*, [QTextDocument::FindFlags](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html#FindFlag-enum) *options* \= QTextDocument::FindFlags())

This is an overloaded function.

Finds the next occurrence, matching the regular expression, *exp*, using the given
*options*. The
[QTextDocument::FindCaseSensitively](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html#FindFlag-enum)
option is ignored for this overload, use
[QRegExp::caseSensitivity](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qregexp.html#caseSensitivity)
instead.

Returns `true` if a match was found and changes the cursor to select the match;
otherwise returns `false`.

This function was introduced in Qt 5.3.

### bool QPlainTextEdit::find(const [QRegularExpression](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qregularexpression.html) \&*exp*, [QTextDocument::FindFlags](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html#FindFlag-enum) *options* \= QTextDocument::FindFlags())

This is an overloaded function.

Finds the next occurrence, matching the regular expression, *exp*, using the given
*options*.

Returns `true` if a match was found and changes the cursor to select the match;
otherwise returns `false`.

**Warning:** For historical reasons, the case sensitivity option set on *exp* is
ignored. Instead, the *options* are used to determine if the search is case sensitive or
not.

This function was introduced in Qt 5.13.

### maximumBlockCount : int

This property holds the limit for blocks in the document.

Specifies the maximum number of blocks the document may have. If there are more blocks
in the document that specified with this property blocks are removed from the beginning
of the document.

A negative or zero value specifies that the document may contain an unlimited amount of
blocks.

The default value is 0\.

Note that setting this property will apply the limit immediately to the document
contents. Setting this property also disables the undo redo history.

**Access functions:**

| int | **maximumBlockCount**() const |
| --- | --- |
| void | **setMaximumBlockCount**(int *maximum*) |

### `[signal]` void QPlainTextEdit::modificationChanged(bool *changed*)

This signal is emitted whenever the content of the document changes in a way that
affects the modification state. If *changed* is true, the document has been modified;
otherwise it is false.

For example, calling setModified(false) on a document and then inserting text causes the
signal to get emitted. If you undo that operation, causing the document to return to its
original unmodified state, the signal will get emitted again.

### overwriteMode : bool

This property holds whether text entered by the user will overwrite existing text

As with many text editors, the plain text editor widget can be configured to insert or
overwrite existing text with new text entered by the user.

If this property is `true`, existing text is overwritten, character-for-character by new
text; otherwise, text is inserted at the cursor position, displacing existing text.

By default, this property is `false` (new text does not overwrite existing text).

| void | **setOverwriteMode**(bool *overwrite*) |

### void QPlainTextEdit::setDocument([QTextDocument](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html) \**document*)

Makes *document* the new document of the text editor.

The parent [QObject](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qobject.html) of the provided
document remains the owner of the object. If the current document is a child of the text
editor, then it is deleted.

The document must have a document layout that inherits
[QPlainTextDocumentLayout](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qplaintextdocumentlayout.html)

[QTextDocument::setDocumentLayout](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html#setDocumentLayout)()).

Changes the text of the text edit to the string *text*. Any previous text is removed.

*text* is interpreted as plain text.

Notes:

- The undo/redo history is also cleared.
- [currentCharFormat](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qplaintextedit.html#currentCharFormat)() is reset, unless [textCursor](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qplaintextedit.html#textCursor)() is already at the beginning of the document.

**Note:** Setter function for property
[plainText](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qplaintextedit.html#plainText-prop).

**See also**
[toPlainText](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qplaintextedit.html#toPlainText)().

Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

A QPolygon object is a
[QVector](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qvector.html)\<[QPoint](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpoint.html)\>.
The easiest way to add points to a QPolygon is to use
[QVector](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qvector.html)'s streaming operator, as
illustrated below:

```
        QPolygon polygon;
        polygon << QPoint(10, 20) << QPoint(20, 30);
```

In addition to the functions provided by
[QVector](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qvector.html), QPolygon provides some
point-specific functions.

Each point in a polygon can be retrieved by passing its index to the
[point](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpolygon.html#point)() function. To populate
the polygon, QPolygon provides the
[setPoint](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpolygon.html#setPoint)() function to set
the point at a given index, the
[setPoints](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpolygon.html#setPoints)() function to
set all the points in the polygon (resizing it to the given number of points), and the
[putPoints](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpolygon.html#putPoints)() function which
copies a number of given points into the polygon from a specified index (resizing the
polygon if necessary).

QPolygon provides the
[boundingRect](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpolygon.html#boundingRect)() and
[translate](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpolygon.html#translate)() functions for
geometry functions. Use the
[QTransform::map](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtransform.html#map)() function for
more general transformations of QPolygons.

The QPolygon class is [implicitly
shared](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/implicit-sharing.html).

## Detailed Description

A QPolygonF is a
[QVector](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qvector.html)\<[QPointF](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpointf.html)\>.
The easiest way to add points to a QPolygonF is to use its streaming operator, as
illustrated below:

```
        QPolygonF polygon;
        polygon << QPointF(10.4, 20.5) << QPointF(20.2, 30.2);
```

In addition to the functions provided by
[QVector](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qvector.html), QPolygonF provides the
[boundingRect](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpolygonf.html#boundingRect)() and
[translate](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpolygonf.html#translate)() functions for
geometry operations. Use the
[QTransform::map](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtransform.html#map)() function for
more general transformations of QPolygonFs.

QPolygonF also provides the
[isClosed](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpolygonf.html#isClosed)() function to
determine whether a polygon's start and end points are the same, and the
[toPolygon](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpolygonf.html#toPolygon)() function
returning an integer precision copy of this polygon.

The QPolygonF class is [implicitly
shared](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/implicit-sharing.html).

PythonQt.QtGui.QPrintDialog.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

The dialog allows users to change document-related settings, such as the paper size and
orientation, type of print (color or grayscale), range of pages, and number of copies to
print.

Controls are also provided to enable users to choose from the printers available,
including any configured network printers.

Typically, QPrintDialog objects are constructed with a
[QPrinter](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qprinter.html) object, and executed using
the [exec](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qprintdialog.html#exec)() function.

```
QPrintDialog printDialog(printer, parent);
if (printDialog.exec() == QDialog::Accepted) {
    // print ...
}
```

If the dialog is accepted by the user, the
[QPrinter](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qprinter.html) object is correctly
configured for printing.

|  |  |
| --- | --- |

The printer dialog (shown above in Plastique style) enables access to common printing
properties. On X11 platforms that use the CUPS printing system, the settings for each
available printer can be modified via the dialog's **Properties** push button.

On Windows and macOS, the native print dialog is used, which means that some
[QWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html) and
[QDialog](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdialog.html) properties set on the dialog
won't be respected. The native print dialog on macOS does not support setting printer
options, i.e.
[setOptions](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qprintdialog.html#options-prop)() and
[setOption](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qprintdialog.html#setOption)() have no
effect.

In Qt 4.4, it was possible to use the static functions to show a sheet on macOS. This is
no longer supported in Qt 4.5. If you want this functionality, use
[QPrintDialog::open](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qprintdialog.html#open)().

Qt 5 reference:

### `[signal]` void QPrintDialog::accepted([QPrinter](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qprinter.html) \**printer*)

This signal is emitted when the user accepts the values set in the print dialog. The
*printer* parameter includes the printer that the settings were applied to.

PythonQt.QtGui.QPrintDialog.done.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

### `[override virtual]` void QPrintDialog::done(int *result*)

Reimplements: [QDialog::done](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdialog.html#done)(int
r).

Closes the dialog and sets its result code to *result*. If this dialog is shown with
[exec](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qprintdialog.html#exec)(), done() causes the
local event loop to finish, and
[exec](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qprintdialog.html#exec)() to return *result*.

**Note:** This function does not apply to the Native Print Dialog on the Mac macOS and
Windows platforms, because the dialog is required to be modal and only the user can

## Detailed Description

Using QPrintPreviewDialog in your existing application is straightforward:

1. Create the QPrintPreviewDialog.

   You can construct a QPrintPreviewDialog with an existing
   [QPrinter](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qprinter.html) object, or you can have
   QPrintPreviewDialog create one for you, which will be the system default printer.
2. Connect the [paintRequested](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qprintpreviewdialog.html#paintRequested)() signal to a slot.

   When the dialog needs to generate a set of preview pages, the
   [paintRequested](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qprintpreviewdialog.html#paintRequested)()
   signal will be emitted. You can use the exact same code for the actual printing as for
   having the preview generated, including calling
   [QPrinter::newPage](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qprinter.html#newPage)() to start
   a new page in the preview. Connect a slot to the
   [paintRequested](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qprintpreviewdialog.html#paintRequested)()
   signal, where you draw onto the
   [QPrinter](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qprinter.html) object that is passed into
   the slot.
3. Call [exec](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdialog.html#exec)().

   Call [QPrintPreviewDialog::exec](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdialog.html#exec)()
   to show the preview dialog.

## Detailed Description

[QPrintPreviewDialog](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qprintpreviewdialog.html) uses
a QPrintPreviewWidget internally, and the purpose of QPrintPreviewWidget is to make it
possible to embed the preview into other widgets. It also makes it possible to build a
different user interface around it than the default one provided with
[QPrintPreviewDialog](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qprintpreviewdialog.html).

Using QPrintPreviewWidget is straightforward:

1. Create the QPrintPreviewWidget

   Construct the QPrintPreviewWidget either by passing in an existing
   [QPrinter](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qprinter.html) object, or have
   QPrintPreviewWidget create a default constructed
   [QPrinter](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qprinter.html) object for you.
2. Connect the [paintRequested](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qprintpreviewwidget.html#paintRequested)() signal to a slot.

   When the widget needs to generate a set of preview pages, a
   [paintRequested](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qprintpreviewwidget.html#paintRequested)()
   signal will be emitted from the widget. Connect a slot to this signal, and draw onto the
   [QPrinter](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qprinter.html) passed in as a signal
   parameter. Call
   [QPrinter::newPage](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qprinter.html#newPage)(), to
   start a new page in the preview.

Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

This device represents a series of pages of printed output, and is used in almost
exactly the same way as other paint devices such as
[QWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html) and
[QPixmap](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpixmap.html). A set of additional
functions are provided to manage device-specific features, such as orientation and
resolution, and to step through the pages in a document as it is generated.

When printing directly to a printer on Windows or macOS, QPrinter uses the built-in
printer drivers. On X11, QPrinter uses the [Common Unix Printing System
(CUPS)](http://www.cups.org/) to send PDF output to the printer. As an alternative, the
[printProgram](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qprinter.html#printProgram)() function
can be used to specify the command or utility to use instead of the system default.

Note that setting parameters like paper size and resolution on an invalid printer is
undefined. You can use
[QPrinter::isValid](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qprinter.html#isValid)() to
verify this before changing any parameters.

QPrinter supports a number of parameters, most of which can be changed by the end user
through a [print dialog](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qprintdialog.html). In
general, QPrinter passes these functions onto the underlying
[QPrintEngine](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qprintengine.html).

The most important parameters are:

- setOrientation() tells QPrinter which page orientation to use.
- setPaperSize() tells QPrinter what paper size to expect from the printer.
- [setResolution](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qprinter.html#setResolution)() tells QPrinter what resolution you wish the printer to provide, in dots per inch (DPI).
- [setFullPage](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qprinter.html#setFullPage)() tells QPrinter whether you want to deal with the full page or just with the part the printer can draw on.
- [setCopyCount](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qprinter.html#setCopyCount)() tells QPrinter how many copies of the document it should print.

Many of these functions can only be called before the actual printing begins (i.e.,
before [QPainter::begin](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpainter.html#begin)() is
called). This usually makes sense because, for example, it's not possible to change the
number of copies when you are halfway through printing. There are also some settings
that the user sets (through the printer dialog) and that applications are expected to
obey. See
[QAbstractPrintDialog](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractprintdialog.html)'s
documentation for more details.

When [QPainter::begin](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpainter.html#begin)() is
called, the QPrinter it operates on is prepared for a new page, enabling the
[QPainter](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpainter.html) to be used immediately to
paint the first page in a document. Once the first page has been painted,
[newPage](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qprinter.html#newPage)() can be called to
request a new blank page to paint on, or
[QPainter::end](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpainter.html#end)() can be called to
finish printing. The second page and all following pages are prepared using a call to
[newPage](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qprinter.html#newPage)() before they are
painted.

The first page in a document does not need to be preceded by a call to
[newPage](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qprinter.html#newPage)(). You only need to
calling [newPage](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qprinter.html#newPage)() after
[QPainter::begin](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpainter.html#begin)() if you need
to insert a blank page at the beginning of a printed document. Similarly, calling
[newPage](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qprinter.html#newPage)() after the last
page in a document is painted will result in a trailing blank page appended to the end
of the printed document.

If you want to abort the print job,
[abort](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qprinter.html#abort)() will try its best to
stop printing. It may cancel the entire job or just part of it.

Since QPrinter can print to any
[QPrintEngine](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qprintengine.html) subclass, it is
possible to extend printing support to cover new types of printing subsystem by
subclassing [QPrintEngine](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qprintengine.html) and
reimplementing its interface.

### bool QPrinter::abort()

Aborts the current print run. Returns `true` if the print run was successfully aborted
and [printerState](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qprinter.html#printerState)() will
return
[QPrinter::Aborted](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qprinter.html#PrinterState-enum);
otherwise returns `false`.

It is not always possible to abort a print job. For example, all the data has gone to
the printer but the printer cannot or will not cancel the job when asked to.

### bool QPrinter::collateCopies() const

Returns `true` if collation is turned on when multiple copies is selected. Returns
`false` if it is turned off when multiple copies is selected. When collating is turned
off the printing of each individual page will be repeated the numCopies() amount before
the next page is started. With collating turned on all pages are printed before the next
copy of those pages is started.

### void QPrinter::setFromTo(int *from*, int *to*)

Sets the range of pages to be printed to cover the pages with numbers specified by
*from* and *to*, where *from* corresponds to the first page in the range and *to*
corresponds to the last.

**Note:** Pages in a document are numbered according to the convention that the first
page is page 1\. However, if *from* and *to* are both set to 0, the *whole document will
be printed*.

This function is mostly used to set a default value that the user can override in the
print dialog when you call setup().

This function was introduced in Qt 4.1.

**See also** [fromPage](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qprinter.html#fromPage)() and
