### void QSessionManager::setRestartCommand(const [QStringList](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstringlist.html) \&*command*)

If the session manager is capable of restoring sessions it will execute *command* in
order to restore the application. The command defaults to

```
appname -session id
```

The `-session` option is mandatory; otherwise
[QGuiApplication](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qguiapplication.html) cannot tell
whether it has been restored or what the current session identifier is. See
[QGuiApplication::isSessionRestored](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qguiapplication.html#isSessionRestored)()
and
[QGuiApplication::sessionId](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qguiapplication.html#sessionId)()
for details.

If your application is very simple, it may be possible to store the entire application
state in additional command line options. This is usually a very bad idea because
command lines are often limited to a few hundred bytes. Instead, use
[QSettings](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsettings.html), temporary files, or a
database for this purpose. By marking the data with the unique
[sessionId](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsessionmanager.html#sessionId)(), you
will be able to restore the application in a future session.

**See also**
[restartCommand](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsessionmanager.html#restartCommand)(),
[setDiscardCommand](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsessionmanager.html#setDiscardCommand)(),
and
[setRestartHint](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsessionmanager.html#setRestartHint)().

Qt 5 reference:

### void QSessionManager::setRestartHint([QSessionManager::RestartHint](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsessionmanager.html#RestartHint-enum) *hint*)

to `RestartIfRunning`.

We recommend setting the restart hint in
[QGuiApplication::saveStateRequest](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qguiapplication.html#saveStateRequest)()
because most session managers perform a checkpoint shortly after an application's

PythonQt.QtGui.QShortcut.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

The QShortcut class provides a way of connecting keyboard shortcuts to Qt's [signals and
slots](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/signalsandslots.html) mechanism, so that
objects can be informed when a shortcut is executed. The shortcut can be set up to
contain all the key presses necessary to describe a keyboard shortcut, including the
states of modifier keys such as **Shift**, **Ctrl**, and **Alt**.

On certain widgets, using '\&' in front of a character will automatically create a
mnemonic (a shortcut) for that character, e.g. "E\&xit" will create the shortcut
**Alt\+X** (use '\&\&' to display an actual ampersand). The widget might consume and
perform an action on a given shortcut. On X11 the ampersand will not be shown and the
character will be underlined. On Windows, shortcuts are normally not displayed until the
user presses the **Alt** key, but this is a setting the user can change. On Mac,
shortcuts are disabled by default. Call
[qt\_set\_sequence\_auto\_mnemonic](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qkeysequence.html#qt_set_sequence_auto_mnemonic)()
to enable them. However, because mnemonic shortcuts do not fit in with Aqua's
guidelines, Qt will not show the shortcut character underlined.

For applications that use menus, it may be more convenient to use the convenience
functions provided in the [QMenu](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmenu.html) class
to assign keyboard shortcuts to menu items as they are created. Alternatively, shortcuts
may be associated with other types of actions in the
[QAction](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qaction.html) class.

The simplest way to create a shortcut for a particular widget is to construct the
shortcut with a key sequence. For example:

```
shortcut = new QShortcut(QKeySequence(tr("Ctrl+O", "File|Open")),
                         parent);
```

When the user types the [key
sequence](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qkeysequence.html) for a given shortcut,
the shortcut's
[activated](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qshortcut.html#activated)() signal is
emitted. (In the case of ambiguity, the
[activatedAmbiguously](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qshortcut.html#activatedAmbiguously)()
signal is emitted.) A shortcut is "listened for" by Qt's event loop when the shortcut's
parent widget is receiving events.

A shortcut's key sequence can be set with
[setKey](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qshortcut.html#key-prop)() and retrieved
with [key](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qshortcut.html#key-prop)(). A shortcut can
be enabled or disabled with
[setEnabled](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qshortcut.html#enabled-prop)(), and can
have "What's This?" help text set with
[setWhatsThis](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qshortcut.html#whatsThis-prop)().

### `[signal]` void QShortcut::activatedAmbiguously()

When a key sequence is being typed at the keyboard, it is said to be ambiguous as long
as it matches the start of more than one shortcut.

When a shortcut's key sequence is completed, activatedAmbiguously() is emitted if the
key sequence is still ambiguous (i.e., it is the start of one or more other shortcuts).
The [activated](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qshortcut.html#activated)() signal is
not emitted in this case.

## Detailed Description

There are two kinds of show events: show events caused by the window system
(spontaneous), and internal show events. Spontaneous
([QEvent::spontaneous](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qevent.html#spontaneous)())
show events are sent just after the window system shows the window; they are also sent
when a top-level window is redisplayed after being iconified. Internal show events are
delivered just before the widget becomes visible.

## Detailed Description

This widget works like the standard Windows resize handle. In the X11 version this
resize handle generally works differently from the one provided by the system if the X11
window manager does not support necessary modern post-ICCCM specifications.

Put this widget anywhere in a widget tree and the user can use it to resize the
top-level window or any widget with the
[Qt::SubWindow](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#WindowType-enum) flag set.
Generally, this should be in the lower right-hand corner.

Note that [QStatusBar](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstatusbar.html) already uses
this widget, so if you have a status bar (e.g., you are using
[QMainWindow](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmainwindow.html)), then you don't need
to use this widget explicitly. The same goes for
[QDialog](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdialog.html), for which you can just call
[QDialog::setSizeGripEnabled()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdialog.html#sizeGripEnabled-prop).

On some platforms the size grip automatically hides itself when the window is shown full
screen or maximised.

| Screenshot of a Fusion style size grip | A size grip widget at the bottom-right corner of a main window, shown in the [Fusion widget style](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/gallery.html). |
| --- | --- |

The QSizeGrip class inherits [QWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html)
and reimplements the
[mousePressEvent()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#mousePressEvent) and
[mouseMoveEvent()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#mouseMoveEvent)
functions to feature the resize functionality, and the
[paintEvent()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#paintEvent) function to
render the size grip widget.

## Detailed Description

The size policy of a widget is an expression of its willingness to be resized in various
ways, and affects how the widget is treated by the [layout
engine](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/layout.html). Each widget returns a
QSizePolicy that describes the horizontal and vertical resizing policy it prefers when
being laid out. You can change this for a specific widget by changing its
[QWidget::sizePolicy](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#sizePolicy-prop)
property.

QSizePolicy contains two independent
[QSizePolicy::Policy](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsizepolicy.html#Policy-enum)
values and two stretch factors; one describes the widgets's horizontal size policy, and
the other describes its vertical size policy. It also contains a flag to indicate
whether the height and width of its preferred size are related.

The horizontal and vertical policies can be set in the constructor, and altered using
the
[setHorizontalPolicy](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsizepolicy.html#setHorizontalPolicy)()
and
[setVerticalPolicy](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsizepolicy.html#setVerticalPolicy)()
functions. The stretch factors can be set using the
[setHorizontalStretch](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsizepolicy.html#setHorizontalStretch)()
and
[setVerticalStretch](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsizepolicy.html#setVerticalStretch)()
functions. The flag indicating whether the widget's
[sizeHint()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#sizeHint-prop) is
width-dependent (such as a menu bar or a word-wrapping label) can be set using the
[setHeightForWidth](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsizepolicy.html#setHeightForWidth)()
function.

The current size policies and stretch factors be retrieved using the
[horizontalPolicy](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsizepolicy.html#horizontalPolicy)(),
[verticalPolicy](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsizepolicy.html#verticalPolicy)(),
[horizontalStretch](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsizepolicy.html#horizontalStretch)()
and
[verticalStretch](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsizepolicy.html#verticalStretch)()
functions. Alternatively, use the
[transpose](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsizepolicy.html#transpose)() function to
swap the horizontal and vertical policies and stretches. The
[hasHeightForWidth](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsizepolicy.html#hasHeightForWidth)()
function returns the current status of the flag indicating the size hint dependencies.

Use the
[expandingDirections](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsizepolicy.html#expandingDirections)()
function to determine whether the associated widget can make use of more space than its
[sizeHint()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#sizeHint-prop) function
indicates, as well as find out in which directions it can expand.

Finally, the QSizePolicy class provides operators comparing this size policy to a given
policy, as well as a [QVariant](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qvariant.html)
operator storing this QSizePolicy as a
[QVariant](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qvariant.html) object.

### void QSizePolicy::setHorizontalStretch(int *stretchFactor*)

Sets the horizontal stretch factor of the size policy to the given *stretchFactor*.
*stretchFactor* must be in the range \[0,255\].

When two widgets are adjacent to each other in a horizontal layout, setting the
horizontal stretch factor of the widget on the left to 2 and the factor of widget on the
right to 1 will ensure that the widget on the left will always be twice the size of the
one on the right.

**See also**
[horizontalStretch](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsizepolicy.html#horizontalStretch)(),
[setVerticalStretch](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsizepolicy.html#setVerticalStretch)(),
and
[setHorizontalPolicy](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsizepolicy.html#setHorizontalPolicy)().

Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

![](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/images/windows-slider.png)

The slider is the classic widget for controlling a bounded value. It lets the user move
a slider handle along a horizontal or vertical groove and translates the handle's
position into an integer value within the legal range.

QSlider has very few of its own functions; most of the functionality is in
[QAbstractSlider](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html). The most
useful functions are
[setValue](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html#value-prop)() to set
the slider directly to some value;
[triggerAction](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html#triggerAction)()
to simulate the effects of clicking (useful for shortcut keys);
[setSingleStep](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html#singleStep-prop)(),
[setPageStep](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html#pageStep-prop)()
to set the steps; and
[setMinimum](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html#minimum-prop)() and
[setMaximum](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html#maximum-prop)() to
define the range of the scroll bar.

QSlider provides methods for controlling tickmarks. You can use
[setTickPosition](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qslider.html#tickPosition-prop)()
to indicate where you want the tickmarks to be,
[setTickInterval](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qslider.html#tickInterval-prop)()
to indicate how many of them you want. the currently set tick position and interval can
be queried using the
[tickPosition](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qslider.html#tickPosition-prop)() and
[tickInterval](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qslider.html#tickInterval-prop)()
functions, respectively.

QSlider inherits a comprehensive set of signals:

| Signal | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [valueChanged](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html#valueChanged)() | Emitted when the slider's value has changed. The tracking() determines whether this signal is emitted during user interaction. |
| [sliderPressed](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html#sliderPressed)() | Emitted when the user starts to drag the slider. |
| [sliderMoved](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html#sliderMoved)() | Emitted when the user drags the slider. |
| [sliderReleased](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html#sliderReleased)() | Emitted when the user releases the slider. |

QSlider only provides integer ranges. Note that although QSlider handles very large
numbers, it becomes difficult for users to use a slider accurately for very large
ranges.

A slider accepts focus on Tab and provides both a mouse wheel and a keyboard interface.
The keyboard interface is the following:

- Left/Right move a horizontal slider by one single step.
- Up/Down move a vertical slider by one single step.
- PageUp moves up one page.
- PageDown moves down one page.
- Home moves to the start (minimum).
- End moves to the end (maximum).

PythonQt.QtGui.QSortFilterProxyModel.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

QSortFilterProxyModel can be used for sorting items, filtering out items, or both. The
model transforms the structure of a source model by mapping the model indexes it
supplies to new indexes, corresponding to different locations, for views to use. This
approach allows a given source model to be restructured as far as views are concerned
without requiring any transformations on the underlying data, and without duplicating
the data in memory.

Let's assume that we want to sort and filter the items provided by a custom model. The
code to set up the model and the view, *without* sorting and filtering, would look like
this:

```
        QTreeView *treeView = new QTreeView;
        MyItemModel *model = new MyItemModel(this);

        treeView->setModel(model);
```

To add sorting and filtering support to `MyItemModel`, we need to create a
QSortFilterProxyModel, call
[setSourceModel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsortfilterproxymodel.html#setSourceModel)()
with the `MyItemModel` as argument, and install the QSortFilterProxyModel on the view:

```
        QTreeView *treeView = new QTreeView;
        MyItemModel *sourceModel = new MyItemModel(this);
        QSortFilterProxyModel *proxyModel = new QSortFilterProxyModel(this);

        proxyModel->setSourceModel(sourceModel);
        treeView->setModel(proxyModel);
```

At this point, neither sorting nor filtering is enabled; the original data is displayed
in the view. Any changes made through the QSortFilterProxyModel are applied to the
original model.

The QSortFilterProxyModel acts as a wrapper for the original model. If you need to
convert source [QModelIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmodelindex.html)es to
sorted/filtered model indexes or vice versa, use
[mapToSource](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsortfilterproxymodel.html#mapToSource)(),
[mapFromSource](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsortfilterproxymodel.html#mapFromSource)(),
[mapSelectionToSource](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsortfilterproxymodel.html#mapSelectionToSource)(),
and
[mapSelectionFromSource](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsortfilterproxymodel.html#mapSelectionFromSource)().

**Note:** By default, the model dynamically re-sorts and re-filters data whenever the
original model changes. This behavior can be changed by setting the
[dynamicSortFilter](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsortfilterproxymodel.html#dynamicSortFilter-prop)
property.

The [Basic Sort/Filter
Model](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtwidgets-itemviews-basicsortfiltermodel-example.html)
and [Custom Sort/Filter
Model](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtwidgets-itemviews-customsortfiltermodel-example.html)
examples illustrate how to use QSortFilterProxyModel to perform basic sorting and
filtering and how to subclass it to implement custom behavior.

### Sorting

[QTableView](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtableview.html) and
[QTreeView](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtreeview.html) have a
[sortingEnabled](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtreeview.html#sortingEnabled-prop)
property that controls whether the user can sort the view by clicking the view's
horizontal header. For example:

```
        treeView->setSortingEnabled(true);
```

When this feature is on (the default is off), clicking on a header section sorts the
items according to that column. By clicking repeatedly, the user can alternate between
ascending and descending order.

![A sorted
QTreeView](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/images/qsortfilterproxymodel-sorting.png)

Behind the scene, the view calls the
[sort](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsortfilterproxymodel.html#sort)() virtual
function on the model to reorder the data in the model. To make your data sortable, you
can either implement
[sort](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsortfilterproxymodel.html#sort)() in your
model, or use a QSortFilterProxyModel to wrap your model \-- QSortFilterProxyModel
provides a generic
[sort](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsortfilterproxymodel.html#sort)()
reimplementation that operates on the
[sortRole](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsortfilterproxymodel.html#sortRole-prop)()
([Qt::DisplayRole](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#ItemDataRole-enum) by
default) of the items and that understands several data types, including `int`,
[QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html), and
[QDateTime](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdatetime.html). For hierarchical models,
sorting is applied recursively to all child items. String comparisons are case sensitive
by default; this can be changed by setting the
[sortCaseSensitivity](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsortfilterproxymodel.html#sortCaseSensitivity-prop)
property.

Custom sorting behavior is achieved by subclassing QSortFilterProxyModel and
reimplementing
[lessThan](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsortfilterproxymodel.html#lessThan)(),
which is used to compare items. For example:

```
bool MySortFilterProxyModel::lessThan(const QModelIndex &left,
                                      const QModelIndex &right) const
{
    QVariant leftData = sourceModel()->data(left);
    QVariant rightData = sourceModel()->data(right);

    if (leftData.userType() == QMetaType::QDateTime) {
        return leftData.toDateTime() < rightData.toDateTime();
    } else {
        static const QRegularExpression emailPattern("[\\w\\.]*@[\\w\\.]*");

        QString leftString = leftData.toString();
        if (left.column() == 1) {
            const QRegularExpressionMatch match = emailPattern.match(leftString);
            if (match.hasMatch())
                leftString = match.captured(0);
        }
        QString rightString = rightData.toString();
        if (right.column() == 1) {
            const QRegularExpressionMatch match = emailPattern.match(rightString);
            if (match.hasMatch())
                rightString = match.captured(0);
        }

        return QString::localeAwareCompare(leftString, rightString) < 0;
    }
}
```

(This code snippet comes from the [Custom Sort/Filter
Model](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtwidgets-itemviews-customsortfiltermodel-example.html)
example.)

An alternative approach to sorting is to disable sorting on the view and to impose a
certain order to the user. This is done by explicitly calling
[sort](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsortfilterproxymodel.html#sort)() with the
desired column and order as arguments on the QSortFilterProxyModel (or on the original
model if it implements
[sort](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsortfilterproxymodel.html#sort)()). For
example:

```
        proxyModel->sort(2, Qt::AscendingOrder);
```

QSortFilterProxyModel can be sorted by column -1, in which case it returns to the sort
order of the underlying source model.

### Filtering

In addition to sorting, QSortFilterProxyModel can be used to hide items that do not
match a certain filter. The filter is specified using a
[QRegExp](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qregexp.html) object and is applied to the
[filterRole](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsortfilterproxymodel.html#filterRole-prop)()
([Qt::DisplayRole](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#ItemDataRole-enum) by
default) of each item, for a given column. The
[QRegExp](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qregexp.html) object can be used to match a
regular expression, a wildcard pattern, or a fixed string. For example:

```
        proxyModel->setFilterRegExp(QRegExp(".png", Qt::CaseInsensitive,
                                            QRegExp::FixedString));
        proxyModel->setFilterKeyColumn(1);
```

For hierarchical models, the filter is applied recursively to all children. If a parent
item doesn't match the filter, none of its children will be shown.

A common use case is to let the user specify the filter regular expression, wildcard
pattern, or fixed string in a
[QLineEdit](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qlineedit.html) and to connect the
[textChanged()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qlineedit.html#textChanged) signal to
[setFilterRegularExpression](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsortfilterproxymodel.html#setFilterRegularExpression)(),
[setFilterWildcard](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsortfilterproxymodel.html#setFilterWildcard)(),
or
[setFilterFixedString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsortfilterproxymodel.html#setFilterFixedString)()
to reapply the filter.

Custom filtering behavior can be achieved by reimplementing the
[filterAcceptsRow](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsortfilterproxymodel.html#filterAcceptsRow)()
and
[filterAcceptsColumn](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsortfilterproxymodel.html#filterAcceptsColumn)()
functions. For example (from the [Custom Sort/Filter
Model](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtwidgets-itemviews-customsortfiltermodel-example.html)
example), the following implementation ignores the
[filterKeyColumn](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsortfilterproxymodel.html#filterKeyColumn-prop)
property and performs filtering on columns 0, 1, and 2:

```
bool MySortFilterProxyModel::filterAcceptsRow(int sourceRow,
                                              const QModelIndex &sourceParent) const
{
    QModelIndex index0 = sourceModel()->index(sourceRow, 0, sourceParent);
    QModelIndex index1 = sourceModel()->index(sourceRow, 1, sourceParent);
    QModelIndex index2 = sourceModel()->index(sourceRow, 2, sourceParent);

    return (sourceModel()->data(index0).toString().contains(filterRegExp())
            || sourceModel()->data(index1).toString().contains(filterRegExp()))
            && dateInRange(sourceModel()->data(index2).toDate());
}
```

(This code snippet comes from the [Custom Sort/Filter
Model](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtwidgets-itemviews-customsortfiltermodel-example.html)
example.)

If you are working with large amounts of filtering and have to invoke
[invalidateFilter](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsortfilterproxymodel.html#invalidateFilter)()
repeatedly, using
[beginResetModel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#beginResetModel)()
/
[endResetModel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#endResetModel)()
may be more efficient, depending on the implementation of your model. However,
[beginResetModel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#beginResetModel)()
/
[endResetModel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#endResetModel)()
returns the proxy model to its original state, losing selection information, and will
cause the proxy model to be repopulated.

### Subclassing

Since [QAbstractProxyModel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractproxymodel.html)
and its subclasses are derived from
[QAbstractItemModel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html), much
of the same advice about subclassing normal models also applies to proxy models. In
addition, it is worth noting that many of the default implementations of functions in
this class are written so that they call the equivalent functions in the relevant source
model. This simple proxying mechanism may need to be overridden for source models with
more complex behavior; for example, if the source model provides a custom
[hasChildren](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsortfilterproxymodel.html#hasChildren)()
implementation, you should also provide one in the proxy model.

**Note:** Some general guidelines for subclassing models are available in the [Model
Subclassing
Reference](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/model-view-programming.html#model-subclassing-reference).

**Note:** With Qt 5, regular expression support has been improved through the
[QRegularExpression](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qregularexpression.html) class.
QSortFilterProxyModel dating back prior to that class creation, it originally supported
only [QRegExp](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qregexp.html). Since Qt 5.12,
[QRegularExpression](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qregularexpression.html) APIs
have been added. Therefore, [QRegExp](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qregexp.html)
APIs should be considered deprecated and the
[QRegularExpression](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qregularexpression.html) version
should be used in place.

**Warning:** Don't mix calls to the getters and setters of different regexp types as
this will lead to unexpected results. For maximum compatibility, the original
implementation has been kept. Therefore, if, for example, a call to
[setFilterRegularExpression](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsortfilterproxymodel.html#setFilterRegularExpression)
is made followed by another one to
[setFilterFixedString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsortfilterproxymodel.html#setFilterFixedString),
the first call will setup a
[QRegularExpression](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qregularexpression.html) object
to use as filter while the second will setup a
[QRegExp](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qregexp.html) in FixedString mode. However,
this is an implementation detail that might change in the future.

### dynamicSortFilter : bool

This property holds whether the proxy model is dynamically sorted and filtered whenever
the contents of the source model change

Note that you should not update the source model through the proxy model when
dynamicSortFilter is true. For instance, if you set the proxy model on a
[QComboBox](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcombobox.html), then using functions
that update the model, e.g.,
[addItem()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcombobox.html#addItem), will not work as
expected. An alternative is to set dynamicSortFilter to false and call
[sort()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsortfilterproxymodel.html#sort) after
adding items to the [QComboBox](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcombobox.html).

The default value is true.

This property was introduced in Qt 4.2.

**Access functions:**

| bool | **dynamicSortFilter**() const |
| --- | --- |
| void | **setDynamicSortFilter**(bool *enable*) |

**See also**
[sortColumn](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsortfilterproxymodel.html#sortColumn)().

### `[virtual protected]` bool QSortFilterProxyModel::filterAcceptsRow(int *source\_row*, const [QModelIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmodelindex.html) \&*source\_parent*) const

Returns `true` if the item in the row indicated by the given *source\_row* and
*source\_parent* should be included in the model; otherwise returns false.

The default implementation returns `true` if the value held by the relevant item matches
the filter string, wildcard string or regular expression.

**Note:** By default, the
[Qt::DisplayRole](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#ItemDataRole-enum) is used
to determine if the row should be accepted or not. This can be changed by setting the
[filterRole](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsortfilterproxymodel.html#filterRole-prop)
property.

**See also**
[filterAcceptsColumn](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsortfilterproxymodel.html#filterAcceptsColumn)(),
[setFilterFixedString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsortfilterproxymodel.html#setFilterFixedString)(),
[setFilterRegExp](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsortfilterproxymodel.html#filterRegExp-prop)(),
and
[setFilterWildcard](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsortfilterproxymodel.html#setFilterWildcard)().
signatures: filterAcceptsRow(self, source_row: int, source_parent: PySide2.QtCore.QModelIndex) -> bool

### filterRegExp : [QRegExp](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qregexp.html)

This property holds the [QRegExp](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qregexp.html) used
to filter the contents of the source model

Setting this property overwrites the current
[filterCaseSensitivity](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsortfilterproxymodel.html#filterCaseSensitivity-prop).
By default, the [QRegExp](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qregexp.html) is an empty
string matching all contents.

If no [QRegExp](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qregexp.html) or an empty string is
set, everything in the source model will be accepted.

**Access functions:**

### `[virtual protected]` bool QSortFilterProxyModel::lessThan(const [QModelIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmodelindex.html) \&*source\_left*, const [QModelIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmodelindex.html) \&*source\_right*) const

Returns `true` if the value of the item referred to by the given index *source\_left* is
less than the value of the item referred to by the given index *source\_right*,
otherwise returns `false`.

This function is used as the \< operator when sorting, and handles the following
[QVariant](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qvariant.html) types:

- [QMetaType::Int](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmetatype.html#Type-enum)
- [QMetaType::UInt](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmetatype.html#Type-enum)
- [QMetaType::LongLong](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmetatype.html#Type-enum)
- [QMetaType::ULongLong](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmetatype.html#Type-enum)
- [QMetaType::Float](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmetatype.html#Type-enum)
- [QMetaType::Double](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmetatype.html#Type-enum)
- [QMetaType::QChar](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmetatype.html#Type-enum)
- [QMetaType::QDate](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmetatype.html#Type-enum)
- [QMetaType::QTime](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmetatype.html#Type-enum)
- [QMetaType::QDateTime](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmetatype.html#Type-enum)
- [QMetaType::QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmetatype.html#Type-enum)

Any other type will be converted to a
[QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html) using
[QVariant::toString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qvariant.html#toString)().

Comparison of [QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html)s is case
sensitive by default; this can be changed using the
[sortCaseSensitivity](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsortfilterproxymodel.html#sortCaseSensitivity-prop)
property.

By default, the
[Qt::DisplayRole](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#ItemDataRole-enum)
associated with the [QModelIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmodelindex.html)es
is used for comparisons. This can be changed by setting the
[sortRole](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsortfilterproxymodel.html#sortRole-prop)
property.

**Note:** The indices passed in correspond to the source model.

**See also**
[sortRole](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsortfilterproxymodel.html#sortRole-prop),
[sortCaseSensitivity](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsortfilterproxymodel.html#sortCaseSensitivity-prop),
and
[dynamicSortFilter](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsortfilterproxymodel.html#dynamicSortFilter-prop).

PythonQt.QtGui.QSpinBox.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

![](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/images/windows-spinbox.png)

QSpinBox is designed to handle integers and discrete sets of values (e.g., month names);
use [QDoubleSpinBox](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdoublespinbox.html) for
floating point values.

QSpinBox allows the user to choose a value by clicking the up/down buttons or pressing
up/down on the keyboard to increase/decrease the value currently displayed. The user can
also type the value in manually. The spin box supports integer values but can be
extended to use different strings with
[validate](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qspinbox.html#validate)(),
[textFromValue](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qspinbox.html#textFromValue)() and
[valueFromText](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qspinbox.html#valueFromText)().

Every time the value changes QSpinBox emits
[valueChanged](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qspinbox.html#valueChanged)() and
[textChanged](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qspinbox.html#textChanged)() signals,
the former providing a int and the latter a
[QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html). The
[textChanged](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qspinbox.html#textChanged)() signal
provides the value with both
[prefix](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qspinbox.html#prefix-prop)() and
[suffix](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qspinbox.html#suffix-prop)(). The current
value can be fetched with
[value](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qspinbox.html#value-prop)() and set with
[setValue](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qspinbox.html#value-prop)().

Clicking the up/down buttons or using the keyboard accelerator's up and down arrows will
increase or decrease the current value in steps of size
[singleStep](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qspinbox.html#singleStep-prop)(). If you
want to change this behaviour you can reimplement the virtual function
[stepBy](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractspinbox.html#stepBy)(). The minimum
and maximum value and the step size can be set using one of the constructors, and can be
changed later with
[setMinimum](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qspinbox.html#minimum-prop)(),
[setMaximum](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qspinbox.html#maximum-prop)() and
[setSingleStep](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qspinbox.html#singleStep-prop)().

Most spin boxes are directional, but QSpinBox can also operate as a circular spin box,
i.e. if the range is 0-99 and the current value is 99, clicking "up" will give 0 if
[wrapping](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractspinbox.html#wrapping-prop)() is
set to true. Use
[setWrapping](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractspinbox.html#wrapping-prop)()
if you want circular behavior.

The displayed value can be prepended and appended with arbitrary strings indicating, for
example, currency or the unit of measurement. See
[setPrefix](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qspinbox.html#prefix-prop)() and
[setSuffix](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qspinbox.html#suffix-prop)(). The text in
the spin box is retrieved with
[text](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractspinbox.html#text-prop)() (which
includes any [prefix](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qspinbox.html#prefix-prop)()
and [suffix](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qspinbox.html#suffix-prop)()), or with
[cleanText](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qspinbox.html#cleanText-prop)() (which
has no [prefix](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qspinbox.html#prefix-prop)(), no
[suffix](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qspinbox.html#suffix-prop)() and no leading
or trailing whitespace).

It is often desirable to give the user a special (often default) choice in addition to
the range of numeric values. See
[setSpecialValueText](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractspinbox.html#specialValueText-prop)()
for how to do this with QSpinBox.

### Subclassing QSpinBox

If using [prefix](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qspinbox.html#prefix-prop)(),
[suffix](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qspinbox.html#suffix-prop)(), and
[specialValueText](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractspinbox.html#specialValueText-prop)()
don't provide enough control, you subclass QSpinBox and reimplement
[valueFromText](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qspinbox.html#valueFromText)() and
[textFromValue](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qspinbox.html#textFromValue)(). For
example, here's the code for a custom spin box that allows the user to enter icon sizes
(e.g., "32 x 32"):

```
int IconSizeSpinBox::valueFromText(const QString &text) const
{
    static const QRegularExpression regExp(tr("(\\d+)(\\s*[xx]\\s*\\d+)?"));
    Q_ASSERT(regExp.isValid());

    const QRegularExpressionMatch match = regExp.match(text);
    if (match.isValid())
        return match.captured(1).toInt();
    return 0;
}

QString IconSizeSpinBox::textFromValue(int value) const
{
    return tr("%1 x %1").arg(value);
}
```

See the [Icons](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtwidgets-widgets-icons-example.html)
example for the full source code.

PythonQt.QtGui.QSplitter.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

A splitter lets the user control the size of child widgets by dragging the boundary
between them. Any number of widgets may be controlled by a single splitter. The typical
use of a QSplitter is to create several widgets and add them using
[insertWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsplitter.html#insertWidget)() or
[addWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsplitter.html#addWidget)().

The following example will show a
[QListView](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qlistview.html),
[QTreeView](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtreeview.html), and
[QTextEdit](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextedit.html) side by side, with two
splitter handles:

```
    QSplitter *splitter = new QSplitter(parent);
    QListView *listview = new QListView;
    QTreeView *treeview = new QTreeView;
    QTextEdit *textedit = new QTextEdit;
    splitter->addWidget(listview);
    splitter->addWidget(treeview);
    splitter->addWidget(textedit);
```

If a widget is already inside a QSplitter when
[insertWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsplitter.html#insertWidget)() or
[addWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsplitter.html#addWidget)() is called, it
will move to the new position. This can be used to reorder widgets in the splitter
later. You can use
[indexOf](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsplitter.html#indexOf)(),
[widget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsplitter.html#widget)(), and
[count](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsplitter.html#count)() to get access to the
widgets inside the splitter.

A default QSplitter lays out its children horizontally (side by side); you can use
[setOrientation](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsplitter.html#orientation-prop)([Qt::Vertical](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#Orientation-enum))
to lay its children out vertically.

By default, all widgets can be as large or as small as the user wishes, between the
[minimumSizeHint](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsplitter.html#minimumSizeHint)()
(or [minimumSize](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#minimumSize-prop)())
and [maximumSize](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#maximumSize-prop)() of
the widgets.

QSplitter resizes its children dynamically by default. If you would rather have
QSplitter resize the children only at the end of a resize operation, call
[setOpaqueResize](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsplitter.html#opaqueResize-prop)(false).

The initial distribution of size between the widgets is determined by multiplying the
initial size with the stretch factor. You can also use
[setSizes](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsplitter.html#setSizes)() to set the
sizes of all the widgets. The function
[sizes](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsplitter.html#sizes)() returns the sizes set
by the user. Alternatively, you can save and restore the sizes of the widgets from a
[QByteArray](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qbytearray.html) using
[saveState](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsplitter.html#saveState)() and
[restoreState](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsplitter.html#restoreState)()
respectively.

When you [hide](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#hide)() a child, its
space will be distributed among the other children. It will be reinstated when you
[show](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#show)() it again.

**Note:** Adding a [QLayout](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qlayout.html) to a
QSplitter is not supported (either through
[setLayout](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#setLayout)() or making the
QSplitter a parent of the [QLayout](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qlayout.html));
use [addWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsplitter.html#addWidget)() instead
(see example above).

### bool QSplitter::restoreState(const [QByteArray](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qbytearray.html) \&*state*)

Restores the splitter's layout to the *state* specified. Returns `true` if the state is
restored; otherwise returns `false`.

Typically this is used in conjunction with
[QSettings](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsettings.html) to restore the size from
a past session. Here is an example:

Restore the splitter's state:

```
    QSettings settings;

Qt 5 reference:

### void QSplitter::setSizes(const [QList](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qlist.html)\<int\> \&*list*)

Sets the child widgets' respective sizes to the values given in the *list*.

If the splitter is horizontal, the values set the width of each widget in pixels, from
left to right. If the splitter is vertical, the height of each widget is set, from top
to bottom.

Extra values in the *list* are ignored. If *list* contains too few values, the result is
undefined, but the program will still be well-behaved.

The overall size of the splitter widget is not affected. Instead, any additional/missing
space is distributed amongst the widgets according to the relative weight of the sizes.

If you specify a size of 0, the widget will be invisible. The size policies of the
widgets are preserved. That is, a value smaller than the minimal size hint of the
respective widget will be replaced by the value of the hint.

**See also** [sizes](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsplitter.html#sizes)().

Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

QStackedLayout can be used to create a user interface similar to the one provided by
[QTabWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtabwidget.html). There is also a
convenience [QStackedWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstackedwidget.html)
class built on top of QStackedLayout.

A QStackedLayout can be populated with a number of child widgets ("pages"). For example:

```
    QWidget *firstPageWidget = new QWidget;
    QWidget *secondPageWidget = new QWidget;
    QWidget *thirdPageWidget = new QWidget;

    QStackedLayout *stackedLayout = new QStackedLayout;
    stackedLayout->addWidget(firstPageWidget);
    stackedLayout->addWidget(secondPageWidget);
    stackedLayout->addWidget(thirdPageWidget);

    QVBoxLayout *mainLayout = new QVBoxLayout;
    mainLayout->addLayout(stackedLayout);
    setLayout(mainLayout);
```

QStackedLayout provides no intrinsic means for the user to switch page. This is
typically done through a [QComboBox](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcombobox.html)
or a [QListWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qlistwidget.html) that stores the
titles of the QStackedLayout's pages. For example:

```
    QComboBox *pageComboBox = new QComboBox;
    pageComboBox->addItem(tr("Page 1"));
    pageComboBox->addItem(tr("Page 2"));
    pageComboBox->addItem(tr("Page 3"));
    connect(pageComboBox, QOverload<int>::of(&QComboBox::activated),
            stackedLayout, &QStackedLayout::setCurrentIndex);
```

When populating a layout, the widgets are added to an internal list. The
[indexOf](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qlayout.html#indexOf)() function returns
the index of a widget in that list. The widgets can either be added to the end of the
list using the
[addWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstackedlayout.html#addWidget)()
function, or inserted at a given index using the
[insertWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstackedlayout.html#insertWidget)()
function. The
[removeWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qlayout.html#removeWidget)() function
removes the widget at the given index from the layout. The number of widgets contained
in the layout, can be obtained using the
[count](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstackedlayout.html#count-prop)() function.

The [widget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstackedlayout.html#widget)() function
returns the widget at a given index position. The index of the widget that is shown on
screen is given by
[currentIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstackedlayout.html#currentIndex-prop)()
and can be changed using
[setCurrentIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstackedlayout.html#currentIndex-prop)().
In a similar manner, the currently shown widget can be retrieved using the
[currentWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstackedlayout.html#currentWidget)()
function, and altered using the
[setCurrentWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstackedlayout.html#setCurrentWidget)()
function.

Whenever the current widget in the layout changes or a widget is removed from the
layout, the
[currentChanged](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstackedlayout.html#currentChanged)()
and
[widgetRemoved](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstackedlayout.html#widgetRemoved)()
signals are emitted respectively.

## Detailed Description

QStackedWidget can be used to create a user interface similar to the one provided by
[QTabWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtabwidget.html). It is a convenience
layout widget built on top of the
[QStackedLayout](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstackedlayout.html) class.

Like [QStackedLayout](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstackedlayout.html),
QStackedWidget can be constructed and populated with a number of child widgets
("pages"):

```
    QWidget *firstPageWidget = new QWidget;
    QWidget *secondPageWidget = new QWidget;
    QWidget *thirdPageWidget = new QWidget;

    QStackedWidget *stackedWidget = new QStackedWidget;
    stackedWidget->addWidget(firstPageWidget);
    stackedWidget->addWidget(secondPageWidget);
    stackedWidget->addWidget(thirdPageWidget);

    QVBoxLayout *layout = new QVBoxLayout;
    layout->addWidget(stackedWidget);
    setLayout(layout);
```

QStackedWidget provides no intrinsic means for the user to switch page. This is
typically done through a [QComboBox](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcombobox.html)
or a [QListWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qlistwidget.html) that stores the
titles of the QStackedWidget's pages. For example:

```
    QComboBox *pageComboBox = new QComboBox;
    pageComboBox->addItem(tr("Page 1"));
    pageComboBox->addItem(tr("Page 2"));
    pageComboBox->addItem(tr("Page 3"));
    connect(pageComboBox, QOverload<int>::of(&QComboBox::activated),
            stackedWidget, &QStackedWidget::setCurrentIndex);
```

When populating a stacked widget, the widgets are added to an internal list. The
[indexOf](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstackedwidget.html#indexOf)() function
returns the index of a widget in that list. The widgets can either be added to the end
of the list using the
[addWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstackedwidget.html#addWidget)()
function, or inserted at a given index using the
[insertWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstackedwidget.html#insertWidget)()
function. The
[removeWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstackedwidget.html#removeWidget)()
function removes a widget from the stacked widget. The number of widgets contained in
the stacked widget can be obtained using the
[count](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstackedwidget.html#count-prop)() function.

The [widget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstackedwidget.html#widget)() function
returns the widget at a given index position. The index of the widget that is shown on
screen is given by
[currentIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstackedwidget.html#currentIndex-prop)()
and can be changed using
[setCurrentIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstackedwidget.html#currentIndex-prop)().
In a similar manner, the currently shown widget can be retrieved using the
[currentWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstackedwidget.html#currentWidget)()
function, and altered using the
[setCurrentWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstackedwidget.html#setCurrentWidget)()
function.

Whenever the current widget in the stacked widget changes or a widget is removed from
the stacked widget, the
[currentChanged](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstackedwidget.html#currentChanged)()
and
[widgetRemoved](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstackedwidget.html#widgetRemoved)()
signals are emitted respectively.

## Detailed Description

Items usually contain text, icons, or checkboxes.

Each item can have its own background brush which is set with the
[setBackground](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstandarditem.html#setBackground)()
function. The current background brush can be found with
[background](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstandarditem.html#background)(). The
text label for each item can be rendered with its own font and brush. These are
specified with the
[setFont](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstandarditem.html#setFont)() and
[setForeground](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstandarditem.html#setForeground)()
functions, and read with
[font](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstandarditem.html#font)() and
[foreground](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstandarditem.html#foreground)().

By default, items are enabled, editable, selectable, checkable, and can be used both as
the source of a drag and drop operation and as a drop target. Each item's flags can be
changed by calling
[setFlags](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstandarditem.html#setFlags)(). Checkable
items can be checked and unchecked with the
[setCheckState](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstandarditem.html#setCheckState)()
function. The corresponding
[checkState](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstandarditem.html#checkState)()
function indicates whether the item is currently checked.

You can store application-specific data in an item by calling
[setData](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstandarditem.html#setData)().

Each item can have a two-dimensional table of child items. This makes it possible to
build hierarchies of items. The typical hierarchy is the tree, in which case the child
table is a table with a single column (a list).

The dimensions of the child table can be set with
[setRowCount](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstandarditem.html#setRowCount)() and
[setColumnCount](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstandarditem.html#setColumnCount)().
Items can be positioned in the child table with
[setChild](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstandarditem.html#setChild)(). Get a
pointer to a child item with
[child](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstandarditem.html#child)(). New rows and
columns of children can also be inserted with
[insertRow](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstandarditem.html#insertRow)() and
[insertColumn](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstandarditem.html#insertColumn)(), or
appended with
[appendRow](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstandarditem.html#appendRow)() and
[appendColumn](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstandarditem.html#appendColumn)().
When using the append and insert functions, the dimensions of the child table will grow
as needed.

An existing row of children can be removed with
[removeRow](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstandarditem.html#removeRow)() or
[takeRow](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstandarditem.html#takeRow)();
correspondingly, a column can be removed with
[removeColumn](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstandarditem.html#removeColumn)() or
[takeColumn](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstandarditem.html#takeColumn)().

An item's children can be sorted by calling
[sortChildren](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstandarditem.html#sortChildren)().

### Subclassing

When subclassing QStandardItem to provide custom items, it is possible to define new
types for them so that they can be distinguished from the base class. The
[type](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstandarditem.html#type)() function should be
reimplemented to return a new type value equal to or greater than
[UserType](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstandarditem.html#ItemType-enum).

Reimplement [data](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstandarditem.html#data)() and
[setData](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstandarditem.html#setData)() if you want
to perform custom handling of data queries and/or control how an item's data is
represented.

Reimplement [clone](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstandarditem.html#clone)() if
you want
[QStandardItemModel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstandarditemmodel.html) to be
able to create instances of your custom item class on demand (see
[QStandardItemModel::setItemPrototype](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstandarditemmodel.html#setItemPrototype)()).

Reimplement [read](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstandarditem.html#read)() and
[write](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstandarditem.html#write)() if you want to
control how items are represented in their serialized form.

Reimplement
[operator\<](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstandarditem.html#operator-lt)() if you
want to control the semantics of item comparison.
[operator\<](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstandarditem.html#operator-lt)()
determines the sorted order when sorting items with
[sortChildren](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstandarditem.html#sortChildren)() or
with
[QStandardItemModel::sort](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstandarditemmodel.html#sort)().

### `[virtual]` void QStandardItem::setData(const [QVariant](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qvariant.html) \&*value*, int *role* \= Qt::UserRole \+ 1\)

Sets the item's data for the given *role* to the specified *value*.

If you subclass [QStandardItem](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstandarditem.html)
and reimplement this function, your reimplementation should:

- call [emitDataChanged](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstandarditem.html#emitDataChanged)() if you do not call the base implementation of setData(). This will ensure that e.g. views using the model are notified of the changes
- call the base implementation for roles you don't handle, otherwise setting flags, e.g. by calling [setFlags](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstandarditem.html#setFlags)(), [setCheckable](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstandarditem.html#setCheckable)(), [setEditable](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstandarditem.html#setEditable)() etc., will not work.

**Note:** The default implementation treats
[Qt::EditRole](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#ItemDataRole-enum) and
[Qt::DisplayRole](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#ItemDataRole-enum) as
referring to the same data.

**See also**
[Qt::ItemDataRole](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#ItemDataRole-enum),
[data](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstandarditem.html#data)(), and
[setFlags](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstandarditem.html#setFlags)().

### void QStandardItem::setEnabled(bool *enabled*)

Sets whether the item is enabled. If *enabled* is true, the item is enabled, meaning
that the user can interact with the item; if *enabled* is false, the user cannot
interact with the item.

This flag takes precedence over the other item flags; e.g. if an item is not enabled, it
cannot be selected by the user, even if the
[Qt::ItemIsSelectable](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#ItemFlag-enum) flag
has been set.

**See also**
[isEnabled](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstandarditem.html#isEnabled)(),
[Qt::ItemIsEnabled](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#ItemFlag-enum), and

PythonQt.QtGui.QStandardItemModel.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

QStandardItemModel can be used as a repository for standard Qt data types. It is one of
the [Model/View
Classes](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/model-view-programming.html#model-view-classes)
and is part of Qt's
[model/view](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/model-view-programming.html) framework.

QStandardItemModel provides a classic item-based approach to working with the model. The
items in a QStandardItemModel are provided by
[QStandardItem](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstandarditem.html).

QStandardItemModel implements the
[QAbstractItemModel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html)
interface, which means that the model can be used to provide data in any view that
supports that interface (such as
[QListView](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qlistview.html),
[QTableView](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtableview.html) and
[QTreeView](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtreeview.html), and your own custom
views). For performance and flexibility, you may want to subclass
[QAbstractItemModel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html) to
provide support for different kinds of data repositories. For example, the QDirModel
provides a model interface to the underlying file system.

When you want a list or tree, you typically create an empty QStandardItemModel and use
[appendRow](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstandarditemmodel.html#appendRow)() to
add items to the model, and
[item](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstandarditemmodel.html#item)() to access an
item. If your model represents a table, you typically pass the dimensions of the table
to the QStandardItemModel constructor and use
[setItem](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstandarditemmodel.html#setItem)() to
position items into the table. You can also use
[setRowCount](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstandarditemmodel.html#setRowCount)()
and
[setColumnCount](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstandarditemmodel.html#setColumnCount)()
to alter the dimensions of the model. To insert items, use
[insertRow](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstandarditemmodel.html#insertRow)() or
[insertColumn](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstandarditemmodel.html#insertColumn)(),
and to remove items, use
[removeRow](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#removeRow)() or
[removeColumn](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html#removeColumn)().

You can set the header labels of your model with
[setHorizontalHeaderLabels](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstandarditemmodel.html#setHorizontalHeaderLabels)()
and
[setVerticalHeaderLabels](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstandarditemmodel.html#setVerticalHeaderLabels)().

You can search for items in the model with
[findItems](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstandarditemmodel.html#findItems)(), and
sort the model by calling
[sort](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstandarditemmodel.html#sort)().

Call [clear](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstandarditemmodel.html#clear)() to
remove all items from the model.

An example usage of QStandardItemModel to create a table:

```
QStandardItemModel model(4, 4);
for (int row = 0; row < model.rowCount(); ++row) {
    for (int column = 0; column < model.columnCount(); ++column) {
        QStandardItem *item = new QStandardItem(QString("row %0, column %1").arg(row).arg(column));
        model.setItem(row, column, item);
    }
}
```

An example usage of QStandardItemModel to create a tree:

```
QStandardItemModel model;
QStandardItem *parentItem = model.invisibleRootItem();
for (int i = 0; i < 4; ++i) {
    QStandardItem *item = new QStandardItem(QString("item %0").arg(i));
    parentItem->appendRow(item);
    parentItem = item;
}
```

After setting the model on a view, you typically want to react to user actions, such as
an item being clicked. Since a
[QAbstractItemView](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemview.html) provides
[QModelIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmodelindex.html)-based signals and
functions, you need a way to obtain the
[QStandardItem](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstandarditem.html) that corresponds
to a given [QModelIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmodelindex.html), and vice
versa.
[itemFromIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstandarditemmodel.html#itemFromIndex)()
and
[indexFromItem](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstandarditemmodel.html#indexFromItem)()
provide this mapping. Typical usage of
[itemFromIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstandarditemmodel.html#itemFromIndex)()
includes obtaining the item at the current index in a view, and obtaining the item that
corresponds to an index carried by a
[QAbstractItemView](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemview.html) signal,
such as
[QAbstractItemView::clicked](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemview.html#clicked)().
First you connect the view's signal to a slot in your class:

```
QTreeView *treeView = new QTreeView(this);
treeView->setModel(myStandardItemModel);
connect(treeView, &QTreeView::clicked,
        this, &MyWidget::clicked);
```

When you receive the signal, you call
[itemFromIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstandarditemmodel.html#itemFromIndex)()
on the given model index to get a pointer to the item:

```
void MyWidget::clicked(const QModelIndex &index)
{
    QStandardItem *item = myStandardItemModel->itemFromIndex(index);
    // Do stuff with the item ...
}
```

Conversely, you must obtain the
[QModelIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmodelindex.html) of an item when you
want to invoke a model/view function that takes an index as argument. You can obtain the
index either by using the model's
[indexFromItem](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstandarditemmodel.html#indexFromItem)()
function, or, equivalently, by calling
[QStandardItem::index](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstandarditem.html#index)():

```
treeView->scrollTo(item->index());
```

You are, of course, not required to use the item-based approach; you could instead rely
entirely on the
[QAbstractItemModel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractitemmodel.html)
interface when working with the model, or use a combination of the two as appropriate.

[QModelIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmodelindex.html) carried by the signal
as argument, to obtain a pointer to the corresponding
[QStandardItem](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstandarditem.html).

[itemPrototype](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstandarditemmodel.html#itemPrototype)()),

[QStandardItemModel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstandarditemmodel.html) needs
to create an item on demand (for instance, when a view or item delegate calls
[setData](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstandarditemmodel.html#setData)())), the
new items will be instances of your custom class.

This function was introduced in Qt 4.2.

PythonQt.QtGui.QStaticText.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

QStaticText provides a way to cache layout data for a block of text so that it can be
drawn more efficiently than by using
[QPainter::drawText](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpainter.html#drawText)() in
which the layout information is recalculated with every call.

The class primarily provides an optimization for cases where the text, its font and the
transformations on the painter are static over several paint events. If the text or its
layout is changed for every iteration,
[QPainter::drawText](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpainter.html#drawText)() is the
more efficient alternative, since the static text's layout would have to be recalculated
to take the new state into consideration.

Translating the painter will not cause the layout of the text to be recalculated, but
will cause a very small performance impact on drawStaticText(). Altering any other parts
of the painter's transformation or the painter's font will cause the layout of the
static text to be recalculated. This should be avoided as often as possible to maximize
the performance benefit of using QStaticText.

In addition, only affine transformations are supported by drawStaticText(). Calling
drawStaticText() on a projected painter will perform slightly worse than using the
regular drawText() call, so this should be avoided.

```
class MyWidget: public QWidget
{
public:
    MyWidget(QWidget *parent = 0) : QWidget(parent), m_staticText("This is static text")

protected:
    void paintEvent(QPaintEvent *)
    {
        QPainter painter(this);
        painter.drawStaticText(0, 0, m_staticText);
    }

private:
    QStaticText m_staticText;
};
```

The QStaticText class can be used to mimic the behavior of
[QPainter::drawText](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpainter.html#drawText)() to a
specific point with no boundaries, and also when
[QPainter::drawText](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpainter.html#drawText)() is
called with a bounding rectangle.

If a bounding rectangle is not required, create a QStaticText object without setting a
preferred text width. The text will then occupy a single line.

If you set a text width on the QStaticText object, this will bound the text. The text
will be formatted so that no line exceeds the given width. The text width set for
QStaticText will not automatically be used for clipping. To achieve clipping in addition
to line breaks, use
[QPainter::setClipRect](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpainter.html#setClipRect)().
The position of the text is decided by the argument passed to
[QPainter::drawStaticText](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpainter.html#drawStaticText)()
and can change from call to call with a minimal impact on performance.

For extra convenience, it is possible to apply formatting to the text using the HTML
subset supported by
[QTextDocument](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextdocument.html). QStaticText will
attempt to guess the format of the input text using
[Qt::mightBeRichText](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt-sub-qtgui.html#mightBeRichText)(),
and interpret it as rich text if this function returns `true`. To force QStaticText to
display its contents as either plain text or rich text, use the function
[QStaticText::setTextFormat](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstatictext.html#setTextFormat)()
and pass in, respectively,
[Qt::PlainText](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#TextFormat-enum) and
[Qt::RichText](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#TextFormat-enum).

QStaticText can only represent text, so only HTML tags which alter the layout or
appearance of the text will be respected. Adding an image to the input HTML, for
instance, will cause the image to be included as part of the layout, affecting the
positions of the text glyphs, but it will not be displayed. The result will be an empty
area the size of the image in the output. Similarly, using tables will cause the text to
be laid out in table format, but the borders will not be drawn.

If it's the first time the static text is drawn, or if the static text, or the painter's
font has been altered since the last time it was drawn, the text's layout has to be
recalculated. On some paint engines, changing the matrix of the painter will also cause
the layout to be recalculated. In particular, this will happen for any engine except for
the OpenGL2 paint engine. Recalculating the layout will impose an overhead on the
[QPainter::drawStaticText](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpainter.html#drawStaticText)()
call where it occurs. To avoid this overhead in the paint event, you can call
[prepare](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstatictext.html#prepare)() ahead of time
to ensure that the layout is calculated.

### void QStaticText::prepare(const [QTransform](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtransform.html) \&*matrix* \= QTransform(), const [QFont](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfont.html) \&*font* \= QFont())

Prepares the [QStaticText](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstatictext.html) object
for being painted with the given *matrix* and the given *font* to avoid overhead when
the actual drawStaticText() call is made.

When drawStaticText() is called, the layout of the
[QStaticText](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstatictext.html) will be recalculated
if any part of the [QStaticText](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstatictext.html)
object has changed since the last time it was drawn. It will also be recalculated if the
painter's font is not the same as when the
[QStaticText](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstatictext.html) was last drawn, or,
on any other paint engine than the OpenGL2 engine, if the painter's matrix has been
altered since the static text was last drawn.

To avoid the overhead of creating the layout the first time you draw the
[QStaticText](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstatictext.html) after making changes,
you can use the prepare() function and pass in the *matrix* and *font* you expect to use
when drawing the text.

**See also**
[QPainter::setFont](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpainter.html#setFont)() and
[QPainter::setMatrix](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpainter-obsolete.html#setMatrix)().

[QStaticText](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstatictext.html).

Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

Each status indicator falls into one of three categories:

- *Temporary* \- briefly occupies most of the status bar. Used to explain tool tip texts or menu entries, for example.
- *Normal* \- occupies part of the status bar and may be hidden by temporary messages. Used to display the page and line number in a word processor, for example.
- *Permanent* \- is never hidden. Used for important mode indications, for example, some applications put a Caps Lock indicator in the status bar.

QStatusBar lets you display all three types of indicators.

Typically, a request for the status bar functionality occurs in relation to a
[QMainWindow](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmainwindow.html) object.
[QMainWindow](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmainwindow.html) provides a main
application window, with a menu bar, tool bars, dock widgets *and* a status bar around a
large central widget. The status bar can be retrieved using the
[QMainWindow::statusBar](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmainwindow.html#statusBar)()
function, and replaced using the
[QMainWindow::setStatusBar](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmainwindow.html#setStatusBar)()
function.

Use the [showMessage](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstatusbar.html#showMessage)()
slot to display a *temporary* message:

```
void MainWindow::createStatusBar()
{
    statusBar()->showMessage(tr("Ready"));
}
```

To remove a temporary message, use the
[clearMessage](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstatusbar.html#clearMessage)() slot,
or set a time limit when calling
[showMessage](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstatusbar.html#showMessage)(). For
example:

```
void MainWindow::print()
{
#if defined(QT_PRINTSUPPORT_LIB) && QT_CONFIG(printdialog)
    QTextDocument *document = textEdit->document();
    QPrinter printer;

    QPrintDialog dlg(&printer, this);
    if (dlg.exec() != QDialog::Accepted) {
        return;
    }

    document->print(&printer);
    statusBar()->showMessage(tr("Ready"), 2000);
#endif
}
```

Use the
[currentMessage](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstatusbar.html#currentMessage)()
function to retrieve the temporary message currently shown. The QStatusBar class also
provide the
[messageChanged](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstatusbar.html#messageChanged)()
signal which is emitted whenever the temporary status message changes.

*Normal* and *Permanent* messages are displayed by creating a small widget
([QLabel](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qlabel.html),
[QProgressBar](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qprogressbar.html) or even
[QToolButton](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtoolbutton.html)) and then adding it
to the status bar using the
[addWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstatusbar.html#addWidget)() or the
[addPermanentWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstatusbar.html#addPermanentWidget)()
function. Use the
[removeWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstatusbar.html#removeWidget)()
function to remove such messages from the status bar.

```
statusBar()->addWidget(new MyReadWriteIndication);
```

By default QStatusBar provides a
[QSizeGrip](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsizegrip.html) in the lower-right
corner. You can disable it using the
[setSizeGripEnabled](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstatusbar.html#sizeGripEnabled-prop)()
function. Use the
[isSizeGripEnabled](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstatusbar.html#sizeGripEnabled-prop)()
function to determine the current status of the size grip.

![A status bar shown in the Fusion widget
style](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/images/fusion-statusbar-sizegrip.png)

### void QStatusBar::addPermanentWidget([QWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#QWidget) \**widget*, int *stretch* \= 0\)

Adds the given *widget* permanently to this status bar, reparenting the widget if it
isn't already a child of this
[QStatusBar](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstatusbar.html) object. The *stretch*
parameter is used to compute a suitable size for the given *widget* as the status bar
grows and shrinks. The default stretch factor is 0, i.e giving the widget a minimum of
space.

Permanently means that the widget may not be obscured by temporary messages. It is is
located at the far right of the status bar.

[removeWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstatusbar.html#removeWidget)(), and

### void QStatusBar::addWidget([QWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#QWidget) \**widget*, int *stretch* \= 0\)

Adds the given *widget* to this status bar, reparenting the widget if it isn't already a

## Detailed Description

Status tips can be set on a widget using the
[QWidget::setStatusTip](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#statusTip-prop)()
function. They are shown in the status bar when the mouse cursor enters the widget. For
example:

| ``` MainWindow::MainWindow(QWidget *parent)     : QMainWindow(parent) {     QWidget *myWidget = new QWidget;     myWidget->setStatusTip(tr("This is my widget."));      setCentralWidget(myWidget);     ... } ``` | Widget with status tip. |
| --- | --- |

Status tips can also be set on actions using the
[QAction::setStatusTip](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qaction.html#statusTip-prop)()
function:

| ``` MainWindow::MainWindow(QWidget *parent)     : QMainWindow(parent) {     QMenu *fileMenu = menuBar()->addMenu(tr("File"));      QAction *newAct = new QAction(tr("&New"), this);     newAct->setStatusTip(tr("Create a new file."));     fileMenu->addAction(newAct);     ... } ``` | Action with status tip. |
| --- | --- |

Finally, status tips are supported for the item view classes through the
[Qt::StatusTipRole](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#ItemDataRole-enum) enum
value.

PythonQt.QtGui.QStringListModel.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

QStringListModel is an editable model that can be used for simple cases where you need
to display a number of strings in a view widget, such as a
[QListView](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qlistview.html) or a
[QComboBox](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcombobox.html).

The model provides all the standard functions of an editable model, representing the
data in the string list as a model with one column and a number of rows equal to the
number of items in the list.

Model indexes corresponding to items are obtained with the
[index()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractlistmodel.html#index) function,
and item flags are obtained with
[flags](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstringlistmodel.html#flags)(). Item data is
read with the [data](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstringlistmodel.html#data)()
function and written with
[setData](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstringlistmodel.html#setData)(). The
number of rows (and number of items in the string list) can be found with the
[rowCount](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstringlistmodel.html#rowCount)()
function.

The model can be constructed with an existing string list, or strings can be set later
with the
[setStringList](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstringlistmodel.html#setStringList)()
convenience function. Strings can also be inserted in the usual way with the
[insertRows](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstringlistmodel.html#insertRows)()
function, and removed with
[removeRows](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstringlistmodel.html#removeRows)(). The
contents of the string list can be retrieved with the
[stringList](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstringlistmodel.html#stringList)()
convenience function.

An example usage of QStringListModel:

```
    QStringListModel *model = new QStringListModel();
    QStringList list;
    list << "a" << "b" << "c";
    model->setStringList(list);
```
