### [QWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#QWidget) \*QWidget::window() const

Returns the window for this widget, i.e. the next ancestor widget that has (or could
have) a window-system frame.

If the widget is a window, the widget itself is returned.

Typical usage is changing the window title:

```
aWidget->window()->setWindowTitle("New Window Title");
```

**See also** [isWindow](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#isWindow)().

PythonQt.QtGui.QWidget.windowFilePath.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

### windowFilePath : [QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html)

This property holds the file path associated with a widget

This property only makes sense for windows. It associates a file path with a window. If
you set the file path, but have not set the window title, Qt sets the window title to
the file name of the specified path, obtained using
[QFileInfo::fileName](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qfileinfo.html#fileName)().

If the window title is set at any point, then the window title takes precedence and will
be shown instead of the file path string.

Additionally, on macOS, this has an added benefit that it sets the [proxy
icon](http://developer.apple.com/documentation/UserExperience/Conceptual/OSXHIGuidelines/XHIGWindows/chapter_17_section_3.html)
for the window, assuming that the file path exists.

If no file path is set, this property contains an empty string.

By default, this property contains an empty string.

This property was introduced in Qt 4.4.

**Access functions:**

| QString | **windowFilePath**() const |
| --- | --- |
| void | **setWindowFilePath**(const QString \&*filePath*) |

**See also**
[windowTitle](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#windowTitle-prop) and
[windowIcon](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#windowIcon-prop).

### windowFlags : [Qt::WindowFlags](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#WindowType-enum)

Window flags are a combination of a type (e.g.
[Qt::Dialog](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#WindowType-enum)) and zero or
more hints to the window system (e.g.
[Qt::FramelessWindowHint](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#WindowType-enum)).

If the widget had type
[Qt::Widget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#WindowType-enum) or
[Qt::SubWindow](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#WindowType-enum) and becomes
a window ([Qt::Window](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#WindowType-enum),
[Qt::Dialog](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#WindowType-enum), etc.), it is
put at position (0, 0\) on the desktop. If the widget is a window and becomes a
[Qt::Widget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#WindowType-enum) or
[Qt::SubWindow](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#WindowType-enum), it is put
at position (0, 0\) relative to its parent widget.

**Note:** This function calls
[setParent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#setParent)() when changing
the flags for a window, causing the widget to be hidden. You must call
[show](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#show)() to make the widget
visible again..

### windowModified : bool

This property holds whether the document shown in the window has unsaved changes

A modified window is a window whose content has changed but has not been saved to disk.
This flag will have different effects varied by the platform. On macOS the close button
will have a modified look; on other platforms, the window title will have an '\*'
(asterisk).

The window title must contain a "\[\*\]" placeholder, which indicates where the '\*'
should appear. Normally, it should appear right after the file name (e.g.,
"document1.txt\[\*\] \- Text Editor"). If the window isn't modified, the placeholder is
simply removed.

Note that if a widget is set as modified, all its ancestors will also be set as
modified. However, if you call `setWindowModified(false)` on a widget, this will not
propagate to its parent because other children of the parent might have been modified.

### windowOpacity : double

This property holds the level of opacity for the window.

The valid range of opacity is from 1.0 (completely opaque) to 0.0 (completely
transparent).

By default the value of this property is 1.0.

This feature is available on Embedded Linux, macOS, Windows, and X11 platforms that
support the Composite extension.

**Note:** On X11 you need to have a composite manager running, and the X11 specific
\_NET\_WM\_WINDOW\_OPACITY atom needs to be supported by the window manager you are
using.

**Warning:** Changing this property from opaque to transparent might issue a paint event
that needs to be processed before the window is displayed correctly. This affects mainly
the use of
[QScreen::grabWindow](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qscreen.html#grabWindow)().
Also note that semi-transparent windows update and resize significantly slower than
opaque windows.

### windowTitle : [QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html)

This property holds the window title (caption)

[windowFilePath](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#windowFilePath-prop).

[QGuiApplication::applicationDisplayName](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qguiapplication.html#applicationDisplayName-prop))
is added at the end of the window title, if set. This is done by the QPA plugin, so it

PythonQt.QtGui.QWidgetAction.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

Most actions in an application are represented as items in menus or buttons in toolbars.
However sometimes more complex widgets are necessary. For example a zoom action in a
word processor may be realized using a
[QComboBox](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcombobox.html) in a
[QToolBar](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtoolbar.html), presenting a range of
different zoom levels. [QToolBar](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtoolbar.html)
provides
[QToolBar::insertWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtoolbar.html#insertWidget)()
as convenience function for inserting a single widget. However if you want to implement
an action that uses custom widgets for visualization in multiple containers then you
have to subclass QWidgetAction.

If a QWidgetAction is added for example to a
[QToolBar](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtoolbar.html) then
[QWidgetAction::createWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidgetaction.html#createWidget)()
is called. Reimplementations of that function should create a new custom widget with the
specified parent.

If the action is removed from a container widget then
[QWidgetAction::deleteWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidgetaction.html#deleteWidget)()
is called with the previously created custom widget as argument. The default
implementation hides the widget and deletes it using
[QObject::deleteLater](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qobject.html#deleteLater)().

If you have only one single custom widget then you can set it as default widget using
[setDefaultWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidgetaction.html#setDefaultWidget)().
That widget will then be used if the action is added to a
[QToolBar](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtoolbar.html), or in general to an action
container that supports QWidgetAction. If a QWidgetAction with only a default widget is
added to two toolbars at the same time then the default widget is shown only in the
first toolbar the action was added to. QWidgetAction takes over ownership of the default
widget.

Note that it is up to the widget to activate the action, for example by reimplementing
mouse event handlers and calling
[QAction::trigger](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qaction.html#trigger)().

**macOS**: If you add a widget to a menu in the application's menu bar on macOS, the
widget will be added and it will function but with some limitations:

1. The widget is reparented away from the [QMenu](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qmenu.html) to the native menu view. If you show the menu in some other place (e.g. as a popup menu), the widget will not be there.
2. Focus/Keyboard handling of the widget is not possible.
3. Due to Apple's design, mouse tracking on the widget currently does not work.
4. Connecting the [triggered](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qaction.html#triggered)() signal to a slot that opens a modal dialog will cause a crash in macOS 10.4 (known bug acknowledged by Apple), a workaround is to use a QueuedConnection instead of a DirectConnection.

PythonQt.QtGui.QWindow.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

A window that is supplied a parent becomes a native child window of their parent window.

An application will typically use
[QWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html) or
[QQuickView](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qquickview.html) for its UI, and not
QWindow directly. Still, it is possible to render directly to a QWindow with
[QBackingStore](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qbackingstore.html) or
[QOpenGLContext](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglcontext.html), when wanting
to keep dependencies to a minimum or when wanting to use OpenGL directly. The [Raster
Window Example](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtgui-rasterwindow-example.html) and
[OpenGL Window
Example](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtgui-openglwindow-example.html) are useful
reference examples for how to render to a QWindow using either approach.

### Resource Management

Windows can potentially use a lot of memory. A usual measurement is width times height
times color depth. A window might also include multiple buffers to support double and
triple buffering, as well as depth and stencil buffers. To release a window's memory
resources, call the [destroy](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwindow.html#destroy)()
function.

### Content Orientation

QWindow has
[reportContentOrientationChange](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwindow.html#contentOrientation-prop)()
that can be used to specify the layout of the window contents in relation to the screen.
The content orientation is simply a hint to the windowing system about which orientation
the window contents are in. It's useful when you wish to keep the same window size, but
rotate the contents instead, especially when doing rotation animations between different
orientations. The windowing system might use this value to determine the layout of
system popups or dialogs.

### Visibility and Windowing System Exposure

By default, the window is not visible, and you must call
[setVisible](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwindow.html#visible-prop)(true), or
[show](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwindow.html#show)() or similar to make it
visible. To make a window hidden again, call
[setVisible](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwindow.html#visible-prop)(false) or
[hide](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwindow.html#hide)(). The visible property
describes the state the application wants the window to be in. Depending on the
underlying system, a visible window might still not be shown on the screen. It could,
for instance, be covered by other opaque windows or moved outside the physical area of
the screen. On windowing systems that have exposure notifications, the
[isExposed](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwindow.html#isExposed)() accessor
describes whether the window should be treated as directly visible on screen. The
[exposeEvent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwindow.html#exposeEvent)() function is
called whenever an area of the window is invalidated, for example due to the exposure in
the windowing system changing. On windowing systems that do not make this information
visible to the application,
[isExposed](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwindow.html#isExposed)() will simply
return the same value as
[isVisible](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwindow.html#visible-prop)().

[QWindow::Visibility](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwindow.html#Visibility-enum)
queried through
[visibility](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwindow.html#visibility-prop)() is a
convenience API combining the functions of visible() and
[windowStates](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwindow.html#windowStates)().

### Rendering

There are two Qt APIs that can be used to render content into a window,
[QBackingStore](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qbackingstore.html) for rendering
with a [QPainter](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpainter.html) and flushing the
contents to a window with type
[QSurface::RasterSurface](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsurface.html#SurfaceType-enum),
and [QOpenGLContext](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglcontext.html) for
rendering with OpenGL to a window with type
[QSurface::OpenGLSurface](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsurface.html#SurfaceType-enum).

The application can start rendering as soon as
[isExposed](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwindow.html#isExposed)() returns `true`,
and can keep rendering until it
[isExposed](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwindow.html#isExposed)() returns
`false`. To find out when
[isExposed](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwindow.html#isExposed)() changes,
reimplement
[exposeEvent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwindow.html#exposeEvent)(). The window
will always get a resize event before the first expose event.

### Initial Geometry

If the window's width and height are left uninitialized, the window will get a
reasonable default geometry from the platform window. If the position is left
uninitialized, then the platform window will allow the windowing system to position the
window. For example on X11, the window manager usually does some kind of smart
positioning to try to avoid having new windows completely obscure existing windows.
However [setGeometry](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwindow.html#setGeometry)()
initializes both the position and the size, so if you want a fixed size but an automatic
position, you should call
[resize](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwindow.html#resize)() or
[setWidth](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwindow.html#width-prop)() and
[setHeight](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwindow.html#height-prop)() instead.

### `[slot]` void QWindow::alert(int *msec*)

Causes an alert to be shown for *msec* miliseconds. If *msec* is `0` (the default), then
the alert is shown indefinitely until the window becomes active again. This function has
no effect on an active window.

In alert state, the window indicates that it demands attention, for example by flashing
or bouncing the taskbar entry.

This function was introduced in Qt 5.1.

### contentOrientation : [Qt::ScreenOrientation](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#ScreenOrientation-enum)

This property holds the orientation of the window's contents

This is a hint to the window manager in case it needs to display additional content like
popups, dialogs, status bars, or similar in relation to the window.

The recommended orientation is
[QScreen::orientation](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qscreen.html#orientation-prop)()
but an application doesn't have to support all possible orientations, and thus can opt
to ignore the current screen orientation.

The difference between the window and the content orientation determines how much to
rotate the content by.
[QScreen::angleBetween](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qscreen.html#angleBetween)(),
[QScreen::transformBetween](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qscreen.html#transformBetween)(),
and [QScreen::mapBetween](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qscreen.html#mapBetween)()
can be used to compute the necessary transform.

The default value is
[Qt::PrimaryOrientation](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#ScreenOrientation-enum)

| --- | --- |

| --- | --- |

### void QWindow::create()

Allocates the platform resources associated with the window.

It is at this point that the surface format set using
[setFormat](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwindow.html#setFormat)() gets resolved
into an actual native surface. However, the window remains hidden until
[setVisible](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwindow.html#visible-prop)() is called.

Note that it is not usually necessary to call this function directly, as it will be
implicitly called by [show](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwindow.html#show)(),
[setVisible](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwindow.html#visible-prop)(), and other
functions that require access to the platform resources.

Call [destroy](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwindow.html#destroy)() to free the
platform resources if necessary.

**See also** [destroy](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwindow.html#destroy)().

PythonQt.QtGui.QWindow.exposeEvent.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

### `[virtual protected]` void QWindow::exposeEvent([QExposeEvent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qexposeevent.html) \**ev*)

The expose event (*ev*) is sent by the window system whenever an area of the window is
invalidated, for example due to the exposure in the windowing system changing.

The application can start rendering into the window with
[QBackingStore](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qbackingstore.html) and
[QOpenGLContext](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglcontext.html) as soon as it
gets an exposeEvent() such that
[isExposed](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwindow.html#isExposed)() is true.

If the window is moved off screen, is made totally obscured by another window, iconified
or similar, this function might be called and the value of
[isExposed](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwindow.html#isExposed)() might change to
false. When this happens, an application should stop its rendering as it is no longer
visible to the user.

A resize event will always be sent before the expose event the first time a window is
shown.

**See also** [isExposed](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwindow.html#isExposed)().

Qt 5 reference:

### `[override virtual]` [QSurfaceFormat](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsurfaceformat.html) QWindow::format() const

Reimplements:
[QSurface::format](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsurface.html#format)() const.

Returns the actual format of this window.

After the window has been created, this function will return the actual surface format
of the window. It might differ from the requested format if the requested format could
not be fulfilled by the platform. It might also be a superset, for example certain
buffer sizes may be larger than requested.

**Note:** Depending on the platform, certain values in this surface format may still
contain the requested values, that is, the values that have been passed to
[setFormat](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwindow.html#setFormat)(). Typical
examples are the OpenGL version, profile and options. These may not get updated during
[create](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwindow.html#create)() since these are
context specific and a single window may be used together with multiple contexts over
its lifetime. Use the
[QOpenGLContext](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qopenglcontext.html)'s format()
instead to query such values.

**See also** [setFormat](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwindow.html#setFormat)(),
[create](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwindow.html#create)(),
[requestedFormat](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwindow.html#requestedFormat)(),
and

### `[static]` [QWindow](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwindow.html#QWindow) \*QWindow::fromWinId(WId *id*)

Creates a local representation of a window created by another process or by using native
libraries below Qt.

Given the handle *id* to a native window, this method creates a
[QWindow](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwindow.html) object which can be used to
represent the window when invoking methods like
[setParent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwindow.html#setParent)() and
setTransientParent().

This can be used, on platforms which support it, to embed a
[QWindow](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwindow.html) inside a native window, or to
embed a native window inside a
[QWindow](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwindow.html).

If foreign windows are not supported or embedding the native window failed in the
platform plugin, this function returns `nullptr`.

**Note:** The resulting [QWindow](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwindow.html)
should not be used to manipulate the underlying native window (besides re-parenting), or
to observe state changes of the native window. Any support for these kind of operations
is incidental, highly platform dependent and untested.

**See also** [setParent](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwindow.html#setParent)().

### bool QWindow::isActive() const

Returns `true` if the window is active.

This is the case for the window that has input focus as well as windows that are in the
same parent / transient parent chain as the focus window.

Typically active windows should appear active from a style perspective.

To get the window that currently has focus, use
[QGuiApplication::focusWindow](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qguiapplication.html#focusWindow)().

### opacity : [qreal](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtglobal.html#qreal-typedef)

This property holds the opacity of the window in the windowing system.

If the windowing system supports window opacity, this can be used to fade the window in
and out, or to make it semitransparent.

A value of 1.0 or above is treated as fully opaque, whereas a value of 0.0 or below is
treated as fully transparent. Values inbetween represent varying levels of translucency
between the two extremes.

The default value is 1.0.

This property was introduced in Qt 5.1.

PythonQt.QtGui.QWindow.requestUpdate.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

### `[slot]` void QWindow::requestUpdate()

Schedules a
[QEvent::UpdateRequest](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qevent.html#Type-enum) event
to be delivered to this window.

The event is delivered in sync with the display vsync on platforms where this is
possible. Otherwise, the event is delivered after a delay of 5 ms. The additional time
is there to give the event loop a bit of idle time to gather system events, and can be
overridden using the QT\_QPA\_UPDATE\_IDLE\_TIME environment variable.

When driving animations, this function should be called once after drawing has
completed. Calling this function multiple times will result in a single event being
delivered to the window.

Subclasses of [QWindow](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwindow.html) should
reimplement [event](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwindow.html#event)(), intercept
the event and call the application's rendering code, then call the base class
implementation.

**Note:** The subclass' reimplementation of
[event](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwindow.html#event)() must invoke the base
class implementation, unless it is absolutely sure that the event does not need to be
handled by the base class. For example, the default implementation of this function
relies on [QEvent::Timer](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qevent.html#Type-enum)
events. Filtering them away would therefore break the delivery of the update events.

This function was introduced in Qt 5.5.

### void QWindow::setFormat(const [QSurfaceFormat](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsurfaceformat.html) \&*format*)

Sets the window's surface *format*.

The format determines properties such as color depth, alpha, depth and stencil buffer
size, etc. For example, to give a window a transparent background (provided that the
window system supports compositing, and provided that other content in the window does
not make it opaque again):

```
QSurfaceFormat format;
format.setAlphaBufferSize(8);
window.setFormat(format);
```

The surface format will be resolved in the
[create](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwindow.html#create)() function. Calling
this function after [create](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwindow.html#create)()
has been called will not re-resolve the surface format of the native surface.

When the format is not explicitly set via this function, the format returned by
[QSurfaceFormat::defaultFormat](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsurfaceformat.html#defaultFormat)()
will be used. This means that when having multiple windows, individual calls to this
function can be replaced by one single call to
[QSurfaceFormat::setDefaultFormat](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsurfaceformat.html#setDefaultFormat)()
before creating the first window.

**See also** [format](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwindow.html#format)(),
[create](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwindow.html#create)(),
[destroy](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwindow.html#destroy)(), and
[QSurfaceFormat::setDefaultFormat](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qsurfaceformat.html#setDefaultFormat)().

[create](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwindow.html#create)() to release the old

Qt 5 reference:

### `[slot]` bool QWindow::startSystemMove()

Start a system-specific move operation

Calling this will start an interactive move operation on the window by platforms that
support it. The actual behavior may vary depending on the platform. Usually, it will
make the window follow the mouse cursor until a mouse button is released.

On platforms that support it, this method of moving windows is preferred over
`setPosition`, because it allows a more native look-and-feel of moving windows, e.g.
letting the window manager snap this window against other windows, or special tiling or
resizing behavior with animations when dragged to the edge of the screen. Furthermore,
on some platforms such as Wayland, `setPosition` is not supported, so this is the only
way the application can influence its position.

Returns true if the operation was supported by the system.

This function was introduced in Qt 5.15.

PythonQt.QtGui.QWindow.startSystemResize.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

### `[slot]` bool QWindow::startSystemResize([Qt::Edges](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qt.html#Edge-enum) *edges*)

Start a system-specific resize operation

Calling this will start an interactive resize operation on the window by platforms that
support it. The actual behavior may vary depending on the platform. Usually, it will
make the window resize so that its edge follows the mouse cursor.

On platforms that support it, this method of resizing windows is preferred over
`setGeometry`, because it allows a more native look-and-feel of resizing windows, e.g.
letting the window manager snap this window against other windows, or special resizing
behavior with animations when dragged to the edge of the screen.

*edges* should either be a single edge, or two adjacent edges (a corner). Other values
are not allowed.

Returns true if the operation was supported by the system.

This function was introduced in Qt 5.15.

PythonQt.QtGui.QWindow.visible.doc:

### visible : bool

This property holds whether the window is visible or not

This property controls the visibility of the window in the windowing system.

By default, the window is not visible, you must call setVisible(true), or
[show](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwindow.html#show)() or similar to make it
visible.

**Note:** Hiding a window does not remove the window from the windowing system, it only
hides it. On windowing systems that give full screen applications a dedicated desktop
(such as macOS), hiding a full screen window will not remove that desktop, but leave it
blank. Another window from the same application might be shown full screen, and will
fill that desktop. Use
[QWindow::close](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwindow.html#close) to completely
remove a window from the windowing system.

**Access functions:**

| --- | --- |

### `[virtual protected]` void QWizard::initializePage(int *id*)

This virtual function is called by
[QWizard](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizard.html) to prepare page *id* just
before it is shown either as a result of
[QWizard::restart](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizard.html#restart)() being

[QWizard::IndependentPages](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizard.html#WizardOption-enum)

By reimplementing this function, you can ensure that the page's fields are properly
initialized based on fields from previous pages.

The default implementation calls
[QWizardPage::initializePage](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizardpage.html#initializePage)()
on page(*id*).

[QWizardPage::initializePage](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizardpage.html#initializePage)()

### `[virtual]` int QWizard::nextId() const

[QWizard](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizard.html) to find out which page to

### void QWizard::setButtonLayout(const [QList](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qlist.html)\<[QWizard::WizardButton](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizard.html#WizardButton-enum)\> \&*layout*)

Sets the order in which buttons are displayed to *layout*, where *layout* is a list of
[WizardButton](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizard.html#WizardButton-enum)s.

The default layout depends on the options (e.g., whether
[HelpButtonOnRight](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizard.html#WizardOption-enum))
that are set. You can call this function if you need more control over the buttons'
layout than what
[options](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtwidgets-cmake-qt-wrap-ui.html#options)
already provides.

You can specify horizontal stretches in the layout using
[Stretch](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizard.html#WizardButton-enum).

Example:

```
MyWizard::MyWizard(QWidget *parent)
    : QWizard(parent)
{
    ...
    QList<QWizard::WizardButton> layout;
    layout << QWizard::Stretch << QWizard::BackButton << QWizard::CancelButton
           << QWizard::NextButton << QWizard::FinishButton;
    setButtonLayout(layout);
    ...
}
```

**See also** [setButton](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizard.html#setButton)(),
[setButtonText](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizard.html#setButtonText)(), and
[setOptions](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizard.html#options-prop)().

### void QWizard::setSideWidget([QWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#QWidget) \**widget*)

Sets the given *widget* to be shown on the left side of the wizard. For styles which use
the [WatermarkPixmap](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizard.html#WizardPixmap-enum)
([ClassicStyle](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizard.html#WizardStyle-enum) and
[ModernStyle](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizard.html#WizardStyle-enum)) the
side widget is displayed on top of the watermark, for other styles or when the watermark
is not provided the side widget is displayed on the left side of the wizard.

Passing `nullptr` shows no side widget.

When the *widget* is not `nullptr` the wizard reparents it.

Any previous side widget is hidden.

You may call setSideWidget() with the same widget at different times.

All widgets set here will be deleted by the wizard when it is destroyed unless you
separately reparent the widget after setting some other side widget (or `nullptr`).

By default, no side widget is present.

This function was introduced in Qt 4.7.

**See also** [sideWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizard.html#sideWidget)().

Qt 5 reference:

### `[virtual]` bool QWizard::validateCurrentPage()

This virtual function is called by
[QWizard](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizard.html) when the user clicks **Next**
or **Finish** to perform some last-minute validation. If it returns `true`, the next
page is shown (or the wizard finishes); otherwise, the current page stays up.

The default implementation calls
[QWizardPage::validatePage](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizardpage.html#validatePage)()
on the [currentPage](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizard.html#currentPage)().

When possible, it is usually better style to disable the **Next** or **Finish** button
(by specifying [mandatory
fields](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizard.html#mandatory-fields) or by
reimplementing
[QWizardPage::isComplete](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizardpage.html#isComplete)())
than to reimplement validateCurrentPage().

**See also**
[QWizardPage::validatePage](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizardpage.html#validatePage)()
and [currentPage](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizard.html#currentPage)().

PythonQt.QtGui.QWizardPage.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

[QWizard](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizard.html) represents a wizard. Each
page is a QWizardPage. When you create your own wizards, you can use QWizardPage
directly, or you can subclass it for more control.

A page has the following attributes, which are rendered by
[QWizard](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizard.html): a
[title](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizardpage.html#title-prop), a
[subTitle](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizardpage.html#subTitle-prop), and a
[set of pixmaps](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizardpage.html#setPixmap). See
[Elements of a Wizard
Page](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizard.html#elements-of-a-wizard-page) for
details. Once a page is added to the wizard (using
[QWizard::addPage](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizard.html#addPage)() or
[QWizard::setPage](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizard.html#setPage)()),
[wizard](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizardpage.html#wizard)() returns a pointer
to the associated [QWizard](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizard.html) object.

Page provides five virtual functions that can be reimplemented to provide custom
behavior:

- [initializePage](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizardpage.html#initializePage)() is called to initialize the page's contents when the user clicks the wizard's **Next** button. If you want to derive the page's default from what the user entered on previous pages, this is the function to reimplement.
- [cleanupPage](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizardpage.html#cleanupPage)() is called to reset the page's contents when the user clicks the wizard's **Back** button.
- [validatePage](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizardpage.html#validatePage)() validates the page when the user clicks **Next** or **Finish**. It is often used to show an error message if the user has entered incomplete or invalid information.
- [nextId](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizardpage.html#nextId)() returns the ID of the next page. It is useful when [creating non-linear wizards](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizard.html#creating-non-linear-wizards), which allow different traversal paths based on the information provided by the user.
- [isComplete](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizardpage.html#isComplete)() is called to determine whether the **Next** and/or **Finish** button should be enabled or disabled. If you reimplement [isComplete](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizardpage.html#isComplete)(), also make sure that [completeChanged](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizardpage.html#completeChanged)() is emitted whenever the complete state changes.

Normally, the **Next** button and the **Finish** button of a wizard are mutually
exclusive. If
[isFinalPage](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizardpage.html#isFinalPage)() returns
`true`, **Finish** is available; otherwise, **Next** is available. By default,
[isFinalPage](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizardpage.html#isFinalPage)() is true
only when [nextId](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizardpage.html#nextId)() returns
-1. If you want to show **Next** and **Final** simultaneously for a page (letting the
user perform an "early finish"), call
[setFinalPage](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizardpage.html#setFinalPage)(true)
on that page. For wizards that support early finishes, you might also want to set the
[HaveNextButtonOnLastPage](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizard.html#WizardOption-enum)
and
[HaveFinishButtonOnEarlyPages](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizard.html#WizardOption-enum)
options on the wizard.

In many wizards, the contents of a page may affect the default values of the fields of a
later page. To make it easy to communicate between pages,
[QWizard](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizard.html) supports a ["field"
mechanism](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizard.html#registering-and-using-fields)
that allows you to register a field (e.g., a
[QLineEdit](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qlineedit.html)) on a page and to access
its value from any page. Fields are global to the entire wizard and make it easy for any
single page to access information stored by another page, without having to put all the
logic in [QWizard](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizard.html) or having the pages
know explicitly about each other. Fields are registered using
[registerField](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizardpage.html#registerField)() and
can be accessed at any time using
[field](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizardpage.html#field)() and
[setField](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizardpage.html#setField)().

### `[virtual]` void QWizardPage::cleanupPage()

This virtual function is called by
[QWizard::cleanupPage](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizard.html#cleanupPage)()
when the user leaves the page by clicking **Back** (unless the
[QWizard::IndependentPages](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizard.html#WizardOption-enum)

### `[signal]` void QWizardPage::completeChanged()

This signal is emitted whenever the complete state of the page (i.e., the value of
[isComplete](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizardpage.html#isComplete)()) changes.

If you reimplement
[isComplete](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizardpage.html#isComplete)(), make
sure to emit completeChanged() whenever the value of
[isComplete](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizardpage.html#isComplete)() changes,
to ensure that [QWizard](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizard.html) updates the
enabled or disabled state of its buttons.

**See also**
[isComplete](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizardpage.html#isComplete)().

PythonQt.QtGui.QWizardPage.initializePag.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

### `[virtual]` void QWizardPage::initializePage()

This virtual function is called by
[QWizard::initializePage](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizard.html#initializePage)()
to prepare the page just before it is shown either as a result of
[QWizard::restart](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizard.html#restart)() being
called, or as a result of the user clicking **Next**. (However, if the
[QWizard::IndependentPages](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizard.html#WizardOption-enum)
option is set, this function is only called the first time the page is shown.)

By reimplementing this function, you can ensure that the page's fields are properly
initialized based on fields from previous pages. For example:

```
void OutputFilesPage::initializePage()
{
    QString className = field("className").toString();
    headerLineEdit->setText(className.toLower() + ".h");
    implementationLineEdit->setText(className.toLower() + ".cpp");
    outputDirLineEdit->setText(QDir::toNativeSeparators(QDir::tempPath()));
}
```

The default implementation does nothing.

**See also**
[QWizard::initializePage](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizard.html#initializePage)(),
[cleanupPage](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizardpage.html#cleanupPage)(), and
[QWizard::IndependentPages](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizard.html#WizardOption-enum).

PythonQt.QtGui.QWizardPage.isComplete.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

### `[virtual]` bool QWizardPage::isComplete() const

This virtual function is called by
[QWizard](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizard.html) to determine whether the
**Next** or **Finish** button should be enabled or disabled.

The default implementation returns `true` if all [mandatory
fields](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizard.html#mandatory-fields) are filled;
otherwise, it returns `false`.

If you reimplement this function, make sure to emit
[completeChanged](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizardpage.html#completeChanged)(),
from the rest of your implementation, whenever the value of isComplete() changes. This
ensures that [QWizard](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizard.html) updates the
enabled or disabled state of its buttons. An example of the reimplementation is
available
[here](http://doc.qt.io/archives/qq/qq22-qwizard.html#validatebeforeitstoolate).

**See also**
[completeChanged](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizardpage.html#completeChanged)()
and [isFinalPage](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizardpage.html#isFinalPage)().

PythonQt.QtGui.QWizardPage.isFinalPage.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

### bool QWizardPage::isFinalPage() const

This function is called by [QWizard](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizard.html) to
determine whether the **Finish** button should be shown for this page or not.

By default, it returns `true` if there is no next page (i.e.,
[nextId](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizardpage.html#nextId)() returns -1);
otherwise, it returns `false`.

By explicitly calling
[setFinalPage](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizardpage.html#setFinalPage)(true),
you can let the user perform an "early finish".

**See also**
[isComplete](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizardpage.html#isComplete)() and
[QWizard::HaveFinishButtonOnEarlyPages](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizard.html#WizardOption-enum).

PythonQt.QtGui.QWizardPage.registerField.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

### `[protected]` void QWizardPage::registerField(const [QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html) \&*name*, [QWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwidget.html#QWidget) \**widget*, const char \**property* \= nullptr, const char \**changedSignal* \= nullptr)

Creates a field called *name* associated with the given *property* of the given
*widget*. From then on, that property becomes accessible using
[field](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizardpage.html#field)() and
[setField](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizardpage.html#setField)().

Fields are global to the entire wizard and make it easy for any single page to access
information stored by another page, without having to put all the logic in
[QWizard](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizard.html) or having the pages know
explicitly about each other.

If *name* ends with an asterisk (`*`), the field is a mandatory field. When a page has
mandatory fields, the **Next** and/or **Finish** buttons are enabled only when all
mandatory fields are filled. This requires a *changedSignal* to be specified, to tell
[QWizard](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizard.html) to recheck the value stored
by the mandatory field.

[QWizard](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizard.html) knows the most common Qt
widgets. For these (or their subclasses), you don't need to specify a *property* or a
*changedSignal*. The table below lists these widgets:

| Widget | Property | Change Notification Signal |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [QAbstractButton](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractbutton.html) | bool [checked](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractbutton.html#checked-prop) | [toggled()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractbutton.html#toggled) |
| [QAbstractSlider](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html) | int [value](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html#value-prop) | [valueChanged()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractslider.html#valueChanged) |
| [QComboBox](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcombobox.html) | int [currentIndex](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcombobox.html#currentIndex-prop) | [currentIndexChanged()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qcombobox.html#currentIndexChanged) |
| [QDateTimeEdit](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdatetimeedit.html) | [QDateTime](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdatetime.html) [dateTime](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdatetimeedit.html#dateTime-prop) | [dateTimeChanged()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdatetimeedit.html#dateTimeChanged) |
| [QLineEdit](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qlineedit.html) | [QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html) [text](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qlineedit.html#text-prop) | [textChanged()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qlineedit.html#textChanged) |
| [QListWidget](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qlistwidget.html) | int [currentRow](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qlistwidget.html#currentRow-prop) | [currentRowChanged()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qlistwidget.html#currentRowChanged) |
| [QSpinBox](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qspinbox.html) | int [value](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qspinbox.html#value-prop) | [valueChanged()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qspinbox.html#valueChanged) |

You can use
[QWizard::setDefaultProperty](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizard.html#setDefaultProperty)()
to add entries to this table or to override existing entries.

To consider a field "filled", [QWizard](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizard.html)
simply checks that their current value doesn't equal their original value (the value
they had before
[initializePage](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizardpage.html#initializePage)()
was called). For [QLineEdit](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qlineedit.html), it also
checks that
[hasAcceptableInput()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qlineedit.html#acceptableInput-prop)
returns true, to honor any validator or mask.

### void QWizardPage::setCommitPage(bool *commitPage*)

Sets this page to be a commit page if *commitPage* is true; otherwise, sets it to be a
normal page.

A commit page is a page that represents an action which cannot be undone by clicking
**Back** or **Cancel**.

A **Commit** button replaces the **Next** button on a commit page. Clicking this button
simply calls [QWizard::next](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizard.html#next)()
just like clicking **Next** does.

A page entered directly from a commit page has its **Back** button disabled.

**See also**
[isCommitPage](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qwizardpage.html#isCommitPage)().

PythonQt.QtNetwork.QAbstractSocket.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

QAbstractSocket is the base class for
[QTcpSocket](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtcpsocket.html) and
[QUdpSocket](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qudpsocket.html) and contains all common
functionality of these two classes. If you need a socket, you have two options:

- Instantiate [QTcpSocket](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtcpsocket.html) or [QUdpSocket](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qudpsocket.html).
- Create a native socket descriptor, instantiate QAbstractSocket, and call [setSocketDescriptor](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#setSocketDescriptor)() to wrap the native socket.

TCP (Transmission Control Protocol) is a reliable, stream-oriented, connection-oriented
transport protocol. UDP (User Datagram Protocol) is an unreliable, datagram-oriented,
connectionless protocol. In practice, this means that TCP is better suited for
continuous transmission of data, whereas the more lightweight UDP can be used when
reliability isn't important.

QAbstractSocket's API unifies most of the differences between the two protocols. For
example, although UDP is connectionless,
[connectToHost](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#connectToHost)()
establishes a virtual connection for UDP sockets, enabling you to use QAbstractSocket in
more or less the same way regardless of the underlying protocol. Internally,
QAbstractSocket remembers the address and port passed to
[connectToHost](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#connectToHost)(),
and functions like [read](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qiodevice.html#read)() and
[write](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qiodevice.html#write)() use these values.

At any time, QAbstractSocket has a state (returned by
[state](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#state)()). The initial
state is
[UnconnectedState](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#SocketState-enum).
After calling
[connectToHost](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#connectToHost)(),
the socket first enters
[HostLookupState](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#SocketState-enum).
If the host is found, QAbstractSocket enters
[ConnectingState](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#SocketState-enum)
and emits the
[hostFound](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#hostFound)() signal.
When the connection has been established, it enters
[ConnectedState](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#SocketState-enum)
and emits
[connected](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#connected)(). If an
error occurs at any stage,
[errorOccurred](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#errorOccurred)()
is emitted. Whenever the state changes,
[stateChanged](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#stateChanged)()
is emitted. For convenience,
[isValid](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#isValid)() returns
`true` if the socket is ready for reading and writing, but note that the socket's state
must be
[ConnectedState](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#SocketState-enum)
before reading and writing can occur.

Read or write data by calling
[read](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qiodevice.html#read)() or
[write](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qiodevice.html#write)(), or use the
convenience functions
[readLine](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qiodevice.html#readLine)() and
[readAll](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qiodevice.html#readAll)(). QAbstractSocket
also inherits [getChar](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qiodevice.html#getChar)(),
[putChar](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qiodevice.html#putChar)(), and
[ungetChar](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qiodevice.html#ungetChar)() from
[QIODevice](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qiodevice.html), which work on single
bytes. The
[bytesWritten](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qiodevice.html#bytesWritten)() signal
is emitted when data has been written to the socket. Note that Qt does not limit the
write buffer size. You can monitor its size by listening to this signal.

The [readyRead](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qiodevice.html#readyRead)() signal is
emitted every time a new chunk of data has arrived.
[bytesAvailable](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#bytesAvailable)()
then returns the number of bytes that are available for reading. Typically, you would
connect the [readyRead](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qiodevice.html#readyRead)()
signal to a slot and read all available data there. If you don't read all the data at
once, the remaining data will still be available later, and any new incoming data will
be appended to QAbstractSocket's internal read buffer. To limit the size of the read
buffer, call
[setReadBufferSize](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#setReadBufferSize)().

To close the socket, call
[disconnectFromHost](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#disconnectFromHost)().
QAbstractSocket enters
[QAbstractSocket::ClosingState](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#SocketState-enum).
After all pending data has been written to the socket, QAbstractSocket actually closes
the socket, enters
[QAbstractSocket::UnconnectedState](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#SocketState-enum),
and emits
[disconnected](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#disconnected)().
If you want to abort a connection immediately, discarding all pending data, call
[abort](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#abort)() instead. If the
remote host closes the connection, QAbstractSocket will emit
[errorOccurred](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#errorOccurred)([QAbstractSocket::RemoteHostClosedError](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#SocketError-enum)),
during which the socket state will still be
[ConnectedState](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#SocketState-enum),
and then the
[disconnected](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#disconnected)()
signal will be emitted.

The port and address of the connected peer is fetched by calling
[peerPort](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#peerPort)() and
[peerAddress](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#peerAddress)().
[peerName](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#peerName)() returns
the host name of the peer, as passed to
[connectToHost](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#connectToHost)().
[localPort](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#localPort)() and
[localAddress](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#localAddress)()
return the port and address of the local socket.

QAbstractSocket provides a set of functions that suspend the calling thread until
certain signals are emitted. These functions can be used to implement blocking sockets:

- [waitForConnected](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#waitForConnected)() blocks until a connection has been established.
- [waitForReadyRead](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#waitForReadyRead)() blocks until new data is available for reading.
- [waitForBytesWritten](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#waitForBytesWritten)() blocks until one payload of data has been written to the socket.
- [waitForDisconnected](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#waitForDisconnected)() blocks until the connection has closed.

We show an example:

```
    int numRead = 0, numReadTotal = 0;
    char buffer[50];

    forever {
        numRead  = socket.read(buffer, 50);

        // do whatever with array

        numReadTotal += numRead;
        if (numRead == 0 && !socket.waitForReadyRead())
            break;
    }
```

If
[waitForReadyRead()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qiodevice.html#waitForReadyRead)
returns `false`, the connection has been closed or an error has occurred.

Programming with a blocking socket is radically different from programming with a
non-blocking socket. A blocking socket doesn't require an event loop and typically leads
to simpler code. However, in a GUI application, blocking sockets should only be used in
non-GUI threads, to avoid freezing the user interface. See the
[fortuneclient](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtnetwork-fortuneclient-example.html)
and
[blockingfortuneclient](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtnetwork-blockingfortuneclient-example.html)
examples for an overview of both approaches.

**Note:** We discourage the use of the blocking functions together with signals. One of
the two possibilities should be used.

QAbstractSocket can be used with
[QTextStream](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtextstream.html) and
[QDataStream](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qdatastream.html)'s stream operators
(operator\<\<() and operator\>\>()). There is one issue to be aware of, though: You must
make sure that enough data is available before attempting to read it using
operator\>\>().

### bool QAbstractSocket::bind(const [QHostAddress](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qhostaddress.html) \&*address*, [quint16](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtglobal.html#quint16-typedef) *port* \= 0, [QAbstractSocket::BindMode](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#BindFlag-enum) *mode* \= ...)

Binds to *address* on port *port*, using the
[BindMode](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#BindFlag-enum)
*mode*.

For UDP sockets, after binding, the signal
[QUdpSocket::readyRead](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qiodevice.html#readyRead)()
is emitted whenever a UDP datagram arrives on the specified address and port. Thus, this
function is useful to write UDP servers.

For TCP sockets, this function may be used to specify which interface to use for an
outgoing connection, which is useful in case of multiple network interfaces.

By default, the socket is bound using the
[DefaultForPlatform](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#BindFlag-enum)
[BindMode](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#BindFlag-enum). If a
port is not specified, a random port is chosen.

On success, the function returns `true` and the socket enters
[BoundState](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#SocketState-enum);
otherwise it returns `false`.

This function was introduced in Qt 5.0.

Qt 5 reference:

### `[virtual]` void QAbstractSocket::connectToHost(const [QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html) \&*hostName*, [quint16](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtglobal.html#quint16-typedef) *port*, [QIODevice::OpenMode](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qiodevice.html#OpenModeFlag-enum) *openMode* \= ReadWrite, [QAbstractSocket::NetworkLayerProtocol](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#NetworkLayerProtocol-enum) *protocol* \= AnyIPProtocol)

Attempts to make a connection to *hostName* on the given *port*. The *protocol*
parameter can be used to specify which network protocol to use (eg. IPv4 or IPv6).

The socket is opened in the given *openMode* and first enters
[HostLookupState](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#SocketState-enum),
then performs a host name lookup of *hostName*. If the lookup succeeds,
[hostFound](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#hostFound)() is
emitted and [QAbstractSocket](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html)
enters
[ConnectingState](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#SocketState-enum).
It then attempts to connect to the address or addresses returned by the lookup. Finally,
if a connection is established,
[QAbstractSocket](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html) enters
[ConnectedState](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#SocketState-enum)
and emits
[connected](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#connected)().

At any point, the socket can emit
[errorOccurred](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#errorOccurred)()
to signal that an error occurred.

*hostName* may be an IP address in string form (e.g., "43.195.83.32"), or it may be a
host name (e.g., "example.com").
[QAbstractSocket](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html) will do a
lookup only if required. *port* is in native byte order.

**See also** [state](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#state)(),
[peerName](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#peerName)(),
[peerAddress](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#peerAddress)(),
[peerPort](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#peerPort)(), and
[waitForConnected](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#waitForConnected)().

### bool QAbstractSocket::flush()

This function writes as much as possible from the internal write buffer to the
underlying network socket, without blocking. If any data was written, this function
returns `true`; otherwise false is returned.

Call this function if you need
[QAbstractSocket](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html) to start
sending buffered data immediately. The number of bytes successfully written depends on
the operating system. In most cases, you do not need to call this function, because
[QAbstractSocket](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html) will start
sending data automatically once control goes back to the event loop. In the absence of
an event loop, call
[waitForBytesWritten](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#waitForBytesWritten)()
instead.

**See also** [write](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qiodevice.html#write)() and
[waitForBytesWritten](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#waitForBytesWritten)().

### `[virtual]` void QAbstractSocket::resume()

Continues data transfer on the socket. This method should only be used after the socket
has been set to pause upon notifications and a notification has been received. The only
notification currently supported is QSslSocket::sslErrors(). Calling this method if the
socket is not paused results in undefined behavior.

This function was introduced in Qt 5.0.

**See also**
[pauseMode](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#pauseMode)() and
[setPauseMode](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#setPauseMode)().

### void QAbstractSocket::setPauseMode([QAbstractSocket::PauseModes](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#PauseMode-enum) *pauseMode*)

Controls whether to pause upon receiving a notification. The *pauseMode* parameter
specifies the conditions in which the socket should be paused. The only notification
currently supported is QSslSocket::sslErrors(). If set to
[PauseOnSslErrors](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#PauseMode-enum),
data transfer on the socket will be paused and needs to be enabled explicitly again by
calling [resume](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#resume)(). By
default this option is set to
[PauseNever](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#PauseMode-enum).
This option must be called before connecting to the server, otherwise it will result in
undefined behavior.

This function was introduced in Qt 5.0.

**See also**
[pauseMode](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#pauseMode)() and
[resume](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#resume)().

### void QAbstractSocket::setProxy(const [QNetworkProxy](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qnetworkproxy.html) \&*networkProxy*)

Sets the explicit network proxy for this socket to *networkProxy*.

To disable the use of a proxy for this socket, use the
[QNetworkProxy::NoProxy](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qnetworkproxy.html#ProxyType-enum)
proxy type:

```
socket->setProxy(QNetworkProxy::NoProxy);
```

The default value for the proxy is
[QNetworkProxy::DefaultProxy](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qnetworkproxy.html#ProxyType-enum),
which means the socket will use the application settings: if a proxy is set with
[QNetworkProxy::setApplicationProxy](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qnetworkproxy.html#setApplicationProxy),
it will use that; otherwise, if a factory is set with
[QNetworkProxyFactory::setApplicationProxyFactory](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qnetworkproxyfactory.html#setApplicationProxyFactory),
it will query that factory with type
[QNetworkProxyQuery::TcpSocket](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qnetworkproxyquery.html#QueryType-enum).

This function was introduced in Qt 4.1.

**See also** [proxy](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#proxy)(),
[QNetworkProxy](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qnetworkproxy.html), and
[QNetworkProxyFactory::queryProxy](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qnetworkproxyfactory.html#queryProxy)().

### `[virtual]` void QAbstractSocket::setReadBufferSize([qint64](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtglobal.html#qint64-typedef) *size*)

Sets the size of
[QAbstractSocket](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html)'s internal
read buffer to be *size* bytes.

If the buffer size is limited to a certain size,
[QAbstractSocket](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html) won't buffer
more than this size of data. Exceptionally, a buffer size of 0 means that the read
buffer is unlimited and all incoming data is buffered. This is the default.

This option is useful if you only read the data at certain points in time (e.g., in a
real-time streaming application) or if you want to protect your socket against receiving
too much data, which may eventually cause your application to run out of memory.

Only [QTcpSocket](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtcpsocket.html) uses
[QAbstractSocket](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html)'s internal
buffer; [QUdpSocket](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qudpsocket.html) does not use
any buffering at all, but rather relies on the implicit buffering provided by the
operating system. Because of this, calling this function on
[QUdpSocket](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qudpsocket.html) has no effect.

**See also**
[readBufferSize](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#readBufferSize)()
and [read](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qiodevice.html#read)().

### `[override virtual]` bool QAbstractSocket::waitForBytesWritten(int *msecs* \= 30000\)

Reimplements:
[QIODevice::waitForBytesWritten](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qiodevice.html#waitForBytesWritten)(int
msecs).

This function blocks until at least one byte has been written on the socket and the
[bytesWritten()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qiodevice.html#bytesWritten) signal
has been emitted. The function will timeout after *msecs* milliseconds; the default
timeout is 30000 milliseconds.

The function returns `true` if the
[bytesWritten](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qiodevice.html#bytesWritten)() signal
is emitted; otherwise it returns `false` (if an error occurred or the operation timed
out).

**Note:** This function may fail randomly on Windows. Consider using the event loop and
the [bytesWritten](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qiodevice.html#bytesWritten)()
signal if your software will run on Windows.

**See also**
[waitForReadyRead](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#waitForReadyRead)().

### `[virtual]` bool QAbstractSocket::waitForConnected(int *msecs* \= 30000\)

Waits until the socket is connected, up to *msecs* milliseconds. If the connection has
been established, this function returns `true`; otherwise it returns `false`. In the
case where it returns `false`, you can call
[error](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#error)() to determine
the cause of the error.

The following example waits up to one second for a connection to be established:

```
socket->connectToHost("imap", 143);
if (socket->waitForConnected(1000))
    qDebug("Connected!");
```

If msecs is -1, this function will not time out.

**Note:** This function may wait slightly longer than *msecs*, depending on the time it
takes to complete the host lookup.

**Note:** Multiple calls to this functions do not accumulate the time. If the function
times out, the connecting process will be aborted.

**Note:** This function may fail randomly on Windows. Consider using the event loop and
the [connected](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#connected)()
signal if your software will run on Windows.

**See also**
[connectToHost](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#connectToHost)()
and [connected](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#connected)().

Qt 5 reference:

### `[virtual]` bool QAbstractSocket::waitForDisconnected(int *msecs* \= 30000\)

Waits until the socket has disconnected, up to *msecs* milliseconds. If the connection
was successfully disconnected, this function returns `true`; otherwise it returns
`false` (if the operation timed out, if an error occurred, or if this
[QAbstractSocket](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html) is already
disconnected). In the case where it returns `false`, you can call
[error](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#error)() to determine
the cause of the error.

The following example waits up to one second for a connection to be closed:

```
socket->disconnectFromHost();
if (socket->state() == QAbstractSocket::UnconnectedState
    || socket->waitForDisconnected(1000)) {
        qDebug("Disconnected!");
}
```

If msecs is -1, this function will not time out.

**Note:** This function may fail randomly on Windows. Consider using the event loop and
the
[disconnected](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#disconnected)()
signal if your software will run on Windows.

**See also**
[disconnectFromHost](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#disconnectFromHost)()
and [close](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html#close)().

## Detailed Description

The QAuthenticator class is usually used in the
[authenticationRequired()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qnetworkaccessmanager.html#authenticationRequired)
and
[proxyAuthenticationRequired()](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qnetworkaccessmanager.html#proxyAuthenticationRequired)
signals of
[QNetworkAccessManager](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qnetworkaccessmanager.html)
and [QAbstractSocket](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qabstractsocket.html). The
class provides a way to pass back the required authentication information to the socket
when accessing services that require authentication.

QAuthenticator supports the following authentication methods:

- Basic
- NTLM version 2
- Digest-MD5
- SPNEGO/Negotiate

### Options

In addition to the username and password required for authentication, a QAuthenticator
object can also contain additional options. The
[options](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qauthenticator.html#options)() function can
be used to query incoming options sent by the server; the
[setOption](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qauthenticator.html#setOption)() function
can be used to set outgoing options, to be processed by the authenticator calculation.
The options accepted and provided depend on the authentication type (see method()).

The following tables list known incoming options as well as accepted outgoing options.
The list of incoming options is not exhaustive, since servers may include additional
information at any time. The list of outgoing options is exhaustive, however, and no
unknown options will be treated or sent back to the server.

#### Basic

| Option | Direction | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `realm` | Incoming | [QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html) | Contains the realm of the authentication, the same as [realm](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qauthenticator.html#realm)() |

The Basic authentication mechanism supports no outgoing options.

#### NTLM version 2

The NTLM authentication mechanism currently supports no incoming or outgoing options. On
Windows, if no *user* has been set, domain\\user credentials will be searched for on the
local system to enable Single-Sign-On functionality.

#### Digest-MD5

| Option | Direction | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `realm` | Incoming | [QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html) | Contains the realm of the authentication, the same as [realm](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qauthenticator.html#realm)() |

The Digest-MD5 authentication mechanism supports no outgoing options.

#### SPNEGO/Negotiate

This authentication mechanism currently supports no incoming or outgoing options.

PythonQt.QtNetwork.QHostAddress.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

## Detailed Description

This class holds an IPv4 or IPv6 address in a platform- and protocol-independent manner.

QHostAddress is normally used with the
[QTcpSocket](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtcpsocket.html),
[QTcpServer](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qtcpserver.html), and
[QUdpSocket](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qudpsocket.html) to connect to a host or
to set up a server.

A host address is set with
[setAddress](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qhostaddress.html#setAddress)(), and
retrieved with
[toIPv4Address](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qhostaddress.html#toIPv4Address)(),
[toIPv6Address](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qhostaddress.html#toIPv6Address)(),
or [toString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qhostaddress.html#toString)(). You can
check the type with
[protocol](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qhostaddress.html#protocol)().

**Note:** Please note that QHostAddress does not do DNS lookups.
[QHostInfo](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qhostinfo.html) is needed for that.

The class also supports common predefined addresses:
[Null](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qhostaddress.html#SpecialAddress-enum),
[LocalHost](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qhostaddress.html#SpecialAddress-enum),
[LocalHostIPv6](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qhostaddress.html#SpecialAddress-enum),
[Broadcast](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qhostaddress.html#SpecialAddress-enum),
and [Any](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qhostaddress.html#SpecialAddress-enum).

PythonQt.QtNetwork.QHostAddress.isInSubn.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

### bool QHostAddress::isInSubnet(const [QHostAddress](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qhostaddress.html#QHostAddress) \&*subnet*, int *netmask*) const

Returns `true` if this IP is in the subnet described by the network prefix *subnet* and
netmask *netmask*.

An IP is considered to belong to a subnet if it is contained between the lowest and the
highest address in that subnet. In the case of IP version 4, the lowest address is the
network address, while the highest address is the broadcast address.

The *subnet* argument does not have to be the actual network address (the lowest address
in the subnet). It can be any valid IP belonging to that subnet. In particular, if it is
equal to the IP address held by this object, this function will always return true
(provided the netmask is a valid value).

This function was introduced in Qt 4.5.

**See also**
[parseSubnet](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qhostaddress.html#parseSubnet)().

### bool QHostAddress::isInSubnet(const [QPair](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpair.html)\<[QHostAddress](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qhostaddress.html#QHostAddress), int\> \&*subnet*) const

This is an overloaded function.

Returns `true` if this IP is in the subnet described by *subnet*. The
[QHostAddress](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qhostaddress.html) member of *subnet*
contains the network prefix and the int (second) member contains the netmask (prefix
length).

This function was introduced in Qt 4.5.
signatures: isInSubnet(self, subnet: PySide2.QtNetwork.QHostAddress, netmask: int) -> bool

PythonQt.QtNetwork.QHostAddress.parseSub.doc:
Qt 5 reference:

### `[static]` [QPair](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qpair.html)\<[QHostAddress](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qhostaddress.html#QHostAddress), int\> QHostAddress::parseSubnet(const [QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html) \&*subnet*)

Parses the IP and subnet information contained in *subnet* and returns the network
prefix for that network and its prefix length.

The IP address and the netmask must be separated by a slash (/).

This function supports arguments in the form:

- 123.123.123.123/n where n is any value between 0 and 32
- 123.123.123.123/255.255.255.255
- \<ipv6-address\>/n where n is any value between 0 and 128

For IP version 4, this function accepts as well missing trailing components (i.e., less
than 4 octets, like "192.168.1"), followed or not by a dot. If the netmask is also
missing in that case, it is set to the number of octets actually passed (in the example
above, it would be 24, for 3 octets).

This function was introduced in Qt 4.5.

**See also**
[isInSubnet](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qhostaddress.html#isInSubnet)().

Qt 5 reference:

### [QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html) QHostAddress::scopeId() const

Returns the scope ID of an IPv6 address. For IPv4 addresses, or if the address does not
contain a scope ID, an empty [QString](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qstring.html)
is returned.

The IPv6 scope ID specifies the scope of *reachability* for non-global IPv6 addresses,
limiting the area in which the address can be used. All IPv6 addresses are associated
with such a reachability scope. The scope ID is used to disambiguate addresses that are
not guaranteed to be globally unique.

IPv6 specifies the following four levels of reachability:

- Node-local: Addresses that are only used for communicating with services on the same interface (e.g., the loopback interface "::1").
- Link-local: Addresses that are local to the network interface (*link*). There is always one link-local address for each IPv6 interface on your host. Link-local addresses ("fe80...") are generated from the MAC address of the local network adaptor, and are not guaranteed to be unique.
- Global: For globally routable addresses, such as public servers on the Internet.

When using a link-local or site-local address for IPv6 connections, you must specify the
scope ID. The scope ID for a link-local address is usually the same as the interface
name (e.g., "eth0", "en1") or number (e.g., "1", "2").

This function was introduced in Qt 4.1.

**See also**
[setScopeId](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qhostaddress.html#setScopeId)(),
[QNetworkInterface](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qnetworkinterface.html), and
[QNetworkInterface::interfaceFromName](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qt-5.15/qnetworkinterface.html#interfaceFromName).
